pmid:18854539.finding: High-dose B vitamins (folate 5 mg, B6 25 mg, B12 1 mg) lowered homocysteine but did not slow cognitive decline over 18 months; depression adverse events were more frequent.

pmid:36856616.authors: Allen NC, Martin AJ, Snaidr VA, et al.
pmid:36856616.title: Nicotinamide for Skin-Cancer Chemoprevention in Transplant Recipients.
pmid:36856616.finding: ONTRANS: in immunosuppressed transplant recipients, nicotinamide 500 mg twice daily for 12 months did not reduce keratinocyte cancers (207 vs 210; rate ratio 1.0); the trial stopped early for poor recruitment.

pmid:16029679.authors: Bissett DL, Oblong JE, Berge CA
pmid:16029679.title: Niacinamide: A B vitamin that improves aging facial skin appearance.
pmid:16029679.finding: Procter & Gamble split-face trial: 5% topical niacinamide twice daily for 12 weeks reduced fine lines, hyperpigmented spots, red blotchiness and sallowness and improved elasticity versus vehicle.

pmid:40960808.authors: Breglio KF, Knox KM, Hwang J, et al.
pmid:40960808.title: Nicotinamide for Skin Cancer Chemoprevention.
pmid:40960808.finding: In Veterans Affairs records, nicotinamide 500 mg twice daily was associated with 14% lower skin-cancer risk overall and 54% lower risk when started after a first skin cancer; no overall reduction was seen in transplant recipients.

pmid:26488693.authors: Chen AC, Martin AJ, Choy B, et al.
pmid:26488693.title: A Phase 3 Randomized Trial of Nicotinamide for Skin-Cancer Chemoprevention.
pmid:26488693.finding: ONTRAC: nicotinamide 500 mg twice daily for 12 months cut new non-melanoma skin cancers by 23% (95% CI 4-38) and actinic keratoses by 11-20% versus placebo; there was no benefit after stopping.

pmid:24965307.authors: Clarke R, Bennett D, Parish S, et al.
pmid:24965307.title: Effects of homocysteine lowering with B vitamins on cognitive aging: meta-analysis of 11 trials with cognitive data on 22,000 individuals.
pmid:24965307.finding: Lowering homocysteine by about 25% with B vitamins had no effect on global or domain-specific cognitive aging, excluding benefits larger than 1 month per year.

pmid:21780182.authors: de Jager CA, Oulhaj A, Jacoby R, et al.
pmid:21780182.title: Cognitive and clinical outcomes of homocysteine-lowering B-vitamin treatment in mild cognitive impairment: a randomized controlled trial.
pmid:21780182.finding: B vitamins lowered homocysteine 30% and stabilized executive function; global cognition, memory and clinical ratings benefited only when baseline homocysteine was above the median (11.3 umol/L).

pmid:23690582.authors: Douaud G, Refsum H, de Jager CA, et al.
pmid:23690582.title: Preventing Alzheimer's disease-related gray matter atrophy by B-vitamin treatment.
pmid:23690582.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:23690582.finding: B vitamins reduced atrophy up to seven-fold in Alzheimer-vulnerable grey-matter regions, with benefit confined to those with high baseline homocysteine.

pmid:25877495.authors: Jernerén F, Elshorbagy AK, Oulhaj A, et al.
pmid:25877495.title: Brain atrophy in cognitively impaired elderly: the importance of long-chain ω-3 fatty acids and B vitamin status in a randomized controlled trial.
pmid:25877495.finding: B vitamins slowed atrophy by 40% in those with high baseline omega-3 (>590 umol/L) but not in those with low omega-3 (<390 umol/L).

pmid:35134311.authors: Mainville L, Smilga AS, Fortin PR
pmid:35134311.title: Effect of Nicotinamide in Skin Cancer and Actinic Keratoses Chemoprophylaxis, and Adverse Effects Related to Nicotinamide: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
pmid:35134311.finding: Nicotinamide halved skin cancers versus control (rate ratio 0.50, 0.29-0.85; 5 trials, 552 patients), with heterogeneity explained by risk of bias, and slightly increased digestive adverse effects.

pmid:15583582.authors: Middelkamp-Hup MA, Pathak MA, Parrado C, et al.
pmid:15583582.title: Oral Polypodium leucotomos extract decreases ultraviolet-induced damage of human skin.
pmid:15583582.finding: A single oral dose of Polypodium leucotomos extract (7.5 mg/kg) reduced UV erythema, sunburn cells, cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers and mast-cell infiltration in irradiated skin (uncontrolled within-person design).

pmid:26757190.authors: Oulhaj A, Jernerén F, Refsum H, et al.
pmid:26757190.title: Omega-3 Fatty Acid Status Enhances the Prevention of Cognitive Decline by B Vitamins in Mild Cognitive Impairment.
pmid:26757190.finding: Post hoc VITACOG analysis: B-vitamin effects on memory, global cognition and dementia rating increased with baseline plasma omega-3 levels; no benefit in those with low omega-3.

pmid:20838622.authors: Smith AD, Smith SM, de Jager CA, et al.
pmid:20838622.title: Homocysteine-lowering by B vitamins slows the rate of accelerated brain atrophy in mild cognitive impairment: a randomized controlled trial.
pmid:20838622.finding: VITACOG: folic acid 0.8 mg, B6 20 mg and B12 0.5 mg daily for 2 years slowed brain atrophy (0.76% vs 1.08%/year) and by 53% in those with homocysteine above 13 umol/L.

pmid:29480200.authors: Smith AD, Refsum H, Bottiglieri T, et al.
pmid:29480200.title: Homocysteine and Dementia: An International Consensus Statement.
pmid:29480200.finding: International consensus (Bradford Hill criteria): elevated plasma homocysteine is a modifiable risk factor for cognitive decline, dementia and Alzheimer disease in older people.

pmid:40196953.authors: Zundell MP, Katz A, Shah M, et al.
pmid:40196953.title: The Utility of Oral Polypodium Leucotomos Extract for Dermatologic Diseases: A Systematic Review.
pmid:40196953.finding: Systematic review of oral Polypodium leucotomos extract across photoaging/skin cancer, actinic keratosis, photodermatoses, melasma, vitiligo and atopic dermatitis: promising photoprotective signals and good safety, from small studies.

pmid:28056690.authors: Alexander EK, Pearce EN, Brent GA, et al.
pmid:28056690.title: 2017 Guidelines of the American Thyroid Association for the Diagnosis and Management of Thyroid Disease During Pregnancy and the Postpartum
pmid:28056690.finding: ATA 2017 pregnancy guideline including recommendations on iodine nutrition before and during pregnancy and lactation.

pmid:19420095.authors: Ashton K, Hooper L, Harvey LJ, et al.
pmid:19420095.title: Methods of assessment of selenium status in humans: a systematic review
pmid:19420095.finding: Plasma/whole-blood selenium, selenoprotein P and GPx activity respond to selenium intake and are usable status markers.

pmid:34815068.authors: Penzias A, Azziz R, Bendikson K, et al.
pmid:34815068.title: Optimizing natural fertility: a committee opinion
pmid:34815068.finding: ASRM committee opinion on optimizing natural fertility, including preconception folic acid.

pmid:23150011.title: Multiplicities in the assessment of multiple vitamins: is it too soon to tell men that vitamins prevent cancer?
pmid:23150011.finding: JAMA editorial questioning whether the PHS II cancer result, given multiple comparisons, justified telling men vitamins prevent cancer.

pmid:38922621.authors: Barnard ND, Kahleova H, Becker R
pmid:38922621.title: The Limited Value of Multivitamin Supplements
pmid:38922621.finding: Commentary on the cohort study arguing that multivitamins have limited value for healthy people.

pmid:23706508.authors: Bath SC, Steer CD, Golding J, et al.
pmid:23706508.title: Effect of inadequate iodine status in UK pregnant women on cognitive outcomes in their children: results from the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC)
pmid:23706508.finding: Children of mothers with iodine:creatinine <150 ug/g had higher odds of low verbal IQ (OR 1.58) and poor reading scores.

pmid:17620657.authors: Bleys J, Navas-Acien A, Guallar E
pmid:17620657.title: Selenium and diabetes: more bad news for supplements
pmid:17620657.finding: Editorial on the NPC diabetes result titled 'more bad news for supplements'.

pmid:31160241.authors: Buhling K, Schumacher A, Eulenburg CZ, et al.
pmid:31160241.title: Influence of oral vitamin and mineral supplementation on male infertility: a meta-analysis and systematic review
pmid:31160241.finding: Selenium (100-200 ug/day), CoQ10 and carnitines improved semen parameters in small trials; pregnancy data were scarce.

pmid:10357726.title: Toward a new recommended dietary allowance for vitamin C based on antioxidant and health effects in humans
pmid:10357726.finding: Argued that 90-100 mg/day vitamin C is needed for optimal chronic disease risk reduction and proposed an RDA of 120 mg/day.

pmid:27130885.authors: Chapman LE, Darling AL, Brown JE
pmid:27130885.title: Association between metformin and vitamin B(12) deficiency in patients with type 2 diabetes: A systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:27130885.finding: Metformin lowered B12 by about 57 pmol/L, causing deficiency or borderline status in some patients.

pmid:17624345.authors: Chavarro JE, Rich-Edwards JW, Rosner BA, et al.
pmid:17624345.title: Use of multivitamins, intake of B vitamins, and risk of ovulatory infertility
pmid:17624345.finding: Multivitamin use 6+ times a week was associated with 41% lower ovulatory infertility (RR 0.59), partly explained by folic acid.

pmid:17551129.authors: Cole BF, Baron JA, Sandler RS, et al.
pmid:17551129.title: Folic acid for the prevention of colorectal adenomas: a randomized clinical trial
pmid:17551129.finding: 1 mg/day folic acid did not reduce colorectal adenomas and may have raised advanced lesions (RR 1.67, P = .05).

pmid:26081493.authors: Cueto HT, Riis AH, Hatch EE, et al.
pmid:26081493.title: Folic acid supplementation and fecundability: a Danish prospective cohort study
pmid:26081493.finding: Folic acid supplement users had 15% higher fecundability (FR 1.15).

pmid:1550052.title: Longitudinal changes of manganese-dependent superoxide dismutase and other indexes of manganese and iron status in women
pmid:1550052.finding: 15 mg/day manganese raised lymphocyte MnSOD activity, showing SOD2 activity responds to manganese supply.

pmid:35506389.authors: de Ligny W, Smits RM, Mackenzie-Proctor R, et al.
pmid:35506389.title: Antioxidants for male subfertility
pmid:35506389.finding: Cochrane update: possible live birth increase (OR 1.43, very low certainty), no effect in low-risk-of-bias trials.

pmid:29387426.authors: DiNicolantonio JJ, O'Keefe JH, Wilson W
pmid:29387426.title: Subclinical magnesium deficiency: a principal driver of cardiovascular disease and a public health crisis
pmid:29387426.finding: Opinion review claiming subclinical magnesium deficiency is a principal driver of cardiovascular disease and a public health crisis (lead author discloses a related book).

pmid:19920243.title: Assessing cancer prevention studies--a matter of time
pmid:19920243.finding: Editorial on the Norwegian folic acid/B12 cancer finding discussing timing and interpretation of cancer prevention trials.

pmid:19920236.authors: Ebbing M, Bønaa KH, Nygård O, et al.
pmid:19920236.title: Cancer incidence and mortality after treatment with folic acid and vitamin B12
pmid:19920236.finding: Folic acid (0.8 mg) plus B12 raised cancer incidence (HR 1.21), cancer death (HR 1.38) and all-cause death (HR 1.18) in an unfortified population.

foundations:nut-efsa2006.authors: EFSA Scientific Committee on Food / Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition and Allergies
foundations:nut-efsa2006.title: Tolerable Upper Intake Levels for Vitamins and Minerals
foundations:nut-efsa2006.finding: EFSA/SCF compendium of tolerable upper intake levels (e.g. zinc 25 mg, copper 5 mg, iodine 600 ug, supplemental magnesium 250 mg per day for adults).

pmid:37965303.authors: EFSA NDA Panel: Turck D, Bohn T, Castenmiller J, et al.
pmid:37965303.title: Scientific opinion on the tolerable upper intake level for folate
pmid:37965303.finding: EFSA retained a 1000 ug/day UL for synthetic folic acid in adults, based on masking/progression of B12-deficiency neuropathy; cancer links judged insufficient.

pmid:36698500.authors: EFSA NDA Panel: Turck D, Bohn T, Castenmiller J, et al.
pmid:36698500.title: Scientific opinion on the tolerable upper intake level for selenium
pmid:36698500.finding: EFSA set a selenium UL of 255 ug/day for adults (including pregnancy), based on alopecia in SELECT at 330 ug/day.

pmid:6486080.authors: Fischer PW, Giroux A, L'Abbé MR
pmid:6486080.title: Effect of zinc supplementation on copper status in adult man
pmid:6486080.finding: 50 mg/day zinc for 6 weeks lowered erythrocyte Cu,Zn-superoxide dismutase activity, an early sign of reduced copper status.

pmid:2407097.title: Zinc toxicity
pmid:2407097.finding: Zinc at 100-300 mg/day induces copper deficiency with anaemia and neutropenia; even lower doses may impair copper and iron use and lower HDL.

pmid:24563520.authors: Frankel PH, Parker RS, Madsen FC, et al.
pmid:24563520.title: Baseline selenium and prostate cancer risk: comments and open questions
pmid:24563520.finding: Editorial raising open questions about the SELECT baseline-selenium analysis.

pmid:26354529.authors: Gaskins AJ, Chiu YH, Williams PL, et al.
pmid:26354529.title: Association between serum folate and vitamin B-12 and outcomes of assisted reproductive technologies
pmid:26354529.finding: Highest vs lowest quartile of serum B12 (>701 pg/mL) doubled live birth probability (RR 2.04); folate and B12 above the median together raised live birth by 26 points.

pmid:24490265.authors: Grodstein F, O'Brien J, Kang JH, et al.
pmid:24490265.title: Long-term multivitamin supplementation and cognitive function in men: a randomized trial
pmid:24490265.finding: Long-term multivitamin use did not slow cognitive decline.

pmid:33333394.authors: Hosseini R, Ferns GA, Sahebkar A, et al.
pmid:33333394.title: Zinc supplementation is associated with a reduction in serum markers of inflammation and oxidative stress in adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmid:33333394.finding: Zinc supplements lowered CRP (-0.92 mg/L), TNF-alpha and malondialdehyde, with very high heterogeneity.

pmid:33601291.authors: Hosseini R, Ferns GA, Sahebkar A, et al.
pmid:33601291.title: Response to commentary on 'zinc supplementation is associated with a reduction in serum markers of inflammation and oxidative stress in adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials'
pmid:33601291.finding: Authors' reply defending their zinc meta-analysis.

pmid:25771069.authors: Huo Y, Li J, Qin X, et al.
pmid:25771069.title: Efficacy of folic acid therapy in primary prevention of stroke among adults with hypertension in China: the CSPPT randomized clinical trial
pmid:25771069.finding: CSPPT: enalapril plus 0.8 mg folic acid cut first stroke by 21% (HR 0.79) vs enalapril alone in a population without folate fortification.

pmid:20181815.authors: Hurst R, Armah CN, Dainty JR, et al.
pmid:20181815.title: Establishing optimal selenium status: results of a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
pmid:20181815.finding: Selenoprotein P was optimised with ~50 ug/day selenium on top of a ~55 ug/day habitual intake; platelet GPx did not change.

pmid:23115811.authors: Institute of Medicine (US) Standing Committee on the Scientific Evaluation of Dietary Reference Intakes
pmid:23115811.title: Dietary Reference Intakes for Calcium, Phosphorus, Magnesium, Vitamin D, and Fluoride
pmid:23115811.finding: IOM DRI report for calcium, phosphorus, magnesium, vitamin D and fluoride (magnesium RDA 310-420 mg; UL 350 mg from supplements).

pmid:23193625.authors: Institute of Medicine (US) Standing Committee on the Scientific Evaluation of Dietary Reference Intakes and its Panel on Folate, Other B Vitamins, and Choline
pmid:23193625.title: Dietary Reference Intakes for Thiamin, Riboflavin, Niacin, Vitamin B(6), Folate, Vitamin B(12), Pantothenic Acid, Biotin, and Choline
pmid:23193625.finding: IOM DRI report for B vitamins and choline (riboflavin, folate, B12; folic acid UL 1000 ug; no UL for riboflavin or B12).

pmid:25077263.authors: Institute of Medicine (US) Panel on Dietary Antioxidants and Related Compounds
pmid:25077263.title: Dietary Reference Intakes for Vitamin C, Vitamin E, Selenium, and Carotenoids
pmid:25077263.finding: IOM DRI report for vitamin C, vitamin E, selenium and carotenoids (ULs: vitamin C 2000 mg, vitamin E 1000 mg, selenium 400 ug).

pmid:25057538.authors: Institute of Medicine (US) Panel on Micronutrients
pmid:25057538.title: Dietary Reference Intakes for Vitamin A, Vitamin K, Arsenic, Boron, Chromium, Copper, Iodine, Iron, Manganese, Molybdenum, Nickel, Silicon, Vanadium, and Zinc
pmid:25057538.finding: IOM DRI report for vitamin A, copper, iodine, iron, manganese, zinc and others (ULs: zinc 40 mg, copper 10 mg, iron 45 mg, iodine 1100 ug, manganese 11 mg, preformed vitamin A 3000 ug).

pmid:33571933.title: Comments on "Zinc supplementation is associated with a reduction in serum markers of inflammation and oxidative stress in adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials"
pmid:33571933.finding: Letter criticising the zinc meta-analysis for inadequate search, methodological flaws and interpretation that might bias results.

pmid:20232210.title: Copper deficiency myelopathy
pmid:20232210.finding: Copper deficiency myelopathy mimics B12 deficiency; risk factors include zinc overload, upper GI surgery and malabsorption; cytopenias in 78%.

pmid:34656303.authors: Jenkins T, Aston K, Carrell D, et al.
pmid:34656303.title: The impact of zinc and folic acid supplementation on sperm DNA methylation: results from the folic acid and zinc supplementation randomized clinical trial (FAZST)
pmid:34656303.finding: Folic acid plus zinc did not significantly change sperm DNA methylation patterns.

pmid:36626340.title: Expression of Concern: Efficacy of Selenium and/or N-Acetyl-Cysteine for Improving Semen Parameters in Infertile Men: A Double-Blind, Placebo Controlled, Randomized Study
pmid:36626340.finding: Journal of Urology Expression of Concern regarding the Safarinejad selenium/NAC trial.

pmid:12374615.title: The labile iron pool: characterization, measurement, and participation in cellular processes(1)
pmid:12374615.finding: The labile (chelatable, redox-active) iron pool promotes ROS formation and rises and falls with iron import, chelation and ferritin turnover.

pmid:42219800.authors: Korevaar TIM, Leung AM, Alexander EK, et al.
pmid:42219800.title: American Thyroid Association 2026 Guidelines for Thyroid Disease in Preconception, Pregnancy, and Postpartum
pmid:42219800.finding: ATA 2026 update of the pregnancy, preconception and postpartum thyroid guideline, including iodine supplementation recommendations.

pmid:24327038.authors: Lam JR, Schneider JL, Zhao W, et al.
pmid:24327038.title: Proton pump inhibitor and histamine 2 receptor antagonist use and vitamin B12 deficiency
pmid:24327038.finding: Two or more years of PPIs (OR 1.65) or H2 blockers (OR 1.25) was associated with vitamin B12 deficiency, more at higher PPI doses.

pmid:11504949.authors: Levine M, Wang Y, Padayatty SJ, et al.
pmid:11504949.title: A new recommended dietary allowance of vitamin C for healthy young women
pmid:11504949.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:11504949.finding: Plasma and cells saturated at 400 mg/day; F2-isoprostanes did not change at any vitamin C dose in these replete women.

pmid:38922615.authors: Loftfield E, O'Connell CP, Abnet CC, et al.
pmid:38922615.title: Multivitamin Use and Mortality Risk in 3 Prospective US Cohorts
pmid:38922615.finding: Daily multivitamin use was not associated with lower mortality (HR 1.04 in the first half of follow-up).

pmid:28816346.authors: Martí-Carvajal AJ, Solà I, Lathyris D, et al.
pmid:28816346.title: Homocysteine-lowering interventions for preventing cardiovascular events
pmid:28816346.finding: Cochrane: B-vitamin homocysteine lowering did not reduce MI or death but modestly reduced stroke (RR 0.90).

pmid:37603429.authors: McNulty H, Pentieva K, Ward M
pmid:37603429.title: Causes and Clinical Sequelae of Riboflavin Deficiency
pmid:37603429.finding: Subclinical riboflavin deficiency may be widespread even in high-income countries but goes undetected; linked to anaemia and hypertension.

pmid:29340704.authors: Mills JL, Buck Louis GM, Kannan K, et al.
pmid:29340704.title: Delayed conception in women with low-urinary iodine concentrations: a population-based prospective cohort study
pmid:29340704.finding: Women with iodine:creatinine <50 ug/g had 46% lower fecundability per cycle (OR 0.54).

pmid:35787614.authors: Ni Z, Li Y, Song D, et al.
pmid:35787614.title: Iron-overloaded follicular fluid increases the risk of endometriosis-related infertility by triggering granulosa cell ferroptosis and oocyte dysmaturity
pmid:35787614.finding: Iron-overloaded follicular fluid from women with endometriosis triggered granulosa-cell ferroptosis and impaired oocyte maturation in mouse models; vitamin E and deferoxamine helped.

pmid:21199787.authors: Nielsen FH, Johnson LK, Zeng H
pmid:21199787.title: Magnesium supplementation improves indicators of low magnesium status and inflammatory stress in adults older than 51 years with poor quality sleep
pmid:21199787.finding: 320 mg/day magnesium lowered CRP only in those with baseline CRP >3 mg/L; 58% ate below the magnesium EAR.

pmid:39373282.authors: Niklewicz A, Hannibal L, Warren M, et al.
pmid:39373282.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of functional vitamin B12 status among adult vegans
pmid:39373282.finding: Vegans had lower serum B12 and higher homocysteine and methylmalonic acid than omnivores, indicating functional B12 deficiency.

pmid:39218000.authors: Passarelli S, Free CM, Shepon A, et al.
pmid:39218000.title: Global estimation of dietary micronutrient inadequacies: a modelling analysis
pmid:39218000.finding: From food alone, >5 billion people under-consume iodine, vitamin E and calcium and >4 billion under-consume iron, riboflavin, folate and vitamin C.

pmid:29454039.authors: Rayman MP, Winther KH, Pastor-Barriuso R, et al.
pmid:29454039.title: Effect of long-term selenium supplementation on mortality: Results from a multiple-dose, randomised controlled trial
pmid:29454039.finding: 300 ug/day selenium for 5 years raised all-cause mortality over 10 years (HR 1.59, 1.02-2.46); 100 and 200 ug showed no harm.

pmid:19091331.title: Efficacy of selenium and/or N-acetyl-cysteine for improving semen parameters in infertile men: a double-blind, placebo controlled, randomized study
pmid:19091331.finding: Reported that 200 ug selenium and/or 600 mg NAC improved all semen parameters; the journal issued an Expression of Concern in 2023.

pmid:31910279.authors: Schisterman EF, Sjaarda LA, Clemons T, et al.
pmid:31910279.title: Effect of Folic Acid and Zinc Supplementation in Men on Semen Quality and Live Birth Among Couples Undergoing Infertility Treatment: A Randomized Clinical Trial
pmid:31910279.n: 2370 men in couples seeking infertility care (FAZST)
pmid:31910279.finding: 5 mg folic acid plus 30 mg zinc for 6 months did not improve semen quality or live birth (34% vs 35%) and slightly raised sperm DNA fragmentation (+2.4 points).

pmid:19675106.authors: Schleicher RL, Carroll MD, Ford ES, et al.
pmid:19675106.title: Serum vitamin C and the prevalence of vitamin C deficiency in the United States: 2003-2004 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
pmid:19675106.finding: 7.1% of the US population was vitamin C deficient; smokers had about one-third lower concentrations.

pmid:9698665.authors: Scott R, MacPherson A, Yates RW, et al.
pmid:9698665.title: The effect of oral selenium supplementation on human sperm motility
pmid:9698665.n: 69 subfertile Scottish men with low selenium status
pmid:9698665.finding: Selenium (100 ug/day) for 3 months raised sperm motility vs placebo; 11% achieved paternity vs none on placebo.

pmid:35294969.authors: Sesso HD, Rist PM, Aragaki AK, et al.
pmid:35294969.title: Multivitamins in the prevention of cancer and cardiovascular disease: the COcoa Supplement and Multivitamin Outcomes Study (COSMOS) randomized clinical trial
pmid:35294969.finding: A daily multivitamin for a median 3.6 years did not reduce total cancer (HR 0.97) or CVD (HR 0.98); lung cancer was lower (HR 0.62).

pmid:38870258.authors: Sohn SY, Inoue K, Rhee CM, et al.
pmid:38870258.title: Risks of Iodine Excess
pmid:38870258.finding: Excess iodine (supplements, contrast media, amiodarone) can trigger hypo- or hyperthyroidism in susceptible people.

pmid:31689852.authors: Srinutta T, Chewcharat A, Takkavatakarn K, et al.
pmid:31689852.title: Proton pump inhibitors and hypomagnesemia: A meta-analysis of observational studies
pmid:31689852.finding: PPI use was associated with hypomagnesaemia (adjusted OR 1.71), more with high doses (OR 2.13).

pmid:23706509.title: Iodine and pregnancy: a call to action
pmid:23706509.finding: Lancet comment calling for action on iodine nutrition in pregnancy.

pmid:25770867.title: Folate supplements for stroke prevention: targeted trial trumps the rest
pmid:25770867.finding: JAMA editorial arguing that the CSPPT targeted trial in a low-folate population outweighs earlier null trials in fortified populations.

pmid:28985560.authors: Stockwell BR, Friedmann Angeli JP, Bayir H, et al.
pmid:28985560.title: Ferroptosis: A Regulated Cell Death Nexus Linking Metabolism, Redox Biology, and Disease
pmid:28985560.finding: Ferroptosis review: iron, polyunsaturated lipid peroxidation and loss of GPX4/glutathione defences link metabolism, redox biology and disease.

pmid:10464096.authors: Ursini F, Heim S, Kiess M, et al.
pmid:10464096.title: Dual function of the selenoprotein PHGPx during sperm maturation
pmid:10464096.finding: The selenoprotein PHGPx (GPX4) becomes a structural protein making up >=50% of the sperm midpiece mitochondrial capsule, explaining midpiece fragility in selenium deficiency.

pmid:37526713.authors: Barry MJ, Nicholson WK, Silverstein M, et al.
pmid:37526713.title: Folic Acid Supplementation to Prevent Neural Tube Defects: US Preventive Services Task Force Reaffirmation Recommendation Statement
pmid:37526713.finding: USPSTF (A recommendation): everyone who could become pregnant should take 400-800 ug folic acid daily.

pmid:35277037.authors: Veronese N, Pizzol D, Smith L, et al.
pmid:35277037.title: Effect of Magnesium Supplementation on Inflammatory Parameters: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
pmid:35277037.finding: Magnesium supplements lowered serum CRP and raised nitric oxide.

pmid:38244989.authors: Vyas CM, Manson JE, Sesso HD, et al.
pmid:38244989.title: Effect of multivitamin-mineral supplementation versus placebo on cognitive function: results from the clinic subcohort of the COcoa Supplement and Multivitamin Outcomes Study (COSMOS) randomized clinical trial and meta-analysis of 3 cognitive studies within COSMOS
pmid:38244989.n: 573 COSMOS-Clinic participants plus meta-analysis of 3 COSMOS cohorts
pmid:38244989.finding: A multivitamin improved episodic memory over 2 years; pooled COSMOS data showed small benefits on global cognition (0.07 SD).

pmid:23209782.title: Estimating the global prevalence of zinc deficiency: results based on zinc availability in national food supplies and the prevalence of stunting
pmid:23209782.finding: An estimated 17.3% of the world's population is at risk of inadequate zinc intake, highest in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.

pmid:23608654.authors: Wilson CP, McNulty H, Ward M, et al.
pmid:23608654.title: Blood pressure in treated hypertensive individuals with the MTHFR 677TT genotype is responsive to intervention with riboflavin: findings of a targeted randomized trial
pmid:23608654.finding: 1.6 mg/day riboflavin for 16 weeks lowered systolic BP by 5.6 mmHg vs placebo in this genotype.

pmid:26932683.authors: Zhao J, Dong X, Hu X, et al.
pmid:26932683.title: Zinc levels in seminal plasma and their correlation with male infertility: A systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:26932683.finding: Infertile men had lower seminal zinc; pooled small trials suggested zinc improved volume, motility and morphology.

pmid:29627894.authors: Zhou H, Wang T, Li Q, et al.
pmid:29627894.title: Prevention of Keshan Disease by Selenium Supplementation: a Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
pmid:29627894.finding: Selenium supplementation in endemic areas cut Keshan disease (selenium-deficiency cardiomyopathy) incidence by 86% (RR 0.14).

pmid:25604397.authors: Albert BB, Derraik JG, Cameron-Smith D, et al.
pmid:25604397.title: Fish oil supplements in New Zealand are highly oxidised and do not meet label content of n-3 PUFA.
pmid:25604397.finding: Of 32 New Zealand fish-oil supplements, 83% exceeded the recommended peroxide value, 25% anisidine value and 50% TOTOX; only 8% met all limits and most contained <67% of labelled EPA+DHA.

pmid:28469193.authors: Bannenberg G, Mallon C, Edwards H, et al.
pmid:28469193.title: Omega-3 Long-Chain Polyunsaturated Fatty Acid Content and Oxidation State of Fish Oil Supplements in New Zealand.
pmid:28469193.finding: Industry-association (GOED) testing of 47 New Zealand fish-oil products found 72-86% compliant with voluntary oxidation limits and 91% meeting EPA/DHA label claims, contradicting Albert 2015.

pmid:23863036.authors: García-Hernández VM, Gallar M, Sánchez-Soriano J, et al.
pmid:23863036.title: Effect of omega-3 dietary supplements with different oxidation levels in the lipidic profile of women: a randomized controlled trial.
pmid:23863036.finding: Less-oxidized omega-3 capsules lowered triglycerides and cholesterol over 30 days, whereas highly oxidized capsules worsened cholesterol.

pmid:26688721.authors: Jackowski SA, Alvi AZ, Mirajkar A, et al.
pmid:26688721.title: Oxidation levels of North American over-the-counter n-3 (omega-3) supplements and the influence of supplement formulation and delivery form on evaluating oxidative safety.
pmid:26688721.finding: Of 171 North American omega-3 supplements, 50% exceeded voluntary oxidation limits; flavoured products, bulk oils and children's products were more oxidized than plain capsules; most authors were affiliated with an omega-3 company.

pmid:28011269.title: Omega-3 fatty acid fish oil dietary supplements contain saturated fats and oxidized lipids that may interfere with their intended biological benefits.
pmid:28011269.finding: Three top-selling US fish-oil supplements exceeded oxidation limits (a prescription product did not), and omega-3 isolated from them failed to inhibit small dense LDL oxidation in vitro.

pmid:22136711.authors: Ottestad I, Vogt G, Retterstøl K, et al.
pmid:22136711.title: Oxidised fish oil does not influence established markers of oxidative stress in healthy human subjects: a randomised controlled trial.
pmid:22136711.finding: 7 weeks of 8 g/day oxidized fish oil (1.6 g EPA+DHA) did not change urinary 8-iso-PGF2alpha, plasma HNE/HHE, hs-CRP or antioxidant enzymes vs fresh fish oil or high-oleic sunflower oil.

pmid:28558855.authors: Rundblad A, Holven KB, Ottestad I, et al.
pmid:28558855.title: High-quality fish oil has a more favourable effect than oxidised fish oil on intermediate-density lipoprotein and LDL subclasses: a randomised controlled trial.
pmid:28558855.finding: High-quality fish oil (PV 4) lowered IDL and LDL particle subclasses compared with oxidized fish oil (PV 18, AV 9) and high-oleic sunflower oil.

pmid:27284082.authors: Alda M, McKinnon M, Blagdon R, et al.
pmid:27284082.title: Methylene blue treatment for residual symptoms of bipolar disorder: randomised crossover study
pmid:27284082.finding: Methylene blue 195 mg/day vs 15 mg added to lamotrigine improved residual depression and anxiety, but not cognition.

pmid:30322941.title: Prolonging healthy aging: Longevity vitamins and proteins
pmid:30322941.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:30322941.finding: Proposed 'longevity vitamins', including ergothioneine, PQQ and astaxanthin, and taurine as a conditional vitamin, based largely on mechanistic and observational reasoning.

pmid:17129214.title: Disparate patterns of age-related changes in lipid peroxidation in long-lived naked mole-rats and shorter-lived mice
pmid:17129214.finding: Young naked mole-rats (lifespan >28 years) had at least twice the lipid peroxidation (urinary isoprostanes, liver MDA) of mice (lifespan ~3.5 years).

pmid:22166671.authors: Anisimov VN, Egorov MV, Krasilshchikova MS, et al.
pmid:22166671.title: Effects of the mitochondria-targeted antioxidant SkQ1 on lifespan of rodents
pmid:22166671.finding: SkQ1 increased lifespan in some mouse strains and housing conditions, with effects strongly dependent on vivarium pathogen status and sex.

pmid:33557850.authors: Antonio J, Candow DG, Forbes SC, et al.
pmid:33557850.title: Common questions and misconceptions about creatine supplementation: what does the scientific evidence really show?
pmid:33557850.finding: Reviews misconceptions: creatine does not harm healthy kidneys, does not cause dehydration or cramps, and has no consistent link to hair loss.

pmid:29704637.authors: Avgerinos KI, Spyrou N, Bougioukas KI, et al.
pmid:29704637.title: Effects of creatine supplementation on cognitive function of healthy individuals: A systematic review of randomized controlled trials
pmid:29704637.finding: Systematic review: creatine may improve short-term memory and reasoning in healthy people, especially vegetarians; other domains were inconsistent and young people showed little effect.

pmid:34548082.authors: Ba DM, Gao X, Al-Shaar L, et al.
pmid:34548082.title: Prospective study of dietary mushroom intake and risk of mortality: results from continuous National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2003-2014 and a meta-analysis
pmid:34548082.finding: Mushroom intake was associated with slightly lower all-cause mortality (pooled RR 0.94) in cohort studies; the NHANES analysis alone was non-significant.

pmid:22529837.authors: Bannai M, Kawai N, Ono K, et al.
pmid:22529837.title: The effects of glycine on subjective daytime performance in partially sleep-restricted healthy volunteers
pmid:22529837.finding: 3 g glycine before bed during 3 nights of 25% sleep restriction reduced daytime fatigue and improved psychomotor vigilance compared with placebo.

pmid:23642158.title: Updating the mitochondrial free radical theory of aging: an integrated view, key aspects, and confounding concepts
pmid:23642158.finding: Defends an updated mitochondrial free-radical theory: long-lived animals have low mitochondrial ROS generation (complex I) and oxidation-resistant macromolecules; many criticisms rest on misconceptions.

pmid:31722088.authors: Besag FMC, Vasey MJ, Lao KSJ, et al.
pmid:31722088.title: Adverse Events Associated with Melatonin for the Treatment of Primary or Secondary Sleep Disorders: A Systematic Review
pmid:31722088.finding: Systematic review: melatonin adverse events in sleep-disorder trials were generally mild and short-lived (e.g., daytime sleepiness, headache, dizziness), but long-term data are scarce.

pmid:36562403.title: Adverse events in long-term studies of exogenous melatonin
pmid:36562403.finding: Long-term (6 months or more) melatonin studies report few clinically significant adverse events, but placebo-controlled long-term data are scarce.

pmid:24137022.authors: Boldyrev AA, Aldini G, Derave W
pmid:24137022.title: Physiology and pathophysiology of carnosine
pmid:24137022.finding: Carnosine (beta-alanyl-L-histidine) is abundant in muscle and brain and acts as a pH buffer, metal chelator, antioxidant and anti-glycation agent in experimental models.

pmid:35235774.authors: Brakedal B, Dölle C, Riemer F, et al.
pmid:35235774.title: The NADPARK study: A randomized phase I trial of nicotinamide riboside supplementation in Parkinson's disease
pmid:35235774.n: 30 people with newly diagnosed Parkinson disease
pmid:35235774.finding: NR 1000 mg/day for 30 days raised brain NAD levels in some patients and lowered inflammatory cytokines, with mild clinical improvement in responders (phase I).

pmid:31788888.title: Astaxanthin: How much is too much? A safety review
pmid:31788888.finding: Of 87 human studies of natural astaxanthin, none found safety concerns, 35 at 12 mg/day or more; approved doses range 2-24 mg/day, and EFSA's 2 mg ADI was based on synthetic astaxanthin in rats.

pmid:34326206.title: Comment on "Nicotinamide mononucleotide increases muscle insulin sensitivity in prediabetic women"
pmid:34326206.finding: Comment arguing the Yoshino NMN trial was not effectively randomized: the NMN group had far less liver fat at baseline (6.3% vs 14.8%).

pmid:35201920.authors: Broome SC, Atiola RD, Braakhuis AJ, et al.
pmid:35201920.title: Mitochondria-targeted antioxidant supplementation does not affect muscle soreness or recovery of maximal voluntary isometric contraction force following muscle-damaging exercise in untrained men: a randomized clinical trial
pmid:35201920.finding: MitoQ 20 mg/day for 14 days did not reduce muscle soreness after eccentric exercise, delayed recovery of eccentric torque and increased creatine kinase.

pmid:26660938.authors: Brzheskiy VV, Efimova EL, Vorontsova TN, et al.
pmid:26660938.title: Results of a Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Masked, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Study of the Efficacy and Safety of Visomitin Eye Drops in Patients with Dry Eye Syndrome
pmid:26660938.finding: Visomitin (SkQ1) eye drops three times daily for 6 weeks improved tear film stability and dry eye symptoms vs placebo (company-funded).

pmid:27444382.authors: Cheah IK, Feng L, Tang RMY, et al.
pmid:27444382.title: Ergothioneine levels in an elderly population decrease with age and incidence of cognitive decline; a risk factor for neurodegeneration?
pmid:27444382.finding: Whole-blood ergothioneine declined after age 60 and was lower in people with mild cognitive impairment.

pmid:27488221.authors: Cheah IK, Tang RM, Yew TS, et al.
pmid:27488221.title: Administration of Pure Ergothioneine to Healthy Human Subjects: Uptake, Metabolism, and Effects on Biomarkers of Oxidative Damage and Inflammation
pmid:27488221.finding: Oral pure ergothioneine was avidly absorbed and retained; oxidative damage and inflammation markers showed mostly non-significant downward trends.

pmid:29138605.authors: Chilibeck PD, Kaviani M, Candow DG, et al.
pmid:29138605.title: Effect of creatine supplementation during resistance training on lean tissue mass and muscular strength in older adults: a meta-analysis
pmid:29138605.finding: Creatine during resistance training added 1.37 kg lean mass and improved chest press (SMD 0.35) and leg press (SMD 0.24) strength.

pmid:37097362.authors: Cohen PA, Avula B, Wang YH, et al.
pmid:37097362.title: Quantity of Melatonin and CBD in Melatonin Gummies Sold in the US
pmid:37097362.finding: In US melatonin gummies, actual melatonin ranged from 74% to 347% of the label; only 3 of 25 were within 10%, and one contained undeclared CBD and no melatonin.

pmid:31278280.authors: Conze D, Brenner C, Kruger CL
pmid:31278280.title: Safety and Metabolism of Long-term Administration of NIAGEN (Nicotinamide Riboside Chloride) in a Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-controlled Clinical Trial of Healthy Overweight Adults
pmid:31278280.finding: NR 100, 300 or 1000 mg/day for 8 weeks raised whole-blood NAD+ by 22%, 51% and 142% with no excess adverse events.

pmid:38888087.authors: Cruz-Sanabria F, Bruno S, Crippa A, et al.
pmid:38888087.title: Optimizing the Time and Dose of Melatonin as a Sleep-Promoting Drug: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis
pmid:38888087.finding: Melatonin's effect on sleep onset and total sleep rose with dose up to about 4 mg/day, and taking it about 3 hours before bedtime worked better.

pmid:19451351.authors: Dai DF, Santana LF, Vermulst M, et al.
pmid:19451351.title: Overexpression of catalase targeted to mitochondria attenuates murine cardiac aging
pmid:19451351.finding: Mitochondrial catalase attenuated age-related cardiac hypertrophy, diastolic dysfunction, fibrosis and mitochondrial DNA mutations in mice.

pmid:27040154.authors: de Courten B, Jakubova M, de Courten MP, et al.
pmid:27040154.title: Effects of carnosine supplementation on glucose metabolism: Pilot clinical trial
pmid:27040154.finding: Carnosine 2 g/day for 12 weeks prevented a rise in fasting insulin and insulin resistance seen on placebo (pilot).

pmid:31375416.authors: de Souza E Silva A, Pertille A, Reis Barbosa CG, et al.
pmid:31375416.title: Effects of Creatine Supplementation on Renal Function: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmid:31375416.finding: Creatine supplementation did not cause renal damage at studied doses and durations; small serum creatinine changes reflect creatine metabolism, not kidney injury.

pmid:24576864.title: Creatine supplementation during resistance training in older adults-a meta-analysis
pmid:24576864.finding: Adding creatine to resistance training in older adults increased fat-free mass and chest- and leg-press strength more than training alone.

pmid:29992272.authors: Dollerup OL, Christensen B, Svart M, et al.
pmid:29992272.title: A randomized placebo-controlled clinical trial of nicotinamide riboside in obese men: safety, insulin-sensitivity, and lipid-mobilizing effects
pmid:29992272.finding: NR 2 g/day for 12 weeks was safe but did not improve insulin sensitivity, glucose metabolism, energy expenditure or body composition.

pmid:31710095.authors: Dollerup OL, Chubanava S, Agerholm M, et al.
pmid:31710095.title: Nicotinamide riboside does not alter mitochondrial respiration, content or morphology in skeletal muscle from obese and insulin-resistant men
pmid:31710095.finding: NR 2 g/day for 12 weeks did not change muscle mitochondrial respiration, content or morphology, or muscle NAD+ levels.

pmid:36644917.title: Letter to the Editor: Double-counting due to inadequate statistics leads to false-positive findings in "Effects of creatine supplementation on memory in healthy individuals: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials"
pmid:36644917.finding: Letter arguing the Prokopidis creatine-memory meta-analysis double-counted data, inflating a possibly false-positive result.

pmid:32625352.authors: EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition and Allergies (NDA)
pmid:32625352.title: Statement on the safety of synthetic l-ergothioneine as a novel food - supplementary dietary exposure and safety assessment for infants and young children, pregnant and breastfeeding women
pmid:32625352.finding: EFSA concluded synthetic L-ergothioneine is safe as a novel food at proposed use levels, including for pregnant and breastfeeding women and young children (NOAEL 800 mg/kg/day).

pmid:32625350.authors: EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition and Allergies (NDA)
pmid:32625350.title: Safety of pyrroloquinoline quinone disodium salt as a novel food pursuant to Regulation (EC) No 258/97
pmid:32625350.finding: EFSA judged PQQ disodium salt safe as a novel food in supplements up to 20 mg/day for healthy adults (not pregnant or lactating women).

pmid:15531919.authors: Elchuri S, Oberley TD, Qi W, et al.
pmid:15531919.title: CuZnSOD deficiency leads to persistent and widespread oxidative damage and hepatocarcinogenesis later in life
pmid:15531919.finding: Sod1-knockout mice had widespread oxidative damage, more than 70% developed liver nodules or carcinoma, and they had shorter lives.

pmid:31412242.authors: Elhassan YS, Kluckova K, Fletcher RS, et al.
pmid:31412242.title: Nicotinamide Riboside Augments the Aged Human Skeletal Muscle NAD(+) Metabolome and Induces Transcriptomic and Anti-inflammatory Signatures
pmid:31412242.finding: NR 1 g/day for 21 days raised the muscle NAD+ metabolome and lowered inflammatory cytokines but did not change mitochondrial bioenergetics.

pmid:27855744.title: Melatonin Natural Health Products and Supplements: Presence of Serotonin and Significant Variability of Melatonin Content
pmid:27855744.finding: Melatonin content ranged from -83% to +478% of label; over 71% of products were outside 10% of label and 26% contained serotonin.

foundations:lon-fda2025nmn.authors: US Food and Drug Administration, Human Foods Program
foundations:lon-fda2025nmn.title: Response letter to Natural Products Association and Alliance for Natural Health USA regarding the regulatory status of beta-nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), Docket FDA-2023-P-0872
foundations:lon-fda2025nmn.finding: FDA reversed its 2022 position and determined that NMN is not excluded from the dietary supplement definition, granting the industry petition in part (September 29, 2025).

foundations:lon-fdandi.title: Submitted 75-Day Premarket Notifications for New Dietary Ingredients
foundations:lon-fdandi.finding: Lists new-dietary-ingredient notifications for beta-NMN (NDIN 1444, filed November 2025, FDA response January 2026) and reduced NMN (NDIN 1451).

pmid:40472098.authors: Fernandez ME, Bernier M, Price NL, et al.
pmid:40472098.title: Is taurine an aging biomarker?
pmid:40472098.n: three human cohorts plus monkeys and mice
pmid:40472098.finding: Circulating taurine increased or stayed unchanged with age in three human cohorts, monkeys and mice measured longitudinally; links between taurine and health outcomes were inconsistent.

pmid:23691095.authors: Ferracioli-Oda E, Qawasmi A, Bloch MH
pmid:23691095.title: Meta-analysis: melatonin for the treatment of primary sleep disorders
pmid:23691095.finding: Melatonin shortened sleep onset by about 7 minutes and lengthened total sleep by about 8 minutes in primary sleep disorders, with small improvement in sleep quality.

pmid:37068054.authors: Freeberg KA, Udovich CC, Martens CR, et al.
pmid:37068054.title: Dietary Supplementation With NAD+-Boosting Compounds in Humans: Current Knowledge and Future Directions
pmid:37068054.journal: J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci
pmid:37068054.finding: NAD+-boosting compounds are safe and raise NAD+ metabolites in human tissues, but small, heterogeneous trials limit conclusions about physiological benefit.

pmid:20492507.authors: Gane EJ, Weilert F, Orr DW, et al.
pmid:20492507.title: The mitochondria-targeted anti-oxidant mitoquinone decreases liver damage in a phase II study of hepatitis C patients
pmid:20492507.finding: MitoQ 40 or 80 mg/day for 28 days lowered liver enzymes (ALT) from baseline, but differences vs placebo were not significant and viral load was unchanged.

pmid:27863809.authors: Gauthier S, Feldman HH, Schneider LS, et al.
pmid:27863809.title: Efficacy and safety of tau-aggregation inhibitor therapy in patients with mild or moderate Alzheimer's disease: a randomised, controlled, double-blind, parallel-arm, phase 3 trial
pmid:27863809.finding: LMTM (a stabilized reduced methylene blue) at 75 or 125 mg twice daily for 15 months did not slow cognitive or functional decline (negative primary analysis).

pmid:33185572.authors: Ghorbaninejad P, Sheikhhossein F, Djafari F, et al.
pmid:33185572.title: Effects of melatonin supplementation on oxidative stress: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmid:33185572.finding: Melatonin raised total antioxidant capacity and lowered MDA and protein carbonyls, with high heterogeneity and mostly patient populations.

pmid:20142303.title: CNS toxicity involving methylene blue: the exemplar for understanding and predicting drug interactions that precipitate serotonin toxicity
pmid:20142303.finding: 13 of 14 reported cases of CNS toxicity with methylene blue met criteria for serotonin toxicity; even 0.75-1 mg/kg reaches MAO-A-inhibiting levels, so serotonergic drugs are a major hazard.

pmid:24159899.title: The free radical theory of aging is dead. Long live the damage theory!
pmid:24159899.finding: Argues the free-radical theory is dead: ROS are one of many by-products of imperfect biological processes, and aging reflects accumulation of all such damage.

pmid:27060562.title: Aging: progressive decline in fitness due to the rising deleteriome adjusted by genetic, environmental, and stochastic processes
pmid:27060562.finding: Introduces the 'deleteriome': the sum of cumulative deleterious age-related changes at all levels, adjusted by genetic, environmental and stochastic processes, as a unifying model of aging.

pmid:38418482.authors: Gordji-Nejad A, Matusch A, Kleedörfer S, et al.
pmid:38418482.title: Single dose creatine improves cognitive performance and induces changes in cerebral high energy phosphates during sleep deprivation
pmid:38418482.finding: A single 0.35 g/kg creatine dose during 21 h of sleep deprivation changed brain high-energy phosphates and improved processing speed and cognitive performance.

pmid:15795384.authors: Gründemann D, Harlfinger S, Golz S, et al.
pmid:15795384.title: Discovery of the ergothioneine transporter
pmid:15795384.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:15795384.finding: Identified OCTN1 (SLC22A4) as a dedicated ergothioneine transporter; cells expressing it accumulate and retain dietary ergothioneine.

pmid:24111525.authors: Gullo D, Evans JL, Sortino G, et al.
pmid:24111525.title: Insulin autoimmune syndrome (Hirata Disease) in European Caucasians taking α-lipoic acid
pmid:24111525.finding: Six European patients developed insulin autoimmune syndrome with severe hypoglycaemia 30-120 days after starting ALA 600 mg/day, linked to HLA-DRB1*04:03.

pmid:29851075.authors: Halliwell B, Cheah IK, Tang RMY
pmid:29851075.title: Ergothioneine - a diet-derived antioxidant with therapeutic potential
pmid:29851075.finding: Ergothioneine is a diet-derived thiol antioxidant concentrated by a specific transporter, with protective effects in cell and animal models and therapeutic potential still untested in humans.

pmid:5016631.title: The biologic clock: the mitochondria?
pmid:5016631.finding: Narrowed the free-radical theory to mitochondria, proposing them as both the main source and the main target of the radicals that set lifespan.

pmid:24231099.authors: Harris CB, Chowanadisai W, Mishchuk DO, et al.
pmid:24231099.title: Dietary pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ) alters indicators of inflammation and mitochondrial-related metabolism in human subjects
pmid:24231099.finding: PQQ 0.2-0.3 mg/kg briefly lowered CRP and IL-6 and altered urinary metabolites in a tiny short study.

pmid:19587680.authors: Harrison DE, Strong R, Sharp ZD, et al.
pmid:19587680.title: Rapamycin fed late in life extends lifespan in genetically heterogeneous mice
pmid:19587680.finding: Rapamycin fed from 600 days of age extended median and maximal lifespan of male and female genetically heterogeneous mice (90th-percentile age +14% females, +9% males).

pmid:24245565.authors: Harrison DE, Strong R, Allison DB, et al.
pmid:24245565.title: Acarbose, 17-α-estradiol, and nordihydroguaiaretic acid extend mouse lifespan preferentially in males
pmid:24245565.finding: In the NIA Interventions Testing Program, methylene blue did not change median lifespan of male or female mice (small rise in female maximum lifespan).

pmid:33788371.authors: Harrison DE, Strong R, Reifsnyder P, et al.
pmid:33788371.title: 17-a-estradiol late in life extends lifespan in aging UM-HET3 male mice; nicotinamide riboside and three other drugs do not affect lifespan in either sex
pmid:33788371.finding: In the NIA Interventions Testing Program, nicotinamide riboside did not extend lifespan in male or female mice.

pmid:38041783.authors: Harrison DE, Strong R, Reifsnyder P, et al.
pmid:38041783.title: Astaxanthin and meclizine extend lifespan in UM-HET3 male mice; fisetin, SG1002 (hydrogen sulfide donor), dimethyl fumarate, mycophenolic acid, and 4-phenylbutyrate do not significantly affect lifespan in either sex at the doses and schedules used
pmid:38041783.finding: In the NIA Interventions Testing Program, astaxanthin extended median male mouse lifespan by 12%, with no significant effect in females or on 90th-percentile lifespan.

pmid:28701493.authors: Hersch SM, Schifitto G, Oakes D, et al.
pmid:28701493.title: The CREST-E study of creatine for Huntington disease: A randomized controlled trial
pmid:28701493.finding: Up to 40 g/day creatine for up to 48 months did not slow functional decline (stopped for futility); gastrointestinal side effects were more common.

pmid:31860387.authors: Hwang PS, Machek SB, Cardaci TD, et al.
pmid:31860387.title: Effects of Pyrroloquinoline Quinone (PQQ) Supplementation on Aerobic Exercise Performance and Indices of Mitochondrial Biogenesis in Untrained Men
pmid:31860387.finding: PQQ 20 mg/day during 6 weeks of endurance training raised muscle PGC-1alpha protein but did not improve aerobic performance vs placebo.

pmid:35927255.authors: Igarashi M, Nakagawa-Nagahama Y, Miura M, et al.
pmid:35927255.title: Chronic nicotinamide mononucleotide supplementation elevates blood nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide levels and alters muscle function in healthy older men
pmid:35927255.finding: NMN 250 mg/day for 6-12 weeks raised blood NAD+; gait speed and grip improvements were only nominally significant and body composition did not change.

pmid:31685720.authors: Irie J, Inagaki E, Fujita M, et al.
pmid:31685720.title: Effect of oral administration of nicotinamide mononucleotide on clinical parameters and nicotinamide metabolite levels in healthy Japanese men
pmid:31685720.finding: Single-arm, non-randomized study: single oral NMN doses of 100-500 mg were safe and dose-dependently raised NAD+ breakdown products in plasma.

pmid:26782228.authors: Itoh Y, Hine K, Miura H, et al.
pmid:26782228.title: Effect of the Antioxidant Supplement Pyrroloquinoline Quinone Disodium Salt (BioPQQ™) on Cognitive Functions
pmid:26782228.finding: PQQ 20 mg/day for 12 weeks reduced decline on a Stroop interference test; other effects appeared only in subgroups.

pmid:37191826.authors: Kaeberlein TL, Green AS, Haddad G, et al.
pmid:37191826.title: Evaluation of off-label rapamycin use to promote healthspan in 333 adults
pmid:37191826.finding: Survey of off-label rapamycin users was presented as initial evidence that rapamycin can be used safely in healthy adults; data are self-reported and uncontrolled, and several authors have commercial ties to longevity medicine.

pmid:25533534.authors: Kawai N, Sakai N, Okuro M, et al.
pmid:25533534.title: The sleep-promoting and hypothermic effects of glycine are mediated by NMDA receptors in the suprachiasmatic nucleus
pmid:25533534.finding: In rats, glycine promoted NREM sleep and lowered core temperature via NMDA receptors in the suprachiasmatic nucleus, causing peripheral vasodilation.

pmid:25668262.authors: Writing Group for the NINDS Exploratory Trials in Parkinson Disease (NET-PD) Investigators; Kieburtz K, Tilley BC, Elm JJ, et al.
pmid:25668262.title: Effect of creatine monohydrate on clinical progression in patients with Parkinson disease: a randomized clinical trial
pmid:25668262.finding: Creatine 10 g/day for at least 5 years did not slow clinical progression of Parkinson disease; the trial was stopped for futility.

pmid:37560769.authors: Kirkman DL, Stock JM, Shenouda N, et al.
pmid:37560769.title: Effects of a mitochondrial-targeted ubiquinol on vascular function and exercise capacity in chronic kidney disease: a randomized controlled pilot study
pmid:37560769.finding: MitoQ 20 mg/day for 4 weeks improved flow-mediated dilation vs placebo but did not change exercise capacity (pilot).

pmid:28615996.authors: Kreider RB, Kalman DS, Antonio J, et al.
pmid:28615996.title: International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: safety and efficacy of creatine supplementation in exercise, sport, and medicine
pmid:28615996.finding: ISSN position stand: creatine monohydrate is the most effective ergogenic supplement for high-intensity exercise and lean mass, and is safe at recommended doses (3-5 g/day; up to 30 g/day for 5 years studied).

pmid:28295905.authors: Kucukgoncu S, Zhou E, Lucas KB, et al.
pmid:28295905.title: Alpha-lipoic acid (ALA) as a supplementation for weight loss: results from a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmid:28295905.finding: ALA produced a small short-term weight loss of 1.27 kg more than placebo.

pmid:35268089.authors: Kumar P, Osahon OW, Sekhar RV
pmid:35268089.title: GlyNAC (Glycine and N-Acetylcysteine) Supplementation in Mice Increases Length of Life by Correcting Glutathione Deficiency, Oxidative Stress, Mitochondrial Dysfunction, Abnormalities in Mitophagy and Nutrient Sensing, and Genomic Damage
pmid:35268089.finding: GlyNAC-fed C57BL/6J mice lived 24% longer than controls in a single-lab study.

pmid:22461615.authors: Lamming DW, Ye L, Katajisto P, et al.
pmid:22461615.title: Rapamycin-induced insulin resistance is mediated by mTORC2 loss and uncoupled from longevity
pmid:22461615.finding: In mice, chronic rapamycin causes insulin resistance by disrupting mTORC2, while lifespan extension is linked to mTORC1 inhibition.

pmid:27466898.authors: LaRosa DA, Ellery SJ, Snow RJ, et al.
pmid:27466898.title: Maternal creatine supplementation during pregnancy prevents acute and long-term deficits in skeletal muscle after birth asphyxia: a study of structure and function of hind limb muscle in the spiny mouse
pmid:27466898.finding: In spiny mice, maternal creatine supplementation during pregnancy prevented asphyxia-induced skeletal muscle damage in offspring.

pmid:38310895.authors: Lee DJW, Hodzic Kuerec A, Maier AB
pmid:38310895.title: Targeting ageing with rapamycin and its derivatives in humans: a systematic review
pmid:38310895.finding: Systematic review: rapamycin and rapalogs improved some immune, cardiovascular and skin ageing measures; in patients with disease they increased infections and blood lipids.

pmid:35653284.authors: Lelak K, Vohra V, Neuman MI, et al.
pmid:35653284.title: Pediatric Melatonin Ingestions - United States, 2012-2021
pmid:35653284.finding: US pediatric melatonin ingestions reported to poison centres rose 530% from 2012 to 2021, with more hospitalizations; five children needed ventilation and two died.

pmid:37942539.authors: Linder BA, Stute NL, Hutchison ZJ, et al.
pmid:37942539.title: Acute high-dose MitoQ does not increase urinary kidney injury markers in healthy adults: a randomized crossover trial
pmid:37942539.finding: An acute high dose of MitoQ (100-160 mg) did not raise urinary kidney injury markers.

pmid:38243785.authors: Liu C, Dong X, Jia J, et al.
pmid:38243785.title: Effects of Astaxanthin Supplementation on Fatigue, Motor Function and Cognition: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
pmid:38243785.n: RCTs on fatigue, motor function and cognition
pmid:38243785.finding: Astaxanthin had no significant effect on reaction time and a marginal effect on cognitive accuracy, but improved exercise performance when combined with training.

pmid:35821844.authors: Lizzo G, Migliavacca E, Lamers D, et al.
pmid:35821844.title: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial in Healthy Older Adults to Determine Efficacy of Glycine and N-Acetylcysteine Supplementation on Glutathione Redox Status and Oxidative Damage
pmid:35821844.finding: Industry-run RCT: GlyNAC at 2.4, 4.8 or 7.2 g/day for 2 weeks did not raise glutathione or the GSH:GSSG ratio (primary endpoint); a post-hoc subgroup with high oxidative stress and low glutathione responded.

pmid:35091276.authors: Ma B, Lu J, Kang T, et al.
pmid:35091276.title: Astaxanthin supplementation mildly reduced oxidative stress and inflammation biomarkers: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmid:35091276.finding: Astaxanthin modestly lowered blood MDA (SMD -0.95) and, in type 2 diabetes, IL-6; data on other markers were limited.

pmid:25540326.authors: Mannick JB, Del Giudice G, Lattanzi M, et al.
pmid:25540326.title: mTOR inhibition improves immune function in the elderly
pmid:25540326.finding: The rapalog everolimus (RAD001) for 6 weeks improved influenza vaccine response by about 20% and lowered PD-1-positive T cells.

pmid:29997249.authors: Mannick JB, Morris M, Hockey HP, et al.
pmid:29997249.title: TORC1 inhibition enhances immune function and reduces infections in the elderly
pmid:29997249.finding: Low-dose TORC1 inhibition for 6 weeks was associated with fewer reported infections over a year and better influenza vaccine response.

pmid:29599478.authors: Martens CR, Denman BA, Mazzo MR, et al.
pmid:29599478.title: Chronic nicotinamide riboside supplementation is well-tolerated and elevates NAD(+) in healthy middle-aged and older adults
pmid:29599478.finding: NR 1 g/day for 6 weeks was well tolerated and raised blood NAD+ metabolism, with possible small benefits on blood pressure and arterial stiffness to be tested.

pmid:33472172.authors: Masuoka N, Lei C, Li H, et al.
pmid:33472172.title: Anserine, HClO-scavenger, protected against cognitive decline in individuals with mild cognitive impairment
pmid:33472172.finding: Anserine 500 mg/day for 12 weeks improved MMSE change score vs placebo (1.9 vs 0 points).

pmid:34333586.authors: Matthews JJ, Dolan E, Swinton PA, et al.
pmid:34333586.title: Effect of Carnosine or β-Alanine Supplementation on Markers of Glycemic Control and Insulin Resistance in Humans and Animals: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
pmid:34333586.finding: Carnosine or beta-alanine may lower fasting glucose, HbA1c and HOMA-IR in humans, based on only four human studies.

pmid:37289872.title: Taurine linked with healthy aging
pmid:37289872.finding: Science perspective on Singh et al.: reversing age-associated taurine loss improved mouse longevity and monkey health, but human trials are needed.

pmid:31828942.authors: Menon K, Marquina C, Liew D, et al.
pmid:31828942.title: Histidine-containing dipeptides reduce central obesity and improve glycaemic outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmid:31828942.finding: Histidine-containing dipeptides (carnosine, anserine) lowered waist circumference by 3.5 cm and HbA1c by 0.76%, with smaller effects in low-bias trials.

pmid:22331979.authors: Mijnhout GS, Kollen BJ, Alkhalaf A, et al.
pmid:22331979.title: Alpha lipoic Acid for symptomatic peripheral neuropathy in patients with diabetes: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmid:22331979.finding: IV ALA 600 mg/day for 3 weeks clinically reduced neuropathic symptoms; the clinical relevance of 3-5 weeks of oral ALA above 600 mg/day was unclear.

pmid:30916479.authors: Miller RA, Harrison DE, Astle CM, et al.
pmid:30916479.title: Glycine supplementation extends lifespan of male and female mice
pmid:30916479.finding: In the NIA Interventions Testing Program, an 8% glycine diet extended lifespan of male and female genetically heterogeneous mice by 4-6%.

pmid:40188830.authors: Moel M, Harinath G, Lee V, et al.
pmid:40188830.title: Influence of rapamycin on safety and healthspan metrics after one year: PEARL trial results
pmid:40188830.finding: Compounded rapamycin 5 or 10 mg weekly for 48 weeks was relatively safe but did not change visceral fat (primary outcome); lean mass and pain improved only in women on 10 mg.

pmid:33540766.authors: Muccini AM, Tran NT, de Guingand DL, et al.
pmid:33540766.title: Creatine Metabolism in Female Reproduction, Pregnancy and Newborn Health
pmid:33540766.finding: Creatine metabolism supports energy in female reproductive tissues and placenta; antenatal creatine protects against birth asphyxia in animal models, but human evidence is lacking.

pmid:30393373.title: Mitochondria as a therapeutic target for common pathologies
pmid:30393373.finding: Reviews mitochondria as drug targets in common diseases and mitochondria-targeted compounds such as MitoQ; few agents have reached clinical trials.

pmid:41052075.authors: Nedeljkovic D, Todorovic N, Javorac D, et al.
pmid:41052075.title: The effects of 8-week creatine supplementation with and without ubiquinol on sperm quality biomarkers in normospermic and oligospermic men: A randomized controlled pilot trial
pmid:41052075.finding: Exploratory pilot: 8 weeks of creatine (with or without ubiquinol) gave a non-significant trend toward higher sperm concentration.

pmid:19077044.authors: Pérez VI, Van Remmen H, Bokov A, et al.
pmid:19077044.title: The overexpression of major antioxidant enzymes does not extend the lifespan of mice
pmid:19077044.finding: Mice overexpressing CuZnSOD, catalase, CuZnSOD plus catalase, or CuZnSOD plus MnSOD did not live longer than controls.

pmid:19223593.authors: Pérez VI, Buffenstein R, Masamsetti V, et al.
pmid:19223593.title: Protein stability and resistance to oxidative stress are determinants of longevity in the longest-living rodent, the naked mole-rat
pmid:19223593.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:19223593.finding: Naked mole-rats carry more lipid, protein and DNA oxidation than mice from a young age, but their proteins are more stable and their proteasome activity is higher.

pmid:26733410.authors: Petrov A, Perekhvatova N, Skulachev M, et al.
pmid:26733410.title: SkQ1 Ophthalmic Solution for Dry Eye Treatment: Results of a Phase 2 Safety and Efficacy Clinical Study in the Environment and During Challenge in the Controlled Adverse Environment Model
pmid:26733410.finding: SkQ1 eye drops improved some signs and symptoms of dry eye vs placebo over 29 days (phase 2).

pmid:32458156.authors: Pham T, MacRae CL, Broome SC, et al.
pmid:32458156.title: MitoQ and CoQ10 supplementation mildly suppresses skeletal muscle mitochondrial hydrogen peroxide levels without impacting mitochondrial function in middle-aged men
pmid:32458156.finding: MitoQ 20 mg/day or CoQ10 200 mg/day for 6 weeks mildly lowered muscle mitochondrial H2O2 but did not change mitochondrial function, urinary F2-isoprostanes or plasma TBARS.

pmid:35984306.authors: Prokopidis K, Giannos P, Triantafyllidis KK, et al.
pmid:35984306.title: Effects of creatine supplementation on memory in healthy individuals: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmid:35984306.finding: Creatine improved memory overall (SMD 0.29), driven by older adults (SMD 0.88), with no effect in people aged 11-31.

pmid:40275690.authors: Prokopidis K, Moriarty F, Bahat G, et al.
pmid:40275690.title: The Effect of Nicotinamide Mononucleotide and Riboside on Skeletal Muscle Mass and Function: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmid:40275690.finding: NMN did not improve skeletal muscle index, grip strength, gait speed or chair-stand time; evidence does not support NMN or NR for preserving muscle in older adults.

pmid:17721552.authors: Ramsay RR, Dunford C, Gillman PK
pmid:17721552.title: Methylene blue and serotonin toxicity: inhibition of monoamine oxidase A (MAO A) confirms a theoretical prediction
pmid:17721552.finding: Methylene blue is a potent, tight-binding inhibitor of MAO-A, explaining serotonin toxicity when given to patients on SSRIs.

pmid:28864909.authors: Reiter RJ, Rosales-Corral S, Tan DX, et al.
pmid:28864909.title: Melatonin as a mitochondria-targeted antioxidant: one of evolution's best ideas
pmid:28864909.finding: Argues melatonin is a mitochondria-targeted antioxidant made within mitochondria, scavenging radicals and upregulating antioxidant enzymes (largely cell and animal data).

pmid:32320006.authors: Remie CME, Roumans KHM, Moonen MPB, et al.
pmid:32320006.title: Nicotinamide riboside supplementation alters body composition and skeletal muscle acetylcarnitine concentrations in healthy obese humans
pmid:32320006.finding: NR 1 g/day for 6 weeks did not improve insulin sensitivity, mitochondrial function, liver fat or blood pressure; it slightly increased fat-free mass.

pmid:20350594.title: How increased oxidative stress promotes longevity and metabolic health: The concept of mitochondrial hormesis (mitohormesis)
pmid:20350594.finding: Defines mitohormesis: a transient rise in mitochondrial ROS during energy restriction or exercise triggers adaptive stress resistance, and antioxidants block the benefit.

pmid:27351678.authors: Rodriguez P, Zhou W, Barrett DW, et al.
pmid:27351678.title: Multimodal Randomized Functional MR Imaging of the Effects of Methylene Blue in the Human Brain
pmid:27351678.finding: A single low oral dose of methylene blue increased fMRI responses during attention and memory tasks and raised correct memory retrieval by 7%.

pmid:22067440.authors: Rojas JC, Bruchey AK, Gonzalez-Lima F
pmid:22067440.title: Neurometabolic mechanisms for memory enhancement and neuroprotection of methylene blue
pmid:22067440.finding: Reviews animal evidence that low-dose methylene blue cycles electrons in the respiratory chain, enhances cytochrome oxidase and memory, and is neuroprotective.

pmid:27998379.authors: Sateia MJ, Buysse DJ, Krystal AD, et al.
pmid:27998379.title: Clinical Practice Guideline for the Pharmacologic Treatment of Chronic Insomnia in Adults: An American Academy of Sleep Medicine Clinical Practice Guideline
pmid:27998379.finding: AASM guideline: suggests clinicians not use melatonin for chronic insomnia in adults (weak recommendation, low-quality evidence).

pmid:15879174.authors: Schriner SE, Linford NJ, Martin GM, et al.
pmid:15879174.title: Extension of murine life span by overexpression of catalase targeted to mitochondria
pmid:15879174.finding: Mice expressing catalase targeted to mitochondria (MCAT) lived about 5 months longer (median and maximum), with less oxidative damage, delayed cardiac pathology and cataracts.

pmid:17908557.authors: Schulz TJ, Zarse K, Voigt A, et al.
pmid:17908557.title: Glucose restriction extends Caenorhabditis elegans life span by inducing mitochondrial respiration and increasing oxidative stress
pmid:17908557.finding: Glucose restriction extended worm lifespan by raising mitochondrial respiration and ROS; antioxidants abolished the extension, the first direct evidence for 'mitohormesis'.

pmid:21404063.authors: Sestili P, Martinelli C, Colombo E, et al.
pmid:21404063.title: Creatine as an antioxidant
pmid:21404063.finding: Reviews cell and animal evidence that creatine has direct and indirect antioxidant actions as part of its cytoprotective effects.

pmid:18325648.title: Risk assessment for the amino acids taurine, L-glutamine and L-arginine
pmid:18325648.finding: Risk assessment set an observed safe level for supplemental taurine of 3 g/day based on human trials, with no systematic adverse effects found.

pmid:34415830.authors: Shiojima Y, Takahashi M, Takahashi R, et al.
pmid:34415830.title: Effect of Dietary Pyrroloquinoline Quinone Disodium Salt on Cognitive Function in Healthy Volunteers: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Parallel-Group Study
pmid:34415830.finding: PQQ disodium salt 21.5 mg/day for 12 weeks improved several computerized cognitive scores vs placebo (manufacturer-linked trial).

pmid:37289866.authors: Singh P, Gollapalli K, Mangiola S, et al.
pmid:37289866.title: Taurine deficiency as a driver of aging
pmid:37289866.finding: Circulating taurine fell with age in mice, monkeys and humans; taurine supplementation extended mouse median lifespan and improved healthspan in mice and middle-aged monkeys; human low taurine correlated with age-related disease.

pmid:31672783.authors: Smith E, Ottosson F, Hellstrand S, et al.
pmid:31672783.title: Ergothioneine is associated with reduced mortality and decreased risk of cardiovascular disease
pmid:31672783.finding: Higher plasma ergothioneine was associated with lower coronary disease (HR 0.85/SD), cardiovascular mortality (HR 0.79) and overall mortality (HR 0.86) over 21 years.

pmid:20568096.authors: Snow BJ, Rolfe FL, Lockhart MM, et al.
pmid:20568096.title: A double-blind, placebo-controlled study to assess the mitochondria-targeted antioxidant MitoQ as a disease-modifying therapy in Parkinson's disease
pmid:20568096.finding: MitoQ 40 or 80 mg/day for 12 months did not slow Parkinson disease progression on any measure.

pmid:26781281.authors: Sun Q, Wang B, Li Y, et al.
pmid:26781281.title: Taurine Supplementation Lowers Blood Pressure and Improves Vascular Function in Prehypertension: Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study
pmid:26781281.finding: Taurine 1.6 g/day for 12 weeks lowered clinic systolic BP by 7.2 vs 2.6 mmHg (placebo) and improved endothelial function.

pmid:27721479.authors: Trammell SA, Schmidt MS, Weidemann BJ, et al.
pmid:27721479.title: Nicotinamide riboside is uniquely and orally bioavailable in mice and humans
pmid:27721479.finding: Single oral doses of 100-1000 mg NR produced dose-dependent rises in the blood NAD+ metabolome (industry-sponsored).

pmid:16332961.authors: Trifunovic A, Hansson A, Wredenberg A, et al.
pmid:16332961.title: Somatic mtDNA mutations cause aging phenotypes without affecting reactive oxygen species production
pmid:16332961.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:16332961.finding: mtDNA mutator mice age prematurely from accumulated mtDNA mutations, but without any increase in ROS production, breaking the predicted 'vicious cycle'.

pmid:38755142.authors: Tzang CC, Chi LY, Lin LH, et al.
pmid:38755142.title: Taurine reduces the risk for metabolic syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmid:38755142.finding: Taurine 0.5-6 g/day lowered systolic BP by ~4 mmHg, diastolic BP by ~1.5 mmHg, fasting glucose by ~5.9 mg/dL and triglycerides by ~18 mg/dL, with no excess adverse effects.

pmid:41917677.authors: van Maanen E, Gonçalves A, Chen L, et al.
pmid:41917677.title: Atypical population pharmacokinetics of hydromethylthionine in patients with Alzheimer's disease explains unexpected phase 3 trial results
pmid:41917677.finding: TauRx-affiliated pharmacokinetic modelling argued that the 4 mg methylthioninium 'control' in LMTM phase 3 trials reached active plasma levels, explaining unexpected symptomatic effects in the control arm.

pmid:19197346.title: Deletion of the mitochondrial superoxide dismutase sod-2 extends lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans
pmid:19197346.finding: In C. elegans, deleting any of the five sod genes (singly or in combinations) did not shorten lifespan, and sod-2 deletion extended it despite more protein oxidation.

pmid:14679299.authors: Van Remmen H, Ikeno Y, Hamilton M, et al.
pmid:14679299.title: Life-long reduction in MnSOD activity results in increased DNA damage and higher incidence of cancer but does not accelerate aging
pmid:14679299.finding: Sod2+/- mice with 50% less MnSOD had more oxidative DNA damage (8-oxodG) and twice the tumour incidence, but identical mean and maximum lifespan.

pmid:29546641.authors: Waldron M, Patterson SD, Tallent J, et al.
pmid:29546641.title: The Effects of an Oral Taurine Dose and Supplementation Period on Endurance Exercise Performance in Humans: A Meta-Analysis
pmid:29546641.finding: Taurine 1-6 g taken acutely or for up to 2 weeks gave a small-to-moderate improvement in endurance performance (Hedges' g 0.40).

pmid:32810739.authors: Williamson J, Hughes CM, Cobley JN, et al.
pmid:32810739.title: The mitochondria-targeted antioxidant MitoQ, attenuates exercise-induced mitochondrial DNA damage
pmid:32810739.finding: 21 days of MitoQ 20 mg/day attenuated exercise-induced nuclear and mitochondrial DNA damage in lymphocytes and muscle; a single dose had no effect.

pmid:39070254.authors: Xu C, Bi S, Zhang W, et al.
pmid:39070254.title: The effects of creatine supplementation on cognitive function in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:39070254.finding: Creatine monohydrate improved memory (SMD 0.31) and attention time, with little effect on other cognitive domains.

pmid:39544014.authors: Yau YF, Cheah IK, Mahendran R, et al.
pmid:39544014.title: Investigating the efficacy of ergothioneine to delay cognitive decline in mild cognitively impaired subjects: A pilot study
pmid:39544014.finding: Ergothioneine 25 mg three times weekly for one year was safe, improved a verbal learning test and stabilized neurofilament light chain vs placebo (pilot).

pmid:36482258.authors: Yi L, Maier AB, Tao R, et al.
pmid:36482258.title: The efficacy and safety of β-nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) supplementation in healthy middle-aged adults: a randomized, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, dose-dependent clinical trial
pmid:36482258.finding: NMN 300-900 mg/day for 60 days raised blood NAD+ (plateau at 600 mg) and increased 6-minute walk distance; HOMA-IR did not change.

pmid:33888596.authors: Yoshino M, Yoshino J, Kayser BD, et al.
pmid:33888596.title: Nicotinamide mononucleotide increases muscle insulin sensitivity in prediabetic women
pmid:33888596.finding: NMN 250 mg/day for 10 weeks increased muscle insulin sensitivity (clamp) and insulin signalling vs placebo.

pmid:24561260.title: Mitohormesis
pmid:24561260.finding: Mild mitochondrial stress activates cytosolic signalling and nuclear gene expression that leave cells more resistant to later stress (mitohormesis).

pmid:19776219.authors: Zhang Y, Ikeno Y, Qi W, et al.
pmid:19776219.title: Mice deficient in both Mn superoxide dismutase and glutathione peroxidase-1 have increased oxidative damage and a greater incidence of pathology but no reduction in longevity
pmid:19776219.journal: J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci
pmid:19776219.finding: Mice lacking Gpx1 and half of Sod2 had more DNA and protein oxidation and more cancer, but no reduction in lifespan.

pmid:11600532.authors: Zhdanova IV, Wurtman RJ, Regan MM, et al.
pmid:11600532.title: Melatonin treatment for age-related insomnia
pmid:11600532.finding: A physiological 0.3 mg melatonin dose restored sleep efficiency in older insomniacs; 3 mg caused hypothermia and melatonin levels persisting into daytime.

pmid:17065669.authors: Ziegler D, Ametov A, Barinov A, et al.
pmid:17065669.title: Oral treatment with alpha-lipoic acid improves symptomatic diabetic polyneuropathy: the SYDNEY 2 trial
pmid:17065669.finding: Oral ALA 600, 1200 or 1800 mg/day for 5 weeks reduced neuropathy symptoms by about half vs 32% on placebo; higher doses caused more nausea and vomiting.

pmid:21775755.authors: Ziegler D, Low PA, Litchy WJ, et al.
pmid:21775755.title: Efficacy and safety of antioxidant treatment with α-lipoic acid over 4 years in diabetic polyneuropathy: the NATHAN 1 trial
pmid:21775755.finding: ALA 600 mg/day for 4 years did not improve the primary composite endpoint; some secondary impairment scores improved, and serious adverse events were more frequent (38% vs 28%).

pmid:11352861.authors: Shapiro TA, Fahey JW, Wade KL, et al.
pmid:11352861.title: Chemoprotective glucosinolates and isothiocyanates of broccoli sprouts: metabolism and excretion in humans.
pmid:11352861.finding: Isothiocyanates were ~6x more bioavailable than glucosinolates; excretion was linear from 25-200 µmol; chewing sprouts thoroughly increased excretion.

pmid:16965241.authors: Shapiro TA, Fahey JW, Dinkova-Kostova AT, et al.
pmid:16965241.title: Safety, tolerance, and metabolism of broccoli sprout glucosinolates and isothiocyanates: a clinical phase I study.
pmid:16965241.finding: Glucosinolate extracts converted ~18-20% vs ~71% for isothiocyanate extracts; no toxicity including liver and thyroid tests over 7 days.

pmid:29573889.authors: López-Chillón MT, Carazo-Díaz C, Prieto-Merino D, et al.
pmid:29573889.title: Effects of long-term consumption of broccoli sprouts on inflammatory markers in overweight subjects.
pmid:29573889.finding: 30 g/day fresh broccoli sprouts for 10 weeks lowered IL-6 and CRP (uncontrolled before-after design).

pmid:21816223.authors: Clarke JD, Hsu A, Riedl K, et al.
pmid:21816223.title: Bioavailability and inter-conversion of sulforaphane and erucin in human subjects consuming broccoli sprouts or broccoli supplement in a cross-over study design.
pmid:21816223.finding: A myrosinase-free broccoli supplement produced dramatically lower plasma and urinary isothiocyanates than 40 g fresh sprouts.
