pmid:21385509.finding: 10 mg/day resveratrol for 4 weeks reduced HOMA-IR and urinary ortho-tyrosine, an oxidative-stress marker.

pmid:37252983.authors: Brickman AM, Yeung LK, Alschuler DM, et al.
pmid:37252983.title: Dietary flavanols restore hippocampal-dependent memory in older adults with lower diet quality and lower habitual flavanol consumption.
pmid:37252983.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:37252983.finding: 500 mg/day cocoa flavanols did not improve memory overall at 1 year (primary endpoint) but did in people with the lowest habitual flavanol intake or diet quality (COSMOS-Web).

pmid:36066009.authors: Cheatham CL, Canipe LG 3rd, Millsap G, et al.
pmid:36066009.title: Six-month intervention with wild blueberries improved speed of processing in mild cognitive decline: a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized clinical trial.
pmid:36066009.n: 86 older adults with mild cognitive decline
pmid:36066009.finding: Daily wild blueberry powder for 6 months improved processing speed vs placebo.

pmid:12960117.authors: Chow HH, Cai Y, Hakim IA, et al.
pmid:12960117.title: Pharmacokinetics and safety of green tea polyphenols after multiple-dose administration of epigallocatechin gallate and polyphenon E in healthy individuals.
pmid:12960117.finding: 800 mg/day EGCG for 4 weeks caused only mild side effects; free EGCG exposure rose by more than 60% with once-daily bolus dosing.

pmid:30004553.authors: Cortés-Martín A, García-Villalba R, González-Sarrías A, et al.
pmid:30004553.title: The gut microbiota urolithin metabotypes revisited: the human metabolism of ellagic acid is mainly determined by aging.
pmid:30004553.finding: Age is the main determinant of urolithin metabotype distribution in a Caucasian cohort.

pmid:41305552.authors: Crișan D, Gavrilaș L, Păltinean R, et al.
pmid:41305552.title: Effects of Moringa oleifera Lam. Supplementation on Cardiometabolic Outcomes: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials with GRADE Assessment.
pmid:41305552.finding: Moringa supplementation had no consistent effect on glucose, lipids or body measures; a small diastolic BP reduction was not robust and certainty was very low for all outcomes.

pmid:41174221.authors: Denk D, Singh A, Kasler HG, et al.
pmid:41174221.title: Effect of the mitophagy inducer urolithin A on age-related immune decline: a randomized, placebo-controlled trial.
pmid:41174221.finding: 1000 mg/day urolithin A for 4 weeks expanded naive-like CD8+ T cells and raised their fatty-acid oxidation capacity (primary outcomes).

pmid:36207170.authors: Di Pede G, Mena P, Bresciani L, et al.
pmid:36207170.title: Revisiting the bioavailability of flavan-3-ols in humans: A systematic review and comprehensive data analysis.
pmid:36207170.finding: Mean flavan-3-ol bioavailability was ~31%, largely as microbial phenyl-gamma-valerolactones; ~82% for pure (-)-epicatechin vs ~25% for tea, cocoa, apple and grape.

pmid:17951477.authors: Edwards RL, Lyon T, Litwin SE, et al.
pmid:17951477.title: Quercetin reduces blood pressure in hypertensive subjects.
pmid:17951477.n: 41 adults with prehypertension or stage 1 hypertension
pmid:17951477.finding: 730 mg/day quercetin for 28 days lowered blood pressure by 7/5 mmHg in stage 1 hypertension only, and did not change plasma or urinary oxidative-stress markers.

pmid:27841876.authors: Eisenberg T, Abdellatif M, Schroeder S, et al.
pmid:27841876.title: Cardioprotection and lifespan extension by the natural polyamine spermidine.
pmid:27841876.finding: Spermidine extended mouse lifespan and protected the ageing heart through autophagy (lost in Atg5-deficient cardiomyocytes); dietary spermidine correlated with lower blood pressure and CVD in humans.

pmid:38956196.authors: Farr JN, Atkinson EJ, Achenbach SJ, et al.
pmid:38956196.title: Effects of intermittent senolytic therapy on bone metabolism in postmenopausal women: a phase 2 randomized controlled trial.
pmid:38956196.finding: Intermittent dasatinib plus quercetin for 20 weeks did not change the primary bone-resorption marker; benefits appeared only in an exploratory high-senescence subgroup.

pmid:29359958.authors: Fogacci F, Tocci G, Presta V, et al.
pmid:29359958.title: Effect of resveratrol on blood pressure: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized, controlled, clinical trials.
pmid:29359958.finding: Resveratrol had no overall effect on blood pressure; reductions appeared only at 300 mg/day or more and in people with diabetes.

pmid:22475430.authors: Fogarty MC, Hughes CM, Burke G, et al.
pmid:22475430.title: Acute and chronic watercress supplementation attenuates exercise-induced peripheral mononuclear cell DNA damage and lipid peroxidation.
pmid:22475430.finding: Acute and 8-week watercress supplementation attenuated the rise in mononuclear-cell DNA damage and lipid peroxidation after exhaustive exercise.

pmid:10952093.authors: Fowke JH, Longcope C, Hebert JR
pmid:10952093.title: Brassica vegetable consumption shifts estrogen metabolism in healthy postmenopausal women.
pmid:10952093.finding: After adjustment, each extra 10 g/day of Brassica vegetables raised the urinary 2:16alpha-hydroxyestrone ratio by 0.08.

pmid:24569543.authors: Frankenfeld CL, Atkinson C, Wähälä K, et al.
pmid:24569543.title: Obesity prevalence in relation to gut microbial environments capable of producing equol or O-desmethylangolensin from the isoflavone daidzein.
pmid:24569543.finding: About 25-60% of people harbour gut bacteria able to make equol and 80-95% can make O-DMA; obesity was linked to O-DMA non-production but not equol status.

pmid:17403273.authors: Fuller Z, Louis P, Mihajlovski A, et al.
pmid:17403273.title: Influence of cabbage processing methods and prebiotic manipulation of colonic microflora on glucosinolate breakdown in man.
pmid:17403273.finding: Lightly cooked (2-min microwaved) cabbage yielded more allyl isothiocyanate (urinary allyl mercapturic acid) than fully cooked cabbage; raising bifidobacteria with inulin did not help.

pmid:35237893.authors: Gharaei R, Alyasin A, Mahdavinezhad F, et al.
pmid:35237893.title: Randomized controlled trial of astaxanthin impacts on antioxidant status and assisted reproductive technology outcomes in women with polycystic ovarian syndrome.
pmid:35237893.finding: 8 mg/day astaxanthin for 40 days raised serum antioxidant capacity, granulosa-cell Nrf2 targets, and MII-oocyte and top-quality embryo rates, but not pregnancy rates.

pmid:17284750.authors: Gill CI, Haldar S, Boyd LA, et al.
pmid:17284750.title: Watercress supplementation in diet reduces lymphocyte DNA damage and alters blood antioxidant status in healthy adults.
pmid:17284750.finding: 85 g/day raw watercress for 8 weeks reduced basal lymphocyte DNA damage by 17% and oxidative purine damage by 24%, more in smokers; plasma lutein doubled.

pmid:23878368.authors: Gliemann L, Schmidt JF, Olesen J, et al.
pmid:23878368.title: Resveratrol blunts the positive effects of exercise training on cardiovascular health in aged men.
pmid:23878368.finding: 250 mg/day resveratrol during 8 weeks of high-intensity training cut the VO2max gain by 45% and abolished training-induced improvements in blood pressure, LDL and triglycerides.

pmid:37679434.authors: Gonzales MM, Garbarino VR, Kautz TF, et al.
pmid:37679434.title: Senolytic therapy in mild Alzheimer's disease: a phase 1 feasibility trial.
pmid:37679434.finding: Dasatinib plus quercetin for 12 weeks was tolerated; dasatinib reached CSF but quercetin was not detected there, and cognitive endpoints did not change.

pmid:33068691.authors: Harper SA, Bassler JR, Peramsetty S, et al.
pmid:33068691.title: Resveratrol and exercise combined to treat functional limitations in late life: A pilot randomized controlled trial.
pmid:33068691.finding: Pilot: resveratrol 500 or 1000 mg/day with 12 weeks of exercise was safe and feasible; 6-minute walk gains were larger in resveratrol arms but efficacy was not formally tested.

pmid:8634661.authors: Hecht SS, Chung FL, Richie JP Jr, et al.
pmid:8634661.title: Effects of watercress consumption on metabolism of a tobacco-specific lung carcinogen in smokers.
pmid:8634661.finding: Eating 57 g of watercress at each meal for 3 days (at least 19-38 mg PEITC/day) raised urinary excretion of detoxified NNK metabolites by 33.5%.

pmid:39038797.authors: Heidari Z, Farahmandpour F, Bazyar H, et al.
pmid:39038797.title: Effects of Hesperidin Supplementation on Cardiometabolic Markers: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
pmid:39038797.finding: Hesperidin supplementation modestly lowered fasting glucose, triglycerides, total and LDL cholesterol, systolic BP and TNF-alpha; effects were clearer above 500 mg/day and beyond 12 weeks.

pmid:20478383.authors: Heinz SA, Henson DA, Austin MD, et al.
pmid:20478383.title: Quercetin supplementation and upper respiratory tract infection: A randomized community clinical trial.
pmid:20478383.finding: 500 or 1000 mg/day quercetin for 12 weeks did not reduce upper respiratory infections overall; a post-hoc subgroup of fit adults aged 40+ had 31-36% fewer sick days and lower severity on 1000 mg.

pmid:31542391.authors: Hickson LJ, Langhi Prata LGP, Bobart SA, et al.
pmid:31542391.title: Senolytics decrease senescent cells in humans: Preliminary report from a clinical trial of Dasatinib plus Quercetin in individuals with diabetic kidney disease.
pmid:31542391.finding: Three days of dasatinib 100 mg plus quercetin 1000 mg reduced senescent-cell markers in fat and skin and circulating SASP factors 11 days later.

pmid:7491892.authors: Hollman PC, de Vries JH, van Leeuwen SD, et al.
pmid:7491892.title: Absorption of dietary quercetin glycosides and quercetin in healthy ileostomy volunteers.
pmid:7491892.finding: Quercetin absorption was 52% from onion glucosides, 24% from the pure aglycone and 17% from rutin; urine contained only 0.5% of the absorbed amount.

pmid:36037472.authors: Inoue-Choi M, Ramirez Y, Cornelis MC, et al.
pmid:36037472.title: Tea Consumption and All-Cause and Cause-Specific Mortality in the UK Biobank : A Prospective Cohort Study.
pmid:36037472.finding: Drinking 2 or more cups a day of (mostly black) tea was associated with 9-13% lower all-cause mortality over 11 years in the UK Biobank.

pmid:25120110.authors: Jówko E, Długołęcka B, Makaruk B, et al.
pmid:25120110.title: The effect of green tea extract supplementation on exercise-induced oxidative stress parameters in male sprinters.
pmid:25120110.finding: 980 mg/day green tea polyphenols for 4 weeks prevented the sprint-induced rise in plasma MDA, did not change performance and did not appear to blunt antioxidant-enzyme adaptation.

pmid:30616998.authors: Justice JN, Nambiar AM, Tchkonia T, et al.
pmid:30616998.title: Senolytics in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: Results from a first-in-human, open-label, pilot study.
pmid:30616998.finding: Intermittent dasatinib plus quercetin (1250 mg/day) was feasible and improved 6-minute walk and gait speed, without changing lung function.

pmid:17685090.authors: Karppi J, Rissanen TH, Nyyssönen K, et al.
pmid:17685090.title: Effects of astaxanthin supplementation on lipid peroxidation.
pmid:17685090.finding: 8 mg/day astaxanthin for 3 months lowered plasma 12- and 15-hydroxy fatty acids within the group; the between-group difference was borderline.

pmid:29955838.authors: Kiechl S, Pechlaner R, Willeit P, et al.
pmid:29955838.title: Higher spermidine intake is linked to lower mortality: a prospective population-based study.
pmid:29955838.finding: Each 1-SD higher dietary spermidine intake was associated with 24% lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.76) over 20 years; replicated in a second cohort (HR 0.71).

pmid:32686219.title: Senolytic drugs: from discovery to translation.
pmid:32686219.finding: Senolytics (dasatinib, quercetin, fisetin, navitoclax) can be given intermittently ('hit and run'); the authors state it is too early to use them outside clinical trials.

pmid:21606866.authors: Kressler J, Millard-Stafford M, Warren GL
pmid:21606866.title: Quercetin and endurance exercise capacity: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:21606866.finding: Quercetin (median 1000 mg/day for 11 days) improved endurance capacity by a trivial-to-small ~2% (effect size 0.15).

pmid:40126033.authors: Lagou V, Greyling A, Ferruzzi MG, et al.
pmid:40126033.title: Impact of flavan-3-ols on blood pressure and endothelial function in diverse populations: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
pmid:40126033.finding: Flavan-3-ol interventions (~586 mg/day) lowered office BP by 2.8/2.0 mmHg (5.9/2.7 mmHg in hypertension) and raised FMD by 1.7-2.0 percentage points.

pmid:30322091.authors: Leone A, Bertoli S, Di Lello S, et al.
pmid:30322091.title: Effect of Moringa oleifera Leaf Powder on Postprandial Blood Glucose Response: In Vivo Study on Saharawi People Living in Refugee Camps.
pmid:30322091.finding: Adding 20 g of moringa leaf powder to a meal lowered the post-meal glucose response in diabetics but not healthy people; palatability was poor.

pmid:35050355.authors: Liu S, D'Amico D, Shankland E, et al.
pmid:35050355.title: Effect of Urolithin A Supplementation on Muscle Endurance and Mitochondrial Health in Older Adults: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
pmid:35050355.finding: 1000 mg/day urolithin A for 4 months improved hand and leg muscle endurance and lowered CRP and acylcarnitines, but the primary endpoints (6-minute walk, maximal ATP production) did not differ from placebo.

pmid:29371440.authors: Madeo F, Eisenberg T, Pietrocola F, et al.
pmid:29371440.title: Spermidine in health and disease.
pmid:29371440.finding: Spermidine behaves as a caloric-restriction mimetic via protein deacetylation and autophagy; evidence is mainly rodent plus human epidemiology.

pmid:32078436.authors: McDermott MM, Criqui MH, Domanchuk K, et al.
pmid:32078436.title: Cocoa to Improve Walking Performance in Older People With Peripheral Artery Disease: The COCOA-PAD Pilot Randomized Clinical Trial.
pmid:32078436.finding: 15 g cocoa (75 mg epicatechin) daily for 6 months improved 6-minute walk by 42.6 m 2.5 h after a dose (18 m at 24 h, not significant) and calf mitochondrial COX activity.

pmid:9168187.authors: Michnovicz JJ, Adlercreutz H, Bradlow HL
pmid:9168187.title: Changes in levels of urinary estrogen metabolites after oral indole-3-carbinol treatment in humans.
pmid:9168187.finding: Indole-3-carbinol 6-7 mg/kg/day raised urinary 2-hydroxylated estrogens and lowered estradiol, estrone, estriol and 16alpha-hydroxyestrone.

pmid:21068346.authors: Morand C, Dubray C, Milenkovic D, et al.
pmid:21068346.title: Hesperidin contributes to the vascular protective effects of orange juice: a randomized crossover study in healthy volunteers.
pmid:21068346.finding: 500 mL/day orange juice or matched hesperidin for 4 weeks lowered diastolic BP, and both improved post-meal microvascular reactivity.

diet:phy-nct03675724.title: AFFIRM-LITE: A Phase 2 Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Study of Alleviation by Fisetin of Frailty, Inflammation, and Related Measures in Older Adults (NCT03675724), record accessed 2026-10-01.
diet:phy-nct03675724.finding: Fisetin 20 mg/kg/day orally for 2 consecutive days vs placebo; started November 2018 and still listed as enrolling, with primary completion estimated for November 2026.

pmid:19927026.authors: Nieman DC, Williams AS, Shanely RA, et al.
pmid:19927026.title: Quercetin's influence on exercise performance and muscle mitochondrial biogenesis.
pmid:19927026.finding: 1000 mg/day quercetin for 2 weeks improved 12-minute treadmill distance by ~3% vs placebo, with non-significant trends in mitochondrial-biogenesis markers.

pmid:37960261.authors: Nouchi R, Kawata NYS, Saito T, et al.
pmid:37960261.title: Benefits of Wasabi Supplements with 6-MSITC (6-Methylsulfinyl Hexyl Isothiocyanate) on Memory Functioning in Healthy Adults Aged 60 Years and Older: Evidence from a Double-Blinded Randomized Controlled Trial.
pmid:37960261.finding: 12 weeks of a wasabi 6-MSITC supplement improved working and episodic memory vs placebo but no other cognitive domain.

pmid:33540959.title: Toxicology studies of indole-3-carbinol in F344/N rats and B6C3F1/N mice and toxicology and carcinogenesis studies of indole-3-carbinol in Harlan Sprague Dawley rats and B6C3F1/N mice (gavage studies).
pmid:33540959.journal: Natl Toxicol Program Tech Rep Ser
pmid:33540959.finding: Two-year gavage studies found clear evidence of carcinogenicity of indole-3-carbinol (liver tumours) in male mice and some evidence (uterine adenocarcinoma) in female rats; none in male rats or female mice.

pmid:24514907.authors: Olesen J, Gliemann L, Biensø R, et al.
pmid:24514907.title: Exercise training, but not resveratrol, improves metabolic and inflammatory status in skeletal muscle of aged men.
pmid:24514907.finding: Resveratrol 250 mg/day gave no metabolic benefit on its own and blunted exercise-induced falls in muscle protein carbonylation and TNF-alpha mRNA.

pmid:20205737.authors: Park JS, Chyun JH, Kim YK, et al.
pmid:20205737.title: Astaxanthin decreased oxidative stress and inflammation and enhanced immune response in humans.
pmid:20205737.finding: 2 or 8 mg/day astaxanthin for 8 weeks lowered a DNA-damage biomarker and (at 2 mg) CRP, but did not change lipid peroxidation.

pmid:23193181.authors: Poulsen MM, Vestergaard PF, Clasen BF, et al.
pmid:23193181.title: High-dose resveratrol supplementation in obese men: an investigator-initiated, randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial of substrate metabolism, insulin sensitivity, and body composition.
pmid:23193181.finding: High-dose resveratrol for 4 weeks had no effect on insulin sensitivity, blood pressure, body fat or inflammatory markers.

pmid:17164373.authors: Reed GA, Arneson DW, Putnam WC, et al.
pmid:17164373.title: Single-dose and multiple-dose administration of indole-3-carbinol to women: pharmacokinetics based on 3,3'-diindolylmethane.
pmid:17164373.n: women in a phase I dose-escalation trial
pmid:17164373.finding: Indole-3-carbinol itself is undetectable in plasma; DIM is the only circulating product, plateauing above ~1000 mg (Cmax ~607 ng/mL), with large differences between people.

pmid:33383165.authors: Reed KE, Camargo J, Hamilton-Reeves J, et al.
pmid:33383165.title: Neither soy nor isoflavone intake affects male reproductive hormones: An expanded and updated meta-analysis of clinical studies.
pmid:33383165.finding: Neither soy protein nor isoflavones altered testosterone, free testosterone, estradiol, estrone or SHBG in men, regardless of dose or duration.

pmid:23431291.authors: Riche DM, McEwen CL, Riche KD, et al.
pmid:23431291.title: Analysis of safety from a human clinical trial with pterostilbene.
pmid:23431291.finding: Pterostilbene up to 250 mg/day for 6-8 weeks showed no hepatic, renal or glucose safety signals.

pmid:25057276.authors: Riche DM, Riche KD, Blackshear CT, et al.
pmid:25057276.title: Pterostilbene on metabolic parameters: a randomized, double-blind, and placebo-controlled trial.
pmid:25057276.finding: Pterostilbene 125 mg twice daily lowered BP by 7.8/7.3 mmHg but raised LDL by 17 mg/dL; the LDL rise was not seen when combined with grape extract.

pmid:21346065.authors: Rizza S, Muniyappa R, Iantorno M, et al.
pmid:21346065.title: Citrus polyphenol hesperidin stimulates production of nitric oxide in endothelial cells while improving endothelial function and reducing inflammatory markers in patients with metabolic syndrome.
pmid:21346065.finding: 500 mg/day hesperidin for 3 weeks raised FMD (10.3% vs 7.8%) and lowered CRP and other inflammatory markers.

pmid:24126178.authors: Rodriguez-Leyva D, Weighell W, Edel AL, et al.
pmid:24126178.title: Potent antihypertensive action of dietary flaxseed in hypertensive patients.
pmid:24126178.finding: 30 g/day milled flaxseed for 6 months lowered systolic BP ~10 and diastolic ~7 mmHg vs placebo (15 mmHg systolic in hypertensives); enterolignans rose 2-50-fold.

pmid:30358831.authors: Rodriguez-Mateos A, Weber T, Skene SS, et al.
pmid:30358831.title: Assessing the respective contributions of dietary flavanol monomers and procyanidins in mediating cardiovascular effects in humans: randomized, controlled, double-masked intervention trial.
pmid:30358831.finding: A cocoa extract with 130 mg epicatechin improved FMD, blood pressure and pulse wave velocity, while a procyanidin-rich extract with little epicatechin did not.

pmid:27400265.authors: Ryu D, Mouchiroud L, Andreux PA, et al.
pmid:27400265.title: Urolithin A induces mitophagy and prolongs lifespan in C. elegans and increases muscle function in rodents.
pmid:27400265.finding: Urolithin A induced mitophagy, extended C. elegans lifespan and improved exercise capacity in aged mice and young rats.

pmid:34716791.authors: Sarapis K, George ES, Marx W, et al.
pmid:34716791.title: Extra virgin olive oil high in polyphenols improves antioxidant status in adults: a double-blind, randomized, controlled, cross-over study (OLIVAUS).
pmid:34716791.finding: 60 mL/day of high-polyphenol (320 mg/kg) vs low-polyphenol (86 mg/kg) olive oil for 3 weeks: no significant between-treatment differences; oxLDL fell only within the high-polyphenol arm, more in abdominal obesity.

pmid:35616942.authors: Schwarz C, Benson GS, Horn N, et al.
pmid:35616942.title: Effects of Spermidine Supplementation on Cognition and Biomarkers in Older Adults With Subjective Cognitive Decline: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
pmid:35616942.finding: Twelve months of 0.9 mg/day spermidine (wheat-germ extract) did not change memory or biomarkers vs placebo (SmartAge phase 2b).

pmid:25211703.authors: Scribbans TD, Ma JK, Edgett BA, et al.
pmid:25211703.title: Resveratrol supplementation does not augment performance adaptations or fibre-type-specific responses to high-intensity interval training in humans.
pmid:25211703.finding: 150 mg/day resveratrol during 4 weeks of HIIT blunted the gain in peak aerobic power and the training-induced rise in PGC-1alpha, SIRT1 and SOD2 expression.

pmid:27405810.authors: Serban MC, Sahebkar A, Zanchetti A, et al.
pmid:27405810.title: Effects of Quercetin on Blood Pressure: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
pmid:27405810.finding: Quercetin lowered blood pressure by ~3.0/2.6 mmHg overall; the effect was confined to doses of 500 mg/day or more (-4.5/-3.0 mmHg).

pmid:12468591.authors: Setchell KD, Brown NM, Lydeking-Olsen E
pmid:12468591.title: The clinical importance of the metabolite equol-a clue to the effectiveness of soy and its isoflavones.
pmid:12468591.finding: Equol is made only by gut bacteria from daidzein, and only some adults produce it; the producer/non-producer split may explain inconsistent soy trial results.

pmid:35584623.authors: Singh A, D'Amico D, Andreux PA, et al.
pmid:35584623.title: Urolithin A improves muscle strength, exercise performance, and biomarkers of mitochondrial health in a randomized trial in middle-aged adults.
pmid:35584623.finding: 500-1000 mg/day urolithin A for 4 months raised muscle strength ~12% and improved VO2peak and 6-minute walk, but not the primary endpoint (peak power output); company-sponsored.

pmid:28560655.authors: Thomson CA, Chow HHS, Wertheim BC, et al.
pmid:28560655.title: A randomized, placebo-controlled trial of diindolylmethane for breast cancer biomarker modulation in patients taking tamoxifen.
pmid:28560655.finding: DIM 150 mg twice daily for 12 months raised the 2/16 ratio and SHBG but lowered plasma tamoxifen metabolites including endoxifen; breast density was unchanged.

pmid:22055504.authors: Timmers S, Konings E, Bilet L, et al.
pmid:22055504.title: Calorie restriction-like effects of 30 days of resveratrol supplementation on energy metabolism and metabolic profile in obese humans.
pmid:22055504.finding: 150 mg/day resveratrol for 30 days produced calorie-restriction-like changes: lower metabolic rate, liver fat, glucose and systolic BP.

pmid:24976365.authors: Tomás-Barberán FA, García-Villalba R, González-Sarrías A, et al.
pmid:24976365.title: Ellagic acid metabolism by human gut microbiota: consistent observation of three urolithin phenotypes in intervention trials, independent of food source, age, and health status.
pmid:24976365.finding: Across intervention trials, 25-80% of people produce only urolithin A (metabotype A), 10-50% also make isourolithin A/urolithin B (B) and 5-25% make none (0), regardless of food source.

pmid:24886552.authors: Tresserra-Rimbau A, Rimm EB, Medina-Remón A, et al.
pmid:24886552.title: Polyphenol intake and mortality risk: a re-analysis of the PREDIMED trial.
pmid:24886552.finding: The highest vs lowest quintile of total food polyphenol intake had 37% lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.63); stilbenes and lignans were the subclasses most strongly associated.

pmid:26362286.authors: Turner RS, Thomas RG, Craft S, et al.
pmid:26362286.title: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of resveratrol for Alzheimer disease.
pmid:26362286.finding: Resveratrol escalated to 1 g twice daily for 52 weeks altered Abeta40 trajectories but increased brain-volume loss; nausea, diarrhoea and weight loss were common.

pmid:25577465.authors: Vanegas JC, Afeiche MC, Gaskins AJ, et al.
pmid:25577465.title: Soy food intake and treatment outcomes of women undergoing assisted reproductive technology.
pmid:25577465.finding: Higher soy isoflavone intake was associated with higher live-birth rates in ART (OR ~1.8 for 2.6-28 mg/day vs none).

pmid:38070683.authors: Vyas CM, Manson JE, Sesso HD, et al.
pmid:38070683.title: Effect of cocoa extract supplementation on cognitive function: results from the clinic subcohort of the COSMOS trial.
pmid:38070683.finding: Cocoa extract (500 mg flavanols/day) for 2 years had no effect on global cognition, memory or executive function (COSMOS-Clinic).

pmid:31434498.authors: Wang L, Cao D, Wu H, et al.
pmid:31434498.title: Fisetin Prolongs Therapy Window of Brain Ischemic Stroke Using Tissue Plasminogen Activator: A Double-Blind Randomized Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial.
pmid:31434498.n: patients with ischaemic stroke receiving rt-PA
pmid:31434498.finding: Fisetin added to thrombolysis improved NIH Stroke Scale outcomes in patients treated late and lowered MMP-2, MMP-9 and CRP; a non-senolytic use of fisetin.

pmid:24731259.authors: Waterman C, Cheng DM, Rojas-Silva P, et al.
pmid:24731259.title: Stable, water extractable isothiocyanates from Moringa oleifera leaves attenuate inflammation in vitro.
pmid:24731259.finding: Water extraction of fresh moringa leaves lets their own myrosinase form stable moringa isothiocyanates (1.66% of the concentrate; ~80% stable after 30 days at 37 C) that were anti-inflammatory in macrophages.

pmid:25620073.authors: Waterman C, Rojas-Silva P, Tumer TB, et al.
pmid:25620073.title: Isothiocyanate-rich Moringa oleifera extract reduces weight gain, insulin resistance, and hepatic gluconeogenesis in mice.
pmid:25620073.finding: A moringa isothiocyanate concentrate (66 mg/kg/day isothiocyanates) improved glucose tolerance and prevented fatty liver in high-fat-fed mice.

pmid:40839339.authors: Whitfield J, McKay AKA, Tee N, et al.
pmid:40839339.title: Evaluating the Impact of Urolithin A Supplementation on Running Performance, Recovery, and Mitochondrial Biomarkers in Highly Trained Male Distance Runners.
pmid:40839339.finding: 1000 mg/day urolithin A for 4 weeks lowered creatine kinase and perceived exertion but did not improve 3000-m time-trial performance or VO2max relative to placebo.

pmid:32747995.authors: Whyte AR, Rahman S, Bell L, et al.
pmid:32747995.title: Improved metabolic function and cognitive performance in middle-aged adults following a single dose of wild blueberry.
pmid:32747995.finding: A single 1-cup-equivalent wild blueberry drink maintained memory and executive function over 8 hours and lowered post-meal glucose and insulin vs placebo.

pmid:30388439.authors: Wirth M, Benson G, Schwarz C, et al.
pmid:30388439.title: The effect of spermidine on memory performance in older adults at risk for dementia: A randomized controlled trial.
pmid:30388439.finding: Three-month pilot: a spermidine-rich plant extract moderately improved mnemonic discrimination vs placebo (Cohen's d ~0.77, confidence interval touching zero).

pmid:15223075.authors: Wiswedel I, Hirsch D, Kropf S, et al.
pmid:15223075.title: Flavanol-rich cocoa drink lowers plasma F(2)-isoprostane concentrations in humans.
pmid:15223075.finding: High-flavanol cocoa prevented the rise in GC-MS-measured plasma F2-isoprostanes seen after low-flavanol cocoa, most clearly when combined with strenuous exercise.

pmid:24899709.authors: Witte AV, Kerti L, Margulies DS, et al.
pmid:24899709.title: Effects of resveratrol on memory performance, hippocampal functional connectivity, and glucose metabolism in healthy older adults.
pmid:24899709.finding: 200 mg/day resveratrol for 26 weeks improved word retention and hippocampal connectivity and lowered HbA1c vs placebo.

pmid:30279143.authors: Yousefzadeh MJ, Zhu Y, McGowan SJ, et al.
pmid:30279143.title: Fisetin is a senotherapeutic that extends health and lifespan.
pmid:30279143.finding: Fisetin was the most potent senolytic of 10 flavonoids screened; late-life dosing reduced senescence markers and extended median and maximum lifespan in mice.

pmid:28765194.authors: Yu Z, Samavat H, Dostal AM, et al.
pmid:28765194.title: Effect of Green Tea Supplements on Liver Enzyme Elevation: Results from a Randomized Intervention Study in the United States.
pmid:28765194.finding: High-dose green tea extract for 12 months raised ALT and AST; 5.1% developed moderate or worse liver abnormalities (OR 7.0), with positive rechallenge.

pmid:26951845.authors: Yuan JM, Stepanov I, Murphy SE, et al.
pmid:26951845.title: Clinical Trial of 2-Phenethyl Isothiocyanate as an Inhibitor of Metabolic Activation of a Tobacco-Specific Lung Carcinogen in Cigarette Smokers.
pmid:26951845.finding: PEITC 10 mg four times daily for 1 week reduced the metabolic activation ratio of the tobacco carcinogen NNK by 7.7%.

pmid:34320173.authors: Zeraattalab-Motlagh S, Jayedi A, Shab-Bidar S
pmid:34320173.title: The effects of resveratrol supplementation in patients with type 2 diabetes, metabolic syndrome, and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease: an umbrella review of meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials.
pmid:34320173.finding: Resveratrol effects in type 2 diabetes, metabolic syndrome and fatty liver were trivial or of very low certainty; the evidence does not support supplementation (short-term HbA1c the exception).

pmid:19960458.title: Allyl isothiocyanate as a cancer chemopreventive phytochemical.
pmid:19960458.finding: Allyl isothiocyanate is ~90% absorbed in animal studies and excreted as mercapturic acids, with urinary levels at least 10x plasma, concentrating exposure in the bladder.

pmid:34070285.authors: Acharya P, Acharya C, Thongprayoon C, et al.
pmid:34070285.title: Incidence and Characteristics of Kidney Stones in Patients on Ketogenic Diet: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
pmid:34070285.finding: Pooled kidney-stone incidence on ketogenic diets was 5.9% (children 5.8%, adults 7.9%) over ~3.7 years; about half were uric acid stones.

pmid:19188683.authors: Anderson EJ, Lustig ME, Boyle KE, et al.
pmid:19188683.title: Mitochondrial H2O2 emission and cellular redox state link excess fat intake to insulin resistance in both rodents and humans.
pmid:19188683.n: rodents plus a small human feeding study
pmid:19188683.finding: High fat intake increased the H2O2-emitting potential of skeletal-muscle mitochondria and shifted cellular redox to a more oxidised state in rodents and humans; blocking mitochondrial H2O2 preserved insulin sensitivity in rodents.

pmid:34631141.authors: Anderson JC, Mattar SG, Greenway FL, et al.
pmid:34631141.title: Measuring ketone bodies for the monitoring of pathologic and therapeutic ketosis.
pmid:34631141.finding: Healthy people have ~0.1 mmol/L BHB and ~1 ppm breath acetone; ketoacidosis can raise BHB about 30-fold and breath acetone about 1000-fold.

pmid:32437658.authors: Ang QY, Alexander M, Newman JC, et al.
pmid:32437658.title: Ketogenic Diets Alter the Gut Microbiome Resulting in Decreased Intestinal Th17 Cells.
pmid:32437658.finding: Ketogenic diets shifted the human and mouse gut microbiome differently from high-fat diets, depleting bifidobacteria (ketone bodies inhibited their growth) and lowering intestinal Th17 cells in mice.

pmid:29712560.authors: Bhanpuri NH, Hallberg SJ, Williams PT, et al.
pmid:29712560.title: Cardiovascular disease risk factor responses to a type 2 diabetes care model including nutritional ketosis induced by sustained carbohydrate restriction at 1 year: an open label, non-randomized, controlled study.
pmid:29712560.finding: At 1 year of nutritional ketosis, small LDL particles fell 21%, apoB was unchanged, LDL-C rose 10%, and hsCRP and white cell count fell; carotid IMT was unchanged.

pmid:42063954.authors: Bonnechère B, Stephens EB, Boileau AC, et al.
pmid:42063954.title: The effect of exogenous ketone bodies on cognition across health and disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:42063954.finding: Exogenous ketones produced a small improvement in cognitive performance vs placebo (SMD 0.29) across healthy and clinical groups.

pmid:39372369.authors: Budoff M, Manubolu VS, Kinninger A, et al.
pmid:39372369.title: Carbohydrate Restriction-Induced Elevations in LDL-Cholesterol and Atherosclerosis: The KETO Trial.
pmid:39372369.n: 80 ketogenic dieters with LDL-C >= 190 mg/dL vs 80 matched controls
pmid:39372369.finding: Lean ketogenic dieters with LDL-C averaging 272 mg/dL for ~4.7 years did not have more coronary plaque than matched controls with lower LDL (cross-sectional, self-selected).

pmid:23651522.authors: Bueno NB, de Melo IS, de Oliveira SL, et al.
pmid:23651522.title: Very-low-carbohydrate ketogenic diet v. low-fat diet for long-term weight loss: a meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
pmid:23651522.finding: At >= 12 months, very-low-carbohydrate ketogenic diets (<= 50 g/day) gave 0.91 kg more weight loss than low-fat diets, lower triglycerides, higher HDL and higher LDL (+0.12 mmol/L).

pmid:33801247.authors: Burén J, Ericsson M, Damasceno NRT, et al.
pmid:33801247.title: A Ketogenic Low-Carbohydrate High-Fat Diet Increases LDL Cholesterol in Healthy, Young, Normal-Weight Women: A Randomized Controlled Feeding Trial.
pmid:33801247.finding: A 4-week ketogenic diet (4% carbohydrate) raised LDL-C in every woman (treatment effect +1.82 mmol/L) and raised apoB and small dense LDL.

pmid:28012184.authors: Burke LM, Ross ML, Garvican-Lewis LA, et al.
pmid:28012184.title: Low carbohydrate, high fat diet impairs exercise economy and negates the performance benefit from intensified training in elite race walkers.
pmid:28012184.finding: Three weeks of a < 50 g/day ketogenic diet raised fat oxidation and VO2peak but worsened exercise economy, and the 10-km race time did not improve (-1.6%) vs +6.6% and +5.3% on high or periodised carbohydrate.

pmid:32697366.authors: Burke LM, Whitfield J, Heikura IA, et al.
pmid:32697366.title: Adaptation to a low carbohydrate high fat diet is rapid but impairs endurance exercise metabolism and performance despite enhanced glycogen availability.
pmid:32697366.finding: Only 5-6 days of a < 50 g/day carbohydrate diet raised exercise fat oxidation to levels seen after weeks to months, raised oxygen cost by 5-8%, and acute carbohydrate restoration did not rescue race performance.

pmid:16848698.title: Fuel metabolism in starvation.
pmid:16848698.finding: Autobiographical review of human starvation physiology: D-beta-hydroxybutyrate, used by the brain, is what lets humans survive prolonged starvation.

pmid:17882137.authors: Chavarro JE, Rich-Edwards JW, Rosner BA, et al.
pmid:17882137.title: A prospective study of dietary carbohydrate quantity and quality in relation to risk of ovulatory infertility.
pmid:17882137.finding: Highest vs lowest quintile of total carbohydrate (RR 1.91) and glycaemic load (RR 1.92) was associated with ovulatory infertility in the Nurses' Health Study II.

pmid:30679586.authors: Chriett S, Dąbek A, Wojtala M, et al.
pmid:30679586.title: Prominent action of butyrate over β-hydroxybutyrate as histone deacetylase inhibitor, transcriptional modulator and anti-inflammatory molecule.
pmid:30679586.finding: Across several cell types and in vivo, butyrate was a strong HDAC inhibitor but R-BHB showed no detectable HDAC inhibition and was slightly pro-inflammatory in endothelial cells.

pmid:31006978.authors: Churuangsuk C, Griffiths D, Lean MEJ, et al.
pmid:31006978.title: Impacts of carbohydrate-restricted diets on micronutrient intakes and status: A systematic review.
pmid:31006978.finding: Systematic review: carbohydrate-restricted diets lowered intakes of thiamine, folate, magnesium, calcium, iron and iodine by 10-70%.

pmid:22561291.authors: Clarke K, Tchabanenko K, Pawlosky R, et al.
pmid:22561291.title: Kinetics, safety and tolerability of (R)-3-hydroxybutyl (R)-3-hydroxybutyrate in healthy adult subjects.
pmid:22561291.finding: A single ketone monoester dose of 714 mg/kg raised blood BHB to ~3.3 mmol/L within 1-2 h (half-life 0.8-3.1 h); multi-day dosing was tolerated apart from GI effects at the highest dose.

pmid:27475046.authors: Cox PJ, Kirk T, Ashmore T, et al.
pmid:27475046.title: Nutritional Ketosis Alters Fuel Preference and Thereby Endurance Performance in Athletes.
pmid:27475046.finding: A ketone ester drink lowered muscle glycolysis and plasma lactate and raised intramuscular fat oxidation during exercise, even with normal glycogen and co-ingested carbohydrate.

pmid:41793518.authors: Drabińska-Fois N, Ogrodowczyk AM, Bauer W, et al.
pmid:41793518.title: Immune-modulating effects of energy-restricted ketogenic diet in women with overweight and obesity: KETO-MINOX study.
pmid:41793518.finding: At equal calories (1750 kcal) an 8-week Mediterranean-style ketogenic diet gave more fat loss than a standard diet; both reduced inflammatory markers and differences were gone at 1 year.

pmid:30429127.authors: Ebbeling CB, Feldman HA, Klein GL, et al.
pmid:30429127.title: Effects of a low carbohydrate diet on energy expenditure during weight loss maintenance: randomized trial.
pmid:30429127.finding: During weight-loss maintenance, total energy expenditure was 209 kcal/day higher on a 20%-carbohydrate diet than on a 60%-carbohydrate diet.

pmid:35380602.authors: Falkenhain K, Daraei A, Forbes SC, et al.
pmid:35380602.title: Effects of Exogenous Ketone Supplementation on Blood Glucose: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
pmid:35380602.finding: Acute exogenous ketones raised BHB by ~2 mmol/L and lowered blood glucose by ~0.5 mmol/L vs placebo, with larger effects for monoesters than salts.

pmid:40935153.authors: Feng S, Liu R, Thompson C, et al.
pmid:40935153.title: Effects of carbohydrate-restricted diets and macronutrient replacements on cardiovascular health and body composition in adults: a meta-analysis of randomized trials.
pmid:40935153.finding: Carbohydrate-restricted diets lowered triglycerides, blood pressure, CRP and TNF-alpha and raised HDL, but modestly raised LDL and total cholesterol; ketogenic versions gave larger changes.

pmid:18046594.authors: Forsythe CE, Phinney SD, Fernandez ML, et al.
pmid:18046594.title: Comparison of low fat and low carbohydrate diets on circulating fatty acid composition and markers of inflammation.
pmid:18046594.finding: Over 12 weeks a very-low-carbohydrate diet (12% energy) lowered TNF-alpha, IL-6, IL-8, MCP-1, E-selectin, ICAM and PAI-1 more than a low-fat diet with similar calories.

pmid:33103819.authors: Fortier M, Castellano CA, St-Pierre V, et al.
pmid:33103819.title: A ketogenic drink improves cognition in mild cognitive impairment: Results of a 6-month RCT.
pmid:33103819.finding: A ketogenic MCT drink (15 g twice daily) for 6 months improved several memory, language and executive tests vs placebo.

pmid:41637092.authors: Gao M, Kirk M, Knight H, et al.
pmid:41637092.title: A Ketogenic Diet for Treatment-Resistant Depression: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
pmid:41637092.finding: A 6-week < 30 g/day ketogenic diet lowered PHQ-9 by 2.2 points more than a well-matched healthy control diet (P = .05), with no difference at 12 weeks or in secondary outcomes.

pmid:29466592.authors: Gardner CD, Trepanowski JF, Del Gobbo LC, et al.
pmid:29466592.title: Effect of Low-Fat vs Low-Carbohydrate Diet on 12-Month Weight Loss in Overweight Adults and the Association With Genotype Pattern or Insulin Secretion: The DIETFITS Randomized Clinical Trial.
pmid:29466592.finding: Over 12 months, healthy low-carbohydrate and healthy low-fat diets produced similar weight loss (-6.0 vs -5.3 kg), with no effect of genotype or insulin secretion.

pmid:35641199.authors: Gardner CD, Landry MJ, Perelman D, et al.
pmid:35641199.title: Effect of a ketogenic diet versus Mediterranean diet on glycated hemoglobin in individuals with prediabetes and type 2 diabetes mellitus: The interventional Keto-Med randomized crossover trial.
pmid:35641199.finding: Keto-Med: HbA1c did not differ between 12 weeks of a well-formulated ketogenic diet and a Mediterranean-plus diet; LDL rose 10% on keto vs fell 5% on Mediterranean, and keto lowered fibre and micronutrient intakes.

pmid:33441384.authors: Goldenberg JZ, Day A, Brinkworth GD, et al.
pmid:33441384.title: Efficacy and safety of low and very low carbohydrate diets for type 2 diabetes remission: systematic review and meta-analysis of published and unpublished randomized trial data.
pmid:33441384.finding: Low-carbohydrate diets (< 130 g/day) achieved more remission at 6 months (57% vs 31%, HbA1c < 6.5%), but benefits mostly faded by 12 months, when LDL and quality of life trended worse.

pmid:27385608.authors: Hall KD, Chen KY, Guo J, et al.
pmid:27385608.title: Energy expenditure and body composition changes after an isocaloric ketogenic diet in overweight and obese men.
pmid:27385608.finding: Switching to an isocaloric ketogenic diet raised energy expenditure only ~57-151 kcal/day and did not speed body-fat loss; fat loss slowed and fat-free mass loss increased.

pmid:33479499.authors: Hall KD, Guo J, Courville AB, et al.
pmid:33479499.title: Effect of a plant-based, low-fat diet versus an animal-based, ketogenic diet on ad libitum energy intake.
pmid:33479499.finding: Eating ad libitum, people ate 689 kcal/day less on a plant-based low-fat diet than on an animal-based ketogenic diet over 2 weeks.

pmid:29417495.authors: Hallberg SJ, McKenzie AL, Williams PT, et al.
pmid:29417495.title: Effectiveness and Safety of a Novel Care Model for the Management of Type 2 Diabetes at 1 Year: An Open-Label, Non-Randomized, Controlled Study.
pmid:29417495.finding: A remotely coached nutritional-ketosis programme cut HbA1c from 7.6% to 6.3% and weight by 13.8 kg at 1 year, with hsCRP -39%, triglycerides -24%, LDL +10% and apoB unchanged (non-randomised).

pmid:32038477.authors: Heikura IA, Burke LM, Hawley JA, et al.
pmid:32038477.title: A Short-Term Ketogenic Diet Impairs Markers of Bone Health in Response to Exercise.
pmid:32038477.finding: 3.5 weeks of a ketogenic diet raised the bone-resorption marker CTX and lowered formation markers P1NP and osteocalcin at rest and after exercise; formation markers stayed low after carbohydrate restoration.

pmid:9870562.authors: Jain SK, Kannan K, Lim G
pmid:9870562.title: Ketosis (acetoacetate) can generate oxygen radicals and cause increased lipid peroxidation and growth inhibition in human endothelial cells.
pmid:9870562.finding: Acetoacetate, but not BHB, generated superoxide (potentiated by Fe2+) and increased lipid peroxidation and growth inhibition in human endothelial cells in culture.

pmid:18466343.authors: Jarrett SG, Milder JB, Liang LP, et al.
pmid:18466343.title: The ketogenic diet increases mitochondrial glutathione levels.
pmid:18466343.finding: Three weeks of ketogenic diet doubled hippocampal mitochondrial glutathione and GSH/GSSG in rats by up-regulating glutamate cysteine ligase.

pmid:31611148.authors: Kirkpatrick CF, Bolick JP, Kris-Etherton PM, et al.
pmid:31611148.title: Review of current evidence and clinical recommendations on the effects of low-carbohydrate and very-low-carbohydrate (including ketogenic) diets for the management of body weight and other cardiometabolic risk factors: A scientific statement from the National Lipid Association Nutrition and Lifestyle Task Force.
pmid:31611148.finding: National Lipid Association statement: low- and very-low-carbohydrate diets are not superior for weight loss, may help appetite, triglycerides and diabetes-medication reduction, have mixed LDL effects, and lack data beyond ~2 years.

pmid:29881797.authors: Kossoff EH, Zupec-Kania BA, Auvin S, et al.
pmid:29881797.title: Optimal clinical management of children receiving dietary therapies for epilepsy: Updated recommendations of the International Ketogenic Diet Study Group.
pmid:29881797.finding: International Ketogenic Diet Study Group: classic 4:1 diet (~90% of energy from fat), modified Atkins 10-15 g/day carbohydrate rising to ~20 g, daily multivitamin, calcium and vitamin D, oral citrate to prevent stones (historic stone rate 3-7%), contraindicated in fatty-acid oxidation and pyruvate carboxylase defects and porphyria, trial for ~3 months.

pmid:38473723.authors: Lambadiari V, Katsimbri P, Kountouri A, et al.
pmid:38473723.title: The Effect of a Ketogenic Diet versus Mediterranean Diet on Clinical and Biochemical Markers of Inflammation in Patients with Obesity and Psoriatic Arthritis: A Randomized Crossover Trial.
pmid:38473723.n: 26 adults with obesity and psoriatic disease (crossover)
pmid:38473723.finding: Both diets cut weight, but only the 8-week ketogenic phase significantly reduced disease activity and IL-6, IL-17 and IL-23 vs baseline.

pmid:29221645.authors: Lean ME, Leslie WS, Barnes AC, et al.
pmid:29221645.title: Primary care-led weight management for remission of type 2 diabetes (DiRECT): an open-label, cluster-randomised trial.
pmid:29221645.finding: DiRECT: a total diet replacement programme (825-853 kcal/day formula, not ketogenic by design) achieved diabetes remission in 46% vs 4% at 12 months, tracking weight loss.

pmid:29109686.authors: Leckey JJ, Ross ML, Quod M, et al.
pmid:29109686.title: Ketone Diester Ingestion Impairs Time-Trial Performance in Professional Cyclists.
pmid:29109686.finding: A ketone diester before a ~31-km time trial worsened performance by ~2%, with gut discomfort and higher perceived effort.

pmid:32588435.authors: Martin-McGill KJ, Bresnahan R, Levy RG, et al.
pmid:32588435.title: Ketogenic diets for drug-resistant epilepsy.
pmid:32588435.finding: Cochrane: in children ketogenic diets increased seizure freedom (RR 3.16) and >= 50% seizure reduction (RR 5.80) vs usual care, on low to very-low certainty evidence; adult data are sparse.

pmid:41197688.authors: Mela V, Ortiz Samur NS, Vijaya AK, et al.
pmid:41197688.title: Ketogenic diet is less effective in ameliorating depression and anxiety in obesity than Mediterranean diet: A pilot study for exploring the GUT-brain axis.
pmid:41197688.finding: Over 3 months a Mediterranean diet improved depression scores more than a ketogenic diet, and stool from keto participants induced anxiety-like behaviour in mice.

pmid:20594978.authors: Milder JB, Liang LP, Patel M
pmid:20594978.title: Acute oxidative stress and systemic Nrf2 activation by the ketogenic diet.
pmid:20594978.finding: In rats a ketogenic diet first raised hippocampal mitochondrial H2O2 and 4-HNE, then activated Nrf2 (NQO1 up) in brain and liver by 3 weeks, while liver glutathione was chronically depleted: an adaptive (hormetic) response.

pmid:32985255.authors: Miller VJ, LaFountain RA, Barnhart E, et al.
pmid:32985255.title: A ketogenic diet combined with exercise alters mitochondrial function in human skeletal muscle while improving metabolic health.
pmid:32985255.finding: 12 weeks of ketogenic diet plus exercise raised muscle-mitochondrial ATP production 36% and the ATP/H2O2 ratio 36% with fat substrate vs a mixed diet, and reduced insulin resistance and visceral fat.

pmid:12081817.authors: Musa-Veloso K, Likhodii SS, Cunnane SC
pmid:12081817.title: Breath acetone is a reliable indicator of ketosis in adults consuming ketogenic meals.
pmid:12081817.finding: Over 12 h of ketogenic meals, breath acetone predicted plasma BHB as well as urinary acetoacetate did (R2 = 0.54 each) and predicted plasma acetoacetate best (R2 = 0.70).

pmid:31599919.authors: Myette-Côté É, Caldwell HG, Ainslie PN, et al.
pmid:31599919.title: A ketone monoester drink reduces the glycemic response to an oral glucose challenge in individuals with obesity: a randomized trial.
pmid:31599919.finding: A ketone monoester (0.45 mL/kg; BHB ~3.4 mmol/L) 30 min before a 75-g glucose load cut glucose AUC 11% without raising insulin.

pmid:33321705.authors: Napolitano A, Longo D, Lucignani M, et al.
pmid:33321705.title: The Ketogenic Diet Increases In Vivo Glutathione Levels in Patients with Epilepsy.
pmid:33321705.finding: MR spectroscopy found higher brain glutathione in children with epilepsy on a ketogenic diet (2.5 vs 2.0 mmol/L) than in controls.

pmid:17663642.authors: Nazarewicz RR, Ziolkowski W, Vaccaro PS, et al.
pmid:17663642.title: Effect of short-term ketogenic diet on redox status of human blood.
pmid:17663642.finding: Two weeks of a calorie-restricted 13%-carbohydrate diet raised plasma total antioxidant status, uric acid and RBC sulfhydryls without changing RBC malondialdehyde, SOD or catalase.

pmid:18456557.authors: Neal EG, Chaffe H, Schwartz RH, et al.
pmid:18456557.title: The ketogenic diet for the treatment of childhood epilepsy: a randomised controlled trial.
pmid:18456557.finding: After 3 months, seizures were 62% of baseline on the ketogenic diet vs 137% in controls; 38% vs 6% had > 50% seizure reduction.

pmid:37814952.authors: Needham N, Campbell IH, Grossi H, et al.
pmid:37814952.title: Pilot study of a ketogenic diet in bipolar disorder.
pmid:37814952.finding: Pilot ketogenic diet was feasible (mean BHB 1.3 mmol/L); the one serious adverse event was euglycaemic ketoacidosis in a participant taking an SGLT2 inhibitor.

pmid:30912285.authors: Neudorf H, Durrer C, Myette-Cote E, et al.
pmid:30912285.title: Oral Ketone Supplementation Acutely Increases Markers of NLRP3 Inflammasome Activation in Human Monocytes.
pmid:30912285.n: 2 crossover experiments in healthy adults (10 men in study 1)
pmid:30912285.finding: Raising blood BHB acutely with ketone salts or a ketone monoester increased caspase-1 activation (and IL-1beta in one study) in stimulated human blood, the opposite of the cell-culture prediction.

pmid:25193333.title: β-hydroxybutyrate: much more than a metabolite.
pmid:25193333.finding: BHB reaches 1-2 mmol/L after 2 days of fasting and over 2 mmol/L on a near carbohydrate-free ketogenic diet; it inhibits class I HDACs in vitro with an IC50 of 2-5 mmol/L.

pmid:26078479.authors: Peters AL, Buschur EO, Buse JB, et al.
pmid:26078479.title: Euglycemic Diabetic Ketoacidosis: A Potential Complication of Treatment With Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibition.
pmid:26078479.finding: Case series describing SGLT2-inhibitor-associated euglycaemic DKA, whose near-normal glucose delayed diagnosis.

pmid:33622392.authors: Phillips MCL, Deprez LM, Mortimer GMN, et al.
pmid:33622392.title: Randomized crossover trial of a modified ketogenic diet in Alzheimer's disease.
pmid:33622392.finding: A 12-week modified ketogenic diet (mean BHB 0.95 mmol/L) improved daily function (+3.1 ADCS-ADL) and quality of life vs a low-fat diet; cognition change was not significant.

pmid:31039280.authors: Poffé C, Ramaekers M, Van Thienen R, et al.
pmid:31039280.title: Ketone ester supplementation blunts overreaching symptoms during endurance training overload.
pmid:31039280.finding: Ketone ester after each session during 3 weeks of training overload blunted overreaching markers and raised sustainable training load and late-session power by 15%.

pmid:28178565.title: Multi-dimensional Roles of Ketone Bodies in Fuel Metabolism, Signaling, and Therapeutics.
pmid:28178565.finding: Circulating ketones are ~100-250 umol/L fed, ~1 mmol/L after a 24-h fast or prolonged exercise and up to ~20 mmol/L in DKA; the liver can make up to ~300 g/day; BHB activates HCAR2 (GPR109A) with an EC50 of ~0.77 mmol/L.

pmid:30408717.authors: Retterstøl K, Svendsen M, Narverud I, et al.
pmid:30408717.title: Effect of low carbohydrate high fat diet on LDL cholesterol and gene expression in normal-weight, young adults: A randomized controlled study.
pmid:30408717.finding: Three weeks of < 20 g/day carbohydrate raised LDL-C 44% vs controls (individual range +5% to +107%) and raised apoB.

pmid:25610820.authors: Rhyu HS, Cho SY, Roh HT
pmid:25610820.title: The effects of ketogenic diet on oxidative stress and antioxidative capacity markers of Taekwondo athletes.
pmid:25610820.finding: During 3 weeks of weight cutting, the non-ketogenic group's malondialdehyde rose while the ketogenic group's did not; ROS and SOD did not differ.

pmid:39683396.authors: Rondanelli M, Gasparri C, Pirola M, et al.
pmid:39683396.title: Does the Ketogenic Diet Mediate Inflammation Markers in Obese and Overweight Adults? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
pmid:39683396.finding: In overweight/obese adults ketogenic diets lowered CRP (mean -0.62 mg/dL) with a non-significant fall in IL-6 (-1.31 pg/mL).

pmid:7768357.authors: Sato K, Kashiwaya Y, Keon CA, et al.
pmid:7768357.title: Insulin, ketone bodies, and mitochondrial energy transduction.
pmid:7768357.finding: In working rat hearts, adding ketones to glucose raised hydraulic efficiency by 25% (36% with insulin) by reducing the NAD couple and oxidising the coenzyme Q couple.

pmid:31961383.authors: Shan Z, Guo Y, Hu FB, et al.
pmid:31961383.title: Association of Low-Carbohydrate and Low-Fat Diets With Mortality Among US Adults.
pmid:31961383.finding: An 'unhealthy' low-carbohydrate pattern was linked to higher mortality (HR 1.07 per 20 percentiles) and a 'healthy' plant-and-unsaturated-fat low-carbohydrate pattern to lower mortality (HR 0.91).

pmid:23223453.authors: Shimazu T, Hirschey MD, Newman J, et al.
pmid:23223453.title: Suppression of oxidative stress by β-hydroxybutyrate, an endogenous histone deacetylase inhibitor.
pmid:23223453.finding: BHB inhibited class I HDACs in cells and mice; a 24-h BHB infusion (blood ~1.2 mmol/L) raised kidney FOXO3A, MnSOD and catalase and roughly halved paraquat-induced protein carbonylation and lipid peroxidation in mice.

pmid:31655093.authors: Soto-Mota A, Vansant H, Evans RD, et al.
pmid:31655093.title: Safety and tolerability of sustained exogenous ketosis using ketone monoester drinks for 28 days in healthy adults.
pmid:31655093.finding: 25 mL (26.8 g) ketone monoester three times daily for 28 days raised BHB to ~4.1 mmol/L after each drink with no change in weight, glucose, lipids, electrolytes or kidney function; nausea after 6 of 2016 drinks.

pmid:38237807.authors: Soto-Mota A, Flores-Jurado Y, Norwitz NG, et al.
pmid:38237807.title: Increased low-density lipoprotein cholesterol on a low-carbohydrate diet in adults with normal but not high body weight: A meta-analysis.
pmid:38237807.finding: On low-carbohydrate diets LDL-C rose 41 mg/dL in trials with mean BMI < 25, did not change at BMI 25-35 and fell 7 mg/dL at BMI >= 35; baseline BMI, not saturated fat, explained the variation.

pmid:42206798.authors: Soto-Mota A, Norwitz NG, Manubolu VS, et al.
pmid:42206798.title: Longitudinal Data from the KETO-CTA Study: Plaque Predicts Plaque, ApoB Does Not: JACC Adv. 2025;4(7):101686.
pmid:42206798.finding: Retraction notice: the 2025 KETO-CTA longitudinal paper claiming plaque progression was unrelated to apoB was retracted at the authors' and editors' request because of methodological errors affecting data reliability.

pmid:29163194.authors: Stubbs BJ, Cox PJ, Evans RD, et al.
pmid:29163194.title: On the Metabolism of Exogenous Ketones in Humans.
pmid:29163194.finding: Drinks delivering ~12-24 g BHB raised D-BHB to 2.8 mmol/L with ketone ester vs 1.0 mmol/L with ketone salts (salts were 50% L-isomer); a meal cut the peak by a third; all drinks lowered glucose.

pmid:15929991.authors: Taggart AK, Kero J, Gan X, et al.
pmid:15929991.title: (D)-beta-Hydroxybutyrate inhibits adipocyte lipolysis via the nicotinic acid receptor PUMA-G.
pmid:15929991.finding: D-BHB activates the niacin receptor PUMA-G/HM74a (HCAR2) at fasting concentrations and inhibits adipocyte lipolysis through it.

pmid:39052901.authors: Umpierrez GE, Davis GM, ElSayed NA, et al.
pmid:39052901.title: Hyperglycemic Crises in Adults With Diabetes: A Consensus Report.
pmid:39052901.finding: ADA/EASD consensus: DKA requires BHB >= 3.0 mmol/L plus acidosis (venous pH < 7.35 and bicarbonate < 18 mmol/L) and glucose >= 200 mg/dL or known diabetes; ~10% present euglycaemic, and very-low-carbohydrate diets are a risk factor for DKA on SGLT2 inhibitors.

pmid:27822291.title: Monitoring for compliance with a ketogenic diet: what is the best time of day to test for urinary ketosis?
pmid:27822291.finding: In stable ketosis (6% energy from carbohydrate), blood BHB varied over the day from 0.33 mmol/L (10:00) to 0.70 mmol/L (03:00); urine ketones were most reliably detected early morning and after dinner.

pmid:32045881.authors: Valenzuela PL, Morales JS, Castillo-García A, et al.
pmid:32045881.title: Acute Ketone Supplementation and Exercise Performance: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
pmid:32045881.finding: Acute ketone supplements (esters or salts) had no effect on exercise performance (Hedges g = -0.05) from sprints to ~50-min events.

pmid:29955698.authors: Vandenberghe C, St-Pierre V, Pierotti T, et al.
pmid:29955698.title: Tricaprylin Alone Increases Plasma Ketone Response More Than Coconut Oil or Other Medium-Chain Triglycerides: An Acute Crossover Study in Healthy Adults.
pmid:29955698.finding: Pure C8 (tricaprylin, 2 x 20 mL) was the most ketogenic oil, raising day-long plasma ketones by ~0.3 mmol/L; coconut oil gave only ~25% of the C8 peak.

pmid:36231929.authors: Vargas-Molina S, Gómez-Urquiza JL, García-Romero J, et al.
pmid:36231929.title: Effects of the Ketogenic Diet on Muscle Hypertrophy in Resistance-Trained Men and Women: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
pmid:36231929.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
pmid:36231929.finding: Ketogenic diets without planned energy restriction did not differ from control diets for fat-free mass gain with resistance training.

pmid:14769489.title: The therapeutic implications of ketone bodies: the effects of ketone bodies in pathological conditions: ketosis, ketogenic diet, redox states, insulin resistance, and mitochondrial metabolism.
pmid:14769489.finding: Argues that D-BHB carries more energy than pyruvate (raising the free energy of ATP hydrolysis) so mild ketosis may help insulin-resistant, free-radical and hypoxic conditions, but notes that ketogenic diets also raise free fatty acids, which may reduce efficiency via PPAR-driven uncoupling proteins.

pmid:25275931.authors: Volek JS, Noakes T, Phinney SD
pmid:25275931.title: Rethinking fat as a fuel for endurance exercise.
pmid:25275931.finding: Defines nutritional ketosis as circulating ketones > 0.5 mmol/L reached by restricting carbohydrate for several weeks ('keto-adaptation'); argues it may benefit some athletes (hypothesis-generating review).

pmid:33367782.authors: Walsh JJ, Neudorf H, Little JP
pmid:33367782.title: 14-Day Ketone Supplementation Lowers Glucose and Improves Vascular Function in Obesity: A Randomized Crossover Trial.
pmid:33367782.finding: A ketone monoester (12 g BHB) before each meal for 14 days lowered 24-h glucose 7.8%, raised flow-mediated dilation from 6.2% to 8.9% and lowered stimulated monocyte caspase-1 activation, with no change in plasma cytokines.

pmid:25686106.authors: Youm YH, Nguyen KY, Grant RW, et al.
pmid:25686106.title: The ketone metabolite β-hydroxybutyrate blocks NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated inflammatory disease.
pmid:25686106.finding: BHB (not acetoacetate) blocked NLRP3 inflammasome activation by preventing K+ efflux and ASC oligomerisation in mouse cells and human monocytes in vitro, and BHB or a ketogenic diet reduced IL-1beta in mouse disease models.

pmid:33512717.authors: Allaf M, Elghazaly H, Mohamed OG, et al.
pmid:33512717.title: Intermittent fasting for the prevention of cardiovascular disease.
pmid:33512717.finding: Cochrane: IF beat ad libitum eating for short-term weight (-2.88 kg) but showed no clinically meaningful difference from continuous energy restriction (-0.88 kg short term, -0.56 kg medium term); no hard CVD outcome data.

pmid:29086496.authors: Anton SD, Moehl K, Donahoo WT, et al.
pmid:29086496.title: Flipping the Metabolic Switch: Understanding and Applying the Health Benefits of Fasting.
pmid:29086496.finding: Defines the 'metabolic switch' from glucose to fatty acids/ketones as typically occurring 12-36 h after the last meal, depending on liver glycogen and activity.

pmid:26094889.authors: Brandhorst S, Choi IY, Wei M, et al.
pmid:26094889.title: A Periodic Diet that Mimics Fasting Promotes Multi-System Regeneration, Enhanced Cognitive Performance, and Healthspan.
pmid:26094889.finding: Bimonthly 4-day FMD cycles in mice extended lifespan, cut visceral fat and cancer incidence and lowered IGF-1; a pilot trial of 3 cycles reduced human risk markers.

pmid:38378685.authors: Brandhorst S, Levine ME, Wei M, et al.
pmid:38378685.title: Fasting-mimicking diet causes hepatic and blood markers changes indicating reduced biological age and disease risk.
pmid:38378685.finding: Exploratory analysis: 3 FMD cycles were associated with lower insulin resistance and liver fat and a 2.5-year drop in a blood-chemistry biological age estimate.

pmid:30646030.authors: Carter S, Clifton PM, Keogh JB
pmid:30646030.title: Effect of Intermittent Compared With Continuous Energy Restricted Diet on Glycemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Randomized Noninferiority Trial.
pmid:30646030.finding: Over 12 months, 2 days/week of 500-600 kcal was equivalent to continuous 1200-1500 kcal/day for HbA1c (-0.3% vs -0.5%), with medication reduction to manage hypoglycaemia.

pmid:40849219.authors: Chen M, Xu L, Van Horn L, et al.
pmid:40849219.title: Association of eating duration less than 8 h with all-cause, cardiovascular, and cancer mortality.
pmid:40849219.finding: Eating duration <8 h on two 24-h recalls (~2% of participants, more often smokers, food-insecure and breakfast-skippers) was associated with higher cardiovascular mortality (HR 2.35, 1.39-3.98) vs 12-14 h but not robustly with all-cause or cancer mortality; requiring <8 h on both days gave HR 1.78 (NS).

pmid:32673591.authors: Cienfuegos S, Gabel K, Kalam F, et al.
pmid:32673591.title: Effects of 4- and 6-h Time-Restricted Feeding on Weight and Cardiometabolic Health: A Randomized Controlled Trial in Adults with Obesity.
pmid:32673591.finding: 8 weeks of 4-h or 6-h TRE cut intake ~550 kcal/day and weight ~3%, lowered 8-isoprostane by 34-37% vs control, did not change TNF-alpha or IL-6, and the 6-h group lost 1.5 kg lean mass.

pmid:7197688.authors: Clemmons DR, Klibanski A, Underwood LE, et al.
pmid:7197688.title: Reduction of plasma immunoreactive somatomedin C during fasting in humans.
pmid:7197688.finding: Ten days of fasting lowered plasma somatomedin C (IGF-1) from 0.83 to 0.21 U/mL, tracking nitrogen loss; it rose promptly with refeeding.

pmid:29405359.authors: Corley BT, Carroll RW, Hall RM, et al.
pmid:29405359.title: Intermittent fasting in Type 2 diabetes mellitus and the risk of hypoglycaemia: a randomized controlled trial.
pmid:29405359.finding: Two 500-600 kcal days/week roughly doubled hypoglycaemia rate in people on glucose-lowering drugs despite medication reduction (RR 2.05), whether fast days were consecutive or not.

pmid:29458369.authors: Finnell JS, Saul BC, Goldhamer AC, et al.
pmid:29458369.title: Is fasting safe? A chart review of adverse events during medically supervised, water-only fasting.
pmid:29458369.finding: Among supervised water-only fasts of >=2 days, most adverse events were mild (fatigue, insomnia, nausea, headache), 212 visits had a grade 3 event, and one grade 4 hyponatraemia occurred on day 9 in a 70-year-old.

pmid:18843793.authors: Fontana L, Weiss EP, Villareal DT, et al.
pmid:18843793.title: Long-term effects of calorie or protein restriction on serum IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 concentration in humans.
pmid:18843793.finding: Long-term severe CR without malnutrition did not lower serum IGF-1 in humans, whereas reducing protein from 1.67 to 0.95 g/kg/day for 3 weeks lowered IGF-1 from 194 to 152 ng/mL.

pmid:38931204.authors: Grundler F, Mesnage R, Ruppert PMM, et al.
pmid:38931204.title: Long-Term Fasting-Induced Ketosis in 1610 Subjects: Metabolic Regulation and Safety.
pmid:38931204.finding: In 4-21-day Buchinger fasts (~75-250 kcal/day) ketonuria was present in >95% from day 4; ketosis stayed far below ketoacidosis, and uric acid rose by ~100-200 umol/L, more with stronger ketosis.

pmid:16051710.authors: Halberg N, Henriksen M, Söderhamn N, et al.
pmid:16051710.title: Effect of intermittent fasting and refeeding on insulin action in healthy men.
pmid:16051710.finding: Beta-hydroxybutyrate was 0.06 mmol/L after an overnight fast and only 0.10 mmol/L after 20 h; 15 days of every-other-day 20-h fasts without weight loss improved insulin-mediated glucose uptake.

pmid:1548337.authors: Hartman ML, Veldhuis JD, Johnson ML, et al.
pmid:1548337.title: Augmented growth hormone (GH) secretory burst frequency and amplitude mediate enhanced GH secretion during a two-day fast in normal men.
pmid:1548337.finding: Two days of fasting produced a ~5-fold increase in 24-h endogenous growth hormone production via more and larger secretory bursts.

pmid:20921964.authors: Harvie MN, Pegington M, Mattson MP, et al.
pmid:20921964.title: The effects of intermittent or continuous energy restriction on weight loss and metabolic disease risk markers: a randomized trial in young overweight women.
pmid:20921964.finding: Over 6 months, 2 days/week of ~650 kcal (5:2-type) and continuous 25% restriction lost similar weight (-6.4 vs -5.6 kg) with slightly greater falls in fasting insulin and HOMA-IR with intermittent restriction.

pmid:31151228.authors: Jamshed H, Beyl RA, Della Manna DL, et al.
pmid:31151228.title: Early Time-Restricted Feeding Improves 24-Hour Glucose Levels and Affects Markers of the Circadian Clock, Aging, and Autophagy in Humans.
pmid:31151228.finding: Four days of eating 8 am-2 pm vs 8 am-8 pm lowered 24-h glucose, raised morning beta-hydroxybutyrate to ~0.15 mmol/L, and increased whole-blood expression of SIRT1 and the autophagy gene LC3A.

pmid:35939311.authors: Jamshed H, Steger FL, Bryan DR, et al.
pmid:35939311.title: Effectiveness of Early Time-Restricted Eating for Weight Loss, Fat Loss, and Cardiometabolic Health in Adults With Obesity: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
pmid:35939311.finding: With matched weight-loss counselling, 8-h early TRE (7:00-15:00) lost 2.3 kg more than a >=12-h window over 14 weeks, equivalent to ~214 kcal/day extra restriction; body fat difference NS.

pmid:32729615.authors: Jones R, Pabla P, Mallinson J, et al.
pmid:32729615.title: Two weeks of early time-restricted feeding (eTRF) improves skeletal muscle insulin and anabolic sensitivity in healthy men.
pmid:32729615.finding: 2 weeks of early TRF (08:00-16:00) improved whole-body insulin sensitivity and muscle glucose and BCAA uptake vs a control diet matched for the same ~400 kcal/day deficit and ~1 kg weight loss.

pmid:6758355.authors: Kerndt PR, Naughton JL, Driscoll CE, et al.
pmid:6758355.title: Fasting: the history, pathophysiology and complications.
pmid:6758355.finding: Weight loss averages ~0.9 kg/day in the first week of fasting (largely sodium and water) and ~0.3 kg/day by week 3; insulin and T3 fall, glucagon rises; complications include gout, urate stones, postural hypotension and arrhythmias.

pmid:31303390.authors: Kraus WE, Bhapkar M, Huffman KM, et al.
pmid:31303390.title: 2 years of calorie restriction and cardiometabolic risk (CALERIE): exploratory outcomes of a multicentre, phase 2, randomised controlled trial.
pmid:31303390.finding: CALERIE: achieved 11.9% CR for 2 years (-7.5 kg, 71% fat) lowered LDL, total/HDL ratio, blood pressure, CRP and insulin resistance vs control.

pmid:34668663.authors: Laurens C, Grundler F, Damiot A, et al.
pmid:34668663.title: Is muscle and protein loss relevant in long-term fasting in healthy men? A prospective trial on physiological adaptations.
pmid:34668663.finding: A 10-day fast (200-250 kcal/day) cut weight 5.9 kg, ~60% lean soft tissue (mostly water and glycogen; 42% metabolically active tissue), lowered BMR 12%, and preserved strength; urinary BHB plateaued from day 4.

pmid:37364268.authors: Lin S, Cienfuegos S, Ezpeleta M, et al.
pmid:37364268.title: Time-Restricted Eating Without Calorie Counting for Weight Loss in a Racially Diverse Population : A Randomized Controlled Trial.
pmid:37364268.finding: Over 12 months, 8-h TRE (noon-8 pm) and 25% CR reduced intake similarly (~-425 vs -405 kcal/day) and weight similarly (-4.6 vs -5.4 kg vs control; difference NS).

pmid:35443107.authors: Liu D, Huang Y, Huang C, et al.
pmid:35443107.title: Calorie Restriction with or without Time-Restricted Eating in Weight Loss.
pmid:35443107.finding: With identical calorie targets for 12 months, 8-h TRE (8 am-4 pm) plus CR lost 8.0 kg vs 6.3 kg with CR alone (difference -1.8 kg, P = 0.11); no differences in fat, lean mass or metabolic risk factors.

pmid:32986097.authors: Lowe DA, Wu N, Rohdin-Bibby L, et al.
pmid:32986097.title: Effects of Time-Restricted Eating on Weight Loss and Other Metabolic Parameters in Women and Men With Overweight and Obesity: The TREAT Randomized Clinical Trial.
pmid:32986097.finding: 12 weeks of 16:8 TRE (noon-8 pm) did not beat 3 structured meals (between-group -0.26 kg, NS) and reduced appendicular lean mass index more (-0.16 kg/m2).

pmid:39348690.authors: Manoogian ENC, Wilkinson MJ, O'Neal M, et al.
pmid:39348690.title: Time-Restricted Eating in Adults With Metabolic Syndrome : A Randomized Controlled Trial.
pmid:39348690.finding: Adding personalised 8-10-h TRE to standard care for 3 months lowered HbA1c by only 0.10% vs standard care alone.

pmid:18583681.authors: Mehanna HM, Moledina J, Travis J
pmid:18583681.title: Refeeding syndrome: what it is, and how to prevent and treat it.
pmid:18583681.finding: NICE-based refeeding risk criteria include little or no intake for >10 days (one criterion alone) or >5 days (with another factor), plus low potassium, phosphate or magnesium before feeding.

pmid:29455546.authors: Mojto V, Gvozdjakova A, Kucharska J, et al.
pmid:29455546.title: Effects of complete water fasting and regeneration diet on kidney function, oxidative stress and antioxidants.
pmid:29455546.finding: An 11-day water-only fast lowered TBARS, weight and blood pressure but raised uric acid and creatinine, lowered GFR and alpha-tocopherol; values normalised after refeeding.

pmid:27737674.authors: Moro T, Tinsley G, Bianco A, et al.
pmid:27737674.title: Effects of eight weeks of time-restricted feeding (16/8) on basal metabolism, maximal strength, body composition, inflammation, and cardiovascular risk factors in resistance-trained males.
pmid:27737674.finding: 8 weeks of isocaloric 16:8 TRE with resistance training reduced fat mass, preserved lean mass and strength, but lowered testosterone, IGF-1 and T3.

pmid:5773093.authors: Owen OE, Felig P, Morgan AP, et al.
pmid:5773093.title: Liver and kidney metabolism during prolonged starvation.
pmid:5773093.finding: During prolonged starvation glucose and insulin fell over the first 3 days, while free fatty acids, beta-hydroxybutyrate and acetoacetate did not plateau until after ~17 days.

pmid:11043913.authors: Pan JW, Rothman TL, Behar KL, et al.
pmid:11043913.title: Human brain beta-hydroxybutyrate and lactate increase in fasting-induced ketosis.
pmid:11043913.finding: Brain beta-hydroxybutyrate rose from 0.05 to 0.60 mmol/L after 2 days and 0.98 mmol/L after 3 days of fasting; brain levels were about a quarter of plasma (slope 0.26).

pmid:34919135.authors: Patikorn C, Roubal K, Veettil SK, et al.
pmid:34919135.title: Intermittent Fasting and Obesity-Related Health Outcomes: An Umbrella Review of Meta-analyses of Randomized Clinical Trials.
pmid:34919135.finding: Umbrella review: most IF benefits were supported by low or very-low quality evidence; only modified ADF for BMI reached high quality, and IF was associated with reduced fat-free mass.

pmid:41160666.authors: Peters B, Schwarz J, Schuppelius B, et al.
pmid:41160666.title: Intended isocaloric time-restricted eating shifts circadian clocks but does not improve cardiometabolic health in women with overweight.
pmid:41160666.finding: In an intended-isocaloric crossover, 2 weeks of early (8:00-16:00) or late (13:00-21:00) 8-h TRE did not improve insulin sensitivity, 24-h glucose, lipids, inflammatory or oxidative stress markers, though it shifted circadian phase.

pmid:38429390.authors: Pietzner M, Uluvar B, Kolnes KJ, et al.
pmid:38429390.title: Systemic proteome adaptions to 7-day complete caloric restriction in humans.
pmid:38429390.finding: A 7-day water-only fast (mean -5.7 kg) produced >1,000 changing plasma proteins, but systemic proteome changes appeared only after ~3 days of fasting.

pmid:31339000.authors: Ravussin E, Beyl RA, Poggiogalle E, et al.
pmid:31339000.title: Early Time-Restricted Feeding Reduces Appetite and Increases Fat Oxidation But Does Not Affect Energy Expenditure in Humans.
pmid:31339000.finding: Isocaloric eating 8 am-2 pm vs 8 am-8 pm for 4 days did not change 24-h energy expenditure but lowered ghrelin and hunger and increased fat oxidation.

pmid:29576535.authors: Redman LM, Smith SR, Burton JH, et al.
pmid:29576535.title: Metabolic Slowing and Reduced Oxidative Damage with Sustained Caloric Restriction Support the Rate of Living and Oxidative Damage Theories of Aging.
pmid:29576535.finding: ~15% CR sustained for 2 years (-8.7 kg) lowered 24-h energy expenditure 80-120 kcal/day beyond weight loss, reduced thyroid axis activity and lowered F2-isoprostane excretion.

pmid:40533200.authors: Semnani-Azad Z, Khan TA, Chiavaroli L, et al.
pmid:40533200.title: Intermittent fasting strategies and their effects on body weight and other cardiometabolic risk factors: systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised clinical trials.
pmid:40533200.finding: Network meta-analysis: all IF forms and continuous restriction beat ad libitum eating; vs continuous restriction only ADF showed a small extra weight loss (-1.29 kg, moderate certainty).

pmid:31471173.authors: Stekovic S, Hofer SJ, Tripolt N, et al.
pmid:31471173.title: Alternate Day Fasting Improves Physiological and Molecular Markers of Aging in Healthy, Non-obese Humans.
pmid:31471173.finding: 4 weeks of strict 36-h/12-h alternate-day fasting cut intake 37%, reduced trunk fat, raised beta-hydroxybutyrate even on eating days, and lowered sICAM-1, LDL and T3 after long-term ADF, without adverse events.

pmid:29778565.authors: Sundfør TM, Svendsen M, Tonstad S
pmid:29778565.title: Effect of intermittent versus continuous energy restriction on weight loss, maintenance and cardiometabolic risk: A randomized 1-year trial.
pmid:29778565.finding: Over 1 year, 400/600 kcal on 2 non-consecutive days/week matched continuous restriction for weight loss (-8.0 vs -9.0 kg) and maintenance, with more hunger.

pmid:34135111.authors: Templeman I, Smith HA, Chowdhury E, et al.
pmid:34135111.title: A randomized controlled trial to isolate the effects of fasting and energy restriction on weight loss and metabolic health in lean adults.
pmid:34135111.finding: 3 weeks of 24-h alternate-day fasts with 150% intake on feed days lost similar weight to matched daily 25% CR but less fat (-0.74 vs -1.75 kg); fasting without energy deficit changed nothing; no fasting-specific metabolic benefit.

pmid:31268131.authors: Tinsley GM, Moore ML, Graybeal AJ, et al.
pmid:31268131.title: Time-restricted feeding plus resistance training in active females: a randomized trial.
pmid:31268131.finding: 8 weeks of ~7.5-h TRE with resistance training and adequate protein (1.6 g/kg) produced the same lean-mass and strength gains as a normal schedule.

pmid:28459931.authors: Trepanowski JF, Kroeger CM, Barnosky A, et al.
pmid:28459931.title: Effect of Alternate-Day Fasting on Weight Loss, Weight Maintenance, and Cardioprotection Among Metabolically Healthy Obese Adults: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
pmid:28459931.finding: Over 1 year, alternate-day fasting (25%/125% days) and daily 25% CR produced the same weight loss (-6.0% vs -5.3% vs control) and cardiometabolic changes; ADF had more dropouts (38%).

pmid:25020061.authors: Vendelbo MH, Møller AB, Christensen B, et al.
pmid:25020061.title: Fasting increases human skeletal muscle net phenylalanine release and this is associated with decreased mTOR signaling.
pmid:25020061.finding: A 72-h fast halved muscle mTOR phosphorylation and raised LC3B-II ~30%, but p62 also rose ~10%, so autophagic flux could not be confirmed; net muscle protein release increased.

pmid:26332798.authors: Villareal DT, Fontana L, Das SK, et al.
pmid:26332798.title: Effect of Two-Year Caloric Restriction on Bone Metabolism and Bone Mineral Density in Non-Obese Younger Adults: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
pmid:26332798.finding: 2 years of CR (-7.5 kg, including -2.2 kg fat-free mass) reduced lumbar spine, hip and femoral neck BMD vs ad libitum and raised bone resorption markers.

pmid:37118425.authors: Waziry R, Ryan CP, Corcoran DL, et al.
pmid:37118425.title: Effect of long-term caloric restriction on DNA methylation measures of biological aging in healthy adults from the CALERIE trial.
pmid:37118425.finding: Post hoc CALERIE analysis: 2 years of CR slowed the DunedinPACE pace-of-aging methylation measure (small effect) but did not change PhenoAge or GrimAge clocks.

pmid:25546413.authors: Wegman MP, Guo MH, Bennion DM, et al.
pmid:25546413.title: Practicality of intermittent fasting in humans and its effect on oxidative stress and genes related to aging and metabolism.
pmid:25546413.finding: Weight-stable alternate-day fasting (25%/175% days) for 3 weeks, with or without vitamins C and E, did not change oxidative stress markers; SIRT3 expression rose 2.7% and insulin fell slightly.

pmid:28202779.authors: Wei M, Brandhorst S, Shelehchi M, et al.
pmid:28202779.title: Fasting-mimicking diet and markers/risk factors for aging, diabetes, cancer, and cardiovascular disease.
pmid:28202779.finding: Three monthly 5-day fasting-mimicking diet cycles lowered body weight, trunk fat, blood pressure and IGF-1 vs usual diet, with larger changes in people at higher baseline risk.

pmid:30601864.authors: Wilhelmi de Toledo F, Grundler F, Bergouignan A, et al.
pmid:30601864.title: Safety, health improvement and well-being during a 4 to 21-day fasting period in an observational study including 1422 subjects.
pmid:30601864.finding: Buchinger fasts of 4-21 days at 200-250 kcal/day lowered weight, waist and blood pressure, raised ketones and were well tolerated, with adverse effects in <1% (uncontrolled, clinic-affiliated authors).

pmid:32517172.authors: Wilhelmi de Toledo F, Grundler F, Goutzourelas N, et al.
