pmid:38745431.finding: Pyrolysis-GC/MS reported microplastics in every testis (mean 328 ug/g in humans, 123 ug/g in dogs), mostly polyethylene; in dogs PVC and PET levels correlated with lower normalized testis weight.

pmid:39432568.authors: Hu CJ, Garcia MA, Nihart A, et al.
pmid:39432568.title: Response to comment on: "Microplastic presence in dog and human testis and its potential association with sperm count and weights of testis and epididymis".
pmid:39432568.finding: Authors' reply: controls were described in their placenta paper; after re-evaluation only 6 of the 12 polymers (PE, PP, PVC, nylon, SBR, PET) give enough confidence for health-based work.

pmid:37343248.authors: Hussain KA, Romanova S, Okur I, et al.
pmid:37343248.title: Assessing the Release of Microplastics and Nanoplastics from Plastic Containers and Reusable Food Pouches: Implications for Human Health.
pmid:37343248.finding: Microwaving polypropylene containers and polyethylene pouches released the most particles (up to 4.2 million micro- and 2.1 billion nanoplastics per cm2 in 3 min); months of fridge or room storage also released particles.

pmid:40801989.authors: Hussey MR, Kornberg TG, Sherrick JM, et al.
pmid:40801989.title: The relationship between PFAS exposure and dyslipidemia: an updated review, meta-analysis, and evaluation of bias.
pmid:40801989.finding: Pooled cross-sectional data link PFOA and PFOS to higher total and LDL cholesterol, but longitudinal estimates trended to null and heterogeneity tracked confounding and recruitment from contaminated areas.

pmid:38718364.authors: Kalkman DN, Renkens MPL, Grundeken MJ
pmid:38718364.title: Microplastics and Nanoplastics in Atheromas.
pmid:38718364.finding: Letter to the editor responding to Marfella 2024 (NEJM correspondence on microplastics in atheromas).

pmid:42503274.authors: Lane T, de Ruijter VN, Wardani I, et al.
pmid:42503274.title: A QA/QC screening framework to assess studies reporting microplastic presence in human organs, tissues, and bodily fluids.
pmid:42503274.finding: A 14-criterion QA/QC screen of human-tissue microplastic studies found none met all essential criteria; blank documentation, positive controls and sample representativeness were common gaps.

pmid:35367073.authors: Leslie HA, van Velzen MJM, Brandsma SH, et al.
pmid:35367073.title: Discovery and quantification of plastic particle pollution in human blood.
pmid:35367073.finding: Double-shot Py-GC/MS quantified plastic particles >=700 nm in whole blood (mean of quantifiable sum 1.6 ug/mL), mainly PET, polyethylene and styrene polymers.

pmid:29133598.authors: Li Y, Fletcher T, Mucs D, et al.
pmid:29133598.title: Half-lives of PFOS, PFHxS and PFOA after end of exposure to contaminated drinking water.
pmid:29133598.finding: After contaminated water was replaced, serum PFHxS, PFOS and PFOA fell 13%, 20% and 26% per year (half-lives 5.3, 3.4 and 2.7 years), faster in women.

pmid:37128027.authors: Li D, Shi Y, Yang L, et al.
pmid:37128027.title: Microplastic release from the degradation of polypropylene feeding bottles during infant formula preparation.
pmid:37128027.finding: Polypropylene infant feeding bottles released up to 16 million microplastic particles per litre during formula preparation, more with sterilization and hot water.

pmid:31884197.authors: Lin CY, Lee HL, Hwang YT, et al.
pmid:31884197.title: The association between total serum isomers of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, lipid profiles, and the DNA oxidative/nitrative stress biomarkers in middle-aged Taiwanese adults.
pmid:31884197.finding: Linear PFOS was associated with higher urinary 8-OHdG and 8-nitroguanine and with LDL cholesterol.

pmid:38668517.authors: Lü L, Liu Y, Yang Y, et al.
pmid:38668517.title: Bisphenol A Exposure Interferes with Reproductive Hormones and Decreases Sperm Counts: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Epidemiological Studies.
pmid:38668517.finding: Urinary BPA was associated with slightly lower sperm concentration and total count and with higher SHBG and estradiol, but not robustly with below-reference semen quality.

pmid:40854835.authors: Lucas A, Harray A, Duong L, et al.
pmid:40854835.title: Randomised controlled trial of a low plastic diet and lifestyle intervention for adults with cardiometabolic risk factors: the Plastic Exposure Reduction Transforms Health (PERTH) trial - a protocol.
pmid:40854835.finding: Protocol of the PERTH RCT testing whether a 4-week low-plastic diet and lifestyle intervention lowers urinary bisphenols and phthalates and improves cardiometabolic markers.

pmid:39393709.authors: MacKeown H, Magi E, Di Carro M, et al.
pmid:39393709.title: Removal of perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances from tap water by means of point-of-use treatment: A review.
pmid:39393709.finding: Point-of-use filters (activated carbon, ion exchange, reverse osmosis) can remove PFAS, but only five real-life studies exist, short-chain PFAS are harder to remove and poorly maintained carbon can raise PFAS in water.

pmid:38446676.authors: Marfella R, Prattichizzo F, Sardu C, et al.
pmid:38446676.title: Microplastics and Nanoplastics in Atheromas and Cardiovascular Events.
pmid:38446676.finding: Polyethylene was detected in 58% of excised carotid plaques (PVC in 12%); patients with detectable plastic had a higher risk of heart attack, stroke or death (HR 4.53, 95% CI 2.00-10.27).

pmid:38718368.title: Microplastics and Nanoplastics in Atheromas. Reply.
pmid:38718368.finding: Authors' reply to the NEJM letters on microplastics in atheromas.

pmid:39436315.authors: Mhaouty-Kodja S, Zalko D, Tait S, et al.
pmid:39436315.title: A critical review to identify data gaps and improve risk assessment of bisphenol A alternatives for human health.
pmid:39436315.finding: Critical review: BPS and BPF are found worldwide in people and are being regulated because of toxicity; newer BPA alternatives have large toxicology data gaps (risk of regrettable substitution).

pmid:38367552.authors: Møller JJ, Lyngberg AC, Hammer PEC, et al.
pmid:38367552.title: Substantial decrease of PFAS with anion exchange resin treatment - A clinical cross-over trial.
pmid:38367552.finding: Cholestyramine 4 g three times daily for 12 weeks lowered serum PFOS by 60% (from a median of 191 ng/mL) and other PFAS by 15-44%, with no serious adverse events.

pmid:35939564.authors: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
pmid:35939564.title: Guidance on PFAS Exposure, Testing, and Clinical Follow-Up
pmid:35939564.finding: NASEM clinical guidance: offer PFAS blood testing to likely exposed patients; for the summed serum level of 7 PFAS, <2 ng/mL usual care, 2-20 ng/mL exposure reduction plus lipid screening, >20 ng/mL add thyroid testing and kidney/testicular cancer and ulcerative colitis assessment.

pmid:39901044.authors: Nihart AJ, Garcia MA, El Hayek E, et al.
pmid:39901044.title: Bioaccumulation of microplastics in decedent human brains.
pmid:39901044.n: decedent brain, liver and kidney samples (2016 and 2024) plus 12 dementia brains
pmid:39901044.finding: Py-GC/MS reported median ~4,900 ug/g of plastic (mostly polyethylene) in 2024 brain samples, 7-30x higher than liver or kidney, rising from 2016 to 2024, and higher still (median ~26,000 ug/g) in dementia brains.

pmid:40164728.authors: Nihart AJ, Garcia MA, El Hayek E, et al.
pmid:40164728.title: Author Correction: Bioaccumulation of microplastics in decedent human brains.
pmid:40164728.finding: Author correction to Nihart 2025: duplicated supplementary microscopy panels removed, mis-sized scale bars fixed, an omitted sample-preparation step added and a supplementary particle-count table recalculated.

pmid:31352597.authors: Peng CY, Tsai EM, Kao TH, et al.
pmid:31352597.title: Canned food intake and urinary bisphenol a concentrations: a randomized crossover intervention study.
pmid:31352597.finding: A canned-food meal raised urinary BPA by up to 206% at 4 h versus fresh food, returning to baseline by 24 h.

pmid:40940416.authors: Plachetka L, Stanislas V, Bauer A, et al.
pmid:40940416.title: Urinary bisphenol levels and blood pressure after soda consumption from cans, PET and glass bottles.
pmid:40940416.finding: Drinking soda from cans raised urinary BPA by 22% versus PET bottles; BPS, BPF and BPE were detected independent of packaging.

pmid:38190543.authors: Qian N, Gao X, Lang X, et al.
pmid:38190543.title: Rapid single-particle chemical imaging of nanoplastics by SRS microscopy.
pmid:38190543.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:38190543.finding: Stimulated Raman scattering imaging counted about 240,000 plastic particles per litre of bottled water, about 90% of them nanoplastics, orders of magnitude more than earlier microplastic-only counts.

pmid:39851066.authors: Rauert C, Charlton N, Bagley A, et al.
pmid:39851066.title: Assessing the Efficacy of Pyrolysis-Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry for Nanoplastic and Microplastic Analysis in Human Blood.
pmid:39851066.finding: Validation study concluding that Py-GC/MS is currently not suitable for polyethylene and PVC in biological matrices because of interferences, with realistic detection limits up to 20x higher than nominal and no other polymers detectable in human blood.

pmid:21450549.authors: Rudel RA, Gray JM, Engel CL, et al.
pmid:21450549.title: Food packaging and bisphenol A and bis(2-ethyhexyl) phthalate exposure: findings from a dietary intervention.
pmid:21450549.finding: Three days of fresh, unpackaged food cut urinary BPA by 66% and DEHP metabolites by 53-56% (geometric means).

pmid:23443238.authors: Sathyanarayana S, Alcedo G, Saelens BE, et al.
pmid:23443238.title: Unexpected results in a randomized dietary trial to reduce phthalate and bisphenol A exposures.
pmid:23443238.finding: A 5-day catered "low-exposure" diet unexpectedly raised urinary DEHP metabolites (median 284 to 7028 nmol/g) and BPA because ingredients such as ground coriander and milk were contaminated.

pmid:40089764.authors: Schlezinger JJ, Bello A, Mangano KM, et al.
pmid:40089764.title: Per- and poly-fluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in circulation in a Canadian population: their association with serum-liver enzyme biomarkers and piloting a novel method to reduce serum-PFAS.
pmid:40089764.finding: In a 4-week dietary fibre trial, long-chain PFAS fell significantly only in the fibre group (secondary analysis; total PFAS fell in both arms).

pmid:31476765.authors: Schwabl P, Köppel S, Königshofer P, et al.
pmid:31476765.title: Detection of Various Microplastics in Human Stool: A Prospective Case Series.
pmid:31476765.finding: All 8 stool samples contained microplastics (median 20 particles per 10 g, 50-500 um), mostly polypropylene and PET.

pmid:38768789.authors: Siwakoti RC, Park S, Ferguson KK, et al.
pmid:38768789.title: Prenatal per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and maternal oxidative stress: Evidence from the LIFECODES study.
pmid:38768789.finding: Each IQR increase in plasma PFOS was associated with 9.7% higher urinary 8-isoprostane; other PFAS showed mixed or inverse associations.

pmid:35977640.authors: Soltani NS, Taylor MP, Wilson SP
pmid:35977640.title: International quantification of microplastics in indoor dust: prevalence, exposure and risk assessment.
pmid:35977640.finding: Synthetic fibres (polyester, polyamide) were common in household dust, mainly from indoor sources; more frequent vacuuming was associated with less microplastic in dust.

pmid:39183960.authors: Symeonides C, Aromataris E, Mulders Y, et al.
pmid:39183960.title: An Umbrella Review of Meta-Analyses Evaluating Associations between Human Health and Exposure to Major Classes of Plastic-Associated Chemicals.
pmid:39183960.finding: Umbrella review: BPA linked to PCOS, type 2 diabetes and CVD; phthalates to pregnancy loss, reduced sperm quality and insulin resistance; some PFAS to lower birth weight; no meta-analyses existed for microplastics.

pmid:42463894.authors: Tefera Y, Shearer C, Day M, et al.
pmid:42463894.title: Is drinking water with low PFAS a significant source of human exposure? Evidence summary.
pmid:42463894.finding: Drinking water with low PFAS (10-100 ng/L) measurably raised blood PFAS, most consistently PFHxS, especially in children and heavy water drinkers; below ~10 ng/L links were inconsistent.

pmid:42164877.authors: Thomas KV, Belz S, Booth AM, et al.
pmid:42164877.title: Communicating Confidence in the Reliability of Micro- and Nanoplastic Identification in Human Health Studies.
pmid:42164877.finding: Proposes confidence levels for micro/nanoplastic identification in human studies, requiring orthogonal analytical techniques and transparent reporting of contamination and limits.

pmid:39475449.authors: Uppu RM, Peijnenburg W, Hays SM
pmid:39475449.title: Comment on: "Microplastic presence in dog and human testis and its potential association with sperm count and weights of testis and epididymis".
pmid:39475449.finding: Comment on Hu 2024: no reported blanks, negative/positive or background controls, unvalidated digestion and ultracentrifugation steps, and no LOD/LOQ, internal standards or matrix spikes for the Py-GC/MS method.

pmid:38592230.authors: Vom Saal FS, Antoniou M, Belcher SM, et al.
pmid:38592230.title: The Conflict between Regulatory Agencies over the 20,000-Fold Lowering of the Tolerable Daily Intake (TDI) for Bisphenol A (BPA) by the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA).
pmid:38592230.finding: Commentary endorsing EFSA's 20,000-fold BPA TDI cut and criticizing the German BfR and US FDA for maintaining higher limits based on guideline studies.

pmid:38718366.title: Microplastics and Nanoplastics in Atheromas.
pmid:38718366.finding: Letter to the editor responding to Marfella 2024 (NEJM correspondence on microplastics in atheromas).

pmid:36504299.authors: Wang H, He H, Wei Y, et al.
pmid:36504299.title: Do phthalates and their metabolites cause poor semen quality? A systematic review and meta-analysis of epidemiological studies on risk of decline in sperm quality.
pmid:36504299.finding: Urinary MBP and MBzP and semen DEHP were associated with lower sperm concentration; other phthalate metabolites and motility/morphology showed no significant association.

pmid:41005444.authors: Yuan M, Chai J, Song J, et al.
pmid:41005444.title: Association of bisphenol A exposure with in vitro fertilization outcomes: A meta-analysis and systematic review.
pmid:41005444.finding: Higher BPA exposure was associated with lower normal fertilization rates and fewer high-quality embryos in IVF/ICSI, but not with clinical pregnancy or implantation.

pmid:38592388.authors: Ahlqvist VH, Sjöqvist H, Dalman C, et al.
pmid:38592388.title: Acetaminophen Use During Pregnancy and Children's Risk of Autism, ADHD, and Intellectual Disability.
pmid:38592388.finding: Small associations of prenatal acetaminophen with autism (HR 1.05) and ADHD (HR 1.07) disappeared in sibling comparisons (HR 0.98 for both), suggesting familial confounding.

pmid:34907341.authors: Alwan S, Conover EA, Harris-Sagaribay L, et al.
pmid:34907341.title: Paracetamol use in pregnancy - caution over causal inference from available data.
pmid:34907341.finding: Letter from teratology and pharmacoepidemiology experts cautioning against causal inference from the observational acetaminophen-pregnancy data.

pmid:31855498.authors: Ambrosone CB, Zirpoli GR, Hutson AD, et al.
pmid:31855498.title: Dietary Supplement Use During Chemotherapy and Survival Outcomes of Patients With Breast Cancer Enrolled in a Cooperative Group Clinical Trial (SWOG S0221).
pmid:31855498.n: 1134 women with breast cancer in a chemotherapy trial
pmid:31855498.finding: Antioxidant supplement use before and during chemotherapy was associated with higher recurrence (adjHR 1.41, CI 0.98-2.04); B12 and iron use were significantly linked to worse outcomes.

pmid:33998174.authors: Anagnostis P, Papanikolaou D, Ioannidou PG, et al.
pmid:33998174.title: The effect of statins on semen parameters in patients with hypercholesterolemia: A systematic review.
pmid:33998174.finding: Systematic review of pravastatin and simvastatin found no consistent harmful effect on semen volume or concentration, with mixed motility and morphology findings.

pmid:35580859.authors: Andersen E, Juhl CR, Kjøller ET, et al.
pmid:35580859.title: Sperm count is increased by diet-induced weight loss and maintained by exercise or GLP-1 analogue treatment: a randomized controlled trial.
pmid:35580859.finding: An 8-week low-calorie diet (-16.5 kg) raised sperm concentration 1.49-fold and count 1.41-fold; the gain was kept at 52 weeks in men who maintained weight loss (including with liraglutide or exercise) but lost in those who regained.

pmid:9120179.authors: Ardissino D, Merlini PA, Savonitto S, et al.
pmid:9120179.title: Effect of transdermal nitroglycerin or N-acetylcysteine, or both, in the long-term treatment of unstable angina pectoris.
pmid:9120179.finding: Transdermal nitroglycerin plus oral NAC reduced outcome events (13% vs 39% placebo) but caused side effects, mainly intolerable headache, in 35%.

pmid:26900641.authors: Aroda VR, Edelstein SL, Goldberg RB, et al.
pmid:26900641.title: Long-term Metformin Use and Vitamin B12 Deficiency in the Diabetes Prevention Program Outcomes Study.
pmid:26900641.finding: Metformin 850 mg twice daily was associated with more low or borderline B12 (<=298 pg/mL: 19.1% vs 9.5% at 5 years); each year of use raised deficiency odds 13%, and neuropathy was more common in metformin users with low B12.

pmid:28865539.authors: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine. Electronic address: ASRM@asrm.org, Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
pmid:28865539.title: Role of metformin for ovulation induction in infertile patients with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS): a guideline.
pmid:28865539.finding: ASRM: metformin raises ovulation versus placebo in PCOS but should not be first-line for anovulation because clomiphene or letrozole are much more effective; no added miscarriage when stopped at conception.

pmid:15812073.authors: Bairati I, Meyer F, Gélinas M, et al.
pmid:15812073.title: A randomized trial of antioxidant vitamins to prevent second primary cancers in head and neck cancer patients.
pmid:15812073.finding: Alpha-tocopherol (with beta-carotene initially) during and after radiotherapy raised second primary cancers during supplementation (HR 2.88).

pmid:25440725.authors: Banach M, Serban C, Sahebkar A, et al.
pmid:25440725.title: Effects of coenzyme Q10 on statin-induced myopathy: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
pmid:25440725.finding: CoQ10 supplementation did not significantly reduce statin-associated muscle pain (SMD -0.53, CI -1.33 to 0.28) or CK.

pmid:25041462.authors: Bannister CA, Holden SE, Jenkins-Jones S, et al.
pmid:25041462.title: Can people with type 2 diabetes live longer than those without? A comparison of mortality in people initiated with metformin or sulphonylurea monotherapy and matched, non-diabetic controls.
pmid:25041462.n: 78,241 metformin users, 12,222 sulphonylurea users, 90,463 matched controls
pmid:25041462.finding: In UK primary-care data, people with type 2 diabetes started on metformin had 15% longer adjusted survival than matched non-diabetic controls; this finding underpins much of the anti-aging interest in metformin.

pmid:27304507.authors: Barzilai N, Crandall JP, Kritchevsky SB, et al.
pmid:27304507.title: Metformin as a Tool to Target Aging.
pmid:27304507.finding: Rationale paper for TAME (Targeting Aging with Metformin), proposing metformin as a first test of a drug targeting aging itself, based largely on observational data in diabetes.

pmid:25784688.authors: Bateman BT, Hernandez-Diaz S, Fischer MA, et al.
pmid:25784688.title: Statins and congenital malformations: cohort study.
pmid:25784688.finding: First-trimester statin use showed no teratogenic effect after adjustment for confounders such as diabetes (RR 1.07, 0.85-1.37).

pmid:41996180.authors: Batsis JA, Gavras A, Gross DC, et al.
pmid:41996180.title: Effect of Incretin-Based and Nonpharmacologic Weight Loss on Body Composition : A Systematic Review.
pmid:41996180.finding: Systematic review: loss of muscle-related indices exceeded prespecified benchmarks in about two thirds of incretin interventions and nearly half of non-drug weight-loss interventions.

pmid:34556849.authors: Bauer AZ, Swan SH, Kriebel D, et al.
pmid:34556849.title: Paracetamol use during pregnancy - a call for precautionary action.
pmid:34556849.finding: Consensus statement by 91 scientists calling for precaution: pregnant women should use acetaminophen only when indicated, at the lowest dose for the shortest time, citing neurodevelopmental and urogenital associations.

pmid:17367938.authors: Block KI, Koch AC, Mead MN, et al.
pmid:17367938.title: Impact of antioxidant supplementation on chemotherapeutic efficacy: a systematic review of the evidence from randomized controlled trials.
pmid:17367938.finding: No trial showed reduced chemotherapy efficacy with antioxidants and many reported fewer toxicities or better survival, but trials were small and underpowered.

pmid:25359661.authors: Bosman E, Esterhuizen AD, Rodrigues FA, et al.
pmid:25359661.title: Effect of metformin therapy and dietary supplements on semen parameters in hyperinsulinaemic males.
pmid:25359661.finding: Uncontrolled study: 3 months of metformin (with or without supplements) raised normal sperm forms from about 4% to 5.5% and improved chromatin packaging in hyperinsulinaemic men.

pmid:21602430.authors: Boulé NG, Robert C, Bell GJ, et al.
pmid:21602430.title: Metformin and exercise in type 2 diabetes: examining treatment modality interactions.
pmid:21602430.finding: Metformin raised exercise heart rate and lactate; adding exercise reduced metformin's lowering of the post-meal glucose response (interaction P=0.05).

pmid:23975325.authors: Boulé NG, Kenny GP, Larose J, et al.
pmid:23975325.title: Does metformin modify the effect on glycaemic control of aerobic exercise, resistance exercise or both?
pmid:23975325.finding: Over 22 weeks of aerobic, resistance or combined training, background metformin use did not significantly change the training effects on HbA1c, fitness, strength or body weight.

pmid:33830637.authors: Bray JJH, Foster-Davies H, Salem A, et al.
pmid:33830637.title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists improve biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
pmid:33830637.finding: GLP-1 receptor agonists lowered CRP (-0.54 mg/L), TNF-alpha and malondialdehyde (SMD -0.84) and raised adiponectin versus standard therapy or placebo; CRP fall tracked blood-pressure and insulin-resistance improvement.

pmid:27418629.authors: Cameron AR, Morrison VL, Levin D, et al.
pmid:27418629.title: Anti-Inflammatory Effects of Metformin Irrespective of Diabetes Status.
pmid:27418629.n: cell, cohort and a nondiabetic heart-failure RCT
pmid:27418629.finding: Metformin suppressed NF-kB-linked inflammatory signalling in cells, lowered the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio versus sulfonylurea in a diabetes cohort, and reduced plasma cytokines in nondiabetic heart failure.

pmid:34967881.authors: Chang JC, Chen YJ, Chen IC, et al.
pmid:34967881.title: Perinatal Outcomes After Statin Exposure During Pregnancy.
pmid:34967881.finding: Statin use in pregnancy was not associated with congenital anomalies but was associated with low birth weight (RR 1.51) and preterm birth (RR 1.99).

pmid:38423229.authors: Chen X, Yang Y, Chen L, et al.
pmid:38423229.title: Pregnancy outcomes and birth defects in offspring following Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs exposure during pregnancy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:38423229.finding: Early-pregnancy NSAID exposure was associated with more congenital anomalies (OR 1.28) and major birth defects (OR 1.19); miscarriage association was not significant (OR 1.20).

pmid:26108134.authors: Cheungpasitporn W, Thongprayoon C, Kittanamongkolchai W, et al.
pmid:26108134.title: Proton pump inhibitors linked to hypomagnesemia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.
pmid:26108134.finding: PPI use was associated with a 43% higher risk of hypomagnesemia (RR 1.43; 1.63 in high-quality studies).

pmid:37060552.authors: Choudhury A, Jena A, Jearth V, et al.
pmid:37060552.title: Vitamin B12 deficiency and use of proton pump inhibitors: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:37060552.finding: PPI users had modestly higher odds of B12 deficiency (OR 1.42) with significant heterogeneity; most studies found no difference in serum B12 levels.

pmid:7282596.title: Effect of vitamin E on prothrombin levels in warfarin-induced vitamin K deficiency.
pmid:7282596.finding: Vitamin E 100-400 IU/day for 4 weeks did not change prothrombin time in warfarin users, though it subtly reduced functional factor II; higher doses may potentiate vitamin K deficiency.

pmid:32665641.title: SGLT2 inhibitors: mechanisms of cardiovascular benefit beyond glycaemic control.
pmid:32665641.finding: Proposed SGLT2-inhibitor benefit mechanisms include natriuresis, ketone use, reduced inflammation and oxidative stress and less AGE signalling; mostly from mechanistic work.

pmid:36049498.title: Effect of statin therapy on muscle symptoms: an individual participant data meta-analysis of large-scale, randomised, double-blind trials.
pmid:36049498.finding: Statins caused a 7% relative excess of muscle pain or weakness in year 1 (about 11 per 1000 person-years); only about 1 in 15 muscle complaints on statins was actually due to the drug.

pmid:41498523.authors: Deameh MG, Ramez M, Rowaiee R, et al.
pmid:41498523.title: Effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists on male reproductive hormones, semen parameters, and metabolic outcomes: a systematic review.
pmid:41498523.finding: GLP-1 agonists consistently raised total testosterone in men with obesity or type 2 diabetes while preserving LH/FSH; semen improvements were reported in obese or hypogonadal men but not in healthy men.

pmid:12427649.authors: De Caterina R, Cipollone F, Filardo FP, et al.
pmid:12427649.title: Low-density lipoprotein level reduction by the 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme-A inhibitor simvastatin is accompanied by a related reduction of F2-isoprostane formation in hypercholesterolemic subjects: no further effect of vitamin E.
pmid:12427649.finding: Simvastatin's LDL lowering was accompanied by a proportional fall in urinary F2-isoprostanes; adding vitamin E 600 mg/day did not lower lipid peroxidation further.

pmid:20488910.authors: de Jager J, Kooy A, Lehert P, et al.
pmid:20488910.title: Long term treatment with metformin in patients with type 2 diabetes and risk of vitamin B-12 deficiency: randomised placebo controlled trial.
pmid:20488910.finding: Metformin 850 mg three times daily for 4.3 years lowered B12 by 19% versus placebo and raised absolute B12-deficiency risk by 7.2 percentage points (number needed to harm ~14), with higher homocysteine.

pmid:29256126.title: Pain Medications and Male Reproduction.
pmid:29256126.finding: Exogenous opioids suppress the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis and act directly on the testis, lowering semen quality and raising DNA fragmentation; NSAIDs have less effect; paracetamol may be of concern.

pmid:42607353.authors: Dutta D, Mahajan K, Jena S, et al.
pmid:42607353.title: Feto-maternal safety of statins in pregnancy: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:42607353.finding: Statins in pregnancy were not associated with congenital malformations (OR 1.05); low birth weight signals were confined to non-pravastatin use in cohort studies.

pmid:41877354.title: Lean Mass Changes With Incretin Therapy Versus Lifestyle Intervention: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomised Controlled Trials.
pmid:41877354.finding: Lean mass made up 25-39% of weight lost on incretin drugs (semaglutide 35%, tirzepatide 25%), similar to diet-based weight loss (26%); adding resistance training cut it to about 17.5%.

pmid:42051241.authors: Etayo-Urtasun P, Sáez de Asteasu ML, Izquierdo M
pmid:42051241.title: The effects of metformin and exercise training on cardiorespiratory, blood pressure, and metabolic adaptations across the spectrum of glucose dysregulation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:42051241.finding: Adding metformin to structured exercise modestly attenuated VO2peak gains (MD -1.19 mL/kg/min) and blood-pressure reductions, with no difference in weight, glycemic or lipid outcomes (moderate certainty for VO2peak).

lifestyle:med-fda-statins2021.title: FDA requests removal of strongest warning against using cholesterol-lowering statins during pregnancy; still advises most pregnant patients should stop taking statins (Drug Safety Communication, 20 July 2021)
lifestyle:med-fda-statins2021.finding: FDA removed the pregnancy contraindication for statins because observational data showed no increase in birth defects, while advising most patients to stop on learning they are pregnant, allowing continuation in very high-risk patients, and advising against breastfeeding.

lifestyle:med-fda-wegovy2021.authors: US Food and Drug Administration; Novo Nordisk
lifestyle:med-fda-wegovy2021.title: WEGOVY (semaglutide) injection, prescribing information (revised 06/2021)
lifestyle:med-fda-wegovy2021.finding: Label section 8.3: discontinue semaglutide at least 2 months before a planned pregnancy because of its long half-life; discontinue when pregnancy is recognized.

lifestyle:med-fda-zepbound2023.authors: US Food and Drug Administration; Eli Lilly
lifestyle:med-fda-zepbound2023.title: ZEPBOUND (tirzepatide) injection, prescribing information (revised 11/2023)
lifestyle:med-fda-zepbound2023.finding: A single 5 mg tirzepatide dose cut ethinyl estradiol Cmax 59% and AUC 20%; users of oral contraceptives should switch to a non-oral method or add a barrier method for 4 weeks after starting and after each dose escalation.

pmid:42139118.authors: Grammer EE, Stahl ME, Ortiz de Zevallos J, et al.
pmid:42139118.title: Influence of metformin on exercise metabolism and capacity: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:42139118.finding: Metformin raised blood lactate during exercise (SMD 0.98) and modulated exercise metabolism; effects on exercise capacity depended on dose, duration and population.

pmid:39511836.authors: Gregorič N, Šikonja J, Janež A, et al.
pmid:39511836.title: Semaglutide improved sperm morphology in obese men with type 2 diabetes mellitus and functional hypogonadism.
pmid:39511836.n: obese men with type 2 diabetes and functional hypogonadism
pmid:39511836.finding: Semaglutide raised normal sperm morphology (median 2% to 4%) and testosterone, whereas testosterone therapy lowered sperm concentration and count.

pmid:14663455.authors: Hall SD, Wang Z, Huang SM, et al.
pmid:14663455.title: The interaction between St John's wort and an oral contraceptive.
pmid:14663455.finding: St John's wort increased norethindrone clearance and halved ethinyl estradiol half-life; breakthrough bleeding rose from 2 to 7 of 12 women.

pmid:3127076.authors: Horowitz JD, Henry CA, Syrjanen ML, et al.
pmid:3127076.title: Combined use of nitroglycerin and N-acetylcysteine in the management of unstable angina pectoris.
pmid:3127076.finding: Adding IV NAC to IV nitroglycerin cut myocardial infarction (3 vs 10 patients) but caused symptomatic hypotension in 7 vs 0 patients.

pmid:27743698.authors: Huijgen NA, de Ridder MA, Verhamme KM, et al.
pmid:27743698.title: Are proton-pump inhibitors harmful for the semen quality of men in couples who are planning pregnancy?
pmid:27743698.finding: PPI use 6-12 months before semen analysis was associated with threefold higher odds of low total motile sperm count (OR 2.96), but use in the preceding 6 months was not.

pmid:26657899.authors: Imhann F, Bonder MJ, Vich Vila A, et al.
pmid:26657899.title: Proton pump inhibitors affect the gut microbiome.
pmid:26657899.finding: PPI use was associated with lower gut microbial diversity and changes in 20% of taxa, including more oral bacteria and potential pathogens, an effect larger than antibiotics at population level.

pmid:35658024.authors: Jastreboff AM, Aronne LJ, Ahmad NN, et al.
pmid:35658024.title: Tirzepatide Once Weekly for the Treatment of Obesity.
pmid:35658024.finding: Tirzepatide 5, 10 and 15 mg weekly cut body weight 15.0%, 19.5% and 20.9% vs 3.1% with placebo over 72 weeks.

pmid:38742535.authors: Javaid M, Kadhim K, Bawamia B, et al.
pmid:38742535.title: Bleeding Risk in Patients Receiving Omega-3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
pmid:38742535.finding: Omega-3 PUFAs did not increase bleeding overall (RR 1.09, 0.91-1.31); high-dose purified EPA raised relative bleeding risk about 50% but absolute risk only 0.6%.

pmid:42449480.authors: Kanbay M, Shah E, AlShiab R, et al.
pmid:42449480.title: Effects of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Dual GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Agonists on Inflammatory and Metabolic Biomarkers in Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
pmid:42449480.finding: Incretin therapies lowered CRP (SMD -0.37) and MDA (SMD -0.98, only 3 trials) and raised adiponectin; IL-6 and TNF-alpha effects were not significant overall.

pmid:29512172.authors: Keihani S, Martin C, Craig JR, et al.
pmid:29512172.title: Semen parameters are unaffected by statin use in men evaluated for infertility.
pmid:29512172.n: 118 statin users vs 7698 unmedicated subfertile men
pmid:29512172.finding: Statin use for over 3 months was not associated with changes in semen parameters other than a small fall in volume in combination users.

pmid:28879865.authors: Keihani S, Craig JR, Zhang C, et al.
pmid:28879865.title: Proton-pump inhibitor use does not affect semen quality in subfertile men.
pmid:28879865.n: 248 PPI users vs 7698 unmedicated subfertile men
pmid:28879865.finding: PPI use for over 3 months was not associated with changes in semen parameters.

pmid:36287641.authors: Keys MT, Thinggaard M, Larsen LA, et al.
pmid:36287641.title: Reassessing the evidence of a survival advantage in Type 2 diabetes treated with metformin compared with controls without diabetes: a retrospective cohort study.
pmid:36287641.n: Danish national registers incl. discordant twins
pmid:36287641.finding: Reanalysis using Danish registers and discordant twins found metformin-treated type 2 diabetes was associated with higher, not lower, mortality than no diabetes (adjusted IRR 1.32 singletons, 1.64 twins), contradicting Bannister 2014.

pmid:23199849.authors: Kokkinos PF, Faselis C, Myers J, et al.
pmid:23199849.title: Interactive effects of fitness and statin treatment on mortality risk in veterans with dyslipidaemia: a cohort study.
pmid:23199849.finding: Statin use and higher fitness were independently associated with lower mortality, and the combination (highly fit statin users HR 0.30) was lowest of all.

pmid:30548390.authors: Konopka AR, Laurin JL, Schoenberg HM, et al.
pmid:30548390.title: Metformin inhibits mitochondrial adaptations to aerobic exercise training in older adults.
pmid:30548390.finding: Metformin (vs placebo) during 12 weeks of aerobic training attenuated the training-induced rise in whole-body insulin sensitivity and VO2max and abolished the rise in muscle mitochondrial respiration; responses were highly variable.

pmid:30746605.title: Taming expectations of metformin as a treatment to extend healthspan.
pmid:30746605.finding: Argues that TAME goals may not match healthspan goals: metformin's benefits are documented in people with chronic disease, and whether they extend to healthy people (and alongside exercise) is unknown.

pmid:21059752.authors: Kristensen DM, Hass U, Lesné L, et al.
pmid:21059752.title: Intrauterine exposure to mild analgesics is a risk factor for development of male reproductive disorders in human and rat.
pmid:21059752.n: Danish and Finnish birth cohorts plus rat studies
pmid:21059752.finding: Mild analgesic use in pregnancy (especially second trimester) was dose-dependently linked to cryptorchidism in the Danish but not the Finnish cohort; paracetamol was anti-androgenic in rats.

pmid:29311296.authors: Kristensen DM, Desdoits-Lethimonier C, Mackey AL, et al.
pmid:29311296.title: Ibuprofen alters human testicular physiology to produce a state of compensated hypogonadism.
pmid:29311296.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:29311296.n: young healthy men plus human testis explants
pmid:29311296.finding: Daily ibuprofen in young men lowered the testosterone/LH ratio, producing compensated hypogonadism, and suppressed testosterone production in human testis explants.

pmid:33071237.authors: Kulkarni AS, Peck BD, Walton RG, et al.
pmid:33071237.title: Metformin alters skeletal muscle transcriptome adaptations to resistance training in older adults.
pmid:33071237.finding: Metformin dampened the muscle gene-expression response to resistance training while shifting some aging-related pathways (senescence, autophagy) in a possibly favourable direction.

pmid:27890768.authors: Lam JR, Schneider JL, Quesenberry CP, et al.
pmid:27890768.title: Proton Pump Inhibitor and Histamine-2 Receptor Antagonist Use and Iron Deficiency.
pmid:27890768.finding: Two or more years of PPI use was associated with iron deficiency (OR 2.49), rising with dose and falling after stopping.

pmid:3584929.title: Therapeutic doses of acetaminophen stimulate the turnover of cysteine and glutathione in man.
pmid:3584929.finding: Single therapeutic doses of acetaminophen (600-1200 mg) markedly increased turnover of the cysteine pool used for glutathione synthesis, showing that normal doses draw on glutathione.

pmid:18505970.authors: Lawenda BD, Kelly KM, Ladas EJ, et al.
pmid:18505970.title: Should supplemental antioxidant administration be avoided during chemotherapy and radiation therapy?
pmid:18505970.finding: Concluded from RCTs that supplemental antioxidants during chemotherapy and radiotherapy should be discouraged because of possible tumour protection.

pmid:29890124.authors: Li DK, Ferber JR, Odouli R, et al.
pmid:29890124.title: Use of nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs during pregnancy and the risk of miscarriage.
pmid:29890124.finding: NSAID use around conception was associated with more miscarriage (aHR 1.89), stronger for early loss and longer use; acetaminophen users were used as an indication control.

pmid:28834248.authors: Lilja M, Mandić M, Apró W, et al.
pmid:28834248.title: High doses of anti-inflammatory drugs compromise muscle strength and hypertrophic adaptations to resistance training in young adults.
pmid:28834248.finding: Ibuprofen 1200 mg/day halved quadriceps growth (3.7% vs 7.5%) in young men and women and blunted strength gains versus low-dose aspirin during 8 weeks of resistance training.

pmid:30102811.title: Analgesic and anti-inflammatory drugs in sports: Implications for exercise performance and training adaptations.
pmid:30102811.finding: NSAIDs and paracetamol inhibit COX; NSAIDs interfere with hypertrophy and strength gains in young people, while effects in elite athletes are unproven.

pmid:22040838.authors: Malin SK, Gerber R, Chipkin SR, et al.
pmid:22040838.title: Independent and combined effects of exercise training and metformin on insulin sensitivity in individuals with prediabetes.
pmid:22040838.finding: Exercise, metformin (2000 mg/day) and both combined all raised clamp insulin sensitivity over 12 weeks; the rise was 25-30% higher with exercise alone than with exercise plus metformin, a non-significant difference read as possible blunting.

pmid:39414354.authors: Meng LC, van Gelder MMHJ, Chuang HM, et al.
pmid:39414354.title: Paternal metformin use and risk of congenital malformations in offspring in Norway and Taiwan: population based, cross national cohort study.
pmid:39414354.finding: After restricting to fathers with type 2 diabetes and adjusting for diabetes severity, paternal metformin during sperm development was not linked to malformations (pooled RR 0.89, 0.77-1.03), including in sibling comparisons.

pmid:21618455.authors: Micu MC, Micu R, Ostensen M
pmid:21618455.title: Luteinized unruptured follicle syndrome increased by inactive disease and selective cyclooxygenase 2 inhibitors in women with inflammatory arthropathies.
pmid:21618455.n: 59 monitored cycles with NSAIDs vs untreated cycles in women with inflammatory arthritis
pmid:21618455.finding: Continuous periovulatory NSAIDs caused luteinized unruptured follicle in 35.6% of cycles vs 3.4% untreated; etoricoxib was the main culprit and ibuprofen 1600 mg/day caused none.

pmid:23583255.authors: Mikus CR, Boyle LJ, Borengasser SJ, et al.
pmid:23583255.title: Simvastatin impairs exercise training adaptations.
pmid:23583255.finding: Simvastatin 40 mg blunted the training-induced gain in cardiorespiratory fitness (1.5% vs 10%) and turned a 13% rise in muscle citrate synthase into a 4.5% fall over 12 weeks.

pmid:32783612.title: Exercise-Pharmacology Interactions: Metformin, Statins, and Healthspan.
pmid:32783612.finding: Reviews how metformin and statins may blunt exercise adaptations and argues their healthspan use in disease-free people must be tested alongside exercise.

pmid:33851013.title: Euglycemic Diabetic Ketoacidosis Caused by SGLT2 Inhibitors and a Ketogenic Diet: A Case Series and Review of Literature.
pmid:33851013.finding: Euglycemic DKA occurred with an SGLT2 inhibitor after only one week of a ketogenic diet; patients on these drugs should avoid ketogenic diets.

pmid:31152740.authors: Moayyedi P, Eikelboom JW, Bosch J, et al.
pmid:31152740.title: Safety of Proton Pump Inhibitors Based on a Large, Multi-Year, Randomized Trial of Patients Receiving Rivaroxaban or Aspirin.
pmid:31152740.finding: Pantoprazole 40 mg for about 3 years caused no excess of pneumonia, fracture, dementia or other harms versus placebo except enteric infections (1.4% vs 1.0%).

pmid:35578807.authors: Moreno-Cabañas A, Morales-Palomo F, Alvarez-Jimenez L, et al.
pmid:35578807.title: Effects of chronic metformin treatment on training adaptations in men and women with hyperglycemia: A prospective study.
pmid:35578807.finding: Among people doing 16 weeks of HIIT, those already taking metformin gained about half as much VO2max (12.7% vs 25.3%) as non-users, although insulin-resistance improvements were similar.

pmid:38937282.authors: Neeland IJ, Linge J, Birkenfeld AL
pmid:38937282.title: Changes in lean body mass with glucagon-like peptide-1-based therapies and mitigation strategies.
pmid:38937282.finding: Lean-mass loss on GLP-1 therapies is largely proportional to weight lost and may be adaptive (less muscle fat, better insulin sensitivity), but older or frail patients risk sarcopenia.

pmid:28057795.authors: Oesterle A, Laufs U, Liao JK
pmid:28057795.title: Pleiotropic Effects of Statins on the Cardiovascular System.
pmid:28057795.finding: Statins block isoprenoid synthesis and thereby Rho/Rac signalling and NADPH oxidase activity, lowering ROS and inflammation in cells and animals; how much this adds clinically beyond LDL lowering is debated.

pmid:10839993.authors: Owen MR, Doran E, Halestrap AP
pmid:10839993.title: Evidence that metformin exerts its anti-diabetic effects through inhibition of complex 1 of the mitochondrial respiratory chain.
pmid:10839993.finding: Metformin slowly accumulates in mitochondria and inhibits respiratory-chain complex I in hepatoma cells and rat liver, which restrains gluconeogenesis.

pmid:30349083.authors: Palleja A, Mikkelsen KH, Forslund SK, et al.
pmid:30349083.title: Recovery of gut microbiota of healthy adults following antibiotic exposure.
pmid:30349083.finding: After a 4-day broad-spectrum antibiotic cocktail, gut microbiota recovered to near-baseline within 1.5 months, though 9 common species were still missing at 180 days.

pmid:26197031.authors: Panza GA, Taylor BA, Thompson PD, et al.
pmid:26197031.title: The Effect of Atorvastatin on Habitual Physical Activity among Healthy Adults.
pmid:26197031.finding: Atorvastatin 80 mg for 6 months did not reduce habitual physical activity differently from placebo.

pmid:41065428.authors: Peel A, Lyons H, Tully CA, et al.
pmid:41065428.title: The effect of obesity interventions on male fertility: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:41065428.finding: Lifestyle weight-loss interventions modestly improved sperm morphology and progressive motility in men; data on GLP-1 agonists and on conception outcomes were too limited to judge.

pmid:32979074.authors: Pilmark NS, Lyngbæk M, Oberholzer L, et al.
pmid:32979074.title: The interaction between metformin and physical activity on postprandial glucose and glucose kinetics: a randomised, clinical trial.
pmid:32979074.finding: Metformin 2 g/day plus 12 weeks of interval cycling was not better than training alone for post-meal glucose; VO2peak rose 15% with no between-group difference.

pmid:25016482.authors: Pons-Rejraji H, Brugnon F, Sion B, et al.
pmid:25016482.title: Evaluation of atorvastatin efficacy and toxicity on spermatozoa, accessory glands and gonadal hormones of healthy men: a pilot prospective clinical trial.
pmid:25016482.finding: Atorvastatin 10 mg for 5 months was followed by a 31% fall in total sperm count and changes in accessory-gland markers, some persisting 3 months after stopping.

pmid:40804730.authors: Prada D, Ritz B, Bauer AZ, et al.
pmid:40804730.title: Evaluation of the evidence on acetaminophen use and neurodevelopmental disorders using the Navigation Guide methodology.
pmid:40804730.finding: Navigation Guide review: 27 of 46 studies reported positive associations of prenatal acetaminophen with ADHD/autism, with higher-quality studies more often positive; authors urge limiting use.

pmid:30371340.authors: Qu H, Guo M, Chai H, et al.
pmid:30371340.title: Effects of Coenzyme Q10 on Statin-Induced Myopathy: An Updated Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
pmid:30371340.finding: CoQ10 reduced statin-associated muscle pain, weakness, cramps and tiredness versus placebo, without changing CK.

pmid:28776086.authors: Rena G, Hardie DG, Pearson ER
pmid:28776086.title: The mechanisms of action of metformin.
pmid:28776086.finding: Metformin acts through AMPK-dependent and independent routes, including inhibition of mitochondrial respiration (complex I) and possibly mitochondrial glycerophosphate dehydrogenase, with a growing role for the gut.

pmid:18997196.authors: Ridker PM, Danielson E, Fonseca FA, et al.
pmid:18997196.title: Rosuvastatin to prevent vascular events in men and women with elevated C-reactive protein.
pmid:18997196.n: 17,802 adults with LDL <130 mg/dL and hsCRP >=2 mg/L (JUPITER)
pmid:18997196.finding: Rosuvastatin 20 mg cut LDL 50% and hsCRP 37% and nearly halved major cardiovascular events (HR 0.56), with more physician-reported diabetes.

pmid:33755728.authors: Rubino D, Abrahamsson N, Davies M, et al.
pmid:33755728.title: Effect of Continued Weekly Subcutaneous Semaglutide vs Placebo on Weight Loss Maintenance in Adults With Overweight or Obesity: The STEP 4 Randomized Clinical Trial.
pmid:33755728.finding: After a 20-week semaglutide run-in (-10.6%), continuing semaglutide lost a further 7.9% by week 68 whereas switching to placebo regained 6.9%.

pmid:23013520.title: The use of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs for exercise-induced muscle damage: implications for skeletal muscle development.
pmid:23013520.finding: Occasional NSAID use is unlikely to impair muscle growth; chronic use is less clear and may be detrimental in people with high growth potential.

pmid:31845767.authors: Sharpe A, Morley LC, Tang T, et al.
pmid:31845767.title: Metformin for ovulation induction (excluding gonadotrophins) in women with polycystic ovary syndrome.
pmid:31845767.finding: Cochrane: in PCOS, metformin may improve live birth versus placebo (OR 1.59, low quality) but quadruples GI side effects; adding it to clomiphene has uncertain effect on live birth; clomiphene beats metformin in obese women.

pmid:18638594.authors: Singh U, Devaraj S, Jialal I, et al.
pmid:18638594.title: Comparison effect of atorvastatin (10 versus 80 mg) on biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress in subjects with metabolic syndrome.
pmid:18638594.finding: Atorvastatin 80 mg cut oxidized LDL 39% (vs 24% with 10 mg) and lowered hsCRP and NF-kB activity over 12 weeks.

pmid:27412248.authors: Smarr MM, Grantz KL, Sundaram R, et al.
pmid:27412248.title: Urinary paracetamol and time-to-pregnancy.
pmid:27412248.finding: Men in the highest quartile of urinary paracetamol had longer time to pregnancy (fecundability OR 0.67); no association when modelled continuously or in women.

pmid:12113640.authors: Stone S, Khamashta MA, Nelson-Piercy C
pmid:12113640.title: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and reversible female infertility: is there a link?
pmid:12113640.finding: COX-2 inhibition blocks follicle rupture; animal data and three small clinical studies link regular NSAIDs to reversible anovulation, so withdrawal should be considered during fertility work-up.

pmid:32478963.title: Warfarin and food, herbal or dietary supplement interactions: A systematic review.
pmid:32478963.finding: Systematic review of warfarin interactions: 45 foods, herbs or supplements potentiated warfarin, some causing serious bleeding; St John's wort, green tea and others flagged.

pmid:25545331.authors: Taylor BA, Lorson L, White CM, et al.
pmid:25545331.title: A randomized trial of coenzyme Q10 in patients with confirmed statin myopathy.
pmid:25545331.n: 120 patients with reported statin myalgia; 41 randomized to CoQ10 or placebo
pmid:25545331.finding: Only 36% of people reporting statin myalgia had symptoms on blinded simvastatin vs placebo; ubiquinol CoQ10 600 mg/day raised serum CoQ10 fourfold but did not reduce pain.

pmid:37580314.authors: Teede HJ, Tay CT, Laven JJE, et al.
pmid:37580314.title: Recommendations From the 2023 International Evidence-based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome.
pmid:37580314.finding: 2023 International Evidence-based PCOS Guideline (endorsed by ASRM, ESHRE, Endocrine Society, ESE): 254 recommendations including letrozole as first-line ovulation induction, metformin for metabolic features, and anti-obesity medicines alongside lifestyle.

pmid:30653978.title: Does metformin therapy influence the effects of intensive lifestyle intervention? Exploring the interaction between first line therapies in the Look AHEAD trial.
pmid:30653978.finding: Background metformin was associated with slightly smaller weight loss (-4.7 vs -5.7 kg) under intensive lifestyle intervention and added little glycemic benefit, but did not change fitness gains.

pmid:21160058.authors: Trappe TA, Carroll CC, Dickinson JM, et al.
pmid:21160058.title: Influence of acetaminophen and ibuprofen on skeletal muscle adaptations to resistance exercise in older adults.
pmid:21160058.journal: Am J Physiol Regul Integr Comp Physiol
pmid:21160058.finding: Over-the-counter doses of acetaminophen (4 g/day) or ibuprofen (1.2 g/day) during 12 weeks of resistance training did not inhibit muscle growth and strength and appeared to enhance them (muscle volume +12.5% and +10.9% vs +8.6% on placebo) in older adults.

pmid:34044205.authors: Vahedian-Azimi A, Makvandi S, Banach M, et al.
pmid:34044205.title: Fetal toxicity associated with statins: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:34044205.finding: Statin use in pregnancy was not significantly associated with birth defects (OR 1.48, 0.90-2.42), though the authors call for more data.

pmid:24472372.authors: Wachira JK, Larson MK, Harris WS
pmid:24472372.title: n-3 Fatty acids affect haemostasis but do not increase the risk of bleeding: clinical observations and mechanistic insights.
pmid:24472372.finding: Omega-3 fatty acids alter platelet function but did not increase clinically significant bleeding, including with antiplatelet or anticoagulant drugs.

pmid:31557380.authors: Walton RG, Dungan CM, Long DE, et al.
pmid:31557380.title: Metformin blunts muscle hypertrophy in response to progressive resistance exercise training in older adults: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial: The MASTERS trial.
pmid:31557380.finding: MASTERS: metformin 1700 mg/day during 14 weeks of progressive resistance training blunted gains in lean body mass and thigh muscle area versus placebo, with a non-significant trend to smaller strength gains.

pmid:16820551.authors: Watkins PB, Kaplowitz N, Slattery JT, et al.
pmid:16820551.title: Aminotransferase elevations in healthy adults receiving 4 grams of acetaminophen daily: a randomized controlled trial.
pmid:16820551.finding: Starting 4 g/day acetaminophen produced ALT >3x the upper limit in 31-44% of healthy adults within 2 weeks versus 0% on placebo.

pmid:35344380.authors: Wensink MJ, Lu Y, Tian L, et al.
pmid:35344380.title: Preconception Antidiabetic Drugs in Men and Birth Defects in Offspring : A Nationwide Cohort Study.
pmid:35344380.finding: Offspring of fathers who filled metformin prescriptions during sperm development had more major birth defects (aOR 1.40), especially genital defects in boys; exposure outside that window showed no excess.

pmid:17010103.authors: Whitten DL, Myers SP, Hawrelak JA, et al.
pmid:17010103.title: The effect of St John's wort extracts on CYP3A: a systematic review of prospective clinical trials.
pmid:17010103.finding: High-hyperforin St John's wort extracts (>10 mg/day) consistently induce CYP3A; low-hyperforin extracts (<4 mg/day) did not.

pmid:33567185.authors: Wilding JPH, Batterham RL, Calanna S, et al.
pmid:33567185.title: Once-Weekly Semaglutide in Adults with Overweight or Obesity.
pmid:33567185.finding: Semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly plus lifestyle cut body weight 14.9% vs 2.4% with placebo over 68 weeks.

pmid:26503419.authors: Yasueda A, Urushima H, Ito T
pmid:26503419.title: Efficacy and Interaction of Antioxidant Supplements as Adjuvant Therapy in Cancer Treatment: A Systematic Review.
pmid:26503419.finding: Harm from antioxidant supplements during cancer therapy remains unclear except for smokers having radiotherapy.

pmid:41815850.authors: Alangari A, Arif J, Al Qureshah F, et al.
pmid:41815850.title: Clinical benefits and risks of high-dose intravenous vitamin C: a systematic review.
pmid:41815850.finding: Systematic review of high-dose IV vitamin C: benefits in sepsis and cancer remain exploratory, and risks include oxalate nephropathy and hemolysis at very high doses in G6PD deficiency, supporting pre-infusion testing.

pmid:18199861.authors: Allen KJ, Gurrin LC, Constantine CC, et al.
pmid:18199861.title: Iron-overload-related disease in HFE hereditary hemochromatosis.
pmid:18199861.finding: Documented iron-overload-related disease developed in 28.4% of male but only 1.2% of female C282Y homozygotes; only one non-homozygote (a compound heterozygote) had such disease.

pmid:36678214.authors: Beretta A, Manuelli M, Cena H
pmid:36678214.title: Favism: Clinical Features at Different Ages.
pmid:36678214.finding: Favism (hemolysis after fava beans in G6PD deficiency) varies widely in severity, is most severe in young children and pregnancy, and often needs hospitalization and transfusion.

pmid:18177777.title: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency.
pmid:18177777.finding: G6PD deficiency, an X-linked defect affecting over 400 million people, causes neonatal jaundice and acute hemolysis triggered by oxidant drugs, infections or fava beans; management is avoidance of oxidative triggers.

pmid:35662478.authors: European Association for the Study of the Liver
pmid:35662478.title: EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines on haemochromatosis.
pmid:35662478.finding: EASL haemochromatosis guideline: in HFE C282Y homozygotes, TSAT >45% with ferritin >200 ug/L (women) or TSAT >50% with ferritin >300 ug/L (men, postmenopausal women) suffices for diagnosis; phlebotomy targets ferritin <50 ug/L in induction and <100 ug/L in maintenance.

pmid:36049896.authors: Gammal RS, Pirmohamed M, Somogyi AA, et al.
pmid:36049896.title: Expanded Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium Guideline for Medication Use in the Context of G6PD Genotype.
pmid:36049896.finding: CPIC classifies dapsone, methylene blue, pegloticase, primaquine, rasburicase, tafenoquine and toluidine blue as high-risk in G6PD deficiency, nitrofurantoin as medium risk, and vitamin C at standard doses as low-to-no risk.

pmid:34028001.authors: Garcia-Casal MN, Pasricha SR, Martinez RX, et al.
pmid:34028001.title: Serum or plasma ferritin concentration as an index of iron deficiency and overload.
pmid:34028001.finding: At a threshold of 30 ug/L, ferritin is reasonably sensitive and very specific for iron deficiency in people presenting for care (low-certainty evidence); evidence that high ferritin detects iron overload is very low certainty, and screening performance in healthy people is unknown.

pmid:31335359.authors: Kowdley KV, Brown KE, Ahn J, et al.
pmid:31335359.title: ACG Clinical Guideline: Hereditary Hemochromatosis.
pmid:31335359.finding: ACG hemochromatosis guideline: ferritin <1,000 ng/mL at diagnosis identifies low risk of advanced fibrosis; elevated ferritin is more often due to fatty liver or alcohol than to hemochromatosis in people who are not C282Y homozygotes or C282Y/H63D compound heterozygotes.

pmid:32702756.authors: Luzzatto L, Ally M, Notaro R
pmid:32702756.title: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency.
pmid:32702756.finding: About 500 million people carry G6PD mutations; most are asymptomatic but can develop severe acute hemolysis after fava beans, drugs such as primaquine or rasburicase, or infection.

pmid:31821471.authors: Méar L, Herr M, Fauconnier A, et al.
pmid:31821471.title: Polymorphisms and endometriosis: a systematic review and meta-analyses.
pmid:31821471.finding: Among many studied polymorphisms, GSTT1 null was among the few robustly associated with endometriosis, while GSTM1 null was among candidates needing confirmation in well-defined cohorts.

pmid:19233695.authors: Nkhoma ET, Poole C, Vannappagari V, et al.
pmid:19233695.title: The global prevalence of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:19233695.finding: G6PD deficiency affects an estimated 400 million people, with the highest prevalence in sub-Saharan Africa and malaria-endemic regions.

pmid:30651232.authors: Pilling LC, Tamosauskaite J, Jones G, et al.
pmid:30651232.title: Common conditions associated with hereditary haemochromatosis genetic variants: cohort study in UK Biobank.
pmid:30651232.finding: C282Y homozygosity was associated with liver disease (OR 4.30), arthritis, diabetes (OR 1.53) and more incident morbidity in both men (15.7% vs 5.0%) and women (10.1% vs 3.4%), supporting re-examination of early case-finding.

pmid:16979952.authors: Walsh A, Dixon JL, Ramm GA, et al.
pmid:16979952.title: The clinical relevance of compound heterozygosity for the C282Y and H63D substitutions in hemochromatosis.
pmid:16979952.n: 249 C282Y/H63D compound heterozygotes and 483 C282Y homozygotes
pmid:16979952.finding: C282Y/H63D compound heterozygotes often had raised iron indices but did not develop progressive disease without cofactors such as fatty liver, diabetes or excess alcohol.

pmid:16880463.authors: Whitlock EP, Garlitz BA, Harris EL, et al.
pmid:16880463.title: Screening for hereditary hemochromatosis: a systematic review for the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force.
pmid:16880463.finding: USPSTF systematic review: up to 38-50% of C282Y homozygotes may develop iron overload and 10-33% hemochromatosis-related morbidity, but evidence was insufficient to estimate the benefit of population genetic screening.

pmid:23877133.authors: Wu W, Lu J, Tang Q, et al.
pmid:23877133.title: GSTM1 and GSTT1 null polymorphisms and male infertility risk: an updated meta-analysis encompassing 6934 subjects.
pmid:23877133.finding: GSTM1 null genotype was associated with a significantly higher risk of male infertility in Asian and Caucasian groups; GSTT1 findings were inconsistent.

pmid:11136685.authors: Ascherio A, Rimm EB, Giovannucci E, et al.
pmid:11136685.title: Blood donations and risk of coronary heart disease in men
pmid:11136685.finding: Lifetime blood donation lowered ferritin but was not associated with MI or fatal CHD (RR 1.2 for >=30 donations vs never).

pmid:21342203.authors: Atsma F, Veldhuizen I, Verbeek A, et al.
pmid:21342203.title: Healthy donor effect: its magnitude in health research among blood donors
pmid:21342203.finding: Donors were healthier than the general population (better self-rated health, fewer GP visits), demonstrating a strong healthy donor effect.

pmid:10027804.title: Coronary heart disease and iron status: meta-analyses of prospective studies
pmid:10027804.finding: Ferritin >=200 vs <200 ug/L showed no association with coronary heart disease (RR 1.0, 0.8-1.3); no strong link for any iron marker.

pmid:20304584.authors: Depalma RG, Hayes VW, Chow BK, et al.
pmid:20304584.title: Ferritin levels, inflammatory biomarkers, and mortality in peripheral arterial disease: a substudy of the Iron (Fe) and Atherosclerosis Study (FeAST) Trial
pmid:20304584.finding: In a FeAST substudy, ferritin correlated with IL-6 and hsCRP, and higher ferritin tracked with mortality, illustrating ferritin's overlap with inflammation.

pmid:28941948.authors: Di Angelantonio E, Thompson SG, Kaptoge S, et al.
pmid:28941948.title: Efficiency and safety of varying the frequency of whole blood donation (INTERVAL): a randomised trial of 45 000 donors
pmid:28941948.finding: INTERVAL: shorter donation intervals collected more blood but caused more symptoms (tiredness, restless legs), lower hemoglobin and ferritin, and more deferrals.

pmid:18612127.authors: Edgren G, Nyrén O, Melbye M
pmid:18612127.title: Cancer as a ferrotoxic disease: are we getting hard stainless evidence?
pmid:18612127.finding: JNCI editorial accompanying the FeAST cancer analysis, questioning how firm the evidence is that iron reduction prevents cancer.

pmid:20100340.authors: Falkingham M, Abdelhamid A, Curtis P, et al.
pmid:20100340.title: The effects of oral iron supplementation on cognition in older children and adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:20100340.finding: Iron supplements improved attention/concentration and, in anaemic people only, IQ by 2.5 points; trials were small and weak.

pmid:40945632.authors: Fiani D, Chahine S, Zaboube M, et al.
pmid:40945632.title: Psychiatric and cognitive outcomes of iron supplementation in non-anemic children, adolescents, and menstruating adults: A meta-analysis and systematic review
pmid:40945632.finding: In non-anaemic iron-deficient youth and menstruating adults, iron improved anxiety, fatigue and memory; effects vanished when iron-replete people were analysed alone.

pmid:39145520.authors: Finkelstein JL, Cuthbert A, Weeks J, et al.
pmid:39145520.title: Daily oral iron supplementation during pregnancy
pmid:39145520.finding: Daily iron in pregnancy reduces maternal anaemia, iron deficiency and iron-deficiency anaemia at term and probably reduces low birthweight (RR 0.84).

pmid:28684612.authors: Gill D, Del Greco M F, Walker AP, et al.
pmid:28684612.title: The Effect of Iron Status on Risk of Coronary Artery Disease: A Mendelian Randomization Study-Brief Report
pmid:28684612.n: ~60,800 CAD cases and 123,500 controls (two-sample Mendelian randomization)
pmid:28684612.finding: Genetically higher iron status was associated with slightly LOWER coronary artery disease risk (OR 0.94 per SD serum iron).

pmid:31220083.authors: Gill D, Benyamin B, Moore LSP, et al.
pmid:31220083.title: Associations of genetically determined iron status across the phenome: A mendelian randomization study
pmid:31220083.finding: Higher genetic iron status lowered iron-deficiency anemia and hypercholesterolemia but raised skin and soft-tissue infections (cellulitis/abscess OR 1.25).

pmid:22647517.authors: Houschyar KS, Lüdtke R, Dobos GJ, et al.
pmid:22647517.title: Effects of phlebotomy-induced reduction of body iron stores on metabolic syndrome: results from a randomized clinical trial
pmid:22647517.finding: Removing 550-800 mL blood lowered systolic BP by 16.6 mmHg vs control at 6 weeks, without changing insulin resistance (HOMA).

pmid:17299200.title: The iron-heart hypothesis: search for the ironclad evidence
pmid:17299200.finding: JAMA editorial accompanying FeAST arguing that conclusive ('ironclad') evidence for the iron-heart hypothesis was still lacking.

pmid:24401818.authors: Hunnicutt J, He K, Xun P
pmid:24401818.title: Dietary iron intake and body iron stores are associated with risk of coronary heart disease in a meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies
pmid:24401818.finding: Heme iron intake was associated with higher CHD incidence (RR 1.57) while total iron, serum iron and transferrin saturation were inversely associated.

pmid:31074789.authors: Jiang L, Wang K, Lo K, et al.
pmid:31074789.title: Sex-Specific Association of Circulating Ferritin Level and Risk of Type 2 Diabetes: A Dose-Response Meta-Analysis of Prospective Studies
pmid:31074789.finding: Each 100 ug/L higher ferritin was associated with 22% higher type 2 diabetes risk, stronger in women (RR 1.53) than men (RR 1.21).

pmid:31383583.authors: Kaptoge S, Di Angelantonio E, Moore C, et al.
pmid:31383583.title: Longer-term efficiency and safety of increasing the frequency of whole blood donation (INTERVAL): extension study of a randomised trial of 20 757 blood donors
pmid:31383583.finding: Each week shorter inter-donation interval lowered ferritin by ~5-6.5% and increased low-hemoglobin deferrals.

pmid:24549403.title: Serum ferritin is an important inflammatory disease marker, as it is mainly a leakage product from damaged cells
pmid:24549403.finding: Argues serum ferritin is largely a leakage product of damaged cells, explaining its correlation with inflammation and oxidative stress as well as with iron stores.

pmid:26670627.authors: Khambalia AZ, Aimone A, Nagubandi P, et al.
pmid:26670627.title: High maternal iron status, dietary iron intake and iron supplement use in pregnancy and risk of gestational diabetes mellitus: a prospective study and systematic review
pmid:26670627.finding: Higher ferritin (OR 1.41 per unit), serum iron and heme iron intake were associated with gestational diabetes; two supplement trials showed no association.

pmid:23381919.authors: Kunutsor SK, Apekey TA, Walley J, et al.
pmid:23381919.title: Ferritin levels and risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective evidence
pmid:23381919.finding: Top vs bottom fifth of ferritin: type 2 diabetes RR 1.73; heme iron intake RR 1.28.

pmid:38497484.authors: Liu Y, Clarke R, Bennett DA, et al.
pmid:38497484.title: Iron Status and Risk of Heart Disease, Stroke, and Diabetes: A Mendelian Randomization Study in European Adults
pmid:38497484.n: UK Biobank plus consortia with 181,522 CAD and 80,154 T2D cases (Mendelian randomization)
pmid:38497484.finding: Genetically higher iron biomarkers were modestly protective for coronary disease (7-14% lower risk per SD) but raised type 2 diabetes risk.

pmid:22647488.title: Back to past leeches: repeated phlebotomies and cardiovascular risk
pmid:22647488.finding: Commentary on the phlebotomy trial noting design drawbacks (unblinded, short) while discussing iron depletion and metabolic risk.

pmid:33285139.authors: Pasricha SR, Tye-Din J, Muckenthaler MU, et al.
pmid:33285139.title: Iron deficiency
pmid:33285139.finding: Iron deficiency is a leading cause of global disease burden; harms occur even without anaemia; hepcidin limits absorption of high-dose oral iron.

pmid:26198451.authors: Peña-Rosas JP, De-Regil LM, Garcia-Casal MN, et al.
pmid:26198451.title: Daily oral iron supplementation during pregnancy
pmid:26198451.finding: Prenatal iron cut anaemia at term by 70% but raised the risk of haemoglobin above 130 g/L.

pmid:26739036.authors: Rahman MM, Abe SK, Rahman MS, et al.
pmid:26739036.title: Maternal anemia and risk of adverse birth and health outcomes in low- and middle-income countries: systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:26739036.n: 26 studies in low- and middle-income countries
pmid:26739036.finding: Maternal anaemia was associated with low birthweight (RR 1.31), preterm birth (RR 1.63) and perinatal mortality (RR 1.51).

pmid:9737556.authors: Salonen JT, Tuomainen TP, Salonen R, et al.
pmid:9737556.title: Donation of blood is associated with reduced risk of myocardial infarction. The Kuopio Ischaemic Heart Disease Risk Factor Study
pmid:9737556.finding: Men who had donated blood in the previous 24 months had 88% lower risk of acute MI (1 event in 153 donors).

pmid:11023623.authors: Sempos CT, Looker AC, Gillum RE, et al.
pmid:11023623.title: Serum ferritin and death from all causes and cardiovascular disease: the NHANES II Mortality Study. National Health and Nutrition Examination Study
pmid:11023623.finding: Serum ferritin was not associated with cardiovascular or all-cause death in US adults; low ferritin predicted higher mortality in Black men.

pmid:6112609.title: Iron and the sex difference in heart disease risk
pmid:6112609.finding: Proposed the 'iron hypothesis': higher stored iron in men and postmenopausal women explains their higher heart disease risk, and suggested phlebotomy as a test.

pmid:32678081.authors: Timmers PRHJ, Wilson JF, Joshi PK, et al.
pmid:32678081.title: Multivariate genomic scan implicates novel loci and haem metabolism in human ageing
pmid:32678081.n: Multivariate GWAS of healthspan, parental lifespan and longevity
pmid:32678081.finding: Identified haem metabolism as a pathway linked to human ageing traits.

pmid:26098293.authors: Ullum H, Rostgaard K, Kamper-Jørgensen M, et al.
pmid:26098293.title: Blood donation and blood donor mortality after adjustment for a healthy donor effect
pmid:26098293.finding: Each extra annual donation was linked to 18.6% lower mortality, shrinking to 7.5% after adjusting for the healthy donor effect; not proof of benefit.

pmid:30070219.authors: van den Hurk K, van Kraaij MGJ, Zalpuri S
pmid:30070219.title: Lessons from the INTERVAL study
pmid:30070219.finding: Letter on INTERVAL urging attention to iron deficiency in frequent donors and ferritin monitoring.

pmid:22777991.authors: Vaucher P, Druais PL, Waldvogel S, et al.
pmid:22777991.title: Effect of iron supplementation on fatigue in nonanemic menstruating women with low ferritin: a randomized controlled trial
pmid:22777991.n: 198 non-anaemic menstruating women with ferritin <50 ug/L
pmid:22777991.finding: 80 mg/day oral iron for 12 weeks reduced fatigue scores by 47.7% vs 28.8% with placebo.

pmid:34147035.authors: Wang X, Fang X, Zheng W, et al.
pmid:34147035.title: Genetic Support of A Causal Relationship Between Iron Status and Type 2 Diabetes: A Mendelian Randomization Study
pmid:34147035.finding: Genetically higher serum iron (OR 1.07), ferritin (OR 1.19) and transferrin saturation (OR 1.06) were associated with higher type 2 diabetes risk.

pmid:15231242.title: The iron-heart disease connection: is it dead or just hiding?
pmid:15231242.finding: Reviewed why the iron-heart hypothesis remained unresolved and called for better measures of the potentially damaging forms of iron.

pmid:37076797.authors: Young MF, Oaks BM, Rogers HP, et al.
pmid:37076797.title: Maternal low and high hemoglobin concentrations and associations with adverse maternal and infant health outcomes: an updated global systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:37076797.finding: Both low and high maternal haemoglobin were associated with adverse outcomes; high Hb with gestational diabetes (OR 1.71), pre-eclampsia and stillbirth.

pmid:17299195.authors: Zacharski LR, Chow BK, Howes PS, et al.
pmid:17299195.title: Reduction of iron stores and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with peripheral arterial disease: a randomized controlled trial
pmid:17299195.finding: FeAST: phlebotomy to lower ferritin did not significantly reduce all-cause death (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.67-1.08) or death plus MI and stroke (HR 0.88, 0.72-1.07).

pmid:18612130.authors: Zacharski LR, Chow BK, Howes PS, et al.
pmid:18612130.title: Decreased cancer risk after iron reduction in patients with peripheral arterial disease: results from a randomized trial
pmid:18612130.finding: FeAST secondary analysis: iron reduction (mean ferritin ~80 vs ~123 ng/mL) was associated with fewer new visceral cancers (HR 0.65, 0.43-0.97).

pmid:22848554.authors: Zhao Z, Li S, Liu G, et al.
pmid:22848554.title: Body iron stores and heme-iron intake in relation to risk of type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:22848554.finding: Highest vs lowest ferritin: prospective T2D RR 1.66; highest vs lowest heme iron intake RR 1.31.

pmid:27307003.authors: Bhatti P, Mirick DK, Randolph TW, et al.
pmid:27307003.title: Oxidative DNA damage during sleep periods among nightshift workers.
pmid:27307003.finding: Night-shift workers excreted less urinary 8-OH-dG during day sleep than day workers during night sleep, interpreted as reduced oxidative DNA repair linked to melatonin disruption.

pmid:40722906.authors: Boeri L, Passarelli F, Basadonna LM, et al.
pmid:40722906.title: Oxidative Stress and Semen Quality Among Night- and Day-Shift Workers: A Cross-Sectional Study.
pmid:40722906.finding: Night-shift work independently predicted elevated oxidative stress (d-ROMs, OR 2.1); in an uncontrolled subgroup, antioxidant supplementation lowered d-ROMs more in night workers.

pmid:35298459.authors: Brown TM, Brainard GC, Cajochen C, et al.
pmid:35298459.title: Recommendations for daytime, evening, and nighttime indoor light exposure to best support physiology, sleep, and wakefulness in healthy adults.
pmid:35298459.finding: Expert consensus: daytime light ≥250 lux melanopic EDI at the eye; ≤10 lux melanopic EDI in the 3 h before bed; ≤1 lux melanopic EDI in the sleep environment (≤10 if some light is needed).

pmid:22496545.authors: Buxton OM, Cain SW, O'Connor SP, et al.
pmid:22496545.title: Adverse metabolic consequences in humans of prolonged sleep restriction combined with circadian disruption.
pmid:22496545.finding: Three weeks of sleep restriction (5.6 h/24 h) combined with 28-h days lowered resting metabolic rate and raised postprandial glucose through inadequate insulin secretion; reversed with recovery.

pmid:25535358.authors: Chang AM, Aeschbach D, Duffy JF, et al.
pmid:25535358.title: Evening use of light-emitting eReaders negatively affects sleep, circadian timing, and next-morning alertness.
pmid:25535358.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:25535358.finding: Reading a light-emitting e-reader for ~4 h before bed for 5 nights, vs a printed book, lengthened sleep onset, suppressed melatonin, delayed the circadian clock and reduced next-morning alertness.

pmid:25762077.title: Reply to Zeitzer: Good science, in or out of the laboratory, should prevail.
pmid:25762077.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:25762077.finding: Authors' reply defending the controlled laboratory design and its relevance to everyday evening device use.

pmid:33867308.authors: Duraccio KM, Zaugg KK, Blackburn RC, et al.
pmid:33867308.title: Does iPhone night shift mitigate negative effects of smartphone use on sleep outcomes in emerging adults?
pmid:33867308.finding: iPhone Night Shift mode did not improve sleep outcomes vs normal phone use; among those sleeping >6.8 h, no phone before bed gave the best sleep.

pmid:28526259.authors: Figueiro MG, Steverson B, Heerwagen J, et al.
pmid:28526259.title: The impact of daytime light exposures on sleep and mood in office workers.
pmid:28526259.finding: High morning circadian-effective light was associated with shorter sleep onset latency, better sleep quality and stronger circadian entrainment, especially in winter.

pmid:25030030.authors: Gan Y, Yang C, Tong X, et al.
pmid:25030030.title: Shift work and diabetes mellitus: a meta-analysis of observational studies.
pmid:25030030.finding: Ever shift work was associated with 9% higher diabetes risk (OR 1.09), higher in men (1.37) and rotating shifts.

pmid:31684766.authors: Gao Y, Gan T, Jiang L, et al.
pmid:31684766.title: Association between shift work and risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of observational studies.
pmid:31684766.finding: Shift work was associated with higher type 2 diabetes risk (~10%), especially night and rotating shifts, with possible dose-response with years of exposure in women.

pmid:26251064.authors: Gaskins AJ, Rich-Edwards JW, Lawson CC, et al.
pmid:26251064.title: Work schedule and physical factors in relation to fecundity in nurses.
pmid:26251064.finding: No shift-work pattern was associated with time to pregnancy; working >40 h/week and heavy lifting were.

pmid:21193540.authors: Gooley JJ, Chamberlain K, Smith KA, et al.
pmid:21193540.title: Exposure to room light before bedtime suppresses melatonin onset and shortens melatonin duration in humans.
pmid:21193540.finding: Room light (<200 lux) before bedtime vs dim light delayed melatonin onset in 99% and shortened melatonin duration by ~90 min; room light during sleep hours suppressed melatonin >50% in 85% of trials.

pmid:32126861.authors: Green A, Barak S, Shine L, et al.
pmid:32126861.title: Exposure by males to light emitted from media devices at night is linked with decline of sperm quality and correlated with sleep quality measures.
pmid:32126861.finding: Evening and post-bedtime smartphone/tablet use correlated negatively with sperm motility, progressive motility and concentration.

pmid:31281097.title: Carcinogenicity of night shift work.
pmid:31281097.finding: IARC Monograph 124 classified night shift work as probably carcinogenic to humans (Group 2A), based on limited human evidence and sufficient animal evidence.

pmid:42318636.authors: Jiang Z, Dou Y, Lei Y, et al.
pmid:42318636.title: Mitochondrial Dysfunction Unravels the Potential Molecular Link Between Night Shift Work-Related Circadian Disruption and Elevated Blood Pressure in Human and Mouse Models.
pmid:42318636.finding: Simulated night-shift work in mice raised blood pressure with clock-gene disruption, mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress; in human night workers exposure duration tracked blood pressure and mitochondrial markers.

pmid:35286195.authors: Mason IC, Grimaldi D, Reid KJ, et al.
pmid:35286195.title: Light exposure during sleep impairs cardiometabolic function.
pmid:35286195.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:35286195.finding: One night of sleeping in 100 lux room light vs <3 lux raised night-time heart rate, lowered heart rate variability and increased next-morning insulin resistance.

pmid:28167499.authors: Mínguez-Alarcón L, Souter I, Williams PL, et al.
pmid:28167499.title: Occupational factors and markers of ovarian reserve and response among women at a fertility centre.
pmid:28167499.n: 313-473 women at a fertility centre (EARTH study)
pmid:28167499.finding: Women working evening/night/rotating shifts had 2.3 fewer mature oocytes retrieved after ovarian stimulation than day workers.

pmid:26858430.authors: Morris CJ, Purvis TE, Hu K, et al.
pmid:26858430.title: Circadian misalignment increases cardiovascular disease risk factors in humans.
pmid:26858430.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:26858430.finding: Three days of circadian misalignment raised 24-h blood pressure (+3.0/1.5 mmHg) and IL-6, CRP, resistin and TNF-alpha by 3-29%.

pmid:23118419.authors: Obayashi K, Saeki K, Iwamoto J, et al.
