pmid:23118419.title: Exposure to light at night, nocturnal urinary melatonin excretion, and obesity/dyslipidemia in the elderly: a cross-sectional analysis of the HEIJO-KYO study.
pmid:23118419.finding: Bedroom light ≥3 lux at night was associated with higher odds of obesity (OR 1.89) and dyslipidaemia (OR 1.72), independent of urinary melatonin.

pmid:31180469.authors: Park YM, White AJ, Jackson CL, et al.
pmid:31180469.title: Association of Exposure to Artificial Light at Night While Sleeping With Risk of Obesity in Women.
pmid:31180469.finding: Sleeping with a TV or light on was associated with gaining ≥5 kg (RR 1.17) and incident obesity (RR 1.33) over ~5.7 years.

pmid:31138694.authors: Phillips AJK, Vidafar P, Burns AC, et al.
pmid:31138694.title: High sensitivity and interindividual variability in the response of the human circadian system to evening light.
pmid:31138694.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:31138694.finding: Half-maximal melatonin suppression occurred at only ~25 lux of evening light; 10, 30 and 50 lux delayed melatonin onset by 22, 77 and 109 min; individual sensitivity varied over 10-fold.

pmid:24996495.authors: Reiter RJ, Tamura H, Tan DX, et al.
pmid:24996495.title: Melatonin and the circadian system: contributions to successful female reproduction.
pmid:24996495.finding: Follicular fluid melatonin exceeds blood levels and protects the oocyte from oxidative stress around ovulation; light at night suppresses melatonin and should be avoided.

pmid:19255424.authors: Scheer FA, Hilton MF, Mantzoros CS, et al.
pmid:19255424.title: Adverse metabolic and cardiovascular consequences of circadian misalignment.
pmid:19255424.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:19255424.finding: Eating and sleeping ~12 h out of phase lowered leptin 17%, raised glucose 6% despite 22% more insulin, reversed the cortisol rhythm and raised blood pressure; 3 of 8 had prediabetic postprandial glucose.

pmid:36854795.authors: Schöllhorn I, Stefani O, Lucas RJ, et al.
pmid:36854795.title: Melanopic irradiance defines the impact of evening display light on sleep latency, melatonin and alertness.
pmid:36854795.finding: At equal screen brightness, low-melanopic display light shortened sleep latency, reduced melatonin suppression and advanced melatonin onset vs high-melanopic light, dose-dependently.

pmid:37593770.authors: Singh S, Keller PR, Busija L, et al.
pmid:37593770.title: Blue-light filtering spectacle lenses for visual performance, sleep, and macular health in adults.
pmid:37593770.finding: Blue-light filtering spectacle lenses probably do not reduce eye strain; effects on sleep quality were indeterminate with mixed results and high risk of bias.

pmid:24901274.authors: Stocker LJ, Macklon NS, Cheong YC, et al.
pmid:24901274.title: Influence of shift work on early reproductive outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:24901274.finding: Shift work was associated with menstrual disruption (aOR 1.15) and infertility (OR 1.80, I² 94%); night shifts with early pregnancy loss (OR 1.29).

pmid:28162893.authors: Stothard ER, McHill AW, Depner CM, et al.
pmid:28162893.title: Circadian Entrainment to the Natural Light-Dark Cycle across Seasons and the Weekend.
pmid:28162893.finding: A summer weekend of camping achieved ~69% of the circadian advance of a full week; the biological night expanded in winter natural light.

pmid:30872663.authors: Teixeira KRC, Dos Santos CP, de Medeiros LA, et al.
pmid:30872663.title: Night workers have lower levels of antioxidant defenses and higher levels of oxidative stress damage when compared to day workers.
pmid:30872663.finding: Night workers had higher TBARS and hydrogen peroxide and lower total antioxidant capacity, catalase and SOD than day workers; social jetlag was not associated with these markers.

pmid:37977357.authors: Tian R, Yang T, Xiao C, et al.
pmid:37977357.title: Outdoor artificial light at night and male sperm quality: A retrospective cohort study in China.
pmid:37977357.finding: Each 100 nW/cm²/sr higher outdoor artificial light at night was associated with lower sperm motility, most strongly in men under 25.

pmid:29247501.authors: Torquati L, Mielke GI, Brown WJ, et al.
pmid:29247501.title: Shift work and the risk of cardiovascular disease. A systematic review and meta-analysis including dose-response relationship.
pmid:29247501.finding: Shift workers had 17% higher risk of any CVD event and 26% higher CHD morbidity; risk rose 7.1% per additional 5 years after the first 5 years.

pmid:27758828.authors: Travis RC, Balkwill A, Fensom GK, et al.
pmid:27758828.title: Night Shift Work and Breast Cancer Incidence: Three Prospective Studies and Meta-analysis of Published Studies.
pmid:27758828.finding: Night shift work was not associated with breast cancer (RR 0.99), even after 20 or 30+ years.

pmid:26606319.authors: van Maanen A, Meijer AM, van der Heijden KB, et al.
pmid:26606319.title: The effects of light therapy on sleep problems: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:26606319.finding: Light therapy improved sleep problems overall (g 0.39), circadian rhythm sleep disorders (g 0.41) and insomnia (g 0.47); effects small to medium, smaller in RCTs, with publication bias.

pmid:27115377.authors: Vetter C, Devore EE, Wegrzyn LR, et al.
pmid:27115377.title: Association Between Rotating Night Shift Work and Risk of Coronary Heart Disease Among Women.
pmid:27115377.finding: Longer duration of rotating night-shift work was associated with a statistically significant but small absolute increase in CHD risk, which waned after stopping shift work.

pmid:40736282.authors: Wang Y, He M, Ling X, et al.
pmid:40736282.title: Rotating shiftwork in men is linked to decreased fecundity, attributable primarily to sperm concentration and vitality: 24-month follow-up in 3425 males of PREBIC cohort.
pmid:40736282.finding: Rotating shift workers had 16% lower hazard of pregnancy within 1 year and ~11% lower sperm concentration and total count; fixed shift workers did not differ from day workers.

pmid:39070751.authors: Windred DP, Burns AC, Rutter MK, et al.
pmid:39070751.title: Personal light exposure patterns and incidence of type 2 diabetes: analysis of 13 million hours of light sensor data and 670,000 person-years of prospective observation.
pmid:39070751.finding: Brighter night-light exposure was associated with higher type 2 diabetes risk (HR 1.29, 1.39 and 1.53 for 50-70th, 70-90th and 90-100th percentiles vs darkest nights); authors disclose lighting-industry funding.

pmid:39405349.authors: Windred DP, Burns AC, Lane JM, et al.
pmid:39405349.title: Brighter nights and darker days predict higher mortality risk: A prospective analysis of personal light exposure in >88,000 individuals.
pmid:39405349.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:39405349.finding: Brighter day light was associated with lower all-cause mortality (aHR ~0.66-0.83 for top decile) and brighter night light with higher mortality (aHR 1.21-1.34 top decile) over 8 years.

pmid:23910656.authors: Wright KP Jr, McHill AW, Birks BR, et al.
pmid:23910656.title: Entrainment of the human circadian clock to the natural light-dark cycle.
pmid:23910656.finding: A week of camping with natural light only advanced the circadian clock (melatonin onset moved toward sunset) and reduced differences between late and early chronotypes.

pmid:25762078.title: Real life trumps laboratory in matters of public health.
pmid:25762078.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:25762078.finding: Letter arguing that the e-reader laboratory findings may not translate to real-life public-health relevance.

pmid:26502459.authors: Allen JG, MacNaughton P, Satish U, et al.
pmid:26502459.title: Associations of Cognitive Function Scores with Carbon Dioxide, Ventilation, and Volatile Organic Compound Exposures in Office Workers: A Controlled Exposure Study of Green and Conventional Office Environments.
pmid:26502459.finding: In a blinded chamber study, cognitive scores were 61% higher under low-VOC "Green" conditions and 101% higher with extra ventilation than under conventional conditions; VOCs and CO2 were independently associated with lower scores.

pmid:34297865.authors: Andersen C, Omelekhina Y, Rasmussen BB, et al.
pmid:34297865.title: Emissions of soot, PAHs, ultrafine particles, NO(x,) and other health relevant compounds from stressed burning of candles in indoor air.
pmid:34297865.finding: Chamber tests showed candles burning in a draught emit soot-dominated PM2.5, PAHs, ultrafine particles, NOx and formaldehyde, with wax and wick type strongly affecting soot and PAH emissions.

pmid:32162221.authors: Angulo Milhem S, Verriele M, Nicolas M, et al.
pmid:32162221.title: Does the ubiquitous use of essential oil-based products promote indoor air quality? A critical literature review.
pmid:32162221.finding: Essential-oil cleaning products and air fresheners are major indoor sources of terpenes, which react with ozone to form secondary pollutants including formaldehyde and fine particles.

pmid:37157132.authors: Arnold WA, Blum A, Branyan J, et al.
pmid:37157132.title: Quaternary Ammonium Compounds: A Chemical Class of Emerging Concern.
pmid:37157132.finding: Multi-institution review finding increased human QAC exposure since COVID-19 and suspected dermal, respiratory, developmental, reproductive and mitochondrial effects, plus antimicrobial-resistance concerns.

pmid:16514772.authors: Bush RK, Portnoy JM, Saxon A, et al.
pmid:16514772.title: The medical effects of mold exposure.
pmid:16514772.finding: AAAAI position paper: moulds cause allergic and well-defined diseases (asthma, rhinitis, ABPA, hypersensitivity pneumonitis), while many newer hypothesized mould illnesses remain unproven.

pmid:28858831.authors: Carignan CC, Mínguez-Alarcón L, Butt CM, et al.
pmid:28858831.title: Urinary Concentrations of Organophosphate Flame Retardant Metabolites and Pregnancy Outcomes among Women Undergoing in Vitro Fertilization.
pmid:28858831.finding: Women in the highest vs lowest quartile of summed urinary organophosphate flame retardant metabolites had 10% lower fertilization, 31% lower implantation, 41% lower clinical pregnancy and 38% lower live birth proportions per IVF cycle.

pmid:25838260.authors: Casas L, Espinosa A, Borràs-Santos A, et al.
pmid:25838260.title: Domestic use of bleach and infections in children: a multicentre cross-sectional study.
pmid:25838260.finding: Children in bleach-using homes had more influenza (RRR 1.20), recurrent tonsillitis (1.35) and any infection (1.18).

pmid:11555684.authors: Cherry N, Labrèche F, Collins J, et al.
pmid:11555684.title: Occupational exposure to solvents and male infertility.
pmid:11555684.finding: High solvent exposure was associated with motile sperm <12 million/mL (OR 3.83 in Montreal, 2.90 in a replication series); moderate exposure replicated in only one series.

pmid:18417551.authors: Cherry N, Moore H, McNamee R, et al.
pmid:18417551.title: Occupation and male infertility: glycol ethers and other exposures.
pmid:18417551.finding: High glycol ether exposure in the 3 months before the clinic visit was associated with low motile sperm count (adjusted OR 2.25, 95% CI 1.08-4.69); moderate exposure OR 1.46 (0.93-2.28).

pmid:7814250.title: Test of the linear-no threshold theory of radiation carcinogenesis for inhaled radon decay products.
pmid:7814250.finding: County lung cancer mortality fell with average home radon, which the author interpreted as failure of the linear no-threshold model.

pmid:39048064.authors: Cohen J, Hubbard H, Özkaynak H, et al.
pmid:39048064.title: Meta-analysis of soil and dust ingestion studies.
pmid:39048064.finding: Mean soil plus dust ingestion was about 36-68 mg/day in infants, 56-72 mg/day in young children and 12-32 mg/day in adolescents and adults.

pmid:37638367.title: The gas stove-childhood asthma kerfuffle: A teaching opportunity.
pmid:37638367.finding: Commentary arguing the gas stove-childhood asthma attributable fraction claim reflects questionable research practices and is not supported as causal.

pmid:19043916.title: A critique of the ACOEM statement on mold: undisclosed conflicts of interest in the creation of an "evidence-based" statement.
pmid:19043916.finding: Critique arguing the 2003 ACOEM mould statement was shaped by undisclosed litigation-related conflicts of interest.

pmid:31695112.title: Potted plants do not improve indoor air quality: a review and analysis of reported VOC removal efficiencies.
pmid:31695112.finding: Translating chamber data into clean air delivery rates showed 10-1000 potted plants per m2 of floor would be needed to match the VOC removal of normal building air exchange.

pmid:15613366.authors: Darby S, Hill D, Auvinen A, et al.
pmid:15613366.title: Radon in homes and risk of lung cancer: collaborative analysis of individual data from 13 European case-control studies.
pmid:15613366.finding: Lung cancer risk rose 16% per 100 Bq/m3 of usual radon (linear, no threshold); absolute risk to age 75 at 0/100/400 Bq/m3 was 0.4/0.5/0.7% for never-smokers and 10/12/16% for smokers.

pmid:34687283.authors: DeSesso JM, Harris SB, Scialli AR, et al.
pmid:34687283.title: Systematic assessment of quaternary ammonium compounds for the potential to elicit developmental and reproductive effects.
pmid:34687283.finding: Systematic assessment relying largely on unpublished guideline studies found no adverse developmental or reproductive effects of QACs at expected exposures and rated the positive mouse studies "not reliable".

pmid:34039757.authors: Ding M, Lawson C, Johnson C, et al.
pmid:34039757.title: Occupational exposure to high-level disinfectants and risk of miscarriage among nurses.
pmid:34039757.finding: Prospectively, occupational high-level disinfectant use was not associated with miscarriage (HR 0.84), except in pregnancies within 12 months of baseline use (HR 1.78).

pmid:9470891.authors: Doyle P, Roman E, Beral V, et al.
pmid:9470891.title: Spontaneous abortion in dry cleaning workers potentially exposed to perchloroethylene.
pmid:9470891.finding: Spontaneous abortion was more common in dry-cleaning machine operators (17.1%) than in non-operators (11.6%) and unexposed pregnancies (10.9%).

pmid:31626315.authors: Dumas O, Varraso R, Boggs KM, et al.
pmid:31626315.title: Association of Occupational Exposure to Disinfectants With Incidence of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Among US Female Nurses.
pmid:31626315.finding: Weekly occupational use of disinfectants to clean surfaces was associated with higher COPD incidence over 2009-2015.

pmid:17661925.authors: Fisk WJ, Lei-Gomez Q, Mendell MJ
pmid:17661925.title: Meta-analyses of the associations of respiratory health effects with dampness and mold in homes.
pmid:17661925.finding: Building dampness and mould were associated with 30-50% increases in respiratory and asthma outcomes (central ORs 1.34-1.75).

pmid:18726993.authors: Friborg JT, Yuan JM, Wang R, et al.
pmid:18726993.title: Incense use and respiratory tract carcinomas: a prospective cohort study.
pmid:18726993.finding: Long-term heavy incense use was associated with squamous cell carcinoma of the respiratory tract (RR 1.8) and upper respiratory tract cancers, but not with lung cancer overall.

pmid:40158504.authors: Garg A, Kashtan Y, Nicholson M, et al.
pmid:40158504.title: Exposure and health risks of benzene from combustion by gas stoves: A modelling approach in U.S. homes.
pmid:40158504.finding: Indoor-air modelling of the highest-emitting 5% of US gas stoves found benzene cancer risks above 1 in a million under medium-high use without ventilation; efficient vented hoods reduced exposure.

pmid:29950671.authors: Gibson EA, Stapleton HM, Calero L, et al.
pmid:29950671.title: Flame retardant exposure assessment: findings from a behavioral intervention study.
pmid:29950671.finding: One week of instructed house cleaning or hand-washing (then both) lowered some urinary flame-retardant metabolites and, in women with above-median baseline exposure, some hand-wipe levels, by about half in some cases.

pmid:20682476.authors: Goodman JE, Biesemeier JA, Johnson GT, et al.
pmid:20682476.title: Fecundability and serum PBDE concentrations in women.
pmid:20682476.finding: Letter (with author reply) disputing the CHAMACOS PBDE-fecundability analysis.

pmid:18425868.title: House dust mite control measures for asthma.
pmid:18425868.finding: Cochrane: chemical and physical house dust mite control (including mattress encasings) had no effect on asthma symptoms, peak flow or medication use (Cochrane has since flagged the review as outdated).

pmid:18001835.authors: Groves-Kirkby CJ, Denman AR, Phillips PS, et al.
pmid:18001835.title: Domestic radon remediation of UK dwellings by Sub-Slab Depressurisation: evidence for a baseline contribution from constructional materials.
pmid:18001835.finding: Sub-slab depressurisation brought all homes below 200 Bq/m3, with mitigation factors below 0.2 (over 80% reduction) in more than 75% of homes.

pmid:36612391.authors: Gruenwald T, Seals BA, Knibbs LD, et al.
pmid:36612391.title: Population Attributable Fraction of Gas Stoves and Childhood Asthma in the United States.
pmid:36612391.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
pmid:36612391.finding: Applying a meta-analytic OR of 1.34 to US gas-stove prevalence, 12.7% (95% CI 6.3-19.3%) of current childhood asthma was attributed to gas stove use.

pmid:20103495.authors: Harley KG, Marks AR, Chevrier J, et al.
pmid:20103495.title: PBDE concentrations in women's serum and fecundability.
pmid:20103495.finding: Higher serum PBDEs were associated with longer time to pregnancy (fecundability OR 0.5-0.7 for BDE-100, BDE-153 and the sum of four congeners), with no link to menstrual cycle characteristics.

pmid:25343780.authors: Hoffman K, Garantziotis S, Birnbaum LS, et al.
pmid:25343780.title: Monitoring indoor exposure to organophosphate flame retardants: hand wipes and house dust.
pmid:25343780.finding: Hand-wipe (not dust) TPHP and TDCIPP predicted their urinary metabolites (top vs bottom hand-wipe TPHP: DPHP 2.4-fold); urinary BDCIPP and DPHP were moderately to strongly reliable over 5 days (ICC 0.81 and 0.51).

pmid:25500365.title: Reproductive toxicology.
pmid:25500365.finding: Letter on behalf of the ADBAC and DDAC industry steering committees disputing the 2014 mouse QAC fertility study (with author reply).

pmid:17324975.authors: Howden-Chapman P, Matheson A, Crane J, et al.
pmid:17324975.title: Effect of insulating existing houses on health inequality: cluster randomised study in the community.
pmid:17324975.finding: Retrofitting insulation made homes warmer and drier (RH -2.3%) and halved reports of poor self-rated health, reduced wheeze (OR 0.57) and days off school and work.

pmid:18812366.authors: Howden-Chapman P, Pierse N, Nicholls S, et al.
pmid:18812366.title: Effects of improved home heating on asthma in community dwelling children: randomised controlled trial.
pmid:18812366.finding: Installing non-polluting, more effective heaters lowered NO2 and reduced school absence, doctor visits, sleep disturbed by wheezing and night cough, but did not significantly improve lung function.

pmid:33868951.authors: Hrubec TC, Seguin RP, Xu L, et al.
pmid:33868951.title: Altered toxicological endpoints in humans from common quaternary ammonium compound disinfectant exposure.
pmid:33868951.finding: QACs were detected in the blood of 80% of volunteers and blood QAC levels tracked higher inflammatory cytokines, lower mitochondrial function and altered sterol synthesis.

pmid:38756207.authors: Hurraß J, Heinzow B, Walser-Reichenbach S, et al.
pmid:38756207.title: AWMF mold guideline "Medical clinical diagnostics for indoor mold exposure" - Update 2023 AWMF Register No. 161/001.
pmid:38756207.finding: German AWMF guideline (2023 update) on medical diagnostics for indoor mould exposure.

pmid:29739653.authors: Ingle ME, Mínguez-Alarcón L, Carignan CC, et al.
pmid:29739653.title: The association between urinary concentrations of phosphorous-containing flame retardant metabolites and semen parameters among men from a fertility clinic.
pmid:29739653.finding: Associations between urinary OPFR metabolites and semen parameters were weak and inconsistent; BDCIPP was about 2-fold higher in summer samples.

pmid:32424407.authors: Ingle ME, Mínguez-Alarcón L, Carignan CC, et al.
pmid:32424407.title: Exploring reproductive associations of serum polybrominated diphenyl ether and hydroxylated brominated diphenyl ether concentrations among women undergoing in vitro fertilization.
pmid:32424407.finding: Contrary to earlier reports, an interquartile rise in serum BDE-153 was associated with higher implantation (RR 1.26), clinical pregnancy (1.32) and live birth (1.34); PBDE levels fell up to 80% between 2005 and 2016 recruits.

pmid:31726298.authors: Ingle ME, Watkins D, Rosario Z, et al.
pmid:31726298.title: An exploratory analysis of urinary organophosphate ester metabolites and oxidative stress among pregnant women in Puerto Rico.
pmid:31726298.finding: Interquartile rises in urinary OPE metabolites were associated with 12-21% higher 8-isoprostane and 18-19% higher 8-OHdG; metabolite ICCs were 0.51-0.60 across pregnancy.

pmid:22572111.authors: Johnson PI, Altshul L, Cramer DW, et al.
pmid:22572111.title: Serum and follicular fluid concentrations of polybrominated diphenyl ethers and in-vitro fertilization outcome.
pmid:22572111.finding: Detectable BDE-153 in follicular fluid was associated with failed embryo implantation (adjusted OR 10.0, 95% CI 1.9-52); serum correlated only moderately with follicular fluid levels.

pmid:37319002.authors: Kashtan YS, Nicholson M, Finnegan C, et al.
pmid:37319002.title: Gas and Propane Combustion from Stoves Emits Benzene and Increases Indoor Air Pollution.
pmid:37319002.finding: Gas and propane burners and ovens emitted 2.8-6.5 ug benzene per minute, 10-25 times more than electric coil or radiant stoves; induction and the food itself emitted none, and benzene spread to bedrooms.

pmid:38701214.authors: Kashtan Y, Nicholson M, Finnegan CJ, et al.
pmid:38701214.title: Nitrogen dioxide exposure, health outcomes, and associated demographic disparities due to gas and propane combustion by U.S. stoves.
pmid:38701214.finding: Modelling estimated that gas and propane stoves add 4.0 ppb to long-term NO2 exposure on average (75% of the WHO guideline), with four-fold higher exposure in homes under 800 ft2 and higher exposure in Black, Hispanic and Native households.

pmid:25695323.title: Notes from the field: Use of unvalidated urine mycotoxin tests for the clinical diagnosis of illness--United States, 2014.
pmid:25695323.finding: CDC/NIOSH warned that direct-to-consumer urine mycotoxin tests are unvalidated and were used to diagnose mould illness without evidence of building mould.

pmid:39653280.authors: Kirkpatrick ZA, Melin VE, Hrubec TC
pmid:39653280.title: Quaternary ammonium compound exposure causes infertility by altering endocrine signaling and gametogenesis.
pmid:39653280.finding: Oral QAC exposure lowered LH, FSH, progesterone and estrogen in mice and disrupted Sertoli cell metabolism and spermatogenesis.

pmid:36861764.authors: Klausen FB, Amidi A, Kjærgaard SK, et al.
pmid:36861764.title: The effect of air quality on sleep and cognitive performance in school children aged 10-12 years: a double-blinded, placebo-controlled, crossover trial.
pmid:36861764.journal: Int J Occup Med Environ Health
pmid:36861764.finding: Sleeping with added CO2 (2,000-3,000 ppm) or reduced ventilation did not affect next-morning cognitive performance.

pmid:15703527.authors: Krewski D, Lubin JH, Zielinski JM, et al.
pmid:15703527.title: Residential radon and risk of lung cancer: a combined analysis of 7 North American case-control studies.
pmid:15703527.finding: Odds of lung cancer were 1.11 at 100 Bq/m3, consistent with extrapolation from miner data, and higher with more accurate dosimetry.

pmid:28799918.authors: Lam J, Lanphear BP, Bellinger D, et al.
pmid:28799918.title: Developmental PBDE Exposure and IQ/ADHD in Childhood: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
pmid:28799918.finding: Navigation Guide review rated the evidence "sufficient" that developmental PBDE exposure lowers IQ: a 10-fold higher PBDE exposure was associated with 3.7 fewer IQ points (95% CI 0.83-6.56); evidence for ADHD was "limited".

pmid:33788856.authors: Lam J, Koustas E, Sutton P, et al.
pmid:33788856.title: Exposure to formaldehyde and asthma outcomes: A systematic review, meta-analysis, and economic assessment.
pmid:33788856.finding: Each 10 ug/m3 more formaldehyde was associated with higher odds of childhood asthma diagnosis (OR 1.20).

pmid:22304790.authors: Lawson CC, Rocheleau CM, Whelan EA, et al.
pmid:22304790.title: Occupational exposures among nurses and risk of spontaneous abortion.
pmid:22304790.finding: Self-reported exposure to sterilizing agents/disinfectants was associated with a 2-fold risk of late (12-20 week) spontaneous abortion; antineoplastic drugs with a 2-fold risk overall.

pmid:35081712.authors: Lebel ED, Finnegan CJ, Ouyang Z, et al.
pmid:35081712.title: Methane and NO(x) Emissions from Natural Gas Stoves, Cooktops, and Ovens in Residential Homes.
pmid:35081712.finding: Gas stoves leak 0.8-1.3% of their gas as unburned methane (three-quarters while off); NOx emissions scale with gas burned, and without a working hood a small kitchen can exceed the 1-h US NO2 standard (100 ppb) within minutes.

pmid:36263944.authors: Lebel ED, Michanowicz DR, Bilsback KR, et al.
pmid:36263944.title: Composition, Emissions, and Air Quality Impacts of Hazardous Air Pollutants in Unburned Natural Gas from Residential Stoves in California.
pmid:36263944.finding: Unburned gas contained benzene in 99% of samples (mean 0.7-12 ppmv by region); leaks from idle stoves could raise indoor benzene above California's 8-h reference level.

pmid:36581274.authors: Li Y, Luo D, Zhao X, et al.
pmid:36581274.title: Urinary concentrations of organophosphate esters in relation to semen quality: A cross-sectional study.
pmid:36581274.finding: Higher urinary DPHP and BMPP were associated with below-reference sperm count and OPE mixtures with lower motility and normal morphology.

pmid:38510536.authors: Li W, Goodman JE, Long C
pmid:38510536.title: Population attributable fraction of gas cooking and childhood asthma: What was missed?
pmid:38510536.finding: Gradient consultancy commentary, funded by the American Gas Association, arguing that the 12.7% population attributable fraction for gas cooking and childhood asthma is not valid.

pmid:37781844.authors: Li C, Li X, Zhang Z
pmid:37781844.title: Oxidative stress and pro-inflammatory cytokines following perchloroethylene exposure in young female dry-cleaning workers.
pmid:37781844.finding: Young female dry-cleaning workers with high plasma perchloroethylene had higher MDA, SOD and catalase and altered cytokines compared with controls.

pmid:41743804.authors: Li C, Guo X, Ren H, et al.
pmid:41743804.title: Urinary Organophosphate Esters and Increased Oxidative Stress in Healthy Older Adults: The China BAPE Study.
pmid:41743804.finding: Urinary OPE metabolites, singly and as a mixture, were associated with higher urinary 8-OHdG, 8-OHG and MDA in a Chinese panel study.

pmid:20064771.authors: McGwin G, Lienert J, Kennedy JI
pmid:20064771.title: Formaldehyde exposure and asthma in children: a systematic review.
pmid:20064771.finding: Pooled mostly cross-sectional studies: OR 1.17 (random effects) for childhood asthma per 10 ug/m3 formaldehyde.

pmid:37840862.authors: McHugh EG, Grady ST, Collins CM, et al.
pmid:37840862.title: Pulmonary, inflammatory, and oxidative effects of indoor nitrogen dioxide in patients with COPD.
pmid:37840862.finding: Low-level indoor NO2 (median 6.8 ppb) was not associated with CRP, urinary 8-OHdG or MDA, with suggestive lung-function decrements in severe COPD.

pmid:9698999.authors: McMartin KI, Chu M, Kopecky E, et al.
pmid:9698999.title: Pregnancy outcome following maternal organic solvent exposure: a meta-analysis of epidemiologic studies.
pmid:9698999.finding: Maternal occupational organic solvent exposure was associated with major malformations (OR 1.64) and a non-significant trend for spontaneous abortion (OR 1.25, 95% CI 0.99-1.58).

pmid:25483128.authors: Melin VE, Potineni H, Hunt P, et al.
pmid:25483128.title: Exposure to common quaternary ammonium disinfectants decreases fertility in mice.
pmid:25483128.finding: Six months of exposure to an ADBAC+DDAC quaternary ammonium disinfectant reduced fertility and fecundity in mice; QAC residues persisted in caging for months.

pmid:26582257.authors: Melin VE, Melin TE, Dessify BJ, et al.
pmid:26582257.title: Quaternary ammonium disinfectants cause subfertility in mice by targeting both male and female reproductive processes.
pmid:26582257.finding: ADBAC+DDAC exposure reduced corpora lutea and estrus time in females and sperm concentration and motility in males.

pmid:9585753.authors: Mendez D, Warner KE, Courant PN
pmid:9585753.title: Effects of radon mitigation vs smoking cessation in reducing radon-related risk of lung cancer.
pmid:9585753.finding: Modelling showed that for smokers, quitting reduces radon-related lung cancer risk more than radon mitigation does.

pmid:11089326.authors: Milton DK, Glencross PM, Walters MD
pmid:11089326.title: Risk of sick leave associated with outdoor air supply rate, humidification, and occupant complaints.
pmid:11089326.finding: Office workers in lower-ventilation areas (about 12 vs 24 L/s per person) had 53% more short-term sick leave.

pmid:27623734.authors: Mitro SD, Dodson RE, Singla V, et al.
pmid:27623734.title: Consumer Product Chemicals in Indoor Dust: A Quantitative Meta-analysis of U.S. Studies.
pmid:27623734.finding: US indoor dust consistently contains phthalates (highest), phenols, replacement flame retardants, fragrances and PFAS; several phthalates and flame retardants had the highest residential intakes.

pmid:15356304.authors: Morgan WJ, Crain EF, Gruchalla RS, et al.
pmid:15356304.title: Results of a home-based environmental intervention among urban children with asthma.
pmid:15356304.finding: A tailored, home-based programme targeting allergens and tobacco smoke reduced symptom days (3.39 vs 4.20 per 2 weeks) during and for a year after the intervention, with falls in dust-mite and cockroach allergen.

pmid:20655097.authors: Moro AM, Charão M, Brucker N, et al.
pmid:20655097.title: Effects of low-level exposure to xenobiotics present in paints on oxidative stress in workers.
pmid:20655097.finding: Painters with solvent biomarkers below exposure limits had higher MDA and antioxidant enzyme activities and lower thiols and ALA-D than unexposed controls.

pmid:20467865.title: Cancer effects of formaldehyde: a proposal for an indoor air guideline value.
pmid:20467865.finding: Argues that the WHO formaldehyde guideline of 0.1 mg/m3 (0.08 ppm) protects against nasal cancer, since nasal cytotoxicity has a non-linear dose-response and no human nasopharyngeal excess was seen below about 1 ppm average.

pmid:33022752.authors: Nussbaumer-Streit B, Mayr V, Dobrescu AI, et al.
pmid:33022752.title: Household interventions for secondary prevention of domestic lead exposure in children.
pmid:33022752.finding: Cochrane: household education and dust-control interventions did not lower children's blood lead (education MD -0.03 log units; environmental interventions also no clear effect).

pmid:41038314.authors: Pacheco Da Silva E, Varraso R, Fezeu LK, et al.
pmid:41038314.title: Longitudinal Associations Between Household Use of "Green" Cleaning Products and Asthma Symptoms.
pmid:41038314.finding: Persistent use of irritant/sprayed cleaning products was associated with more asthma symptoms and incidence over 2 years; "green" product use was also associated with asthma symptoms.

pmid:24329966.authors: Paulin LM, Diette GB, Scott M, et al.
pmid:24329966.title: Home interventions are effective at decreasing indoor nitrogen dioxide concentrations.
pmid:24329966.finding: Replacing the gas stove with electric cut median kitchen NO2 by 51% at 3 months; HEPA-plus-carbon purifiers cut it 27% immediately (20% at 3 months); a new range hood did not significantly lower NO2.

pmid:15075170.authors: Pilotto LS, Nitschke M, Smith BJ, et al.
pmid:15075170.title: Randomized controlled trial of unflued gas heater replacement on respiratory health of asthmatic schoolchildren.
pmid:15075170.finding: Replacing unflued gas heaters in schools lowered classroom NO2 (15.5 vs 47.0 ppb) and cut daytime and night-time asthma symptoms (RR about 0.3-0.45), without changing lung function.

pmid:12705451.title: Smoking as a confounder in ecologic correlations of cancer mortality rates with average county radon levels.
pmid:12705451.finding: Smoking-related cancers showed the same negative county-radon correlation while non-smoking cancers did not, indicating that confounding by smoking explains the ecological finding.

pmid:34426205.authors: Qian X, Wan Y, Wang A, et al.
pmid:34426205.title: Urinary metabolites of multiple volatile organic compounds among general population in Wuhan, central China: Inter-day reproducibility, seasonal difference, and their associations with oxidative stress biomarkers.
pmid:34426205.finding: After false-discovery adjustment, 16 urinary VOC metabolites were positively associated with urinary 8-OHdG and 8-OHG and four with HNE-mercapturic acid.

pmid:23144822.authors: Quansah R, Jaakkola MS, Hugg TT, et al.
pmid:23144822.title: Residential dampness and molds and the risk of developing asthma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:23144822.finding: Dampness and mould were associated with new-onset asthma (summary estimates 1.27-1.48), strongest for mould odour (1.73).

pmid:40314347.authors: Que DE, den Ouden F, Bosschaerts S, et al.
pmid:40314347.title: Trends of Organophosphate Ester Flame Retardant Metabolites in Age- and Sex-Stratified Pooled Australian Urine Samples from the Past Decade (2012-2023).
pmid:40314347.finding: Most OPFR metabolites were stable or rising over the decade, and mean exposures were below derived no-effect levels.

pmid:33770624.authors: Rodgers KM, Bennett D, Moran R, et al.
pmid:33770624.title: Do flame retardant concentrations change in dust after older upholstered furniture is replaced?
pmid:33770624.n: California homes replacing pre-2014 upholstered furniture
pmid:33770624.finding: Replacing older upholstered furniture, or only its foam, with TB117-2013 products lowered dust PBDEs and chlorinated and aryl organophosphate flame retardants in nearly all homes over 6-18 months.

pmid:34068014.authors: Romero Starke K, Friedrich S, Schubert M, et al.
pmid:34068014.title: Are Healthcare Workers at an Increased Risk for Obstructive Respiratory Diseases Due to Cleaning and Disinfection Agents? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
pmid:34068014.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
pmid:34068014.finding: Healthcare workers exposed to cleaning/disinfection agents had higher new-onset asthma risk (bleach ES 2.44, glutaraldehyde 1.91); all studies were at high risk of bias.

pmid:23008272.authors: Satish U, Mendell MJ, Shekhar K, et al.
pmid:23008272.title: Is CO2 an indoor pollutant? Direct effects of low-to-moderate CO2 concentrations on human decision-making performance.
pmid:23008272.finding: Pure CO2 at 1,000 and 2,500 ppm (vs 600 ppm) reduced decision-making scores on six and seven of nine scales in 2.5-h blinded sessions.

pmid:25715323.authors: Sauni R, Verbeek JH, Uitti J, et al.
pmid:25715323.title: Remediating buildings damaged by dampness and mould for preventing or reducing respiratory tract symptoms, infections and asthma.
pmid:25715323.finding: Cochrane: repairing mould-damaged houses and offices reduced wheeze (OR 0.64) and respiratory infections in adults (moderate to very low quality); school remediation evidence was inconsistent.

pmid:31240239.authors: Scully RR, Basner M, Nasrini J, et al.
pmid:31240239.title: Effects of acute exposures to carbon dioxide on decision making and cognition in astronaut-like subjects.
pmid:31240239.finding: Acute CO2 at 600-5,000 ppm showed no clear dose-response on decision-making or cognition, conflicting with earlier chamber studies.

pmid:42398761.authors: Sehgal AR, Schuellerman P, Dolata J, et al.
pmid:42398761.title: Asthma Control Before and After Changing Gas Stoves to Electric Stoves.
pmid:42398761.finding: Uncontrolled before-after study: after gas stoves were replaced with electric ones, indoor NO2 fell from 21.0 to 6.3 ppb and Asthma Control Questionnaire scores improved from 2.6 to 1.5 within 2-3 months.

pmid:38879743.authors: Sehgal N, Morello-Frosch R, Padula AM, et al.
pmid:38879743.title: Mixture effects of prenatal exposure to polybrominated diphenyl ethers on urinary oxidative stress biomarkers in the Chemicals in Our Bodies cohort.
pmid:38879743.finding: Higher second-trimester serum PBDE mixtures were associated with higher urinary 8-iso-PGF2alpha and related isoprostane metabolites.

pmid:22402423.authors: Sethi TK, El-Ghamry MN, Kloecker GH
pmid:22402423.title: Radon and lung cancer.
pmid:22402423.finding: Radon is the second leading cause of lung cancer; alpha-particle DNA damage via reactive oxygen species is a proposed mechanism and a shared pathway with tobacco smoke; US EPA action level 4 pCi/L.

pmid:32004881.authors: Sjödin A, Mueller JF, Jones R, et al.
pmid:32004881.title: Serum elimination half-lives adjusted for ongoing exposure of tri-to hexabrominated diphenyl ethers: Determined in persons moving from North America to Australia.
pmid:32004881.finding: In a person moving from North America to lower-exposure Australia, serum elimination half-lives were about 0.9 (BDE-28), 1.2 (BDE-47), 1.0 (BDE-99), 2.2 (BDE-100) and 4.1 years (BDE-153).

pmid:22431564.authors: Snijder CA, te Velde E, Roeleveld N, et al.
pmid:22431564.title: Occupational exposure to chemical substances and time to pregnancy: a systematic review.
pmid:22431564.finding: Occupational lead and pesticides showed strong indications of longer time to pregnancy; evidence for organic solvents and other metals was equivocal.

pmid:26452168.authors: Strøm-Tejsen P, Zukowska D, Wargocki P, et al.
pmid:26452168.title: The effects of bedroom air quality on sleep and next-day performance.
pmid:26452168.finding: Lowering bedroom CO2 from about 2,400-2,600 ppm to 660-835 ppm by ventilation improved actigraphic sleep quality, next-day sleepiness and a logical-thinking test.

pmid:21204989.authors: Sundell J, Levin H, Nazaroff WW, et al.
pmid:21204989.title: Ventilation rates and health: multidisciplinary review of the scientific literature.
pmid:21204989.finding: Higher office ventilation (up to about 25 L/s per person) is associated with fewer sick building symptoms; home ventilation above 0.5 air changes per hour was linked to fewer allergic manifestations in Nordic children.

pmid:29451393.authors: Svanes Ø, Bertelsen RJ, Lygre SHL, et al.
pmid:29451393.title: Cleaning at Home and at Work in Relation to Lung Function Decline and Airway Obstruction.
pmid:29451393.journal: Am J Respir Crit Care Med
pmid:29451393.finding: Women who cleaned at home (FEV1 decline -22.1 vs -18.5 mL/yr) or worked as cleaners (-22.4 mL/yr) lost lung function faster, with sprays and other agents both implicated; no association in men.

pmid:3228067.authors: Welch LS, Schrader SM, Turner TW, et al.
pmid:3228067.title: Effects of exposure to ethylene glycol ethers on shipyard painters: II. Male reproduction.
pmid:3228067.finding: Shipyard painters exposed to 2-ethoxyethanol and 2-methoxyethanol had more oligospermia and azoospermia and lower sperm counts.

lifestyle:eia-who2009mould.authors: World Health Organization Regional Office for Europe
lifestyle:eia-who2009mould.title: WHO guidelines for indoor air quality: dampness and mould
lifestyle:eia-who2009mould.finding: The most important means of avoiding adverse health effects is preventing or minimising persistent dampness and microbial growth on interior surfaces and in building structures.

lifestyle:eia-who2009radon.title: WHO handbook on indoor radon: a public health perspective
lifestyle:eia-who2009radon.finding: Public-health handbook for national radon programmes; indoor radon causes a substantial number of lung cancers in the general population.

lifestyle:eia-who2010indoor.authors: World Health Organization Regional Office for Europe
lifestyle:eia-who2010indoor.title: WHO guidelines for indoor air quality: selected pollutants (benzene, carbon monoxide, formaldehyde, naphthalene, nitrogen dioxide, PAHs, radon, trichloroethylene, tetrachloroethylene)
lifestyle:eia-who2010indoor.finding: WHO indoor air guidelines for nine pollutants commonly found indoors at levels of health concern, including formaldehyde, NO2, benzene and radon.

lifestyle:eia-who2021aqg.title: WHO global air quality guidelines: particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10), ozone, nitrogen dioxide, sulfur dioxide and carbon monoxide
lifestyle:eia-who2021aqg.finding: 2021 update lowering air quality guideline levels, including for PM2.5 and NO2, based on evidence of harm at lower concentrations than previously understood.

lifestyle:eia-whoradonfs.title: Radon and health (fact sheet)
lifestyle:eia-whoradonfs.finding: WHO recommends a national reference level of 100 Bq/m3 (not above 300 Bq/m3 where that is unachievable); radon causes 3-14% of lung cancers and risk rises about 16% per 100 Bq/m3.

pmid:24429203.authors: Wong GW, Brunekreef B, Ellwood P, et al.
pmid:24429203.title: Cooking fuels and prevalence of asthma: a global analysis of phase three of the International Study of Asthma and Allergies in Childhood (ISAAC).
pmid:24429203.finding: Open-fire cooking was associated with wheeze and asthma symptoms (OR 1.78 in 6-7-year-olds), while gas cooking was not clearly associated with asthma in the global analysis.

pmid:16541737.authors: Yamaguchi T, Nakajima D, Ezoe Y, et al.
pmid:16541737.title: Measurement of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in new residential buildings and VOCs behavior over time.
pmid:16541737.finding: VOCs such as toluene, hexane, MEK and pinene were highest at first occupancy of new homes and declined over the following year.

pmid:32080892.authors: Yu L, Wang B, Cheng M, et al.
pmid:32080892.title: Association between indoor formaldehyde exposure and asthma: A systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.
pmid:32080892.finding: Each 10 ug/m3 increase in indoor formaldehyde was associated with 10% higher childhood asthma risk (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.00-1.21).

pmid:27750136.authors: Yuan Y, Meeker JD, Ferguson KK
pmid:27750136.title: Serum polybrominated diphenyl ether (PBDE) concentrations in relation to biomarkers of oxidative stress and inflammation: The National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2003-2004.
pmid:27750136.finding: Serum PBDEs showed no association with oxidative stress biomarkers and only small positive associations of BDE-153 with alkaline phosphatase and neutrophil count.

pmid:26825447.authors: Zhang X, Wargocki P, Lian Z, et al.
pmid:26825447.title: Effects of exposure to carbon dioxide and bioeffluents on perceived air quality, self-assessed acute health symptoms, and cognitive performance.
pmid:26825447.finding: Adding pure CO2 up to 3,000 ppm had no effect on cognition or symptoms, but reduced ventilation (bioeffluents with CO2 at 3,000 ppm) increased headache, fatigue and sleepiness and slowed some tasks.

pmid:17585104.authors: Zock JP, Plana E, Jarvis D, et al.
pmid:17585104.title: The use of household cleaning sprays and adult asthma: an international longitudinal study.
pmid:17585104.journal: Am J Respir Crit Care Med
pmid:17585104.finding: Weekly use of household cleaning sprays was associated with new asthma symptoms or medication (RR 1.49) and wheeze (RR 1.39), with a dose-response; glass, furniture and air-freshener sprays drove the risk.

pmid:41479821.authors: Aamir AB, Latif R, Sorath F, et al.
pmid:41479821.title: Acute kidney injury induced by topical hair straightening products: A systematic review.
pmid:41479821.finding: Systematic review of acute kidney injury after hair straightening (formaldehyde, glycolic and glyoxylic acid products): median onset 2 days, 6 needed dialysis, all recovered.

pmid:35917669.authors: Adhikari S, Kumar R, Driver EM, et al.
pmid:35917669.title: Mass trends of parabens, triclocarban and triclosan in Arizona wastewater collected after the 2017 FDA ban on antimicrobials and during the COVID-19 pandemic.
pmid:35917669.finding: Arizona wastewater mass loads of triclosan fell 89% and triclocarban 80% after the 2017 FDA ban, while paraben loads rose 72%.

pmid:17683018.authors: Aiello AE, Larson EL, Levy SB
pmid:17683018.title: Consumer antibacterial soaps: effective or just risky?
pmid:17683018.finding: Systematic review: consumer soaps with 0.1-0.45% triclosan were no more effective than plain soap at preventing infectious symptoms or reducing hand bacteria; lab data showed cross-resistance to antibiotics.

pmid:19686543.authors: Allmyr M, Panagiotidis G, Sparve E, et al.
pmid:19686543.title: Human exposure to triclosan via toothpaste does not change CYP3A4 activity or plasma concentrations of thyroid hormones.
pmid:19686543.finding: Triclosan toothpaste raised plasma triclosan from 0.009-0.81 to 26-296 ng/g without changing CYP3A4 activity or thyroid hormones.

pmid:41022397.authors: Bailey JT, Chang CJ, Gaston SA, et al.
pmid:41022397.title: Use of hair straighteners and chemical relaxers and incidence of non-reproductive cancers.
pmid:41022397.finding: Straightener/relaxer use was associated with thyroid (HR 1.71) and pancreatic cancer (HR 2.66) and possibly NHL, with little dose-response across many cancer types tested.

pmid:37821068.authors: Bertrand KA, Delp L, Coogan PF, et al.
pmid:37821068.title: Hair relaxer use and risk of uterine cancer in the Black Women's Health Study.
pmid:37821068.finding: Heavy hair-relaxer use was not associated with uterine cancer overall (HR 1.18, CI 0.81-1.71), but in postmenopausal women heavy and 20+ year use went with HRs of 1.64-1.71.

pmid:30622332.authors: Boronow KE, Brody JG, Schaider LA, et al.
pmid:30622332.title: Serum concentrations of PFASs and exposure-related behaviors in African American and non-Hispanic white women.
pmid:30622332.finding: Flossing with Oral-B Glide was associated with higher serum PFHxS; Glide and competitor flosses contained fluorine; interviews came years after blood draw.

pmid:20056562.authors: Calafat AM, Ye X, Wong LY, et al.
pmid:20056562.title: Urinary concentrations of four parabens in the U.S. population: NHANES 2005-2006.
pmid:20056562.finding: Methylparaben was detected in 99.1% and propylparaben in 92.7% of US urine samples (medians 63.5 and 8.7 ug/L); levels were higher in women and non-Hispanic Black participants, consistent with personal-care product use.

pmid:35347794.title: Modification of cleaning product formulations could improve indoor air quality.
pmid:35347794.finding: Indoor chemistry modelling: terpene fragrances in cleaning products react with ozone to raise formaldehyde and particles for hours after a 10-minute cleaning, more when outdoor ozone is higher.

pmid:36245087.authors: Chang CJ, O'Brien KM, Keil AP, et al.
pmid:36245087.title: Use of Straighteners and Other Hair Products and Incident Uterine Cancer.
pmid:36245087.finding: Straightener use in the prior 12 months was associated with higher uterine cancer incidence (HR 1.80), 2.55 with more than 4 uses a year; dyes and perms were not associated.

pmid:36746253.authors: Dairkee SH, Moore DH, Luciani MG, et al.
pmid:36746253.title: Reduction of daily-use parabens and phthalates reverses accumulation of cancer-associated phenotypes within disease-free breast tissue of study subjects.
pmid:36746253.n: healthy women in a 28-day product-reduction regimen (REDUXE)
pmid:36746253.finding: Stopping paraben- and phthalate-containing products lowered urinary parabens and phthalates and was reported to reverse cancer-associated gene-expression patterns in breast fine-needle aspirates; uncontrolled, surrogate-marker study.

pmid:14745841.authors: Darbre PD, Aljarrah A, Miller WR, et al.
pmid:14745841.title: Concentrations of parabens in human breast tumours.
pmid:14745841.finding: Parabens averaged 20.6 ng/g in 20 breast tumours, mostly methylparaben; no normal-tissue comparison was made.

pmid:11781161.title: Exposure assessment to dioxins from the use of tampons and diapers.
pmid:11781161.finding: Trace dioxins in tampons give exposures 13,000-240,000 times lower than dietary dioxin intake.

pmid:26233661.authors: Dewalque L, Pirard C, Vandepaer S, et al.
pmid:26233661.title: Temporal variability of urinary concentrations of phthalate metabolites, parabens and benzophenone-3 in a Belgian adult population.
pmid:26233661.n: 32 adults, 11 spot urines each over 4 months
pmid:26233661.finding: A single spot urine reasonably represented 4-month exposure for parabens, benzophenone-3 and monoethyl phthalate, but not for DEHP metabolites.

pmid:26332456.authors: Diepgen TL, Ofenloch R, Bruze M, et al.
pmid:26332456.title: Prevalence of fragrance contact allergy in the general population of five European countries: a cross-sectional study.
pmid:26332456.finding: Clinically relevant fragrance contact allergy was estimated at 1.9% (conservative 0.8%) of the general population, about twice as common in women.

pmid:31532304.authors: Ding N, Batterman S, Park SK
pmid:31532304.title: Exposure to Volatile Organic Compounds and Use of Feminine Hygiene Products Among Reproductive-Aged Women in the United States.
pmid:31532304.finding: Frequent vaginal douching (2+ times a month) was associated with 81% higher blood 1,4-dichlorobenzene, and feminine powder with 36% higher ethylbenzene.

pmid:22398195.authors: Dodson RE, Nishioka M, Standley LJ, et al.
pmid:22398195.title: Endocrine disruptors and asthma-associated chemicals in consumer products.
pmid:22398195.finding: Consumer products, including 'alternative' ones, contained 55 endocrine-disrupting or asthma-associated compounds, highest in fragranced products and sunscreens; many were not on the label.

pmid:33682414.authors: Downs CA, DiNardo JC, Stien D, et al.
pmid:33682414.title: Benzophenone Accumulates over Time from the Degradation of Octocrylene in Commercial Sunscreen Products.
pmid:33682414.finding: Octocrylene-containing sunscreens contained benzophenone (mean 39 mg/kg) that rose to a mean 75 mg/kg after accelerated ageing; the octocrylene-free product had none.

pmid:31797377.authors: Eberle CE, Sandler DP, Taylor KW, et al.
pmid:31797377.title: Hair dye and chemical straightener use and breast cancer risk in a large US population of black and white women.
pmid:31797377.finding: Permanent dye use was associated with 45% higher breast cancer risk in Black women and 7% in White women; straightener use HR 1.18 (CI 0.99-1.41) with a frequency trend.

pmid:42097300.authors: Ellison CA, Doyle PR, Haven CA, et al.
pmid:42097300.title: Integrating experimental data and mechanistic modeling to assess potential lead exposure from tampon use.
pmid:42097300.finding: Procter & Gamble scientists' model: under conservative assumptions, less than 1 ng (under 0.3%) of lead released from a tampon over 4 h would be available to vaginal tissue, as lead binds menstrual red cells and is reabsorbed by the tampon.

pmid:33035739.authors: Estill CF, Mayer A, Slone J, et al.
pmid:33035739.title: Assessment of triphenyl phosphate (TPhP) exposure to nail salon workers by air, hand wipe, and urine analysis.
pmid:33035739.finding: Post-shift urinary DPHP (1.35 vs 0.84 ug/g creatinine pre-shift) and hand-wipe TPHP rose over the workday and correlated, pointing to dermal uptake in technicians.

lifestyle:epc-eu2014a.title: Commission Regulation (EU) No 358/2014 of 9 April 2014 amending Annexes II and V to Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 on cosmetic products
lifestyle:epc-eu2014a.journal: Official Journal of the European Union
lifestyle:epc-eu2014a.finding: Banned isopropyl-, isobutyl-, phenyl-, benzyl- and pentylparaben in cosmetics and restricted triclosan to specified products at up to 0.3% (0.2% in mouthwash).

lifestyle:epc-eu2014b.title: Commission Regulation (EU) No 1004/2014 of 18 September 2014 amending Annex V to Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 on cosmetic products
lifestyle:epc-eu2014b.journal: Official Journal of the European Union
lifestyle:epc-eu2014b.finding: Limited butyl- and propylparaben to 0.14% (as acid), barred them from leave-on nappy-area products for children under 3, and kept methyl/ethylparaben at 0.4% each, 0.8% for mixtures.

lifestyle:epc-eu2022.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/1176 of 7 July 2022 amending Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 as regards the use of certain UV filters in cosmetic products
lifestyle:epc-eu2022.journal: Official Journal of the European Union
lifestyle:epc-eu2022.finding: Capped benzophenone-3 at 6% in face, hand and lip products, 2.2% in body products and 0.5% when used only to protect the formulation, and octocrylene at 10% (9% in propellant sprays).

lifestyle:epc-eu2023.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/1545 of 26 July 2023 amending Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 as regards labelling of fragrance allergens in cosmetic products
lifestyle:epc-eu2023.journal: Official Journal of the European Union
lifestyle:epc-eu2023.finding: Requires about 80 fragrance allergens to be named on labels above 0.001% in leave-on and 0.01% in rinse-off products, with transition to 2026 (placing on market) and 2028 (availability).

lifestyle:epc-eu2024.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/996 of 3 April 2024 amending Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 as regards the use of Vitamin A, Alpha-Arbutin and Arbutin and certain substances with potential endocrine disrupting properties in cosmetic products
lifestyle:epc-eu2024.journal: Official Journal of the European Union
lifestyle:epc-eu2024.finding: Prohibited the UV filter 4-methylbenzylidene camphor (from 2025-2026) and further restricted triclosan and triclocarban, including excluding them from mouthwash.

pmid:38364603.authors: Farooq H, Mhatre P, Aggarwal R, et al.
pmid:38364603.title: A systematic review of association between use of hair products and benign and malignant gynecological conditions.
pmid:38364603.journal: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
pmid:38364603.finding: Systematic review: evidence on hair products and gynaecological conditions is insufficient to determine whether a positive association exists; noted permanent dye breast cancer RR 1.08 and relaxer-fibroid and relaxer-fecundability associations.

lifestyle:epc-fda2016.title: Safety and Effectiveness of Consumer Antiseptics; Topical Antimicrobial Drug Products for Over-the-Counter Human Use. Final rule. 81 FR 61106
lifestyle:epc-fda2016.finding: Found 19 consumer antiseptic wash ingredients, including triclosan and triclocarban, not generally recognized as safe and effective, effective September 2017; deferred benzalkonium chloride, benzethonium chloride and chloroxylenol.

lifestyle:epc-fda2019.title: Sunscreen Drug Products for Over-the-Counter Human Use; Proposed Rule. 84 FR 6204
lifestyle:epc-fda2019.finding: Proposed only zinc oxide and titanium dioxide as generally recognized as safe and effective, PABA and trolamine salicylate as not, and 12 organic filters including oxybenzone and avobenzone as needing more data; blood levels under 0.5 ng/mL would waive carcinogenicity studies.

lifestyle:epc-fda2025pfas.title: FDA Finds Insufficient Data to Determine Safety of PFAS in Cosmetic Products (Report on the Use of PFAS in Cosmetic Products and Associated Risks)
lifestyle:epc-fda2025pfas.finding: Under MoCRA, FDA found 51 PFAS in 1,744 cosmetic formulations; of the 25 most used, 5 appeared low concern, 1 had a potential safety concern, and for most safety could not be established because toxicology data were incomplete.

lifestyle:epc-fda2026hair.authors: US Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs / FDA
lifestyle:epc-fda2026hair.title: Use of Formaldehyde and Formaldehyde-Releasing Chemicals as an Ingredient in Hair Smoothing Products or Hair Straightening Products (RIN 0910-AI83), proposed rule: pending EO 12866 regulatory review
lifestyle:epc-fda2026hair.finding: FDA's proposed rule to ban formaldehyde and formaldehyde-releasing chemicals in hair smoothing/straightening products was received for White House review on 6 August 2026 and had not been concluded; no ban is yet in effect.

lifestyle:epc-fdamocra.title: Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act of 2022 (MoCRA)
lifestyle:epc-fdamocra.finding: MoCRA requires safety substantiation records, serious adverse event reporting within 15 business days, facility registration and product listing, mandates an FDA fragrance-allergen labelling rule (not yet issued) and a PFAS report (published December 2025).

lifestyle:epc-fdatampon.title: The Facts on Tampons and Tampon Safety
lifestyle:epc-fdatampon.finding: FDA commissioned an independent literature review of tampon contaminants (2024) and reports that its 2026 laboratory study found the amount of metals likely released during use is too small to cause harm.

pmid:31288179.authors: Ferguson KK, Lan Z, Yu Y, et al.
pmid:31288179.title: Urinary concentrations of phenols in association with biomarkers of oxidative stress in pregnancy: Assessment of effects independent of phthalates.
pmid:31288179.finding: Dichlorophenols, benzophenone-3, triclosan and some parabens were associated with higher urinary 8-OHdG and 8-isoprostane, but none was consistently selected once correlated phthalate metabolites were included.

pmid:37085016.title: The Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act of 2022: What dermatologists need to know.
pmid:37085016.finding: Overview for dermatologists of the US Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act of 2022.

pmid:35417610.authors: Geier J, Schubert S, Reich K, et al.
pmid:35417610.title: Contact sensitization to essential oils: IVDK data of the years 2010-2019.
pmid:35417610.finding: 8.3% of dermatitis patients tested reacted to at least one essential oil (ylang-ylang 3.9%, lemongrass 2.6%); masseurs and cosmeticians were at higher risk.

pmid:16433806.authors: Gonzalez H, Farbrot A, Larkö O, et al.
pmid:16433806.title: Percutaneous absorption of the sunscreen benzophenone-3 after repeated whole-body applications, with and without ultraviolet irradiation.
pmid:16433806.finding: Volunteers excreted 1.2-8.7% of applied BP-3 in urine and were still excreting it 5 days after the last application; UV exposure did not change absorption.

pmid:28632490.authors: Halden RU, Lindeman AE, Aiello AE, et al.
pmid:28632490.title: The Florence Statement on Triclosan and Triclocarban.
pmid:28632490.finding: Florence Statement: triclosan and triclocarban are persistent, bioaccumulative endocrine disruptors without demonstrated benefit in most consumer uses; antimicrobials should be used only where they provide evidence-based health benefit.

pmid:26602792.authors: Han C, Lim YH, Hong YC
pmid:26602792.title: Ten-year trends in urinary concentrations of triclosan and benzophenone-3 in the general U.S. population from 2003 to 2012.
pmid:26602792.finding: Urinary triclosan trended down and BP-3 up after 2005-2006; higher income groups had higher levels of both; BP-3 was higher in women and non-Hispanic Whites.

pmid:36178710.authors: Harris KJ, Munoz G, Woo V, et al.
pmid:36178710.title: Targeted and Suspect Screening of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances in Cosmetics and Personal Care Products.
pmid:36178710.finding: Polyfluoroalkyl phosphate esters (PAPs) were found in 99.7% of products, sometimes at very high levels, with lower PFCAs and PFSAs.

pmid:14745840.title: Significance of the detection of esters of p-hydroxybenzoic acid (parabens) in human breast tumours.
pmid:14745840.finding: Editorial accompanying the Darbre paper discussing its design and what can and cannot be inferred from finding parabens in tumours, explicitly not the cause of the tumours.

pmid:29705122.authors: Helm JS, Nishioka M, Brody JG, et al.
pmid:29705122.title: Measurement of endocrine disrupting and asthma-associated chemicals in hair products used by Black women.
pmid:29705122.finding: Hair products used by Black women contained parabens, diethyl phthalate, nonylphenols, cyclosiloxanes and fragrances, mostly unlabelled; children's relaxers contained chemicals restricted in California or the EU.

pmid:39828620.authors: Hernandez AM, Smith SJ, Vahora MS, et al.
pmid:39828620.title: Systematic Review of the Epidemiology of Hair Relaxer Use and Hormone-Sensitive Reproductive Outcomes Among Black Adult Women in the United States.
pmid:39828620.finding: Systematic review by a private risk-consulting firm (Benchmark Risk Group, which funded it): weight of evidence does not support hair relaxers as a risk factor for breast, ovarian or uterine cancer in US Black women; no study characterised product chemicals.

pmid:35721761.authors: Homburg M, Rasmussen ÅK, Ramhøj L, et al.
pmid:35721761.title: The Influence of Triclosan on the Thyroid Hormone System in Humans - A Systematic Review.
pmid:35721761.finding: Systematic review of human studies: triclosan-thyroid associations were inconsistent in direction and it is not possible to conclude that current exposure affects thyroid function.

pmid:33249036.authors: Huang K, Zhang X, Wang B, et al.
pmid:33249036.title: Accurate assessment of parabens exposure in healthy Chinese female adults: Findings from a multi-pathway exposure assessment coupled with intervention study.
pmid:33249036.finding: Personal-care products supplied over 99% of paraben exposure; unadjusted spot-urine intraclass correlations were poor (0.13-0.30) and improved only after kinetic modelling.

pmid:15788171.authors: Hutter HP, Wallner P, Moshammer H, et al.
pmid:15788171.title: Blood concentrations of polycyclic musks in healthy young adults.
pmid:15788171.finding: Galaxolide and tonalide were the polycyclic musks most often found in plasma (max 4,100 and 800 ng/L); body-lotion use and age predicted galaxolide; women had higher levels.

pmid:19520417.authors: Hutter HP, Wallner P, Moshammer H, et al.
pmid:19520417.title: Synthetic musks in blood of healthy young adults: relationship to cosmetics use.
pmid:19520417.finding: Polycyclic musks in blood were predicted by younger age and use of lotion and perfume; nitro musks were less frequent and lower than in the 1990s.

pmid:20056483.authors: Hutter HP, Wallner P, Hartl W, et al.
pmid:20056483.title: Higher blood concentrations of synthetic musks in women above fifty years than in younger women.
pmid:20056483.finding: Older women had higher plasma synthetic musks than younger women; galaxolide tracked frequent use of perfume, deodorant and shampoo.

pmid:28964967.authors: Iyer AP, Xue J, Honda M, et al.
pmid:28964967.title: Urinary levels of triclosan and triclocarban in several Asian countries, Greece and the USA: Association with oxidative stress.
pmid:28964967.finding: Triclosan was detected in 83% and triclocarban in 19% of samples; triclocarban correlated non-significantly with urinary 8-OHdG.

pmid:15191542.authors: Janjua NR, Mogensen B, Andersson AM, et al.
pmid:15191542.title: Systemic absorption of the sunscreens benzophenone-3, octyl-methoxycinnamate, and 3-(4-methyl-benzylidene) camphor after whole-body topical application and reproductive hormone levels in humans.
pmid:15191542.finding: Whole-body 10% BP-3, OMC and 4-MBC cream reached plasma levels up to 300 ng/mL BP-3; small hormone differences were unrelated to exposure.

pmid:17822133.authors: Janjua NR, Mortensen GK, Andersson AM, et al.
pmid:17822133.title: Systemic uptake of diethyl phthalate, dibutyl phthalate, and butyl paraben following whole-body topical application and reproductive and thyroid hormone levels in humans.
pmid:17822133.finding: Whole-body cream with diethyl phthalate, dibutyl phthalate and butylparaben produced serum peaks within hours but no short-term changes in reproductive or thyroid hormones.

pmid:18221342.authors: Janjua NR, Kongshoj B, Andersson AM, et al.
pmid:18221342.title: Sunscreens in human plasma and urine after repeated whole-body topical application.
pmid:18221342.finding: BP-3, 4-MBC and OMC appeared in plasma 1-2 h after first application; some 96-h plasma levels exceeded 24-h levels, suggesting accumulation.

pmid:40751801.authors: Jaskulak M, Cinkusz M, Franchuk K, et al.
pmid:40751801.title: Endocrine and Reproductive Health Considerations of Sunscreen UV Filters: Insights from a Comprehensive Review 2014-2024.
pmid:40751801.finding: Review of 2014-2024 human evidence: benzophenones associated with poorer sperm quality in some studies, weaker findings for ovarian reserve, mixed prenatal results; stresses balancing endocrine concerns with photoprotection.

pmid:15300720.title: The paper by Darbre et al. (2004) reports the measurement of parabens in 20 human breast tumors.
pmid:15300720.finding: Published letter criticising the Darbre et al. paraben-tumour study, with an author reply.

pmid:42218823.authors: Jin Y, Eppihimer M, Alam MS, et al.
pmid:42218823.title: Do metals in tampons pose a health risk? A toxicological risk assessment study.
pmid:42218823.finding: FDA laboratory study: 19 metals including trace lead, arsenic and cadmium were present, but releases under exaggerated extraction conditions gave margins of safety indicating negligible toxicological concern.

pmid:42001662.authors: Jovanovic N, Bright F, Thomsen C, et al.
pmid:42001662.title: Levers to decrease exposure to harmful chemicals: the case of Personal Care Products and cosmetics.
pmid:42001662.finding: Refraining from usual personal-care products for 5 days lowered urinary phenoxyacetic acid 64%, BPA 39%, methylparaben 30% and MEP 22%, but several chemicals remained detectable; authors argue regulation would be more efficient and fairer.

pmid:9793747.authors: Käfferlein HU, Göen T, Angerer J
pmid:9793747.title: Musk xylene: analysis, occurrence, kinetics, and toxicology.
pmid:9793747.finding: Musk xylene is lipophilic and persistent and found in milk, fat and blood, but there was no evidence of substantial human risk.

pmid:40451416.authors: Kang H, Kim S, Lee H, et al.
pmid:40451416.title: Parabens, bisphenols, and other environmental phenols exposure from cosmetics use in Korean adolescent girls: Findings from a 2-day intervention study.
pmid:40451416.finding: A 2-day cosmetics restriction did not lower chemical levels overall; excluding non-users at baseline, BPA fell 33% and benzophenones 12-23%.

pmid:34186503.authors: Kim JH, Kwak JM, Kang H
pmid:34186503.title: Web-based behavioral intervention to reduce exposure to phthalate metabolites, bisphenol A, triclosan, and parabens in mothers with young children: A randomized controlled trial.
pmid:34186503.finding: A web-based behavioural intervention lowered urinary MEHP, MEOHP, BPA, methylparaben and propylparaben versus written information (decreases of 4-28% after one month).

pmid:22612478.authors: Krause M, Klit A, Blomberg Jensen M, et al.
pmid:22612478.title: Sunscreens: are they beneficial for health? An overview of endocrine disrupting properties of UV-filters.
pmid:22612478.finding: Review of endocrine-disrupting properties of UV filters: rodent reproductive and thyroid effects, rapid skin absorption, BP-3 in 96% of US urine samples, few human outcome studies.

pmid:30933751.authors: Lamplugh A, Harries M, Xiang F, et al.
pmid:30933751.title: Occupational exposure to volatile organic compounds and health risks in Colorado nail salons.
pmid:30933751.finding: Formaldehyde exceeded the NIOSH recommended limit in one salon; modelled 20-year cancer risks from formaldehyde and benzene exceeded EPA benchmarks for technicians.

pmid:24117738.authors: Lundov MD, Opstrup MS, Johansen JD
pmid:24117738.title: Methylisothiazolinone contact allergy--growing epidemic.
pmid:24117738.finding: Methylisothiazolinone contact allergy rose from 2.0% to 3.7% of patch-tested patients in 2010-2012; cosmetics were the most common relevant source.

pmid:40239564.authors: Marcelis Q, Deconinck E, Rogiers V, et al.
pmid:40239564.title: Chemical characterization of menstrual and intimate care products: An extractables & leachables investigation.
pmid:40239564.n: menstrual and intimate care products from EU, US and China
pmid:40239564.finding: Of 55 extractable chemicals, 19 leached under realistic simulated use (fragrances, phthalates, plastic additives); menstrual sea sponges leached the most metals.

pmid:37743685.authors: Marroquin J, Kiomourtzoglou MA, Scranton A, et al.
pmid:37743685.title: Chemicals in menstrual products: A systematic review.
pmid:37743685.finding: Systematic review: phthalates, VOCs, parabens, phenols, fragrance chemicals and dioxins were detected in menstrual products; exposure per cycle and newer products (cups, period underwear) are unstudied.

pmid:31058986.authors: Matta MK, Zusterzeel R, Pilli NR, et al.
pmid:31058986.title: Effect of Sunscreen Application Under Maximal Use Conditions on Plasma Concentration of Sunscreen Active Ingredients: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
pmid:31058986.finding: Under maximal use (4 applications/day for 4 days), avobenzone, oxybenzone, octocrylene and ecamsule exceeded FDA's 0.5 ng/mL threshold on day 1; oxybenzone reached 169-210 ng/mL.

pmid:23469879.authors: Meeker JD, Cantonwine DE, Rivera-González LO, et al.
pmid:23469879.title: Distribution, variability, and predictors of urinary concentrations of phenols and parabens among pregnant women in Puerto Rico.
pmid:23469879.finding: Intraclass correlations ranged from 0.24 (BPA) to 0.62 (benzophenone-3), 0.47 for triclosan; sunscreen and lotion use predicted BP-3, lotion and cosmetics predicted parabens, liquid soap predicted triclosan.

pmid:26485058.authors: Mendelsohn E, Hagopian A, Hoffman K, et al.
pmid:26485058.title: Nail polish as a source of exposure to triphenyl phosphate.
pmid:26485058.finding: Painting nails with a polish containing 0.97% triphenyl phosphate raised its urinary metabolite DPHP about 7-fold 10-14 h later; gloves blocked most uptake, showing the route is dermal.

pmid:31077917.authors: Mínguez-Alarcón L, Chiu YH, Nassan FL, et al.
pmid:31077917.title: Urinary concentrations of benzophenone-3 and reproductive outcomes among women undergoing infertility treatment with assisted reproductive technologies.
pmid:31077917.finding: Benzophenone-3 was associated with higher implantation, pregnancy and live birth among women who did outdoor work, a pattern the authors attribute partly to residual lifestyle confounding.

pmid:30448212.authors: Mohammed YH, Holmes A, Haridass IN, et al.
pmid:30448212.title: Support for the Safe Use of Zinc Oxide Nanoparticle Sunscreens: Lack of Skin Penetration or Cellular Toxicity after Repeated Application in Volunteers.
pmid:30448212.n: human volunteers, 5 days of repeated application
pmid:30448212.finding: Zinc oxide nanoparticle sunscreen stayed on the skin surface and in furrows and did not penetrate or harm the viable epidermis.

pmid:26608183.authors: Moos RK, Angerer J, Dierkes G, et al.
pmid:26608183.title: Metabolism and elimination of methyl, iso- and n-butyl paraben in human urine after single oral dosage.
pmid:26608183.finding: After oral dosing, 80-85% of the captured paraben metabolites were excreted in urine within 24 h; parent methylparaben made up 17% of the dose, butylparabens 6-7%.

pmid:27901017.authors: Moos RK, Apel P, Schröter-Kermani C, et al.
pmid:27901017.title: Daily intake and hazard index of parabens based upon 24 h urine samples of the German Environmental Specimen Bank from 1995 to 2012.
pmid:27901017.finding: Back-calculated median intakes ranged from 1.1 (isobutylparaben) to 47.5 ug/kg/day (methylparaben); about 5% exceeded acceptable intake for individual parabens and the cumulative hazard index was 1.3 at the 95th percentile, under deliberately conservative assumptions.

pmid:36805158.authors: Mustieles V, Balogh RK, Axelstad M, et al.
pmid:36805158.title: Benzophenone-3: Comprehensive review of the toxicological and human evidence with meta-analysis of human biomonitoring studies.
pmid:36805158.finding: BP-3 and its metabolite BP-1 show estrogenic activity at human-relevant concentrations; North Americans' urinary BP-3 averages 10-20 times European and Asian levels; authors endorse EU limits but say people should not stop sunscreen and suggest inorganic filters for susceptible groups.

pmid:28886595.authors: Nassan FL, Coull BA, Gaskins AJ, et al.
pmid:28886595.title: Personal Care Product Use in Men and Urinary Concentrations of Select Phthalate Metabolites and Parabens: Results from the Environment And Reproductive Health (EARTH) Study.
pmid:28886595.finding: Cologne/perfume and deodorant use raised urinary monoethyl phthalate by 83% and 74%; sunscreen and hand/body lotion raised urinary parabens by 66-156% and 79-147%, with the largest effects for use within 6 h of urine collection.

pmid:39808082.authors: Ogunsina K, O'Brien KM, White AJ, et al.
pmid:39808082.title: Hair Straightener Use in Relation to Prevalent and Incident Fibroids in the Sister Study with a Focus on Black Women.
pmid:39808082.n: Sister Study, focus on 4,162 Black women
pmid:39808082.finding: Straightener use at ages 10-13 was associated with young-onset fibroids (ORs about 1.2-1.8); sensitivity analyses suggested possible bias from fibroid misclassification.

pmid:41554644.authors: Ogunsina K, Richardson KA, White A, et al.
pmid:41554644.title: Occupational exposures among hairdressers and the occurrence of hormone-related conditions.
pmid:41554644.finding: Ever working as a hairdresser was associated with endometriosis (HR 1.61) but not fibroids, breast, ovarian or uterine cancer overall.

pmid:24328919.authors: Pak VM, Powers M, Liu J
pmid:24328919.title: Occupational chemical exposures among cosmetologists: risk of reproductive disorders.
pmid:24328919.finding: Review of reproductive risks for cosmetologists exposed to dyes, solvents and nail products; calls for more research and workplace controls.

pmid:23168567.authors: Parlett LE, Calafat AM, Swan SH
pmid:23168567.title: Women's exposure to phthalates in relation to use of personal care products.
pmid:23168567.finding: Women who had used perfume in the prior 24 h had 2.92 times higher urinary monoethyl phthalate; hair spray, nail polish and deodorant also predicted MEP.

pmid:34560323.authors: Patti MA, Henderson NB, Gajjar P, et al.
pmid:34560323.title: Gestational triclosan exposure and infant birth weight: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:34560323.finding: Gestational triclosan was not clearly associated with birth weight (GA-adjusted -12 g, CI -29 to 5); inverse associations were stronger in higher-exposure populations.

pmid:22035353.authors: Pierce JS, Abelmann A, Spicer LJ, et al.
pmid:22035353.title: Characterization of formaldehyde exposure resulting from the use of four professional hair straightening products.
pmid:22035353.finding: Keratin smoothing treatments produced airborne formaldehyde up to 1.19 ppm during application; even a product labelled formaldehyde-free released formaldehyde-releasing chemicals; estimated exposures can meet or exceed occupational limits.

pmid:35959763.authors: Pütz KW, Namazkar S, Plassmann M, et al.
pmid:35959763.title: Are cosmetics a significant source of PFAS in Europe? product inventories, chemical characterization and emission estimates.
pmid:35959763.finding: PFAS emissions from cosmetics in Europe are significant but considerably lower than those from washing PFAS-coated textiles.

pmid:38810496.authors: Ragnarsdóttir O, Abou-Elwafa Abdallah M, Harrad S
pmid:38810496.title: Dermal bioavailability of perfluoroalkyl substances using in vitro 3D human skin equivalent models.
pmid:38810496.finding: In 3D human skin models, shorter-chain PFAS (C5-C8 acids, C4-C7 sulfonates) permeated skin while longer chains were retained in the skin tissue.

pmid:27583790.authors: Rehfeld A, Dissing S, Skakkebæk NE
pmid:27583790.title: Chemical UV Filters Mimic the Effect of Progesterone on Ca(2+) Signaling in Human Sperm Cells.
pmid:27583790.finding: 13 of 29 UV filters induced calcium signals in human sperm in vitro, nine by activating the CatSper channel like progesterone, some at nanomolar levels and additively in mixtures.

pmid:17612154.authors: Reiner JL, Wong CM, Arcaro KF, et al.
pmid:17612154.title: Synthetic musk fragrances in human milk from the United States.
pmid:17612154.finding: Synthetic musks (galaxolide, tonalide, musk xylene, musk ketone) were found in US breast milk; estimated infant intake was lower than for legacy POPs such as PCBs.

pmid:24310847.title: Triclosan/copolymer containing toothpastes for oral health.
pmid:24310847.finding: Cochrane review: triclosan/copolymer fluoride toothpaste reduced plaque, gingivitis and bleeding (moderate quality) and slightly reduced caries versus fluoride toothpaste, with no serious safety concerns over up to 3 years.

pmid:39197585.authors: Robert T, Tang E, Kervadec J, et al.
pmid:39197585.title: Hair-straightening cosmetics containing glyoxylic acid induce crystalline nephropathy.
pmid:39197585.finding: Topical glyoxylic acid, used in 'formaldehyde-free' straighteners, was absorbed, metabolised to oxalate and caused calcium-oxalate kidney injury in mice, explaining recurrent acute kidney injury in a patient.

pmid:31553406.title: Natural Does Not Mean Safe-The Dirt on Clean Beauty Products.
pmid:31553406.finding: JAMA Dermatology editorial arguing that 'natural' and 'clean' labels do not mean safe.

pmid:31688130.authors: Rundle CW, Hu S, Presley CL, et al.
pmid:31688130.title: Triclosen and Its Alternatives in Antibacterial Soaps.
pmid:31688130.n: survey of US antibacterial soap products
pmid:31688130.finding: After the FDA ban, benzalkonium chloride, chloroxylenol and (still) triclosan were the commonest antibacterials in soaps; the authors note antibacterial additives do not improve soap effectiveness.

pmid:29722171.authors: Samarasinghe SVAC, Krishnan K, Naidu R, et al.
pmid:29722171.title: Parabens generate reactive oxygen species in human spermatozoa.
pmid:29722171.finding: In vitro, parabens raised mitochondrial and cytosolic ROS in human sperm and reduced motility and viability in a chain-length-dependent way; methylparaben at clinically used concentrations raised ROS and oxidative DNA adducts but not DNA fragmentation.

pmid:16952905.authors: Sandborgh-Englund G, Adolfsson-Erici M, Odham G, et al.
pmid:16952905.title: Pharmacokinetics of triclosan following oral ingestion in humans.
pmid:16952905.finding: After 4 mg oral triclosan, plasma levels peaked within 1-3 h, the terminal plasma half-life was 21 h, and most was excreted within 24 h.

pmid:38963987.authors: Shearston JA, Upson K, Gordon M, et al.
pmid:38963987.title: Tampons as a source of exposure to metal(loid)s.
pmid:38963987.finding: All 16 metal(loid)s measured were detectable, with geometric means of 120 ng/g lead, 6.74 ng/g cadmium and 2.56 ng/g arsenic; no product category was consistently lower; absorption was not studied.

pmid:39571297.authors: Shearston JA, Upson K, Gordon M, et al.
pmid:39571297.title: Communicating risk in the face of data gaps: Toxic metals in tampons.
pmid:39571297.finding: The tampon-metal authors' published commentary on communicating risk when absorption data are missing.

pmid:36220432.authors: Shin MY, Choi JW, Lee S, et al.
pmid:36220432.title: Pharmacokinetics of transdermal methyl-, ethyl-, and propylparaben in humans following single dermal administration.
