pmid:36220432.finding: After a single whole-arm dermal application of labelled methyl-, ethyl- and propylparaben, terminal half-lives were 9.3-12.2 h, longer than after oral intake, with a larger share of unconjugated (active) paraben in blood.

pmid:30744632.authors: Singh J, Mumford SL, Pollack AZ, et al.
pmid:30744632.title: Tampon use, environmental chemicals and oxidative stress in the BioCycle study.
pmid:30744632.finding: Tampon users had non-significantly higher blood mercury (25%) and urinary isoprostane (about 5%) than non-users; no association with inflammation markers.

pmid:22721761.authors: Smith KW, Braun JM, Williams PL, et al.
pmid:22721761.title: Predictors and variability of urinary paraben concentrations in men and women, including before and during pregnancy.
pmid:22721761.n: fertility-clinic men and women with repeated urine samples
pmid:22721761.finding: Intraclass correlations for methyl- and propylparaben were 0.42-0.54, so a single urine sample reasonably ranked exposure over several months; concentrations were 3.8 times higher in African American participants.

pmid:27867426.title: Fragranced consumer products: exposures and effects from emissions.
pmid:27867426.finding: In a national online survey, 34.7% of adults reported health problems such as migraine or breathing difficulty from fragranced products; self-reported, cross-sectional.

pmid:34324339.title: Letter to the Editor Regarding Benzophenone Accumulates over Time from the Degradation of Octocrylene in Commercial Sunscreen Products.
pmid:34324339.finding: Published letter to the editor challenging the Downs et al. octocrylene-benzophenone study.

pmid:24618224.authors: Taylor KM, Weisskopf M, Shine J
pmid:24618224.title: Human exposure to nitro musks and the evaluation of their potential toxicity: an overview.
pmid:24618224.finding: Nitro musks reach people through skin, dust and inhaled fragrance; human data are limited and animal evidence on developmental effects is conflicting; further epidemiology is warranted.

pmid:35256558.authors: Tran JM, Comstock JR, Reeder MJ
pmid:35256558.title: Natural Is Not Always Better: The Prevalence of Allergenic Ingredients in "Clean" Beauty Products.
pmid:35256558.finding: 93.8% of 'clean' beauty products contained at least one potential contact allergen, most often fragrance/botanicals (82.9%).

pmid:24342029.authors: Turati F, Pelucchi C, Galeone C, et al.
pmid:24342029.title: Personal hair dye use and bladder cancer: a meta-analysis.
pmid:24342029.finding: Personal hair dye use was not associated with bladder cancer (RR 0.93; permanent dyes 0.92).

pmid:35302185.authors: Upson K, Shearston JA, Kioumourtzoglou MA
pmid:35302185.title: Menstrual Products as a Source of Environmental Chemical Exposure: A Review from the Epidemiologic Perspective.
pmid:35302185.finding: Epidemiological review of menstrual products as a route of chemical exposure, noting vaginal tissue's high permeability and the lack of exposure data.

pmid:31419348.authors: Uter W, Aalto-Korte K, Agner T, et al.
pmid:31419348.title: The epidemic of methylisothiazolinone contact allergy in Europe: follow-up on changing exposures.
pmid:31419348.finding: After EU restrictions, methylisothiazolinone contact allergy prevalence fell by half from 2015 (5.97%) to 2017 (2.96%), with fewer leave-on cosmetic culprits.

pmid:17971161.authors: van der Burg B, Schreurs R, van der Linden S, et al.
pmid:17971161.title: Endocrine effects of polycyclic musks: do we smell a rat?
pmid:17971161.finding: Polycyclic musks were very weakly estrogenic in vitro without clear effects in young rats or zebrafish, but showed anti-estrogenic, anti-androgenic and anti-progestagenic activity in cell assays.

pmid:31324419.authors: van Eijk AM, Zulaika G, Lenchner M, et al.
pmid:31324419.title: Menstrual cup use, leakage, acceptability, safety, and availability: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:31324419.finding: Menstrual cups showed no adverse effect on vaginal flora and leakage similar to or lower than pads or tampons; rare harms included toxic shock (5 reports) and IUD dislodgement.

pmid:25681860.authors: Vélez MP, Arbuckle TE, Fraser WD
pmid:25681860.title: Female exposure to phenols and phthalates and time to pregnancy: the Maternal-Infant Research on Environmental Chemicals (MIREC) Study.
pmid:25681860.finding: Women in the top triclosan quartile had lower fecundability (FOR 0.84) on a single post-conception urine; BPA was not associated and some phthalates pointed to shorter time to pregnancy.

pmid:40499412.authors: Wang Z, Yuan G, Sun M, et al.
pmid:40499412.title: Decorative cosmetics and skin care products contribute significantly to short-chain perfluoroalkyl carboxylates exposure.
pmid:40499412.finding: Skin-model permeation plus product concentrations suggested dermal intake of short-chain PFCAs from cosmetics may exceed dietary intake, and that cosmetics can contribute substantially to PFOA intake in regular users.

pmid:25435060.authors: Watkins DJ, Ferguson KK, Anzalota Del Toro LV, et al.
pmid:25435060.title: Associations between urinary phenol and paraben concentrations and markers of oxidative stress and inflammation among pregnant women in Puerto Rico.
pmid:25435060.finding: Per interquartile increase, urinary isoprostane was 17% higher for benzophenone-3, 27% for butylparaben and 20% for propylparaben; triclosan went with 31% higher IL-6.

pmid:22234483.authors: Wise LA, Palmer JR, Reich D, et al.
pmid:22234483.title: Hair relaxer use and risk of uterine leiomyomata in African-American women.
pmid:22234483.finding: Ever use of hair relaxers was associated with 17% higher incidence of uterine fibroids, with trends for frequency, duration and number of scalp burns.

pmid:37005071.authors: Wise LA, Wang TR, Ncube CN, et al.
pmid:37005071.title: Use of Chemical Hair Straighteners and Fecundability in a North American Preconception Cohort.
pmid:37005071.finding: Hair relaxer use was associated with slightly lower fecundability (current FR 0.81, CI 0.64-1.03; former 0.89, CI 0.81-0.98; 10+ years 0.71), with non-monotonic patterns.

pmid:32878860.authors: Zhang Y, Birmann BM, Han J, et al.
pmid:32878860.title: Personal use of permanent hair dyes and cancer risk and mortality in US women: prospective cohort study.
pmid:32878860.finding: Personal permanent hair dye use was not associated with most cancers or cancer mortality (solid cancers HR 0.98); slight increases for basal cell carcinoma and some hormone-receptor-negative breast and ovarian cancers with high cumulative dose.

pmid:36650165.authors: Zhivagui M, Hoda A, Valenzuela N, et al.
pmid:36650165.title: DNA damage and somatic mutations in mammalian cells after irradiation with a nail polish dryer.
pmid:36650165.finding: UV-nail-polish-dryer light caused ROS, 8-oxoguanine-type damage, mitochondrial dysfunction and dose-dependent ROS-signature mutations in mouse and human cells.

pmid:31731171.authors: Zhong Q, Peng M, He J, et al.
pmid:31731171.title: Association of prenatal exposure to phenols and parabens with birth size: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:31731171.finding: Prenatal triclosan, BP-3, BPA and parabens showed mostly non-significant and inconsistent associations with birth size.

pmid:32804211.authors: Bao W, Liu B, Rong S, et al.
pmid:32804211.title: Association Between Bisphenol A Exposure and Risk of All-Cause and Cause-Specific Mortality in US Adults
pmid:32804211.finding: Top vs bottom tertile of urinary BPA: all-cause mortality HR 1.49 (1.01-2.19), CVD mortality 1.46 (0.67-3.15), cancer mortality 0.98; 344 deaths.

pmid:35868575.authors: Beyer A, Schorgg P, Karavasiloglou N, et al.
pmid:35868575.title: Urinary phthalate concentrations and mortality risk: A population-based study
pmid:35868575.finding: Higher MBzP and MnBP (low-molecular-weight phthalate metabolites, not DEHP) were linked to higher mortality (top quartile HR 1.27 and 1.35).

pmid:23013111.authors: Blakey A, Ott K, Peters T, et al.
pmid:23013111.title: Anti-PVC advocacy disguised as science (Response to Carlstedt et al., PVC flooring is related to human uptake of phthalates in infants)
pmid:23013111.finding: Letter titled 'Anti-PVC advocacy disguised as science' disputing the Carlstedt PVC-flooring study; a reply was published.

pmid:25353625.authors: Bornehag CG, Carlstedt F, Jönsson BA, et al.
pmid:25353625.title: Prenatal phthalate exposures and anogenital distance in Swedish boys
pmid:25353625.finding: First-trimester DiNP metabolites (the DEHP replacement) were associated with shorter anoscrotal distance, but the reduction was small (about 4% per IQR).

pmid:22262702.authors: Braun JM, Smith KW, Williams PL, et al.
pmid:22262702.title: Variability of urinary phthalate metabolite and bisphenol A concentrations before and during pregnancy
pmid:22262702.finding: During pregnancy ICCs were 0.50 for MEP, 0.45 for MBP, 0.25 for MBzP, 0.12 for BPA and 0.08 for sum-DEHP; one spot sample adequately classified MEP and MBP but not DEHP or BPA.

pmid:42307947.authors: Buckley JP, Pacyga DC, Xun X, et al.
pmid:42307947.title: Gestational Exposure to 10 Classes of Priority Chemicals and Birth Outcomes in the ECHO Cohort
pmid:42307947.finding: Among 113 analytes in 10 chemical classes, several phthalates and alternative plasticizers were linked to slightly shorter gestation; summed DiNP metabolites: 0.6 days shorter, preterm birth OR 1.16 per IQR.

pmid:15121985.authors: Calafat AM, Needham LL, Silva MJ, et al.
pmid:15121985.title: Exposure to di-(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate among premature neonates in a neonatal intensive care unit
pmid:15121985.finding: Premature infants receiving intensive care via PVC devices had DEHP metabolite levels several-fold to orders of magnitude above the general population (geometric mean MEHP 100 vs 3.4 ng/mL).

pmid:31365888.authors: Camacho L, Lewis SM, Vanlandingham MM, et al.
pmid:31365888.title: A two-year toxicology study of bisphenol A (BPA) in Sprague-Dawley rats: CLARITY-BPA core study results
pmid:31365888.finding: Guideline-compliant 2-year CLARITY-BPA rat study (2.5-25,000 ug/kg/day): no BPA-related effects in in-life data; inconsistent lesions, with a possible relationship only at 25,000 ug/kg/day.

pmid:22563949.authors: Carlstedt F, Jönsson BA, Bornehag CG
pmid:22563949.title: PVC flooring is related to human uptake of phthalates in infants
pmid:22563949.finding: Infants with PVC flooring in the bedroom had significantly higher urinary MBzP (the BBzP metabolite).

pmid:16263507.authors: Duty SM, Ackerman RM, Calafat AM, et al.
pmid:16263507.title: Personal care product use predicts urinary concentrations of some phthalate monoesters
pmid:16263507.finding: Men who used cologne or aftershave in the previous 48 h had about double urinary MEP (265 vs 108 ng/mL); each additional personal-care product raised MEP by 33%.

pmid:32626195.authors: EFSA Panel on Food Contact Materials, Enzymes and Processing Aids (CEP), Silano V, Barat Baviera JM, et al.
pmid:32626195.title: Update of the risk assessment of di-butylphthalate (DBP), butyl-benzyl-phthalate (BBP), bis(2-ethylhexyl)phthalate (DEHP), di-isononylphthalate (DINP) and di-isodecylphthalate (DIDP) for use in food contact materials
pmid:32626195.finding: EFSA set a group TDI of 50 ug/kg bw/day (as DEHP equivalents) for DBP, BBP, DEHP and DINP based on reduced fetal testosterone; aggregated dietary exposure was 0.9-7.2 (mean) to 1.6-11.7 (high) ug/kg/day, up to 23% of the group TDI; assessment called temporary.

pmid:24570250.authors: Ehrlich S, Calafat AM, Humblet O, et al.
pmid:24570250.title: Handling of thermal receipts as a source of exposure to bisphenol A
pmid:24570250.finding: Handling thermal receipts for 2 h without gloves raised urinary BPA from 1.8 to 5.8 ug/L, peaking at 8-12 h; nitrile gloves prevented a significant rise.

lifestyle:ept-eu2024.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/3190 of 19 December 2024 on the use of bisphenol A (BPA) and other bisphenols and bisphenol derivatives in materials and articles intended to come into contact with food
lifestyle:ept-eu2024.journal: Official Journal of the European Union
lifestyle:ept-eu2024.finding: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/3190 bans BPA and its salts in food contact materials (plastics, coatings, varnishes, inks, adhesives, rubbers), with an 18-month transition to 20 July 2026 for most single-use items and 36 months (to 20 January 2028) for some uses; other hazardous bisphenols need authorization.

pmid:17849488.authors: Faber WD, Deyo JA, Stump DG, et al.
pmid:17849488.title: Developmental toxicity and uterotrophic studies with di-2-ethylhexyl terephthalate
pmid:17849488.journal: Birth Defects Res B Dev Reprod Toxicol
pmid:17849488.finding: Guideline developmental toxicity studies of DEHTP in rats (up to 747 mg/kg/day) and mice found no malformations or effects on implantation or fetal weight, and no estrogenic activity in a uterotrophic assay.

pmid:24845688.authors: Ferguson KK, Cantonwine DE, Rivera-González LO, et al.
pmid:24845688.title: Urinary phthalate metabolite associations with biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress across pregnancy in Puerto Rico
pmid:24845688.n: 54 women (oxidative stress) / 120 women (inflammation), PROTECT Puerto Rico
pmid:24845688.finding: Across repeated pregnancy samples, all phthalate metabolites were associated with higher urinary 8-isoprostane and 8-OHdG; IQR rises in MBP and MiBP went with about 49-50% higher 8-isoprostane.

pmid:27751756.authors: Ferguson KK, Cantonwine DE, McElrath TF, et al.
pmid:27751756.title: Repeated measures analysis of associations between urinary bisphenol-A concentrations and biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress in pregnancy
pmid:27751756.finding: An interquartile rise in urinary BPA was associated with 5-9% higher 8-OHdG and 8-isoprostane and 9% higher plasma IL-6 across repeated pregnancy samples.

pmid:27352406.authors: Ferguson KK, Chen YH, VanderWeele TJ, et al.
pmid:27352406.title: Mediation of the Relationship between Maternal Phthalate Exposure and Preterm Birth by Oxidative Stress with Repeated Measurements across Pregnancy
pmid:27352406.n: 482 pregnant women (130 preterm cases, 352 controls; LIFECODES)
pmid:27352406.finding: Counterfactual mediation analysis: 8-isoprostane mediated an estimated 47-60% of the association between the DEHP metabolite MECPP and preterm birth (total OR 1.48-1.67).

pmid:16102138.title: Disruption of reproductive development in male rat offspring following in utero exposure to phthalate esters
pmid:16102138.finding: Review of rat studies: in-utero DBP, DEHP and BBP lower fetal testicular testosterone and INSL3, causing the 'phthalate syndrome' of hypospadias, cryptorchidism, malformed accessory glands, retained nipples and shorter anogenital distance.

pmid:40132438.authors: Friedman A, Welch BM, Keil AP, et al.
pmid:40132438.title: Periods of susceptibility for associations between phthalate exposure and preterm birth: Results from a pooled analysis of 16 US cohorts
pmid:40132438.finding: In the same pooled data, DEHP-metabolite associations with preterm birth were strongest for first- and second-trimester exposure (MEHP OR 1.15 and 1.11 per IQR) and null in the third trimester.

pmid:29431133.authors: Galloway TS, Baglin N, Lee BP, et al.
pmid:29431133.title: An engaged research study to assess the effect of a 'real-world' dietary intervention on urinary bisphenol A (BPA) levels in teenagers
pmid:29431133.finding: A self-designed 7-day diet to avoid BPA did not lower urinary BPA overall (p=0.25); participants found BPA-free food hard to identify and unlikely to sustain.

pmid:38631089.authors: Gerofke A, Lange R, Vogel N, et al.
pmid:38631089.title: Phthalates and substitute plasticizers: Main achievements from the European human biomonitoring initiative HBM4EU
pmid:38631089.finding: Health-based biomonitoring guidance values were exceeded in up to 5% of participants; for about 17% of children and teens, a mixture risk from five reprotoxic phthalates could not be excluded; food and personal-care products were main sources.

pmid:27726525.authors: Hagobian T, Smouse A, Streeter M, et al.
pmid:27726525.title: Randomized Intervention Trial to Decrease Bisphenol A Urine Concentrations in Women: Pilot Study
pmid:27726525.finding: A 3-week intervention (BPA-free products, glass containers, weekly counselling) lowered creatinine-adjusted urinary BPA vs control (treatment x time p=0.04).

pmid:42014506.authors: Harray AJ, Lucas AD, Herrmann SE, et al.
pmid:42014506.title: Low-plastic diet and urinary levels of plastic-associated phthalates and bisphenols: the randomized controlled PERTH Trial
pmid:42014506.finding: A 7-day diet of food sourced to minimize plastic contact, with plastic-free kitchenware and personal-care products, cut urinary MnBP by 37.5%, MBzP by 53.5% and BPA by 59.7% vs no intervention; personal-care swaps alone lowered MnBP; Minderoo-funded.

pmid:15121520.authors: Hauser R, Duty S, Godfrey-Bailey L, et al.
pmid:15121520.title: Medications as a source of human exposure to phthalates
pmid:15121520.finding: A man taking enteric-coated mesalamine (Asacol) had urinary MBP of 16,868 ng/mL, more than two orders of magnitude above the NHANES 95th percentile.

pmid:32682780.authors: Heindel JJ, Belcher S, Flaws JA, et al.
pmid:32682780.title: Data integration, analysis, and interpretation of eight academic CLARITY-BPA studies
pmid:32682780.finding: Integration of eight academic CLARITY-BPA studies on the same animals: developmental BPA affected brain, prostate, urinary tract, ovary, mammary gland and heart, often at the lowest dose (2.5 ug/kg/day) and non-monotonically.

pmid:19270786.authors: Hernández-Díaz S, Mitchell AA, Kelley KE, et al.
pmid:19270786.title: Medications as a potential source of exposure to phthalates in the U.S. population
pmid:19270786.finding: Users of mesalamine formulations that may contain DBP had mean urinary MBP 50 times higher than non-users (2,257 vs 46 ug/L); some didanosine, omeprazole and theophylline products were linked to higher MEP.

pmid:25337790.authors: Hormann AM, Vom Saal FS, Nagel SC, et al.
pmid:25337790.title: Holding thermal receipt paper and eating food after using hand sanitizer results in high serum bioactive and urine total levels of bisphenol A (BPA)
pmid:25337790.finding: Holding thermal receipt paper right after using a hand sanitizer with penetration enhancers, then eating fries by hand, raised serum unconjugated BPA to about 7 ng/mL within 90 min.

pmid:27235111.authors: Hutter HP, Kundi M, Hohenblum P, et al.
pmid:27235111.title: Life without plastic: A family experiment and biomonitoring study
pmid:27235111.finding: After a family removed plastics from their home, urinary BPA was below quantification, but over two further months phthalate metabolites fell in some members and rose in the mother.

pmid:40307157.authors: Hyman S, Acevedo J, Giannarelli C, et al.
pmid:40307157.title: Phthalate exposure from plastics and cardiovascular disease: global estimates of attributable mortality and years life lost
pmid:40307157.finding: Burden model applying a US hazard ratio to regional DEHP exposure estimates: 356,238 cardiovascular deaths in 2018 (13.5% of CVD deaths at ages 55-64) attributed to DEHP; funded by Bloomberg Philanthropies, Beyond Petrochemicals and NIH.

pmid:42077651.authors: Hyman S, Acevedo J, Trasande L
pmid:42077651.title: Preterm birth attributable to exposure to chemicals used in plastic materials: a global estimate
pmid:42077651.finding: Burden model applying a hazard ratio from a previous cohort to global exposure estimates: 1.97 million preterm births in 2018 (8.7% of the global total) attributed to DEHP.

pmid:26672060.authors: Jensen TK, Frederiksen H, Kyhl HB, et al.
pmid:26672060.title: Prenatal Exposure to Phthalates and Anogenital Distance in Male Infants from a Low-Exposed Danish Cohort (2010-2012)
pmid:26672060.finding: In a low-exposed cohort, no consistent associations were seen between any third-trimester phthalate metabolite and anogenital distance or penile width at 3 months.

pmid:38575009.authors: Jiang Y, Xu Y, Xiao S, et al.
pmid:38575009.title: Phthalate and DINCH exposure and ovarian reserve markers among women seeking infertility care
pmid:38575009.finding: Most conventional phthalate metabolites were inversely associated with antral follicle count, DINCH metabolites with higher FSH; the phthalate+DINCH mixture went with 8.6% lower AFC.

pmid:26313703.authors: Johns LE, Cooper GS, Galizia A, et al.
pmid:26313703.title: Exposure assessment issues in epidemiology studies of phthalates
pmid:26313703.finding: Phthalate metabolite half-lives are 3-18 h; intraclass correlations of repeated urine samples are about 0.3-0.6 for DEP, DBP, DiBP and BBzP metabolites and 0.1-0.3 for DEHP, DiNP and DiDP; US and German exposures to DEP, BBzP, DBP and DEHP declined after 2001.

pmid:39432449.authors: Knox KE, Schwarzman MR, Rudel RA, et al.
pmid:39432449.title: Trends in NHANES Biomonitored Exposures in California and the United States following Enactment of California's Proposition 65
pmid:39432449.finding: Median BPA fell 15% after California's Prop 65 listing while unlisted BPS rose 20% over the same period, suggesting substitution.

pmid:14576974.authors: Koch HM, Bolt HM, Angerer J
pmid:14576974.title: Di(2-ethylhexyl)phthalate (DEHP) metabolites in human urine and serum after a single oral dose of deuterium-labelled DEHP
pmid:14576974.finding: After a labelled DEHP dose, urinary metabolites peaked at 2-4 h; first-phase excretion half-lives were about 2 h and second-phase 5-10 h.

pmid:37976583.authors: Kortenkamp A, Martin O, Iacovidou E, et al.
pmid:37976583.title: Drivers of divergent assessments of bisphenol-A hazards to semen quality by various European agencies, regulators and scientists
pmid:37976583.finding: Analysis of why EFSA and the German BfR diverge: BfR proposed an alternative TDI 1,000-fold higher than EFSA's, based on adult sperm-count effects, and rejected the immunotoxicity endpoint; both agencies discounted gestational-exposure studies.

pmid:33711757.authors: Lange R, Apel P, Rousselle C, et al.
pmid:33711757.title: The European Human Biomonitoring Initiative (HBM4EU): Human biomonitoring guidance values for selected phthalates and a substitute plasticizer
pmid:33711757.finding: HBM4EU human-biomonitoring guidance values for adults, e.g. 0.5 mg/L urine for the sum of 5-oxo- and 5-OH-MEHP, 0.19 mg/L MnBP, 3 mg/L MBzP, 4.5 mg/L for DINCH metabolites.

pmid:29978145.authors: Lehmler HJ, Liu B, Gadogbe M, et al.
pmid:29978145.title: Exposure to Bisphenol A, Bisphenol F, and Bisphenol S in U.S. Adults and Children: The National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2013-2014
pmid:29978145.finding: BPA, BPS and BPF were detected in 95.7%, 89.4% and 66.5% of urine samples; median adult BPA 1.24 ug/L vs 0.35-0.37 ug/L for BPF and BPS.

pmid:31491609.authors: Lessmann F, Kolossa-Gehring M, Apel P, et al.
pmid:31491609.title: German Environmental Specimen Bank: 24-hour urine samples from 1999 to 2017 reveal rapid increase in exposure to the para-phthalate plasticizer di(2-ethylhexyl) terephthalate (DEHTP)
pmid:31491609.finding: The DEHP substitute DEHTP went from under 10% detection before 2009 to 100% in 2017 (median 3.35 ug/L metabolite), still far below German guidance values (median intake 0.74 ug/kg/day vs TDI 1,000).

pmid:31629946.authors: Liu C, Duan P, Chen YJ, et al.
pmid:31629946.title: Mediation of the relationship between phthalate exposure and semen quality by oxidative stress among 1034 reproductive-aged Chinese men
pmid:31629946.finding: Every phthalate metabolite rose with urinary 8-OHdG, 8-isoPGF2a and HNE-MA; 8-isoPGF2a suggestively mediated 12% of the MBP-sperm concentration link and 8-OHdG 32% of the MEP-morphology link (p<0.10).

pmid:29161633.authors: Machtinger R, Gaskins AJ, Racowsky C, et al.
pmid:29161633.title: Urinary concentrations of biomarkers of phthalates and phthalate alternatives and IVF outcomes
pmid:29161633.finding: Higher DEHP metabolites were linked to fewer total, mature and fertilized oocytes and top-quality embryos, but no phthalate metabolite was linked to implantation, clinical pregnancy or live birth; DINCH metabolites showed no associations.

pmid:32735599.authors: Martínez Steele E, Khandpur N, da Costa Louzada ML, et al.
pmid:32735599.title: Association between dietary contribution of ultra-processed foods and urinary concentrations of phthalates and bisphenol in a nationally representative sample of the US population aged 6 years and older
pmid:32735599.finding: Urinary DiNP, mCNP, mCPP, MBzP and BPF rose monotonically across quintiles of ultra-processed food intake.

pmid:29272776.authors: Oh J, Choi JW, Ahn YA, et al.
pmid:29272776.title: Pharmacokinetics of bisphenol S in humans after single oral administration
pmid:29272776.finding: Oral BPS was absorbed within about 1 h and excreted with a terminal half-life under 7 h (6.8 h).

pmid:39117051.authors: Oskar S, Mook J, Smith MK, et al.
pmid:39117051.title: Temporal trends in phthalate metabolite exposure of girls in the United States across sociodemographic factors and intersectional social identities: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2001-2018
pmid:39117051.finding: Low- and high-molecular-weight phthalate metabolites declined between 2001 and 2018, with persistent sociodemographic differences in low-molecular-weight phthalates.

pmid:39549769.authors: Potts C, Harbolic A, Murphy M, et al.
pmid:39549769.title: A common phthalate replacement disrupts ovarian function in young adult mice
pmid:39549769.finding: In young adult mice, 10 days of oral DEHTP (from 10 ug/kg) altered ovarian follicle counts and gene expression, and DEHTP/MEHTP slowed follicle growth in vitro.

pmid:37739055.title: WITHDRAWN: Letter to editor: Evidence evaluated by EFSA does not support lowering the temporary tolerable daily intake for bisphenol A
pmid:37739055.finding: RETRACTED/WITHDRAWN letter arguing EFSA's evidence did not support lowering the BPA TDI; withdrawn at the request of the author(s) and/or editor. Cited only to flag it.

pmid:31351310.authors: Radke EG, Glenn BS, Braun JM, et al.
pmid:31351310.title: Phthalate exposure and female reproductive and developmental outcomes: a systematic review of the human epidemiological evidence
pmid:31351310.finding: EPA systematic review: moderate evidence linking DEHP, DBP and DEP to preterm birth; slight or indeterminate evidence for time to pregnancy, puberty and spontaneous abortion.

pmid:25775505.title: Bisphenol S and F: A Systematic Review and Comparison of the Hormonal Activity of Bisphenol A Substitutes
pmid:25775505.finding: BPS and BPF have hormonal potency in the same order of magnitude as BPA (estrogenic, antiestrogenic, androgenic, antiandrogenic); authors employed by TEDX, an endocrine-disruption advocacy nonprofit.

pmid:30529838.authors: Silva MJ, Wong LY, Samandar E, et al.
pmid:30529838.title: Exposure to di-2-ethylhexyl terephthalate in the U.S. general population from the 2015-2016 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey
pmid:30529838.finding: DEHTP metabolites were detected in 96-99.9% of the US population; levels rose with household income and were higher in females and children.

pmid:19479022.authors: Stahlhut RW, Welshons WV, Swan SH
pmid:19479022.title: Bisphenol A data in NHANES suggest longer than expected half-life, substantial nonfood exposure, or both
pmid:19479022.finding: Urinary BPA barely fell with longer fasting (population-based half-life 43 h), suggesting substantial non-food exposure, storage, or both.

pmid:27475039.authors: Sturgeon SR, Flynn D, Kaiser AB, et al.
pmid:27475039.title: Urinary levels of phthalate metabolites and cardiovascular disease mortality (NHANES, 1999-2008)
pmid:27475039.finding: No urinary phthalate metabolite was associated with cardiovascular mortality (top vs bottom quartile HRs 0.73-1.4, all non-significant; 175 CVD deaths).

pmid:16079079.authors: Swan SH, Main KM, Liu F, et al.
pmid:16079079.title: Decrease in anogenital distance among male infants with prenatal phthalate exposure
pmid:16079079.finding: Prenatal MBP, MEP, MBzP and MiBP were inversely related to boys' anogenital index; top vs bottom MBP quartile OR 10.2 for shorter-than-expected AGI.

pmid:25697839.authors: Swan SH, Sathyanarayana S, Barrett ES, et al.
pmid:25697839.title: First trimester phthalate exposure and anogenital distance in newborns
pmid:25697839.finding: First-trimester DEHP metabolites were inversely associated with both anogenital distance measures in boys but not girls; no other phthalate was associated; single urine sample and between-centre differences were limitations.

pmid:21705716.authors: Teeguarden JG, Calafat AM, Ye X, et al.
pmid:21705716.title: Twenty-four hour human urine and serum profiles of bisphenol a during high-dietary exposure
pmid:21705716.finding: During three high-BPA meals, urinary total BPA peaked about 2.75 h after a meal; serum BPA was detectable only at exposures well above the US 95th percentile.

pmid:26115537.authors: Thayer KA, Doerge DR, Hunt D, et al.
pmid:26115537.title: Pharmacokinetics of bisphenol A in humans following a single oral administration
pmid:26115537.finding: After an oral dose of deuterated BPA, unconjugated BPA peaked at 1.3 h and the terminal half-life of total and unconjugated BPA was about 6.2-6.4 h.

pmid:34654571.authors: Trasande L, Liu B, Bao W
pmid:34654571.title: Phthalates and attributable mortality: A population-based longitudinal cohort study and cost analysis
pmid:34654571.finding: High-molecular-weight and DEHP metabolites were linked to higher all-cause mortality (HR 1.14 and 1.10 per unit; top tertile 1.48 and 1.42); extrapolation gave 90,761-107,283 attributable deaths a year among Americans aged 55-64, assuming causality.

pmid:31373935.authors: Vernet C, Philippat C, Agier L, et al.
pmid:31373935.title: An Empirical Validation of the Within-subject Biospecimens Pooling Approach to Minimize Exposure Misclassification in Biomarker-based Studies
pmid:31373935.n: 16 pregnant women (all voids, several weeks) plus simulation
pmid:31373935.finding: One spot urine sample produced 69% attenuation bias in a BPA dose-response; about 18 samples were needed to bring bias down to 10%.

pmid:35816333.authors: Welch BM, Keil AP, Buckley JP, et al.
pmid:35816333.title: Associations Between Prenatal Urinary Biomarkers of Phthalate Exposure and Preterm Birth: A Pooled Study of 16 US Cohorts
pmid:35816333.finding: Each interquartile-range rise in urinary MBP, MiBP, MECPP or MCPP across pregnancy was linked to 12-16% higher odds of preterm birth; modelled 30% and 50% cuts in the phthalate mixture would prevent about 6 and 11 preterm births per 1,000 live births.

pmid:18070048.title: Phthalates: metabolism and exposure
pmid:18070048.finding: At least 74% of an oral DEHP dose and 44% of DiNP are excreted in urine; median daily intakes in Germany were 2.7 ug/kg DEHP, 2.1 DnBP, 1.5 DiBP, 0.6 DiNP; children had higher exposure.

pmid:36988899.authors: Yang TC, Jovanovic N, Chong F, et al.
pmid:36988899.title: Interventions to Reduce Exposure to Synthetic Phenols and Phthalates from Dietary Intake and Personal Care Products: a Scoping Review
pmid:36988899.finding: Scoping review: interventions that removed sources generally lowered phenol and phthalate biomarkers within days, but compliance and contamination limited success, and policy may matter more than individual behaviour.

pmid:21406337.authors: Ye X, Wong LY, Bishop AM, et al.
pmid:21406337.title: Variability of urinary concentrations of bisphenol A in spot samples, first morning voids, and 24-hour collections
pmid:21406337.n: 8 adults collecting every void for a week
pmid:21406337.finding: For spot samples, 70% of BPA variance was within a day, outweighing between-person variance (9%).

pmid:34763012.authors: Yland JJ, Zhang Y, Williams PL, et al.
pmid:34763012.title: Phthalate and DINCH urinary concentrations across pregnancy and risk of preterm birth
pmid:34763012.finding: Mean pregnancy sum-DEHP was imprecisely linked to preterm birth (RR 1.21, 0.84-1.72 per ln unit), with the clearest signal in the third trimester (RR 1.51); detection of a DINCH metabolite also appeared positively related to preterm birth.

pmid:41389798.authors: Zhang Y, Sun Q, Wang YX, et al.
pmid:41389798.title: Plasticisers chemical mixture, vitamin status, and mortality in US adults: a prospective population-based cohort
pmid:41389798.finding: Each tertile rise in a mixture of eight phthalate metabolites plus BPA was linked to higher all-cause mortality (HR 1.35), but only in people with low vitamin D or red-cell folate; authors attributed about 10% of deaths to the mixture.

pmid:37873497.authors: Zoeller RT, Birnbaum LS, Collins TJ, et al.
pmid:37873497.title: European Medicines Agency Conflicts With the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) on Bisphenol A Regulation
pmid:37873497.finding: Perspective: several agencies including the European Medicines Agency formally disagreed with EFSA's BPA TDI; the authors judge the weight of evidence supports EFSA.

pmid:27072648.authors: Zota AR, Phillips CA, Mitro SD
pmid:27072648.title: Recent Fast Food Consumption and Bisphenol A and Phthalates Exposures among the U.S. Population in NHANES, 2003-2010
pmid:27072648.finding: People getting at least 35% of calories from fast food had 24% higher DEHP and 39% higher DiNP metabolites than non-consumers; no dose-response for BPA.

pmid:30358819.authors: Ahmed SM, Noble BN, Joya SA, et al.
pmid:30358819.title: A Prospective Cohort Study Examining the Associations of Maternal Arsenic Exposure With Fetal Loss and Neonatal Mortality.
pmid:30358819.finding: Arsenic exposure was associated with lower mortality early in pregnancy and higher fetal loss/neonatal death after about 20 weeks (HR up to 1.35), suggesting survival bias and stage-specific toxicity.

pmid:38941661.authors: Akhigbe RE, Akhigbe TM, Adegbola CA, et al.
pmid:38941661.title: Toxic impacts of arsenic bioaccumulation on urinary arsenic metabolites and semen quality: A systematic and meta-analysis.
pmid:38941661.finding: Meta-analysis concluding that arsenic exposure lowers semen quality and testosterone, although pooled differences in sperm concentration and motility were not statistically significant.

pmid:37505605.authors: Ali Sultan SA, Ahmed Khan F, Wahab A, et al.
pmid:37505605.title: Assessing Leaching of Potentially Hazardous Elements from Cookware during Cooking: A Serious Public Health Concern.
pmid:37505605.finding: Anodised and non-anodised aluminium cookware leached aluminium, lead, cadmium and nickel into acidic foods, more at lower pH.

pmid:31479458.authors: Alves C, Saleh A, Alaofè H
pmid:31479458.title: Iron-containing cookware for the reduction of iron deficiency anemia among children and females of reproductive age in low- and middle-income countries: A systematic review.
pmid:31479458.finding: Iron pots and ingots raised haemoglobin in some studies (0.32-1.18 g/dL), more often in children, with variable compliance; evidence was mixed.

pmid:29136183.authors: Andreotti G, Koutros S, Hofmann JN, et al.
pmid:29136183.title: Glyphosate Use and Cancer Incidence in the Agricultural Health Study.
pmid:29136183.finding: In the Agricultural Health Study, glyphosate use was not associated with any solid tumour or lymphoid malignancy overall, including NHL; a non-significant excess of acute myeloid leukaemia in the top exposure quartile (RR 2.44, 95% CI 0.94-6.32) needed confirmation.

pmid:36410462.authors: Ashley-Martin J, Huang R, MacPherson S, et al.
pmid:36410462.title: Urinary concentrations and determinants of glyphosate and glufosinate in pregnant Canadian participants in the MIREC study.
pmid:36410462.finding: In the Canadian MIREC cohort, 74% of first-trimester urines had detectable glyphosate (geometric mean 0.11 ug/L); concentrations rose with whole-grain bread intake, implicating diet.

pmid:39294416.authors: Ashley-Martin J, Marro L, Owen J, et al.
pmid:39294416.title: Gestational urinary concentrations of glyphosate and aminomethylphosphonic acid in relation to preterm birth: the MIREC study.
pmid:39294416.finding: In MIREC, urinary glyphosate and AMPA were not associated with preterm birth (OR per doubling 0.98, 0.94-1.03) or shorter gestation.

pmid:29043784.authors: Ayotte JD, Medalie L, Qi SL, et al.
pmid:29043784.title: Estimating the High-Arsenic Domestic-Well Population in the Conterminous United States.
pmid:29043784.finding: An estimated 2.1 million people in the US drink from private wells with arsenic above 10 ug/L.

pmid:10981726.authors: Backer LC, Ashley DL, Bonin MA, et al.
pmid:10981726.title: Household exposures to drinking water disinfection by-products: whole blood trihalomethane levels.
pmid:10981726.finding: A 10-min shower or bath raised blood trihalomethanes more than drinking 1 L of tap water, showing inhalation and skin are major routes.

pmid:31886824.authors: Bao W, Liu B, Simonsen DW, et al.
pmid:31886824.title: Association Between Exposure to Pyrethroid Insecticides and Risk of All-Cause and Cause-Specific Mortality in the General US Adult Population.
pmid:31886824.finding: In NHANES 1999-2002 with 14 years of follow-up, the top vs bottom tertile of urinary 3-PBA was associated with higher all-cause (HR 1.56, 1.08-2.26) and cardiovascular mortality (HR 3.00, 1.02-8.80), but not cancer mortality.

pmid:40203754.authors: Binkhorst G, Jones B, Sargsyan A, et al.
pmid:40203754.title: Potential lead exposure from aluminum cooking pots in lower and middle-income countries.
pmid:40203754.finding: About one in ten aluminium cooking pots from lower- and middle-income countries leached lead at levels modelled to push children's blood lead above 5 ug/dL (under aggressive test conditions).

pmid:31325834.authors: Blaisdell J, Turyk ME, Almberg KS, et al.
pmid:31325834.title: Prenatal exposure to nitrate in drinking water and the risk of congenital anomalies.
pmid:31325834.finding: Prenatal drinking-water nitrate was weakly associated with congenital anomalies, including limb deficiencies, congenital heart and neural tube defects, at levels below EPA standards.

pmid:31384239.title: Low-Level Exposure to Arsenic in Drinking Water and Risk of Lung and Bladder Cancer: A Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis.
pmid:31384239.finding: No increase in lung (RR 1.03 per 10 ug/L) or bladder cancer (RR 1.02) up to 150 ug/L arsenic; the lead author declared work as an expert in arsenic litigation.

pmid:31074704.authors: Bosscher V, Lytle DA, Schock MR, et al.
pmid:31074704.title: POU water filters effectively reduce lead in drinking water: a demonstration field study in flint, Michigan.
pmid:31074704.journal: J Environ Sci Health A Tox Hazard Subst Environ Eng
pmid:31074704.finding: In Flint homes, NSF/ANSI-53 certified carbon-block point-of-use filters reduced lead to below 0.5 ug/L in over 97% of filtered samples, even with influent above 150 ug/L.

pmid:21507776.authors: Bouchard MF, Chevrier J, Harley KG, et al.
pmid:21507776.title: Prenatal exposure to organophosphate pesticides and IQ in 7-year-old children.
pmid:21507776.finding: Children of mothers in the top quintile of prenatal urinary dialkyl phosphates had on average 7.0 IQ points lower scores at age 7 than the bottom quintile; children's own urinary levels were not consistently related.

pmid:24832151.authors: Broadbent JM, Thomson WM, Ramrakha S, et al.
pmid:24832151.title: Community Water Fluoridation and Intelligence: Prospective Study in New Zealand.
pmid:24832151.finding: Childhood exposure to community water fluoridation, fluoride toothpaste or tablets was not associated with IQ at ages 7-13 or 38.

pmid:21112052.authors: Brown MJ, Raymond J, Homa D, et al.
pmid:21112052.title: Association between children's blood lead levels, lead service lines, and water disinfection, Washington, DC, 1998-2006.
pmid:21112052.finding: Lead service lines were a risk factor for elevated blood lead even when the utility met the EPA action level; partial line replacement did not lower risk.

pmid:41576409.authors: Castellanos-Carrizal C, Castillo-Ruiz O, Ramírez-Quintanilla LY, et al.
pmid:41576409.title: Enhanced Leaching of Soluble Lead by Cooking Acidic Food in Glazed Pottery Sold at the Mexico-US Border.
pmid:41576409.finding: Acidic food cooked in lead-glazed pottery from the Mexico-US border contained about 9 times more lead than non-acidic food (median 103 mg/kg).

pmid:42385869.authors: Chambers T, Kim AH, Dean F, et al.
pmid:42385869.title: Nitrate in drinking water and preterm birth: a national retrospective cohort study in New Zealand.
pmid:42385869.finding: The highest quartile of drinking-water nitrate (>0.66 mg/L nitrate-N) vs lowest was associated with 8% higher odds of preterm birth; residual confounding could not be excluded.

pmid:36629488.authors: Chang VC, Andreotti G, Ospina M, et al.
pmid:36629488.title: Glyphosate exposure and urinary oxidative stress biomarkers in the Agricultural Health Study.
pmid:36629488.finding: In first-morning urine of AHS farmers, the top vs bottom glyphosate quartile had 15% higher 8-OHdG (GMR 1.15, 1.03-1.28) and 20% higher MDA; use the previous day also raised 8-OHdG and MDA.

pmid:38055050.authors: Chang VC, Zhou W, Berndt SI, et al.
pmid:38055050.title: Glyphosate Use and Mosaic Loss of Chromosome Y among Male Farmers in the Agricultural Health Study.
pmid:38055050.finding: High lifetime glyphosate use was associated with expanded mosaic loss of chromosome Y (OR 1.75, 1.00-3.07), a marker of genomic instability; first study, needs replication.

pmid:38636272.authors: Chang VC, Ospina M, Xie S, et al.
pmid:38636272.title: Urinary biomonitoring of glyphosate exposure among male farmers and nonfarmers in the Biomarkers of Exposure and Effect in Agriculture (BEEA) study.
pmid:38636272.finding: Glyphosate was detected in urine of 81% of non-farming controls and about 90% of farmers; geometric means 0.39 ug/L (non-farmers) to 0.89 ug/L (recently exposed farmers), higher without gloves or long sleeves.

pmid:27385285.authors: Cimino AM, Boyles AL, Thayer KA, et al.
pmid:27385285.title: Effects of Neonicotinoid Pesticide Exposure on Human Health: A Systematic Review.
pmid:27385285.finding: Systematic review of neonicotinoid human health effects found only a few studies with suggestive but methodologically weak findings for chronic exposure (e.g. tetralogy of Fallot, anencephaly, autism).

pmid:36249267.authors: Coffman VR, Søndergaard Jensen A, Trabjerg BB, et al.
pmid:36249267.title: Prenatal exposure to nitrate from drinking water and the risk of preterm birth: A Danish nationwide cohort study.
pmid:36249267.finding: Preterm birth risk rose with household tap-water nitrate (OR 1.01 per 10 mg/L), also when restricted to levels below the 50 mg/L EU standard.

pmid:38641111.authors: Cole M, Gomiero A, Jaén-Gil A, et al.
pmid:38641111.title: Microplastic and PTFE contamination of food from cookware.
pmid:38641111.finding: Non-plastic cookware added no microplastics to food simulant, whereas plastic and PTFE-containing cookware added PTFE, polyethylene and polypropylene particles (estimated 2,409-4,964 particles a year).

pmid:27815781.authors: Corlin L, Rock T, Cordova J, et al.
pmid:27815781.title: Health Effects and Environmental Justice Concerns of Exposure to Uranium in Drinking Water.
pmid:27815781.finding: Review: uranium in water affects kidney and possibly bone; evidence on cardiovascular and cancer effects is lacking; 5.4% of sampled unregulated Navajo Nation wells exceeded Safe Drinking Water Act standards.

pmid:40440853.authors: Deiana G, Filippini T, Dettori M, et al.
pmid:40440853.title: Exposure to disinfection by-products and risk of birth defects: A systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis.
pmid:40440853.finding: Dose-response meta-analysis: THM above about 60 ug/L was associated with more anencephaly, musculoskeletal and orofacial defects, and above 30 ug/L with term low birth weight.

pmid:18984063.authors: De Vizcaya-Ruiz A, Barbier O, Ruiz-Ramos R, et al.
pmid:18984063.title: Biomarkers of oxidative stress and damage in human populations exposed to arsenic.
pmid:18984063.finding: Review of oxidative-stress biomarkers (urinary 8-OHdG, comet assay, DNA-repair markers) in arsenic-exposed populations and of genetic variation in arsenic metabolism.

pmid:32119975.authors: Dourson M, Gadagbui B, Onyema C, et al.
pmid:32119975.title: A commentary on some epidemiology data for chlorpyrifos.
pmid:32119975.finding: Commentary noting the Columbia chlorpyrifos raw data had not been shared despite requests; re-plotting data extracted from published figures did not reproduce the IQ association.

pmid:32626415.title: Statement on the available outcomes of the human health assessment in the context of the pesticides peer review of the active substance chlorpyrifos.
pmid:32626415.finding: EFSA's 2019 statement found that chlorpyrifos does not meet EU approval criteria because of possible genotoxicity and developmental neurotoxicity supported by epidemiology, and that no safe exposure level could be set.

pmid:37502013.authors: European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), Álvarez F, Arena M, et al.
pmid:37502013.title: Peer review of the pesticide risk assessment of the active substance glyphosate.
pmid:37502013.finding: EFSA's 2023 peer review of glyphosate identified no critical areas of concern for human or animal health; it relied on ECHA's conclusion that glyphosate does not meet the criteria for classification as carcinogenic, mutagenic or reprotoxic, while listing data gaps (an impurity, consumer dietary risk, formulation co-formulants).

pmid:37966213.authors: Ellis LB, Molina K, Robbins CR, et al.
pmid:37966213.title: Adult Organophosphate and Carbamate Insecticide Exposure and Sperm Concentration: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of the Epidemiological Evidence.
pmid:37966213.finding: Higher adult exposure to organophosphate and N-methyl carbamate insecticides was associated with lower sperm concentration (bias-adjusted SMD -0.30, 95% CI -0.49 to -0.10); evidence rated moderate quality and sufficient.

pmid:35429892.title: Nitrates in drinking water and cancers of the colon and rectum: a meta-analysis of epidemiological studies.
pmid:35429892.finding: Colorectal cancer risk rose about 2.4% per mg/L nitrate over a low range; the association was judged weak, inconsistent and possibly due to bias and confounding.

pmid:40628182.authors: Erichsen DW, Bondonno NP, Pokharel P, et al.
pmid:40628182.title: Source-specific nitrate and nitrite intake and association with colorectal cancer in the Danish Diet, Cancer and Health Cohort.
pmid:40628182.n: Danish Diet, Cancer and Health cohort
pmid:40628182.finding: Nitrate from food was not linked to colorectal cancer, but tap-water nitrate >=9.25 mg/L was linked to higher colon cancer rate (HR 1.52), more so in smokers and heavy red-meat eaters and less with high vitamin C, E, folate and flavonoid intake.

pmid:31939704.authors: Evlampidou I, Font-Ribera L, Rojas-Rueda D, et al.
pmid:31939704.title: Trihalomethanes in Drinking Water and Bladder Cancer Burden in the European Union.
pmid:31939704.finding: Assuming causality, current trihalomethane levels account for about 4.9% of bladder cancers in the EU (about 6,561 cases a year), with large differences between countries.

pmid:32797996.authors: Fagan J, Bohlen L, Patton S, et al.
pmid:32797996.title: Organic diet intervention significantly reduces urinary glyphosate levels in U.S. children and adults.
pmid:32797996.finding: Five days of an all-organic diet lowered urinary glyphosate by 71% and AMPA by 77%, with levels dropping within about three days (funded partly by an advocacy organisation).

pmid:15150536.authors: Fujino Y, Guo X, Liu J, et al.
pmid:15150536.title: Chronic arsenic exposure and urinary 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine in an arsenic-affected area in Inner Mongolia, China.
pmid:15150536.finding: Urinary arsenic metabolites were associated with urinary 8-OHdG in residents with arsenic skin lesions, and 8-OHdG was higher after more than 12 years of exposure.

pmid:38534131.authors: George CM, Zacher T, Endres K, et al.
pmid:38534131.title: Effect of an Arsenic Mitigation Program on Arsenic Exposure in American Indian Communities: A Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial of the Community-Led Strong Heart Water Study Program.
pmid:38534131.finding: A community-led program with point-of-use arsenic filters plus phone coaching lowered urinary arsenic by 47% over 2 years (55% in the filter plus mHealth arm).

pmid:29599069.authors: Gómez HF, Borgialli DA, Sharman M, et al.
pmid:29599069.title: Blood Lead Levels of Children in Flint, Michigan: 2006-2016.
pmid:29599069.finding: Children's mean blood lead in Flint fell from 2.33 to 1.15 ug/dL over 2006-2016; the 2014-2015 rise (1.19 to 1.30 ug/dL) was described as consistent with random variation.

pmid:37798092.authors: Grandjean P, Meddis A, Nielsen F, et al.
pmid:37798092.title: Dose dependence of prenatal fluoride exposure associations with cognitive performance at school age in three prospective studies.
pmid:37798092.finding: In a Danish cohort, maternal urinary fluoride was not associated with IQ at 7, but a joint analysis of three cohorts gave a benchmark concentration of 0.45 mg/L (lower limit 0.28 mg/L).

pmid:31424532.authors: Green R, Lanphear B, Hornung R, et al.
pmid:31424532.title: Association Between Maternal Fluoride Exposure During Pregnancy and IQ Scores in Offspring in Canada.
pmid:31424532.finding: Each 1 mg/L higher maternal urinary fluoride was associated with 4.49 lower IQ points in boys but not girls; 1 mg/day higher fluoride intake with 3.66 lower IQ points.

pmid:25706449.title: Metal fume fever and polymer fume fever.
pmid:25706449.finding: Polymer fume fever from overheated fluoropolymers is usually self-limited within 12-48 h but can be serious in people with heart or lung disease.

pmid:20375841.authors: Grellier J, Bennett J, Patelarou E, et al.
pmid:20375841.title: Exposure to disinfection by-products, fetal growth, and prematurity: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:20375841.finding: Third-trimester trihalomethane exposure showed little or no association with low birth weight or preterm delivery, with a possible small association with small-for-gestational-age (OR 1.01 per 10 ug/L).

pmid:31808102.title: The Impact of the Flint Water Crisis on Fertility.
pmid:31808102.finding: Comparing Flint with other Michigan cities, fertility rates fell by 12% after the water switch and birth weight fell by a net 5.4%.

pmid:25801782.authors: Guyton KZ, Loomis D, Grosse Y, et al.
pmid:25801782.title: Carcinogenicity of tetrachlorvinphos, parathion, malathion, diazinon, and glyphosate.
pmid:25801782.finding: IARC Monograph 112 summary: glyphosate classified as 'probably carcinogenic to humans' (Group 2A), based on limited human evidence for non-Hodgkin lymphoma, sufficient animal evidence and strong mechanistic evidence of genotoxicity.

pmid:26691115.authors: Hanna-Attisha M, LaChance J, Sadler RC, et al.
pmid:26691115.title: Elevated Blood Lead Levels in Children Associated With the Flint Drinking Water Crisis: A Spatial Analysis of Risk and Public Health Response.
pmid:26691115.finding: After Flint switched water source, the share of young children with elevated blood lead rose from 2.4% to 4.9%, and by 6.6 points in the highest-water-lead neighbourhoods.

pmid:30189517.authors: He X, Karagas MR, Murray C
pmid:30189517.title: Impact of receipt of private well arsenic test results on maternal use of contaminated drinking water in a U.S. population.
pmid:30189517.finding: Mothers told their well water exceeded 10 ug/L arsenic were less likely to use it for drinking, cooking (OR 0.34) and mixing formula (OR 0.45).

pmid:30356230.authors: Hertz-Picciotto I, Sass JB, Engel S, et al.
pmid:30356230.title: Organophosphate exposures during pregnancy and child neurodevelopment: Recommendations for essential policy reforms.
pmid:30356230.finding: Policy review concluding that organophosphate exposure in pregnancy is linked to cognitive, behavioural and neurological deficits in children and recommending phasing out organophosphates.

pmid:33298332.authors: Hosseini F, Majdi M, Naghshi S, et al.
pmid:33298332.title: Nitrate-nitrite exposure through drinking water and diet and risk of colorectal cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.
pmid:33298332.finding: Dietary nitrate was marginally related to colorectal cancer, but drinking-water nitrate and dietary nitrite were not, in dose-response analyses.

pmid:34627799.authors: Ibarluzea J, Gallastegi M, Santa-Marina L, et al.
pmid:34627799.title: Prenatal exposure to fluoride and neuropsychological development in early childhood: 1-to 4 years old children.
pmid:34627799.finding: In a Spanish cohort at low fluoride exposure, higher maternal urinary fluoride was associated with better cognitive scores in boys at age 4.

pmid:39362658.authors: Iheozor-Ejiofor Z, Walsh T, Lewis SR, et al.
pmid:39362658.title: Water fluoridation for the prevention of dental caries.
pmid:39362658.finding: Cochrane 2024: post-1975 evidence suggests starting fluoridation reduces decay by about a quarter of a tooth (dmft MD 0.24, CI includes no benefit); at 0.7 ppm about 12% have fluorosis of aesthetic concern.

pmid:27258851.authors: Jones RR, Weyer PJ, DellaValle CT, et al.
pmid:27258851.title: Nitrate from Drinking Water and Diet and Bladder Cancer Among Postmenopausal Women in Iowa.
pmid:27258851.finding: Long-term water nitrate above 5 mg/L nitrate-N was associated with bladder cancer, most strongly in current smokers (HR 3.67); dietary nitrate and nitrite were not.

pmid:30871546.authors: Juberg DR, Hoberman AM, Marty S, et al.
pmid:30871546.title: Letter to the editor regarding "safety of safety evaluation of pesticides: developmental neurotoxicity of chlorpyrifos and chlorpyrifos-methyl" by Mie et al. (environmental health. 2018. 17:77).
pmid:30871546.finding: Letter from authors including a Dow scientist disputing Mie et al.'s re-analysis of the chlorpyrifos developmental neurotoxicity studies.

pmid:33447891.authors: Kabat GC, Price WJ, Tarone RE
pmid:33447891.title: On recent meta-analyses of exposure to glyphosate and risk of non-Hodgkin's lymphoma in humans.
pmid:33447891.finding: Re-analysis showing the glyphosate-NHL summary estimate depends on exposure definition and lag choice: RR 1.41 with highest-exposure/20-year-lag estimates, but RR 1.05 (0.87-1.28) for ever-exposure with no lag.

pmid:23984718.authors: Kamerud KL, Hobbie KA, Anderson KA
pmid:23984718.title: Stainless steel leaches nickel and chromium into foods during cooking.
pmid:23984718.finding: Cooking tomato sauce in stainless steel raised nickel up to 34-fold and chromium 35-fold; leaching fell after six uses, leaving about 88 ug nickel and 86 ug chromium per serving by the tenth cycle.

pmid:28539253.authors: Khemiri R, Côté J, Fetoui H, et al.
pmid:28539253.title: Documenting the kinetic time course of lambda-cyhalothrin metabolites in orally exposed volunteers for the interpretation of biomonitoring data.
pmid:28539253.finding: After an oral lambda-cyhalothrin dose, 3-PBA peaked at about 4 h and was eliminated with a half-life of about 6 h.

pmid:40974630.authors: Kono M, Chang WH, Chen NC, et al.
pmid:40974630.title: Association between urinary glyphosate and aminomethylphosphonic acid concentrations and DNA damage biomarkers among rural populations in Taiwan.
pmid:40974630.finding: Each doubling of urinary glyphosate and AMPA was associated with 11-19% higher urinary 8-OHdG and higher N7-methylguanine.

pmid:35981405.authors: Kohsuwan K, Intayoung U, Khacha-Ananda S, et al.
pmid:35981405.title: Urinary glyphosate kinetics after occupational exposure.
pmid:35981405.finding: After spraying, urinary glyphosate peaked at about 11 h with an elimination half-life of 7-18 h.

pmid:37120936.authors: Kumar JV, Moss ME, Liu H, et al.
pmid:37120936.title: Association between low fluoride exposure and children's intelligence: a meta-analysis relevant to community water fluoridation.
pmid:37120936.finding: In studies at fluoride levels relevant to community water fluoridation, fluoride exposure was not associated with lower children's IQ.

pmid:11940450.authors: Kurttio P, Auvinen A, Salonen L, et al.
pmid:11940450.title: Renal effects of uranium in drinking water.
pmid:11940450.finding: Uranium in well water was weakly associated with altered proximal tubule function without a threshold, but not with glomerular function.

pmid:16731292.authors: Kurttio P, Harmoinen A, Saha H, et al.
pmid:16731292.title: Kidney toxicity of ingested uranium from drinking water.
pmid:16731292.finding: At median 25 ug/L (up to 1,500 ug/L), no kidney cytotoxicity was found, but uranium was associated with higher blood pressure and urinary glucose.

pmid:29544878.authors: Lanphear BP, Rauch S, Auinger P, et al.
pmid:29544878.title: Low-level lead exposure and mortality in US adults: a population-based cohort study.
pmid:29544878.finding: Blood lead in the range 1-6.7 ug/dL was associated with higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality; an estimated 18% of US deaths were attributable to low-level lead.

pmid:34339697.authors: Lesseur C, Pathak KV, Pirrotte P, et al.
pmid:34339697.title: Urinary glyphosate concentration in pregnant women in relation to length of gestation.
pmid:34339697.finding: Urinary glyphosate and AMPA were linked to shorter gestation only among spontaneous deliveries (HR 1.31, 1.00-1.71) and not to preterm birth <37 weeks.

pmid:29556976.authors: Levallois P, Barn P, Valcke M, et al.
pmid:29556976.title: Public Health Consequences of Lead in Drinking Water.
pmid:29556976.finding: Review: water lead clearly raises children's blood lead even at low levels; mitigation strategies work; no threshold exists for neurodevelopmental effects.

pmid:16889815.authors: Levesque S, Rodriguez MJ, Serodes J, et al.
pmid:16889815.title: Effects of indoor drinking water handling on trihalomethanes and haloacetic acids.
pmid:16889815.finding: In household tests, refrigerating water in a jug cut THMs by about 30%, boiling plus storage by 87% and a carbon-filter pitcher plus storage by 92%; the pitcher also cut haloacetic acids by 66%, whereas boiling did not lower total HAAs.

pmid:39761058.title: Caution Needed in Interpreting the Evidence Base on Fluoride and IQ.
pmid:39761058.finding: Editorial cautioning that the fluoride-IQ meta-analysis relies largely on high-exposure, high-risk-of-bias studies and does not establish effects at community water fluoridation levels.

pmid:31226556.authors: Li AJ, Martinez-Moral MP, Kannan K
pmid:31226556.title: Temporal variability in urinary pesticide concentrations in repeated-spot and first-morning-void samples and its association with oxidative stress in healthy individuals.
pmid:31226556.finding: Urinary pesticide concentrations were highly variable within people (ICC <0.38); 18-140 samples per person would be needed to estimate an individual's mean; concentrations correlated with oxidative damage markers.

pmid:31869729.authors: Li AJ, Martinez-Moral MP, Kannan K
pmid:31869729.title: Variability in urinary neonicotinoid concentrations in single-spot and first-morning void and its association with oxidative stress markers.
pmid:31869729.finding: Most urinary neonicotinoids had poor reproducibility (ICC 0.02-0.37); 16-172 samples would be needed per person, so one sample misclassifies exposure; some neonicotinoids correlated with oxidative stress markers.

pmid:38143003.authors: Li S, Wu S, Cheng X, et al.
pmid:38143003.title: Adsorption, boiling or membrane filtration for disinfection by-product removal: How to make our drinking water safer?
pmid:38143003.finding: Comparison of point-of-use treatments: boiling removed volatile DBPs but only about 15% of non-volatile haloacetic acids; membrane filtration removed about 45% of THMs and 75% of HAAs.

pmid:33280923.authors: Lin X, Pan W, Liu J
pmid:33280923.title: Variability of urinary pyrethroid biomarkers in Chinese young-aged men and women over one year.
pmid:33280923.finding: 3-PBA reproducibility in spot urine was poor (ICC <0.15); at least four samples 3 months apart were needed for a reliable estimate over a year.

pmid:36631499.authors: Lin L, St Clair S, Gamble GD, et al.
pmid:36631499.title: Nitrate contamination in drinking water and adverse reproductive and birth outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:36631499.finding: Higher drinking-water nitrate was associated with slightly more preterm birth (OR 1.05, 1.01-1.10) and neural tube defects in case-control studies (OR 1.51 high vs low); other birth defects were inconsistent.

pmid:32018134.authors: Liu C, Wang YX, Chen YJ, et al.
pmid:32018134.title: Blood and urinary biomarkers of prenatal exposure to disinfection byproducts and oxidative stress: A repeated measurement analysis.
pmid:32018134.finding: Blood THMs and urinary haloacetic acids were associated in a dose-response manner with urinary 8-OHdG, 8-isoprostane and HNE-MA across pregnancy.

pmid:36030853.authors: Luo Y, Gibson CT, Chuah C, et al.
pmid:36030853.title: Raman imaging for the identification of Teflon microplastics and nanoplastics released from non-stick cookware.
pmid:36030853.finding: Raman imaging suggested thousands to millions of PTFE micro- and nanoplastic particles may be released from scratched non-stick pans during simulated cooking.

pmid:18379423.authors: MacLehose RF, Savitz DA, Herring AH, et al.
pmid:18379423.title: Drinking water disinfection by-products and time to pregnancy.
pmid:18379423.finding: Drinking-water disinfection by-products were not associated with longer time to pregnancy.

pmid:35439459.authors: Makris KC, Efthymiou N, Konstantinou C, et al.
pmid:35439459.title: Oxidative stress of glyphosate, AMPA and metabolites of pyrethroids and chlorpyrifos pesticides among primary school children in Cyprus.
pmid:35439459.finding: Urinary AMPA (but not glyphosate), 3-PBA and TCPy were associated with higher 8-OHdG; no pesticide was associated with 8-isoprostane.

pmid:38767917.authors: Malin AJ, Eckel SP, Hu H, et al.
pmid:38767917.title: Maternal Urinary Fluoride and Child Neurobehavior at Age 36 Months.
pmid:38767917.finding: Each IQR (0.68 mg/L) increase in maternal urinary fluoride was associated with 1.83-fold odds of borderline or clinical total behaviour problems at 36 months.

pmid:34309045.authors: McLaren L, Patterson SK, Faris P, et al.
pmid:34309045.title: Fluoridation cessation and children's dental caries: A 7-year follow-up evaluation of Grade 2 schoolchildren in Calgary and Edmonton, Canada.
pmid:34309045.n: Grade 2 children in Calgary and Edmonton
pmid:34309045.finding: Seven years after Calgary stopped fluoridation, primary-tooth decay increased more than in still-fluoridated Edmonton.

pmid:30442131.authors: Mie A, Rudén C, Grandjean P
pmid:30442131.title: Safety of Safety Evaluation of Pesticides: developmental neurotoxicity of chlorpyrifos and chlorpyrifos-methyl.
pmid:30442131.finding: Re-examination of industry developmental-neurotoxicity studies of chlorpyrifos(-methyl) found effects in the raw data that were not reported in test summaries, suggesting the submitted conclusions may be misleading.

pmid:37259092.title: Non-disclosure of developmental neurotoxicity studies obstructs the safety assessment of pesticides in the European Union.
pmid:37259092.finding: Analysis showing that developmental neurotoxicity studies submitted to US EPA for several pesticides had not been disclosed to EU regulators, obstructing EU safety assessment.

pmid:18783726.authors: Mink PJ, Alexander DD, Barraj LM, et al.
pmid:18783726.title: Low-level arsenic exposure in drinking water and bladder cancer: a review and meta-analysis.
pmid:18783726.finding: Low-level drinking-water arsenic was not a significant independent bladder cancer risk factor (summary RR 1.11, 0.95-1.30); estimates in never-smokers were below 1.0.

pmid:24061511.authors: Moon KA, Guallar E, Umans JG, et al.
pmid:24061511.title: Association between exposure to low to moderate arsenic levels and incident cardiovascular disease. A prospective cohort study.
pmid:24061511.finding: In the Strong Heart Study, low-to-moderate urinary arsenic was associated with incident cardiovascular disease (HR 1.32) and coronary heart disease; associations weakened after adjusting for diabetes, hypertension and kidney measures.

pmid:29040626.authors: Moon KA, Oberoi S, Barchowsky A, et al.
pmid:29040626.title: A dose-response meta-analysis of chronic arsenic exposure and incident cardiovascular disease.
pmid:29040626.finding: Per 20 ug/L water arsenic, CVD incidence was 9% higher and CHD mortality 16% higher, with no evidence of a threshold across low-moderate to high levels.

pmid:26584066.authors: Morgan MK, Sobus JR, Barr DB, et al.
pmid:26584066.title: Temporal variability of pyrethroid metabolite levels in bedtime, morning, and 24-h urine samples for 50 adults in North Carolina.
pmid:26584066.finding: A single urinary 3-PBA measure poorly reflected average exposure (ICC <0.22 over a day, week and six weeks), whatever the sample type or dilution correction.

pmid:6200956.authors: Nolan RJ, Rick DL, Freshour NL, et al.
pmid:6200956.title: Chlorpyrifos: pharmacokinetics in human volunteers.
pmid:6200956.finding: After an oral chlorpyrifos dose, the metabolite TCP was eliminated in urine with a half-life of about 27 h; dermal absorption was below 3%.

pmid:39172715.title: NTP monograph on the state of the science concerning fluoride exposure and neurodevelopment and cognition: a systematic review.
pmid:39172715.finding: NTP concluded with moderate confidence that fluoride exposures above 1.5 mg/L in drinking water are consistently associated with lower IQ in children, while evidence at lower exposures is insufficient.

pmid:31288196.authors: Ospina M, Wong LY, Baker SE, et al.
pmid:31288196.title: Exposure to neonicotinoid insecticides in the U.S. general population: Data from the 2015-2016 national health and nutrition examination survey.
pmid:31288196.finding: About half of the US population aged 3 years and over had recent neonicotinoid exposure; metabolite levels were higher in summer and in young children.

pmid:40490737.authors: Panzacchi S, Tibaldi E, De Angelis L, et al.
pmid:40490737.title: Carcinogenic effects of long-term exposure from prenatal life to glyphosate and glyphosate-based herbicides in Sprague-Dawley rats.
pmid:40490737.finding: Lifelong exposure from prenatal life to glyphosate or glyphosate-based herbicides at doses equal to the EU acceptable daily intake caused dose-related increases in several benign and malignant tumours, including early-onset leukaemias.

pmid:29519238.authors: Parvez S, Gerona RR, Proctor C, et al.
pmid:29519238.title: Glyphosate exposure in pregnancy and shortened gestational length: a prospective Indiana birth cohort study.
pmid:29519238.finding: In an Indiana cohort, >90% of pregnant women had detectable urinary glyphosate, and higher levels correlated weakly with shorter gestation (r = -0.28); no link with fetal growth.

pmid:40272946.authors: Patterson KP, Gold AO, Spratlen MJ, et al.
pmid:40272946.title: Uranium Exposure, Hypertension, and Blood Pressure in the Strong Heart Family Study.
pmid:40272946.finding: Higher urinary uranium was associated with higher hypertension risk at levels typical of the Southwest and Great Plains.

pmid:35217009.authors: Picetti R, Deeney M, Pastorino S, et al.
pmid:35217009.title: Nitrate and nitrite contamination in drinking water and cancer risk: A systematic review with meta-analysis.
pmid:35217009.finding: Drinking-water nitrate was associated with gastric cancer (OR 1.91 per 10 mg/L) but not with colorectal cancer (OR 1.02, 0.96-1.08) or any other site.

pmid:16096677.authors: Powley CR, Michalczyk MJ, Kaiser MA, et al.
pmid:16096677.title: Determination of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) extractable from the surface of commercial cookware under simulated cooking conditions by LC/MS/MS.
pmid:16096677.finding: DuPont scientists found no detectable PFOA extractable from fluoropolymer-coated pans under simulated cooking conditions (limit 100 pg/cm2).

pmid:783195.authors: Rabinowitz MB, Wetherill GW, Kopple JD
pmid:783195.title: Kinetic analysis of lead metabolism in healthy humans.
pmid:783195.finding: Stable-isotope tracing showed blood lead has a mean life of about 35 days, soft tissue about 40 days, and bone a very slow turnover holding most body lead.

pmid:17351293.authors: Rahman A, Vahter M, Ekström EC, et al.
pmid:17351293.title: Association of arsenic exposure during pregnancy with fetal loss and infant death: a cohort study in Bangladesh.
pmid:17351293.finding: Drinking well water with >50 ug/L arsenic during pregnancy was associated with more fetal loss (RR 1.14) and infant death (RR 1.17).

pmid:28615257.authors: Rappaport AI, Whitfield KC, Chapman GE, et al.
pmid:28615257.title: Randomized controlled trial assessing the efficacy of a reusable fish-shaped iron ingot to increase hemoglobin concentration in anemic, rural Cambodian women.
pmid:28615257.finding: Neither a fish-shaped iron ingot nor iron supplements raised haemoglobin at 6 or 12 months where iron deficiency was uncommon.

pmid:21507777.authors: Rauh V, Arunajadai S, Horton M, et al.
pmid:21507777.title: Seven-year neurodevelopmental scores and prenatal exposure to chlorpyrifos, a common agricultural pesticide.
pmid:21507777.finding: Each SD increase in prenatal cord-blood chlorpyrifos was associated with 1.4% lower full-scale IQ and 2.8% lower working memory at age 7, adjusted for maternal IQ, education and home environment.

pmid:35397220.authors: Ravalli F, Yu Y, Bostick BC, et al.
pmid:35397220.title: Sociodemographic inequalities in uranium and other metals in community water systems across the USA, 2006-11: a cross-sectional study.
pmid:35397220.finding: Uranium was under-recognised in US public water and higher in systems serving semi-urban Hispanic communities and in groundwater-reliant systems.

pmid:19064650.authors: Rondeau V, Jacqmin-Gadda H, Commenges D, et al.
pmid:19064650.title: Aluminum and silica in drinking water and the risk of Alzheimer's disease or cognitive decline: findings from 15-year follow-up of the PAQUID cohort.
pmid:19064650.finding: Aluminium intake >=0.1 mg/day from drinking water was associated with faster cognitive decline and dementia risk, but geographic aluminium exposure was not.

pmid:34267307.title: Are there excess fetal deaths attributable to waterborne lead exposure during the Flint Water Crisis? Evidence from bio-kinetic model predictions and Vital Records.
pmid:34267307.finding: Biokinetic modelling and vital records did not support excess fetal deaths or reduced fertility from water lead during the Flint crisis; the 6.8% fertility drop was within normal variation.

pmid:28913736.title: PTFE-coated non-stick cookware and toxicity concerns: a perspective.
pmid:28913736.finding: Perspective: toxicity of ingested PTFE coating flakes is not understood; residual PFOA can be released at cooking temperatures, and replacements such as GenX may be similarly toxic.

pmid:16957027.authors: Savitz DA, Singer PC, Herring AH, et al.
pmid:16957027.title: Exposure to drinking water disinfection by-products and pregnancy loss.
pmid:16957027.finding: In a three-site US study designed to test the earlier finding, trihalomethanes, haloacetic acids and total organic halide were not associated with pregnancy loss (OR 1.1, 0.7-1.7 for the previously high-risk group).

pmid:29435982.authors: Schullehner J, Hansen B, Thygesen M, et al.
pmid:29435982.title: Nitrate in drinking water and colorectal cancer risk: A nationwide population-based cohort study.
pmid:29435982.finding: The highest vs lowest drinking-water nitrate exposure was associated with 16% higher colorectal cancer risk (HR 1.16, 1.08-1.25), with significant increases from 3.87 mg/L nitrate, far below the 50 mg/L standard.

pmid:33949893.authors: Sherris AR, Baiocchi M, Fendorf S, et al.
pmid:33949893.title: Nitrate in Drinking Water during Pregnancy and Spontaneous Preterm Birth: A Retrospective Within-Mother Analysis in California.
pmid:33949893.finding: Comparing siblings born to the same mother, tap-water nitrate 5-<10 mg/L nitrate-N was associated with slightly higher odds of spontaneous preterm birth (OR 1.08 at 32-36 weeks; 2.52 for 20-31 weeks at >=10 mg/L).

pmid:17593716.authors: Sinclair E, Kim SK, Akinleye HB, et al.
pmid:17593716.title: Quantitation of gas-phase perfluoroalkyl surfactants and fluorotelomer alcohols released from nonstick cookware and microwave popcorn bags.
pmid:17593716.finding: Heating four brands of non-stick pans at normal cooking temperatures released 7-337 ng PFOA per pan into the gas phase, decreasing with repeated use; microwave popcorn bags also released PFOA.

pmid:37558699.authors: Spaur M, Glabonjat RA, Schilling K, et al.
pmid:37558699.title: Contribution of arsenic and uranium in private wells and community water systems to urinary biomarkers in US adults: The Strong Heart Study and the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
pmid:37558699.finding: Private-well and public-water arsenic and uranium were major contributors to urinary arsenic and uranium, even at levels below regulatory limits.

pmid:42486290.authors: Spaur M, Schilling K, Glabonjat RA, et al.
pmid:42486290.title: Associations of drinking water and urinary uranium with incident diabetes among U.S. adults: The Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis and the Strong Heart Family Study.
pmid:42486290.n: MESA and Strong Heart Family Study
pmid:42486290.finding: Public-water and urinary uranium were not associated with incident type 2 diabetes at low exposure (median <1.2 ug/L).

pmid:31886823.title: Pyrethroid Insecticides-Time for a Closer Look.
pmid:31886823.finding: Invited commentary on the NHANES pyrethroid-mortality study calling for closer scrutiny and replication of pyrethroid health effects.

pmid:31596611.authors: Susmann HP, Schaider LA, Rodgers KM, et al.
pmid:31596611.title: Dietary Habits Related to Food Packaging and Population Exposure to PFASs.
pmid:31596611.finding: Daily microwave popcorn was associated with up to 63% higher serum PFDA, and more home-cooked food with lower serum PFAS, implicating food packaging.

pmid:39761023.authors: Taylor KW, Eftim SE, Sibrizzi CA, et al.
pmid:39761023.title: Fluoride Exposure and Children's IQ Scores: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
pmid:39761023.finding: Across 74 studies, fluoride exposure was inversely associated with children's IQ (SMD -0.45); IQ fell 1.63 points per 1 mg/L urinary fluoride, but the drinking-water association was null below 1.5 mg/L except in low-risk-of-bias studies; 64 of the 74 studies were cross-sectional and 47 of 59 group-level studies had high risk of bias.

pmid:41393310.authors: Taylor KW, Eftim SE, Sibrizzi CA, et al.
pmid:41393310.title: Addressing Critiques of the Evidence Linking Fluoride and Children's IQ.
pmid:41393310.finding: NTP authors' response to critiques of the fluoride-IQ evidence, maintaining that inverse associations persisted below 1.5 mg/L using urinary and water measures.

pmid:40998639.authors: Temkin AM, Subramaniam V, Friedman A, et al.
pmid:40998639.title: A cumulative dietary pesticide exposure score based on produce consumption is associated with urinary pesticide biomarkers in a U.S. biomonitoring cohort.
pmid:40998639.finding: A produce-based dietary pesticide score tracked urinary organophosphate, pyrethroid and neonicotinoid biomarkers only after excluding potatoes.

pmid:31659427.authors: Tietz T, Lenzner A, Kolbaum AE, et al.
pmid:31659427.title: Aggregated aluminium exposure: risk assessment for the general population.
pmid:31659427.finding: German risk assessment: combined aluminium from food, cosmetics and uncoated aluminium food contact can exceed EFSA's tolerable weekly intake, especially in adolescents.

pmid:34397175.authors: Vicini JL, Jensen PK, Young BM, et al.
pmid:34397175.title: Residues of glyphosate in food and dietary exposure.
pmid:34397175.journal: Compr Rev Food Sci Food Saf
pmid:34397175.finding: Review of glyphosate residues: dietary modelling and urinary biomonitoring indicate exposure under 3% of the EU acceptable daily intake of 0.5 mg/kg body weight.

pmid:15097021.authors: Villanueva CM, Cantor KP, Cordier S, et al.
pmid:15097021.title: Disinfection byproducts and bladder cancer: a pooled analysis.
pmid:15097021.finding: Pooled analysis: men exposed to average trihalomethanes >1 ug/L had OR 1.24 for bladder cancer, rising to 1.44 above 50 ug/L; no association in women.

pmid:17079692.authors: Villanueva CM, Cantor KP, Grimalt JO, et al.
pmid:17079692.title: Bladder cancer and exposure to water disinfection by-products through ingestion, bathing, showering, and swimming in pools.
pmid:17079692.finding: Household THM >49 vs <=8 ug/L was associated with doubled bladder cancer risk (OR 2.10); showering/bathing duration (OR 1.83) and swimming-pool use (OR 1.57) contributed beyond drinking.

pmid:26098935.title: Brief Report: Meta-analysis of Antacid Use and Alzheimer's Disease: Implications for the Aluminum Hypothesis.
pmid:26098935.finding: Regular antacid use, a large aluminium source, was not associated with Alzheimer's disease (case-control OR 1.0; cohort RR 0.8).

pmid:6831427.authors: Wagner DA, Schultz DS, Deen WM, et al.
pmid:6831427.title: Metabolic fate of an oral dose of 15N-labeled nitrate in humans: effect of diet supplementation with ascorbic acid.
pmid:6831427.finding: After an oral dose of labelled nitrate, about 60% appeared in urine within 48 h; the body half-life of nitrate was about 5 hours.

pmid:9504280.authors: Waller K, Swan SH, DeLorenze G, et al.
pmid:9504280.title: Trihalomethanes in drinking water and spontaneous abortion.
pmid:9504280.finding: Drinking >=5 glasses a day of cold tap water with >=75 ug/L total trihalomethanes was associated with spontaneous abortion (OR 1.8, 1.1-3.0), mainly bromodichloromethane.

pmid:34808154.authors: Wang A, Wan Y, Zhou L, et al.
pmid:34808154.title: Neonicotinoid insecticide metabolites in seminal plasma: Associations with semen quality.
pmid:34808154.finding: Neonicotinoid metabolites were detected in seminal plasma; imidacloprid-olefin was associated with 17-21% lower progressive motility, with no other inverse associations.

pmid:38145670.authors: Wang A, Wan Y, Qi W, et al.
pmid:38145670.title: Urinary biomarkers of exposure to organophosphate, pyrethroid, neonicotinoid insecticides and oxidative stress: A repeated measurement analysis among pregnant women.
pmid:38145670.finding: Across repeated urine samples in pregnancy, organophosphate, pyrethroid and neonicotinoid metabolites and their mixture were associated with higher 8-OHdG, 8-OHG and HNE-MA (lipid peroxidation).

pmid:30041450.authors: Ward MH, Jones RR, Brender JD, et al.
pmid:30041450.title: Drinking Water Nitrate and Human Health: An Updated Review.
pmid:30041450.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
pmid:30041450.finding: Updated review: besides methaemoglobinaemia, the strongest evidence for harm from drinking-water nitrate is for colorectal cancer, thyroid disease and neural tube defects, often at levels below regulatory limits; endogenous nitrosation modifies risk.

pmid:35100934.authors: Weidenhamer JD, Chasant M, Gottesfeld P
pmid:35100934.title: Metal exposures from source materials for artisanal aluminum cookware.
