pmid:35100934.finding: Artisanal pots cast from scrap aluminium released aluminium above guidelines and variable lead, cadmium, chromium and nickel; choosing scrap sources did not avoid contamination.

pmid:10854122.authors: Williams GM, Kroes R, Munro IC
pmid:10854122.title: Safety evaluation and risk assessment of the herbicide Roundup and its active ingredient, glyphosate, for humans.
pmid:10854122.finding: RETRACTED (December 2025): an influential review concluding that glyphosate and Roundup pose no human health concern; flagged here only because it was retracted.

pmid:41428335.authors: Williams GM, Kroes R, Munro IC
pmid:41428335.title: Retraction notice to "Safety evaluation and risk assessment of the herbicide roundup and its active ingredient, glyphosate, for humans" [Regul. Toxicol. Pharm. 31 (2000) 117-165].
pmid:41428335.finding: Retraction notice for the 2000 Williams, Kroes and Munro glyphosate safety review in Regulatory Toxicology and Pharmacology.

pmid:39311776.authors: Wolf N, Müller L, Enge S, et al.
pmid:39311776.title: Analysis of PFAS and further VOC from fluoropolymer-coated cookware by thermal desorption-gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (TD-GC-MS).
pmid:39311776.journal: Food Addit Contam Part A Chem Anal Control Expo Risk Assess
pmid:39311776.finding: Thermal extraction at 250 C detected no PFAS in 12 of 18 coated cookware items; a baking tray and baking mat released PFCAs, and emissions disappeared after the first extraction.

pmid:37939249.authors: Wrobel SA, Bury D, Koslitz S, et al.
pmid:37939249.title: Quantitative Metabolism and Urinary Elimination Kinetics of Seven Neonicotinoids and Neonicotinoid-Like Compounds in Humans.
pmid:37939249.finding: Urinary elimination half-times of seven neonicotinoids ranged from 2.5 h (acetamiprid) to 49.5 h (sulfoxaflor).

pmid:40724526.authors: Wu WY, Wang DS, Lin HC, et al.
pmid:40724526.title: Urinary Glyphosate Concentrations and Serum Sex Hormones in a Nationally Representative U.S. Sample: NHANES 2017-2018.
pmid:40724526.finding: Higher urinary glyphosate was associated with lower AMH, androstenedione, oestrogens and progesterone and higher SHBG; the authors note the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.

pmid:22776062.authors: Xu W, Bao H, Liu F, et al.
pmid:22776062.title: Environmental exposure to arsenic may reduce human semen quality: associations derived from a Chinese cross-sectional study.
pmid:22776062.finding: Urinary dimethylarsinic acid above the median was associated with below-reference sperm concentration.

pmid:31342895.authors: Zhang L, Rana I, Shaffer RM, et al.
pmid:31342895.title: Exposure to glyphosate-based herbicides and risk for non-Hodgkin lymphoma: A meta-analysis and supporting evidence.
pmid:31342895.finding: Using the highest-exposure groups from five case-control studies and the 2018 AHS update, high cumulative glyphosate-herbicide exposure was associated with 41% higher NHL risk (meta-RR 1.41, 95% CI 1.13-1.75).

pmid:35344909.title: Human exposure to neonicotinoids and the associated health risks: A review.
pmid:35344909.finding: Review of human biomonitoring: neonicotinoid metabolites are detected more often than parent compounds, Asian levels exceed US/European levels, and large epidemiological studies are lacking.

pmid:19648152.title: On the possible origins of DNA damage in human spermatozoa
pmid:19648152.finding: Proposes the two-step hypothesis: defective chromatin remodelling (poor protamination) during spermiogenesis leaves sperm vulnerable, and oxidative stress then breaks the DNA.

pmid:19494251.authors: De Iuliis GN, Thomson LK, Mitchell LA, et al.
pmid:19494251.title: DNA damage in human spermatozoa is highly correlated with the efficiency of chromatin remodeling and the formation of 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine, a marker of oxidative stress
pmid:19494251.finding: In human sperm, poor protamination correlated strongly with 8-OHdG formation and with DNA fragmentation (P<0.001), supporting the two-step hypothesis.

pmid:18492763.authors: Koppers AJ, De Iuliis GN, Finnie JM, et al.
pmid:18492763.title: Significance of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species in the generation of oxidative stress in spermatozoa
pmid:18492763.finding: Electron leak from mitochondrial complex I in human sperm causes midpiece lipid peroxidation and loss of motility, preventable by alpha-tocopherol in vitro.

pmid:24369131.authors: Aitken RJ, Smith TB, Jobling MS, et al.
pmid:24369131.title: Oxidative stress and male reproductive health
pmid:24369131.finding: Sperm carry only OGG1, the first enzyme of base excision repair; the oocyte must finish repairing oxidised bases before the first S-phase, and errors become mutations in every cell of the embryo.

pmid:27062870.authors: Aitken RJ, Gibb Z, Baker MA, et al.
pmid:27062870.title: Causes and consequences of oxidative stress in spermatozoa
pmid:27062870.finding: Sperm are vulnerable because their membranes are rich in polyunsaturated fatty acids and they have almost no cytoplasm for antioxidant enzymes; stressed sperm default to an apoptotic pathway with mitochondrial ROS and oxidative DNA damage.

pmid:36604857.title: DNA damage in testicular germ cells and spermatozoa. When and how is it induced? How should we measure it? What does it mean?
pmid:36604857.finding: In mature sperm, hydrogen peroxide released from the midpiece (not nucleases) penetrates the nucleus and drives DNA damage; reviews what each SDF assay actually measures.

pmid:37568254.title: Male reproductive ageing: a radical road to ruin
pmid:37568254.finding: Paternal ageing brings more sperm DNA damage, epigenetic change in the germ line and a higher mutational load in offspring.

pmid:14285045.title: KINETICS OF THE GERMINAL EPITHELIUM IN MAN
pmid:14285045.finding: Classic radiolabelling study of the kinetics of the human germinal epithelium, the source of the widely quoted ~74-day duration of spermatogenesis.

pmid:16406920.authors: Misell LM, Holochwost D, Boban D, et al.
pmid:16406920.title: A stable isotope-mass spectrometric method for measuring human spermatogenesis kinetics in vivo
pmid:16406920.finding: Deuterium labelling: newly made sperm first appeared in the ejaculate after 64 +/- 8 days (range 42-76).

pmid:34954800.authors: Newman H, Catt S, Vining B, et al.
pmid:34954800.title: DNA repair and response to sperm DNA damage in oocytes and embryos, and the potential consequences in ART: a systematic review
pmid:34954800.finding: Systematic review: oocytes and early embryos can repair paternal DNA damage, but the capacity is limited and likely declines with maternal age.

pmid:33589137.authors: Setti AS, Braga DPAF, Provenza RR, et al.
pmid:33589137.title: Oocyte ability to repair sperm DNA fragmentation: the impact of maternal age on intracytoplasmic sperm injection outcomes
pmid:33589137.finding: Sperm DNA fragmentation >=30% (SCD) harmed ICSI outcomes only when the woman was over 40 (pregnancy 7.7% vs 20.0%); no effect at 40 or younger.

pmid:17681311.authors: Meseguer M, Martínez-Conejero JA, O'Connor JE, et al.
pmid:17681311.title: The significance of sperm DNA oxidation in embryo development and reproductive outcome in an oocyte donation program: a new model to study a male infertility prognostic factor
pmid:17681311.finding: With the same donor's eggs split between couples, higher sperm DNA oxidation was linked to poorer embryo development and blastocyst formation.

pmid:10632410.authors: Spanò M, Bonde JP, Hjøllund HI, et al.
pmid:10632410.title: Sperm chromatin damage impairs human fertility. The Danish First Pregnancy Planner Study Team
pmid:10632410.finding: In first-pregnancy planners, the chance of conceiving per cycle fell as SCSA-abnormal sperm rose and became small above 40%.

pmid:10221239.authors: Evenson DP, Jost LK, Marshall D, et al.
pmid:10221239.title: Utility of the sperm chromatin structure assay as a diagnostic and prognostic tool in the human fertility clinic
pmid:10221239.finding: No couple conceived naturally when the man's SCSA DNA fragmentation was >=30%; 84% of men whose partners conceived in months 1-3 were below 15%.

pmid:16921163.authors: Bungum M, Humaidan P, Axmon A, et al.
pmid:16921163.title: Sperm DNA integrity assessment in prediction of assisted reproduction technology outcome
pmid:16921163.finding: DFI >30% predicted lower pregnancy and delivery after IUI; with DFI >30%, ICSI did better than conventional IVF.

pmid:22791753.authors: Robinson L, Gallos ID, Conner SJ, et al.
pmid:22791753.title: The effect of sperm DNA fragmentation on miscarriage rates: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:22791753.finding: High sperm DNA damage doubled the risk of miscarriage (RR 2.16, 95% CI 1.54-3.03); strongest with TUNEL (RR 3.94).

pmid:31056315.authors: McQueen DB, Zhang J, Robins JC
pmid:31056315.title: Sperm DNA fragmentation and recurrent pregnancy loss: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:31056315.finding: Male partners of women with recurrent pregnancy loss had sperm DNA fragmentation 11.9 points higher than partners of fertile women.

pmid:27345006.authors: Simon L, Zini A, Dyachenko A, et al.
pmid:27345006.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis to determine the effect of sperm DNA damage on in vitro fertilization and intracytoplasmic sperm injection outcome
pmid:27345006.finding: Sperm DNA damage was associated with lower clinical pregnancy after IVF and/or ICSI (combined OR 1.68).

pmid:25530036.authors: Osman A, Alsomait H, Seshadri S, et al.
pmid:25530036.title: The effect of sperm DNA fragmentation on live birth rate after IVF or ICSI: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:25530036.finding: Low sperm DNA fragmentation was associated with higher live birth after IVF/ICSI (RR 1.17); the ICSI effect was small and not robust in sensitivity analysis.

pmid:23028579.authors: Ribas-Maynou J, García-Peiró A, Fernandez-Encinas A, et al.
pmid:23028579.title: Double stranded sperm DNA breaks, measured by Comet assay, are associated with unexplained recurrent miscarriage in couples without a female factor
pmid:23028579.finding: A high double-strand break profile (neutral Comet) was found in 85% of men from couples with unexplained recurrent miscarriage vs 33% of fertile donors.

pmid:26780327.authors: Sharma R, Ahmad G, Esteves SC, et al.
pmid:26780327.title: Terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick end labeling (TUNEL) assay using bench top flow cytometer for evaluation of sperm DNA fragmentation in fertility laboratories: protocol, reference values, and quality control
pmid:26780327.finding: Flow-cytometric TUNEL reference cut-off of 16.8% had 91.6% specificity but only 32.6% sensitivity.

pmid:23391408.authors: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
pmid:23391408.title: The clinical utility of sperm DNA integrity testing: a guideline
pmid:23391408.finding: ASRM 2013: sperm DNA integrity tests do not reliably predict treatment outcomes and cannot be recommended routinely.

pmid:33309062.authors: Schlegel PN, Sigman M, Collura B, et al.
pmid:33309062.title: Diagnosis and treatment of infertility in men: AUA/ASRM guideline part I
pmid:33309062.finding: AUA/ASRM guideline part I (evaluation): do not order SDF in the initial work-up; do evaluate SDF (and karyotype) in the male partner of couples with recurrent pregnancy loss.

pmid:33309061.authors: Schlegel PN, Sigman M, Collura B, et al.
pmid:33309061.title: Diagnosis and treatment of infertility in men: AUA/ASRM guideline part II
pmid:33309061.finding: AUA/ASRM guideline part II (treatment): counsel that supplements are of questionable clinical utility; consider varicocelectomy for palpable varicocele with abnormal semen; do not prescribe testosterone to men wanting fertility.

pmid:39145501.authors: Brannigan RE, Hermanson L, Kaczmarek J, et al.
pmid:39145501.title: Updates to Male Infertility: AUA/ASRM Guideline (2024)
pmid:39145501.finding: 2024 AUA/ASRM amendment, including the statement that clinicians may consider testicular sperm in nonazoospermic men with elevated DNA fragmentation.

pmid:34511305.authors: Minhas S, Bettocchi C, Boeri L, et al.
pmid:34511305.title: European Association of Urology Guidelines on Male Sexual and Reproductive Health: 2021 Update on Male Infertility
pmid:34511305.finding: EAU 2021: SDF is a useful biomarker for ART outcomes; insufficient evidence for widespread empirical antioxidants or surgical sperm retrieval in men without azoospermia.

pmid:33422457.authors: Tharakan T, Bettocchi C, Carvalho J, et al.
pmid:33422457.title: European Association of Urology Guidelines Panel on Male Sexual and Reproductive Health: A Clinical Consultation Guide on the Indications for Performing Sperm DNA Fragmentation Testing in Men with Infertility and Testicular Sperm Extraction in Nonazoospermic Men
pmid:33422457.finding: EAU consultation guide on when to test SDF and on the still-experimental use of testicular sperm for ICSI in nonazoospermic men.

pmid:29082206.authors: Agarwal A, Cho CL, Majzoub A, et al.
pmid:29082206.title: The Society for Translational Medicine: clinical practice guidelines for sperm DNA fragmentation testing in male infertility
pmid:29082206.finding: Society for Translational Medicine guideline: test SDF in clinical varicocele with borderline semen, recurrent pregnancy loss, ART failure, unexplained infertility and men with lifestyle risk factors.

pmid:29082146.authors: Cho CL, Agarwal A, Majzoub A, et al.
pmid:29082146.title: Clinical utility of sperm DNA fragmentation testing: concise practice recommendations
pmid:29082146.finding: Concise expert practice recommendations on the clinical scenarios where SDF testing changes management.

pmid:33988000.authors: Agarwal A, Farkouh A, Parekh N, et al.
pmid:33988000.title: Sperm DNA Fragmentation: A Critical Assessment of Clinical Practice Guidelines
pmid:33988000.finding: Compares the Agarwal and Esteves SDF guidelines; both use thresholds around 20% for TUNEL/SCD/SCSA (about 26% for alkaline Comet) and link values above 20-30% to worse outcomes.

pmid:27260688.authors: Agarwal A, Sharma R, Roychoudhury S, et al.
pmid:27260688.title: MiOXSYS: a novel method of measuring oxidation reduction potential in semen and seminal plasma
pmid:27260688.finding: Introduced MiOXSYS oxidation-reduction potential (ORP) in semen; proposed a cut-off of 1.48 mV/10^6 sperm/mL.

pmid:31006711.authors: Agarwal A, Panner Selvam MK, Arafa M, et al.
pmid:31006711.title: Multi-center evaluation of oxidation-reduction potential by the MiOXSYS in males with abnormal semen
pmid:31006711.finding: ORP normalised to sperm concentration flagged abnormal semen with 98.1% sensitivity but only 40.6% specificity (AUC 0.765).

pmid:31081299.authors: Agarwal A, Parekh N, Panner Selvam MK, et al.
pmid:31081299.title: Male Oxidative Stress Infertility (MOSI): Proposed Terminology and Clinical Practice Guidelines for Management of Idiopathic Male Infertility
pmid:31081299.finding: Proposes the term 'Male Oxidative Stress Infertility'; 30-80% of infertile men have high seminal ROS; current antioxidant use is not evidence-based.

pmid:33831977.authors: Agarwal A, Finelli R, Selvam MKP, et al.
pmid:33831977.title: A Global Survey of Reproductive Specialists to Determine the Clinical Utility of Oxidative Stress Testing and Antioxidant Use in Male Infertility
pmid:33831977.finding: Global survey: 85.6% of reproductive specialists prescribe antioxidants, mostly for 3-6 months, while most do not test for oxidative stress and rate the supporting evidence as modest.

pmid:25527074.authors: Agarwal A, Mulgund A, Alshahrani S, et al.
pmid:25527074.title: Reactive oxygen species and sperm DNA damage in infertile men presenting with low level leukocytospermia
pmid:25527074.finding: Even low-level leukocytospermia (below 1 million WBC/mL) was associated with higher ROS and SDF (26.5% vs 19.9%).

pmid:36653793.authors: Szabó A, Váncsa S, Hegyi P, et al.
pmid:36653793.title: Lifestyle-, environmental-, and additional health factors associated with an increased sperm DNA fragmentation: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:36653793.finding: Mean SDF increase: varicocele +13.6, impaired glucose tolerance +13.8, age >=50 +12.6, air pollution +9.7, smoking +9.2 percentage points; abstinence length and chlamydia/HPV showed no clear effect.

pmid:41051027.authors: Ragheb A, Abdelbary A, Massoud A, et al.
pmid:41051027.title: Evaluating the effect of smoking and its cessation on semen parameters
pmid:41051027.finding: After quitting smoking, semen improved at 3 and again at 6 months (progressive motility 20.7% -> 35.3% -> 42.3%).

pmid:22809864.authors: Wang YJ, Zhang RQ, Lin YJ, et al.
pmid:22809864.title: Relationship between varicocele and sperm DNA damage and the effect of varicocele repair: a meta-analysis
pmid:22809864.finding: Men with varicocele had 9.8 points more sperm DNA damage than controls; varicocelectomy lowered it by 3.4 points.

pmid:33985792.authors: Lira Neto FT, Roque M, Esteves SC
pmid:33985792.title: Effect of varicocelectomy on sperm deoxyribonucleic acid fragmentation rates in infertile men with clinical varicocele: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:33985792.finding: Varicocelectomy lowered SDF by 7.2 points (95% CI 5.6-8.9), more in men with high pre-operative SDF.

pmid:33890288.authors: Persad E, O'Loughlin CA, Kaur S, et al.
pmid:33890288.title: Surgical or radiological treatment for varicoceles in subfertile men
pmid:33890288.finding: Cochrane: varicocele treatment may raise pregnancy rates (RR 1.55, low certainty); effect on live birth is uncertain.

pmid:31949297.authors: Sepidarkish M, Maleki-Hajiagha A, Maroufizadeh S, et al.
pmid:31949297.title: The effect of body mass index on sperm DNA fragmentation: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:31949297.finding: Only class I obesity (BMI 30-35) showed a small SDF increase (SMD 0.23); data insufficient for a firm BMI-SDF link.

pmid:26380863.authors: Campbell JM, Lane M, Owens JA, et al.
pmid:26380863.title: Paternal obesity negatively affects male fertility and assisted reproduction outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:26380863.finding: Obese men had more infertility (OR 1.66), lower live birth per ART cycle (OR 0.65) and more sperm DNA fragmentation.

pmid:39344112.authors: Santi D, Greco C, Barbonetti A, et al.
pmid:39344112.title: Weight Loss as Therapeutic Option to Restore Fertility in Obese Men: A Meta-Analytic Study
pmid:39344112.finding: Weight loss in obese men (mean baseline BMI 45) raised concentration and motility and lowered DNA fragmentation index (effect size -0.69).

pmid:27410176.authors: Rao M, Xia W, Yang J, et al.
pmid:27410176.title: Transient scrotal hyperthermia affects human sperm DNA integrity, sperm apoptosis, and sperm protein expression
pmid:27410176.finding: Scrotal warming in a 43 C bath for 30 min x 10 sessions reversibly increased SCSA chromatin abnormality, apoptosis and mitochondrial damage; recovery by about 16 weeks.

pmid:17335598.authors: Shefi S, Tarapore PE, Walsh TJ, et al.
pmid:17335598.title: Wet heat exposure: a potentially reversible cause of low semen quality in infertile men
pmid:17335598.finding: After infertile men stopped hot tubs/hot baths, 5 of 11 responded with a 491% rise in total motile sperm count (motility 12% -> 34%).

pmid:30102388.authors: Mínguez-Alarcón L, Gaskins AJ, Chiu YH, et al.
pmid:30102388.title: Type of underwear worn and markers of testicular function among men attending a fertility center
pmid:30102388.finding: Men who mainly wore boxers had 25% higher sperm concentration and 17% higher total count than men who did not.

pmid:15591087.authors: Sheynkin Y, Jung M, Yoo P, et al.
pmid:15591087.title: Increase in scrotal temperature in laptop computer users
pmid:15591087.finding: A working laptop on the lap raised scrotal temperature 2.6-2.8 C in 60 minutes (2.1 C from the closed-thigh posture alone).

pmid:21055743.authors: Sheynkin Y, Welliver R, Winer A, et al.
pmid:21055743.title: Protection from scrotal hyperthermia in laptop computer users
pmid:21055743.finding: Scrotal temperature rose 1 C within 11-28 minutes of laptop use; a lap pad did not prevent it; sitting with legs apart reduced it.

pmid:9756281.authors: Thonneau P, Bujan L, Multigner L, et al.
pmid:9756281.title: Occupational heat exposure and male fertility: a review
pmid:9756281.finding: Occupational heat exposure is a significant risk factor for male infertility, worsening morphology and delaying conception.

pmid:16766665.authors: Wyrobek AJ, Eskenazi B, Young S, et al.
pmid:16766665.title: Advancing age has differential effects on DNA damage, chromatin integrity, gene mutations, and aneuploidies in sperm
pmid:16766665.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:16766665.finding: In healthy non-smokers, sperm DNA fragmentation index rose steadily with age, with no threshold.

pmid:25462195.authors: Johnson SL, Dunleavy J, Gemmell NJ, et al.
pmid:25462195.title: Consistent age-dependent declines in human semen quality: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:25462195.finding: Age was associated with declines in volume, motility, morphology and the share of unfragmented sperm.

pmid:28029592.authors: Ricci E, Al Beitawi S, Cipriani S, et al.
pmid:28029592.title: Semen quality and alcohol intake: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:28029592.finding: Alcohol lowered semen volume and normal morphology, mainly in daily drinkers; occasional drinking did not clearly harm semen.

pmid:25277121.authors: Jensen TK, Gottschau M, Madsen JO, et al.
pmid:25277121.title: Habitual alcohol consumption associated with reduced semen quality and changes in reproductive hormones; a cross-sectional study among 1221 young Danish men
pmid:25277121.finding: Habitual intake above 5 units/week was linked to poorer semen; above 40 units/week, sperm concentration was 33% lower than at 1-5 units.

pmid:32001159.authors: Verhaeghe F, Di Pizio P, Bichara C, et al.
pmid:32001159.title: Cannabis consumption might exert deleterious effects on sperm nuclear quality in infertile men
pmid:32001159.finding: Regular cannabis users had more sperm DNA fragmentation and aneuploidy than non-users (exploratory).

pmid:16650651.authors: Liu PY, Swerdloff RS, Christenson PD, et al.
pmid:16650651.title: Rate, extent, and modifiers of spermatogenic recovery after hormonal male contraception: an integrated analysis
pmid:16650651.finding: After androgen-based suppression, median time for sperm to recover to 20 million/mL was 3.4 months; longer with longer treatment.

pmid:37567343.title: Recovery of spermatogenesis after androgenic anabolic steroids abuse in men. A systematic review of the literature
pmid:37567343.finding: Systematic review: anabolic steroid infertility is often reversible, but sperm production may take over a year to normalise.

pmid:15980006.authors: Rubes J, Selevan SG, Evenson DP, et al.
pmid:15980006.title: Episodic air pollution is associated with increased DNA fragmentation in human sperm without other changes in semen quality
pmid:15980006.n: 36 young men, up to 7 samples over 2 years
pmid:15980006.finding: Young men in Teplice had more SCSA sperm DNA fragmentation after high-pollution periods, without other semen changes.

pmid:17090632.authors: Hauser R, Meeker JD, Singh NP, et al.
pmid:17090632.title: DNA damage in human sperm is related to urinary levels of phthalate monoester and oxidative metabolites
pmid:17090632.finding: Urinary phthalate metabolites MEP and MEHP were associated with more neutral-Comet sperm DNA damage (about 14-18% per IQR rise in MEHP).

pmid:20656017.authors: Meeker JD, Ehrlich S, Toth TL, et al.
pmid:20656017.title: Semen quality and sperm DNA damage in relation to urinary bisphenol A among men from an infertility clinic
pmid:20656017.finding: An IQR rise in urinary BPA was linked to 10% more Comet tail DNA and lower concentration and morphology.

pmid:23445617.authors: Miranda-Contreras L, Gómez-Pérez R, Rojas G, et al.
pmid:23445617.title: Occupational exposure to organophosphate and carbamate pesticides affects sperm chromatin integrity and reproductive hormone levels among Venezuelan farm workers
pmid:23445617.finding: Farm workers exposed to organophosphate and carbamate pesticides had higher sperm DNA fragmentation index.

pmid:17953955.authors: Gallegos G, Ramos B, Santiso R, et al.
pmid:17953955.title: Sperm DNA fragmentation in infertile men with genitourinary infection by Chlamydia trachomatis and Mycoplasma
pmid:17953955.finding: Chlamydia/Mycoplasma infection: SDF 35% vs 11% in fertile controls; after about 4 months of antibiotics SDF fell from 37.7% to 24.2%.

pmid:17434502.authors: Sergerie M, Mieusset R, Croute F, et al.
pmid:17434502.title: High risk of temporary alteration of semen parameters after recent acute febrile illness
pmid:17434502.finding: After a 2-day fever of 39-40 C, DNA fragmentation index rose by 24-36% at days 15-37 and returned toward baseline by day 79.

pmid:41330355.authors: Coleman CM, Wesselink AK, Yland JJ, et al.
pmid:41330355.title: A North American preconception study of sleep health and semen quality
pmid:41330355.finding: Short (<6 h) or long (>=9 h) sleep and poor sleep quality were associated with roughly 15-20% lower sperm counts, with wide confidence intervals.

pmid:24700791.authors: Liu K, Li Y, Zhang G, et al.
pmid:24700791.title: Association between mobile phone use and semen quality: a systemic review and meta-analysis
pmid:24700791.finding: In human studies, mobile phone use had no significant effect on semen parameters; in vitro RF exposure reduced motility and viability.

pmid:34333014.authors: Kim S, Han D, Ryu J, et al.
pmid:34333014.title: Effects of mobile phone usage on sperm quality - No time-dependent relationship on usage: A systematic review and updated meta-analysis
pmid:34333014.finding: Phone exposure was associated with lower motility, viability and concentration, but with no dose-response by hours of use.

pmid:18804757.authors: Agarwal A, Desai NR, Makker K, et al.
pmid:18804757.title: Effects of radiofrequency electromagnetic waves (RF-EMW) from cellular phones on human ejaculated semen: an in vitro pilot study
pmid:18804757.finding: In vitro, phone RF exposure raised ROS and reduced motility and viability of neat semen, but did not change DNA damage.

pmid:21924714.authors: Gosálvez J, González-Martínez M, López-Fernández C, et al.
pmid:21924714.title: Shorter abstinence decreases sperm deoxyribonucleic acid fragmentation in ejaculate
pmid:21924714.finding: SDF was lower after 24-hour, and especially 3-hour, abstinence than after the standard abstinence period.

pmid:36555920.authors: Barbagallo F, Cannarella R, Crafa A, et al.
pmid:36555920.title: The Impact of a Very Short Abstinence Period on Conventional Sperm Parameters and Sperm DNA Fragmentation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmid:36555920.finding: A second ejaculate within 4 hours had lower SDF in men with abnormal semen.

pmid:38828413.authors: Lo Giudice A, Asmundo MG, Cimino S, et al.
pmid:38828413.title: Effects of long and short ejaculatory abstinence on sperm parameters: a meta-analysis of randomized-controlled trials
pmid:38828413.finding: Abstinence longer than 2 days was associated with SDF 3.5 points higher; each extra day added about 0.65 points.

pmid:38197853.authors: Du C, Li Y, Yin C, et al.
pmid:38197853.title: Association of abstinence time with semen quality and fertility outcomes: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis
pmid:38197853.finding: Short versus long abstinence lowered DNA fragmentation index by about 2.4 points in healthy men, at the cost of lower volume and count.

pmid:33179134.authors: Dahan MH, Mills G, Khoudja R, et al.
pmid:33179134.title: Three hour abstinence as a treatment for high sperm DNA fragmentation: a prospective cohort study
pmid:33179134.finding: SDF fell from 34.6% after 3 days of abstinence to 23.7% in a second sample 3 hours later; 55% of men with SDF >35% moved into the normal range.

pmid:24977955.title: Long-term Low-to-Intensive Cycling Training: Impact on Semen Parameters and Seminal Cytokines
pmid:24977955.finding: 16 weeks of intensive road-cycling training raised seminal cytokines and worsened semen; some changes persisted 30 days after training.

pmid:22895856.authors: Robbins WA, Xun L, FitzGerald LZ, et al.
pmid:22895856.title: Walnuts improve semen quality in men consuming a Western-style diet: randomized control dietary intervention trial
pmid:22895856.finding: Adding 75 g/day walnuts for 12 weeks improved sperm vitality, motility and morphology (DNA fragmentation not measured).

pmid:30475967.authors: Salas-Huetos A, Moraleda R, Giardina S, et al.
pmid:30475967.title: Effect of nut consumption on semen quality and functionality in healthy men consuming a Western-style diet: a randomized controlled trial
pmid:30475967.finding: Adding 60 g/day mixed nuts for 14 weeks improved count, vitality, motility and morphology and reduced sperm DNA fragmentation.

pmid:27994040.authors: Karayiannis D, Kontogianni MD, Mendorou C, et al.
pmid:27994040.title: Association between adherence to the Mediterranean diet and semen quality parameters in male partners of couples attempting fertility
pmid:27994040.finding: Men in the lowest Mediterranean-diet tertile had about 2.6 times the odds of abnormal concentration, count and motility.

pmid:40419219.authors: Agarwal R, Salas-Salvadó J, Davila-Cordova E, et al.
pmid:40419219.title: Mediterranean Diet, Semen Quality, and Medically Assisted Reproductive Outcomes in the Male Population: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmid:40419219.finding: Mediterranean diet adherence was associated with higher sperm count (+24 million), motility (+8.8 points) and morphology; no data showing better fertility outcomes.

pmid:28333357.authors: Salas-Huetos A, Bulló M, Salas-Salvadó J
pmid:28333357.title: Dietary patterns, foods and nutrients in male fertility parameters and fecundability: a systematic review of observational studies
pmid:28333357.finding: Systematic review of observational studies: diets rich in fish, fruit, vegetables and whole grains go with better semen; processed meat, sugary drinks, alcohol and soy with worse semen in some studies.

pmid:22888168.authors: Gaskins AJ, Colaci DS, Mendiola J, et al.
pmid:22888168.title: Dietary patterns and semen quality in young men
pmid:22888168.finding: Young men in the top quartile of a 'prudent' diet (fish, chicken, fruit, vegetables, legumes, whole grains) had 11.3 points higher progressive motility.

pmid:24850626.authors: Afeiche MC, Gaskins AJ, Williams PL, et al.
pmid:24850626.title: Processed meat intake is unfavorably and fish intake favorably associated with semen quality indicators among men attending a fertility clinic
pmid:24850626.finding: Highest processed-meat quartile had 1.7 points fewer normal forms; total count rose from 102 to 168 million across fish-intake quartiles.

pmid:24812311.authors: Chiu YH, Afeiche MC, Gaskins AJ, et al.
pmid:24812311.title: Sugar-sweetened beverage intake in relation to semen quality and reproductive hormone levels in young men
pmid:24812311.finding: Young men drinking >=1.3 sugar-sweetened beverages/day had 9.8 points lower progressive motility than those drinking <0.2/day.

pmid:27075904.authors: Chiu YH, Gaskins AJ, Williams PL, et al.
pmid:27075904.title: Intake of Fruits and Vegetables with Low-to-Moderate Pesticide Residues Is Positively Associated with Semen-Quality Parameters among Young Healthy Men
pmid:27075904.finding: Eating >=2.8 servings/day of low-to-moderate-pesticide fruit and vegetables was linked to 169% higher total sperm count; high-pesticide produce was not.

pmid:31591650.authors: Williams EA, Parker M, Robinson A, et al.
pmid:31591650.title: A randomized placebo-controlled trial to investigate the effect of lactolycopene on semen quality in healthy males
pmid:31591650.finding: 14 mg/day lactolycopene for 12 weeks improved fast progressive motility and morphology; the primary endpoint was not significant.

pmid:28646871.authors: Ricci E, Viganò P, Cipriani S, et al.
pmid:28646871.title: Coffee and caffeine intake and male infertility: a systematic review
pmid:28646871.finding: Caffeine from coffee and tea was mostly unrelated to semen parameters; caffeinated soft drinks looked harmful; DNA-damage findings inconsistent.

pmid:18650557.authors: Chavarro JE, Toth TL, Sadio SM, et al.
pmid:18650557.title: Soy food and isoflavone intake in relation to semen quality parameters among men from an infertility clinic
pmid:18650557.finding: Men in the highest soy-food category had 41 million/mL lower sperm concentration; no link to motility or morphology.

pmid:26097060.authors: Mínguez-Alarcón L, Afeiche MC, Chiu YH, et al.
pmid:26097060.title: Male soy food intake was not associated with in vitro fertilization outcomes among couples attending a fertility center
pmid:26097060.finding: Male partners' soy intake was unrelated to fertilization, embryo quality or live birth in IVF.

pmid:31116515.authors: Falsig AL, Gleerup CS, Knudsen UB
pmid:31116515.title: The influence of omega-3 fatty acids on semen quality markers: a systematic PRISMA review
pmid:31116515.finding: 14 of 16 studies found omega-3 intake or supplements associated with improvement in at least one semen marker; studies too heterogeneous to pool.

pmid:31951274.authors: Jensen TK, Priskorn L, Holmboe SA, et al.
pmid:31951274.title: Associations of Fish Oil Supplement Use With Testicular Function in Young Men
pmid:31951274.finding: Young men using fish oil supplements on >=60 days had 0.64 mL more semen volume, larger testes and lower FSH and LH.

pmid:27792396.authors: Martínez-Soto JC, Domingo JC, Cordobilla B, et al.
pmid:27792396.title: Dietary supplementation with docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) improves seminal antioxidant status and decreases sperm DNA fragmentation
pmid:27792396.finding: 1.5 g/day DHA for 10 weeks improved seminal antioxidant status and lowered sperm DNA fragmentation, without changing standard parameters.

pmid:30866036.authors: Smits RM, Mackenzie-Proctor R, Yazdani A, et al.
pmid:30866036.title: Antioxidants for male subfertility
pmid:30866036.finding: Cochrane 2019: live birth OR 1.79 (7 RCTs, 750 men, low-quality evidence); no significant benefit once high-risk-of-bias trials were removed (Peto OR 1.38, 0.89-2.16).

pmid:32111479.authors: Steiner AZ, Hansen KR, Barnhart KT, et al.
pmid:32111479.title: The effect of antioxidants on male factor infertility: the Males, Antioxidants, and Infertility (MOXI) randomized clinical trial
pmid:32111479.finding: MOXI: a 7-ingredient antioxidant for 3-6 months did not improve semen parameters or DNA fragmentation; live birth 15% vs 24% placebo.

pmid:15932912.authors: Greco E, Romano S, Iacobelli M, et al.
pmid:15932912.title: ICSI in cases of sperm DNA damage: beneficial effect of oral antioxidant treatment
pmid:15932912.finding: 1 g vitamin C + 1 g vitamin E daily for 2 months lowered SDF in 76% of men; the next ICSI had 48.2% vs 6.9% pregnancy (uncontrolled before-after).

pmid:17425820.authors: Ménézo YJ, Hazout A, Panteix G, et al.
pmid:17425820.title: Antioxidants to reduce sperm DNA fragmentation: an unexpected adverse effect
pmid:17425820.finding: 90 days of antioxidant vitamins with zinc and selenium lowered DFI by 19% but raised sperm decondensation by 23%.

pmid:40015627.authors: Moazamian A, Hug E, Villeneuve P, et al.
pmid:40015627.title: The dual nature of micronutrients on fertility: too much of a good thing?
pmid:40015627.finding: In healthy mice, high doses of vitamin C, zinc, folate or carnitine disturbed redox balance and damaged sperm DNA; high carnitine cut pregnancy rates, but helped oxidatively stressed mice.

pmid:30298673.authors: Stenqvist A, Oleszczuk K, Leijonhufvud I, et al.
pmid:30298673.title: Impact of antioxidant treatment on DNA fragmentation index: a double-blind placebo-controlled randomized trial
pmid:30298673.finding: Six months of combined antioxidants did not lower DNA fragmentation index in men with DFI >=25%.

pmid:17550489.authors: Tremellen K, Miari G, Froiland D, et al.
pmid:17550489.title: A randomised control trial examining the effect of an antioxidant (Menevit) on pregnancy outcome during IVF-ICSI treatment
pmid:17550489.journal: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
pmid:17550489.finding: Menevit for 3 months before IVF-ICSI: viable pregnancy 38.5% vs 16% per transferred embryo; embryo quality unchanged.

pmid:32330373.authors: Kopets R, Kuibida I, Chernyavska I, et al.
pmid:32330373.title: Dietary supplementation with a novel l-carnitine multi-micronutrient in idiopathic male subfertility involving oligo-, astheno-, teratozoospermia: A randomized clinical study
pmid:32330373.finding: An L-carnitine multi-micronutrient for 6 months raised the share of normal semen analyses (69% vs 22%) and spontaneous pregnancies.

pmid:23912751.authors: Lafuente R, González-Comadrán M, Solà I, et al.
pmid:23912751.title: Coenzyme Q10 and male infertility: a meta-analysis
pmid:23912751.finding: CoQ10 raised sperm concentration and motility, but there was no evidence for higher pregnancy or live birth.

pmid:18395716.authors: Balercia G, Buldreghini E, Vignini A, et al.
pmid:18395716.title: Coenzyme Q10 treatment in infertile men with idiopathic asthenozoospermia: a placebo-controlled, double-blind randomized trial
pmid:18395716.finding: CoQ10 200 mg/day for 6 months increased seminal CoQ10 and motility in idiopathic asthenozoospermia.

pmid:16110353.authors: Comhaire FH, El Garem Y, Mahmoud A, et al.
pmid:16110353.title: Combined conventional/antioxidant "Astaxanthin" treatment for male infertility: a double blind, randomized trial
pmid:16110353.finding: Astaxanthin 16 mg/day for 3 months lowered seminal ROS; pregnancy 54.5% vs 10.5% in a very small trial.

pmid:35128424.authors: Khaw SC, Wong ZZ, Anderson R, et al.
pmid:35128424.title: l-carnitine and l-acetylcarnitine supplementation for idiopathic male infertility
pmid:35128424.finding: Carnitines improved total and progressive motility and morphology, with no demonstrable effect on clinical pregnancy.

pmid:30462179.authors: Salas-Huetos A, Rosique-Esteban N, Becerra-Tomás N, et al.
pmid:30462179.title: The Effect of Nutrients and Dietary Supplements on Sperm Quality Parameters: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials
pmid:30462179.finding: Selenium, zinc, omega-3, CoQ10 and carnitines produced modest improvements in sperm parameters; fertility outcomes not assessed.

pmid:30771790.authors: Jannatifar R, Parivar K, Roodbari NH, et al.
pmid:30771790.title: Effects of N-acetyl-cysteine supplementation on sperm quality, chromatin integrity and level of oxidative stress in infertile men
pmid:30771790.finding: NAC 600 mg/day for 3 months lowered SDF and protamine deficiency and improved count and motility (uncontrolled before-after).

pmid:29126319.authors: Blomberg Jensen M, Lawaetz JG, Petersen JH, et al.
pmid:29126319.title: Effects of Vitamin D Supplementation on Semen Quality, Reproductive Hormones, and Live Birth Rate: A Randomized Clinical Trial
pmid:29126319.finding: Vitamin D (300,000 IU then 1400 IU/day) plus calcium for 150 days did not improve semen quality in vitamin-D-insufficient infertile men.

pmid:28865546.authors: Esteves SC, Roque M, Bradley CK, et al.
pmid:28865546.title: Reproductive outcomes of testicular versus ejaculated sperm for intracytoplasmic sperm injection among men with high levels of DNA fragmentation in semen: systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:28865546.finding: Testicular sperm had 24.6 points lower SDF than ejaculated sperm; ICSI with testicular sperm gave higher pregnancy and live birth and fewer miscarriages in high-SDF men.

pmid:31692293.authors: Esteves SC, Santi D, Simoni M
pmid:31692293.title: An update on clinical and surgical interventions to reduce sperm DNA fragmentation in infertile men
pmid:31692293.finding: Best evidence for lowering SDF is varicocele repair; antioxidants and lifestyle change may lower SDF but their effect on pregnancy is unclear.

pmid:24681577.authors: Afeiche MC, Williams PL, Gaskins AJ, et al.
pmid:24681577.title: Meat intake and reproductive parameters among young men.
pmid:24681577.finding: Processed red meat was inversely related to total sperm count (top vs bottom quartile -78 million, P-trend 0.01), driven by lower ejaculate volume; unprocessed red meat, poultry and fish were not related to any semen parameter.

pmid:35565922.authors: Liu YS, Zhang YX, Wang XB, et al.
pmid:35565922.title: Associations between Meat and Vegetable Intake, Cooking Methods, and Asthenozoospermia: A Hospital-Based Case-Control Study in China.
pmid:35565922.finding: Highest vs lowest tertile of unprocessed meat intake had lower odds of asthenozoospermia (OR 0.61) and total meat OR 0.56; processed meat raised the odds (OR 1.44) and stir-frying meat was associated with higher risk (OR 1.58).

pmid:29193350.authors: Alizadeh F, Javadi M, Karami AA, et al.
pmid:29193350.title: Curcumin nanomicelle improves semen parameters, oxidative stress, inflammatory biomarkers, and reproductive hormones in infertile men: A randomized clinical trial.
pmid:29193350.finding: 80 mg/day curcumin nanomicelle for 10 weeks raised sperm count, concentration and motility and improved TAC, MDA, CRP and TNF-a versus placebo; single small Iranian trial, no pregnancy or DNA-fragmentation outcomes.

pmid:21337449.title: Can curcumin provide an ideal contraceptive?
pmid:21337449.finding: Curcumin added to human and mouse sperm caused concentration-dependent loss of forward motility, capacitation and fertilisation in vitro, and intravaginal curcumin reduced fertility in mice.

pmid:34755901.authors: Sadraei MR, Tavalaee M, Forouzanfar M, et al.
pmid:34755901.title: Effect of curcumin, and nano-curcumin on sperm function in varicocele rat model.
pmid:34755901.finding: In varicocele rats, oral curcumin and nano-curcumin improved sperm concentration, motility, lipid peroxidation and DNA damage.

pmid:33861392.authors: Santonastaso M, Mottola F, Iovine C, et al.
pmid:33861392.title: Protective Effects of Curcumin on the Outcome of Cryopreservation in Human Sperm.
pmid:33861392.finding: Adding 20 uM curcumin to freezing medium improved post-thaw motility and lowered ROS and DNA fragmentation in human sperm (in vitro, cryopreservation only).

pmid:28295950.authors: Jiang XP, Tang JY, Xu Z, et al.
pmid:28295950.title: Sulforaphane attenuates di-N-butylphthalate-induced reproductive damage in pubertal mice: Involvement of the Nrf2-antioxidant system.
pmid:28295950.finding: Sulforaphane attenuated phthalate (DBP)-induced falls in sperm count, motility and testosterone in pubertal mice via Nrf2.

pmid:31004475.authors: Mu Y, Yin TL, Huang XX, et al.
pmid:31004475.title: Sulforaphane ameliorates high-fat diet-induced spermatogenic deficiency in mice†.
pmid:31004475.finding: Sulforaphane injections reversed high-fat-diet-induced spermatogenic impairment in mice and, in vitro, protected mouse and human sperm motility from palmitic acid via AMPK-dependent ER-stress relief.

pmid:33248050.authors: Valipour J, Nashtaei MS, Khosravizadeh Z, et al.
pmid:33248050.title: Effect of sulforaphane on apoptosis, reactive oxygen species and lipids peroxidation of human sperm during cryopreservation.
pmid:33248050.finding: Adding 5 µM sulforaphane to human sperm before freezing improved post-thaw viability, motility and morphology and lowered ROS and lipid peroxidation.

pmid:24801392.authors: Wang Y, Zhang Z, Guo W, et al.
pmid:24801392.title: Sulforaphane reduction of testicular apoptotic cell death in diabetic mice is associated with the upregulation of Nrf2 expression and function.
pmid:24801392.finding: In diabetic mice, 4 months of sulforaphane prevented testicular cell death, oxidative damage and inflammation while up-regulating testicular Nrf2.

pmid:25275520.authors: Fedder MD, Jakobsen HB, Giversen I, et al.
pmid:25275520.title: An extract of pomegranate fruit and galangal rhizome increases the numbers of motile sperm: a prospective, randomised, controlled, double-blinded trial.
pmid:25275520.finding: Pomegranate extract plus galangal tablets for 3 months increased total motile sperm by 62%, vs 20% on placebo.

pmid:33322606.authors: Illiano E, Trama F, Zucchi A, et al.
pmid:33322606.title: Resveratrol-Based Multivitamin Supplement Increases Sperm Concentration and Motility in Idiopathic Male Infertility: A Pilot Clinical Study.
pmid:33322606.finding: A multivitamin containing 150 mg/day resveratrol was followed by higher sperm motility (48% to 59%) and concentration after 3-6 months.

pmid:36149528.authors: Furini C, Spaggiari G, Simoni M, et al.
pmid:36149528.title: Ketogenic state improves testosterone serum levels-results from a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:36149528.finding: Ketogenic diets raised total testosterone (by ~6.75 nmol/L with very-low-calorie KD, ~1 nmol/L with normocaloric KD), proportional to weight loss and age.

pmid:35223950.authors: Liu CY, Chang TC, Lin SH, et al.
pmid:35223950.title: Is a Ketogenic Diet Superior to a High-Fat, High-Cholesterol Diet Regarding Testicular Function and Spermatogenesis?
pmid:35223950.finding: In obese mice, switching from a high-fat high-cholesterol diet to an MCT-based ketogenic diet for 8 weeks lowered testicular lipid peroxidation and restored semen quality.

pmid:33741447.title: Low-fat diets and testosterone in men: Systematic review and meta-analysis of intervention studies.
pmid:33741447.finding: Low-fat diets lowered total testosterone (SMD -0.38) and free testosterone (SMD -0.37) vs higher-fat diets.

pmid:3090956.title: Effects of Ramadhan fast on male fertility.
pmid:3090956.finding: Small study: Ramadan did not harm semen in healthy men; LH and semen volume fell after the fast while sperm count rose during it.

pmid:1904451.authors: Cameron JL, Weltzin TE, McConaha C, et al.
pmid:1904451.title: Slowing of pulsatile luteinizing hormone secretion in men after forty-eight hours of fasting.
pmid:1904451.finding: 48 h of fasting cut mean LH from 2.94 to 1.07 IU/L and halved LH pulse frequency, and lowered FSH and testosterone, without a rise in cortisol.

pmid:35684143.authors: Cienfuegos S, Corapi S, Gabel K, et al.
pmid:35684143.title: Effect of Intermittent Fasting on Reproductive Hormone Levels in Females and Males: A Review of Human Trials.
pmid:35684143.finding: Review of human trials: IF lowers testosterone/free androgen index and raises SHBG in premenopausal women with obesity, does not change oestrogen or gonadotropins, and lowers testosterone in lean active young men.

pmid:37883941.authors: Engel OJ, Doctory N, Sun B, et al.
pmid:37883941.title: The Effect of Month-Long Daily Fasting on Semen Parameters: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
pmid:37883941.finding: Semen samples produced during Ramadan (and 70 days after) had lower post-gradient progressive motility (30% vs 38%) and lower volume than the same men's samples at other times (retrospective).

pmid:39885870.authors: May KT, Behling J, Sochiera-Plegniere K, et al.
pmid:39885870.title: Fasting for male fertility-a mixed methods study.
pmid:39885870.finding: Three 5-day 500 kcal FMD cycles over 4 months produced no clear differences in semen parameters vs waiting-list controls (pilot, underpowered).

pmid:38781203.authors: Poursalehian M, Mohseni S, Shadman Z, et al.
pmid:38781203.title: Impact of Ramadan fasting on serum levels of major endocrinology hormonal and biochemical parameters in healthy non-athlete adults: A systematic review and meta-analyses.
pmid:38781203.finding: Ramadan fasting did not significantly change testosterone, LH, FSH, prolactin or thyroid hormones in healthy non-athletes; morning cortisol tended to fall.

pmid:38861008.authors: Aerts A, Temmerman A, Vanhie A, et al.
pmid:38861008.title: The Effect of Endurance Exercise on Semen Quality in Male Athletes: A Systematic Review.
pmid:38861008.finding: Endurance exercise can lower semen quality, but changes were usually not clinically relevant; some cyclists and triathletes had more abnormal morphology or DNA fragmentation.

pmid:37052052.title: Hungry runners - low energy availability in male endurance athletes and its impact on performance and testosterone: mini-review.
pmid:37052052.finding: Low energy availability is common in male endurance athletes and correlates with lower testosterone, bone density and resting metabolic rate.

pmid:19092301.title: Effects of endurance exercise on the reproductive system of men: the "exercise-hypogonadal male condition".
pmid:19092301.finding: Describes the exercise-hypogonadal male condition as limited to men with years of chronic endurance training and not highly prevalent.

pmid:28195945.authors: Hackney AC, Lane AR, Register-Mihalik J, et al.
pmid:28195945.title: Endurance Exercise Training and Male Sexual Libido.
pmid:28195945.finding: Men with the highest training intensity and duration had greater odds of low libido than those training least.

pmid:32082255.title: Hypogonadism in Exercising Males: Dysfunction or Adaptive-Regulatory Adjustment?
pmid:32082255.finding: Proposes several forms of exercise-related male hypogonadism, some transient and linked to low energy availability or overtraining, others possibly an adaptive readjustment.

pmid:37752011.authors: Mountjoy M, Ackerman KE, Bailey DM, et al.
pmid:37752011.title: 2023 International Olympic Committee's (IOC) consensus statement on Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs).
pmid:37752011.finding: IOC 2023 consensus on Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs), covering reproductive suppression from low energy availability in both sexes.

pmid:28295487.authors: Vaamonde D, Algar-Santacruz C, Abbasi A, et al.
pmid:28295487.title: Sperm DNA fragmentation as a result of ultra-endurance exercise training in male athletes.
pmid:28295487.finding: Elite triathletes in training had high sperm DNA fragmentation (mean 20.4%) and raised round cells.

pmid:17509584.authors: Agarwal A, Deepinder F, Cocuzza M, et al.
pmid:17509584.title: Effect of vaginal lubricants on sperm motility and chromatin integrity: a prospective comparative study.
pmid:17509584.finding: In vitro, FemGlide, Replens and Astroglide reduced progressive motility and FemGlide and K-Y Jelly raised DNA fragmentation (SCSA), whereas Pre-Seed did not differ from culture medium.

pmid:23490168.authors: Agarwal A, Malvezzi H, Sharma R
pmid:23490168.title: Effect of an isotonic lubricant on sperm collection and sperm quality.
pmid:23490168.finding: Using Pre-Seed during masturbation for semen collection did not change motility, viability, ROS, antioxidant capacity or DNA damage.

pmid:9886513.authors: Anderson L, Lewis SE, McClure N
pmid:9886513.title: The effects of coital lubricants on sperm motility in vitro.
pmid:9886513.finding: K-Y jelly, olive oil and saliva (but not baby oil) significantly reduced sperm motility in vitro at 12.5%; olive oil and saliva still did at 6.25%.

pmid:27268162.authors: Bach CC, Vested A, Jørgensen KT, et al.
pmid:27268162.title: Perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances and measures of human fertility: a systematic review.
pmid:27268162.finding: Little consistent evidence that PFAS affect semen quality or hormones in men; associations with longer time to pregnancy appear in parous women and are most likely not causal.

pmid:42570390.authors: Di Nisio A, López-Gil JF, Pizzol D, et al.
pmid:42570390.title: Associations between per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and semen parameters: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:42570390.finding: PFAS were weakly associated with lower progressive motility (r = -0.058) and more sperm DNA fragmentation (r = 0.141), with little association with standard counts.

pmid:38044638.authors: Gumerova E, Rimmer MP, Gellatly SA
pmid:38044638.title: Do sperm and lubricants gel well with each other? A systematic review.
pmid:38044638.finding: Systematic review: only 2 of 24 studies were in vivo; methodological variation and absent pregnancy outcomes prevent an evidence-based "sperm-safe" lubricant guideline.

pmid:40711011.authors: Guo Y, Rong M, Fan Y, et al.
pmid:40711011.title: The Presence of Microplastics in Human Semen and Their Associations with Semen Quality.
pmid:40711011.finding: Laser-direct infrared found microplastics in 34 of 45 semen samples; men with PET particles had borderline lower progressive motility (20.6% vs 34.9%, p=0.056) and no difference in concentration or count.

pmid:19590684.authors: Joensen UN, Bossi R, Leffers H, et al.
pmid:19590684.title: Do perfluoroalkyl compounds impair human semen quality?
pmid:19590684.finding: Men with high combined PFOS+PFOA had fewer morphologically normal sperm (6.2 vs 15.5 million per ejaculate).

pmid:38802004.authors: Li N, Yang H, Dong Y, et al.
pmid:38802004.title: Prevalence and implications of microplastic contaminants in general human seminal fluid: A Raman spectroscopic study.
pmid:38802004.finding: Raman found about 2 microplastic particles per semen sample in all 40 men (mostly polystyrene); PVC-containing samples had lower progressive motility than polystyrene-containing ones.

pmid:25127343.authors: Louis GM, Chen Z, Schisterman EF, et al.
pmid:25127343.title: Perfluorochemicals and human semen quality: the LIFE study.
pmid:25127343.finding: Several PFAS were associated with some semen endpoints, but in varying directions; strongest signals were for PFOSA and sperm head morphology.

pmid:31086364.title: Vaginal lubricants in the couple trying-to-conceive: Assessing healthcare professional recommendations and effect on in vitro sperm function.
pmid:31086364.n: 32 clinician survey responses plus lab testing
pmid:31086364.finding: Aquagel cut progressive motility to 49% of control within 10 min even at 5%, while a sperm-safe lubricant (Pre) had no effect; clinicians' advice was inconsistent.

pmid:29543376.authors: McInerney KA, Hahn KA, Hatch EE, et al.
pmid:29543376.title: Lubricant use during intercourse and time to pregnancy: a prospective cohort study.
pmid:29543376.finding: No lubricant type was associated with lower fecundability (water-based FR 1.02; "fertility-friendly" 1.01; oil-based 1.23; silicone 1.27).

pmid:24717914.title: Effect of vaginal lubricants on natural fertility.
pmid:24717914.finding: In vitro, many lubricants are sperm-toxic while "sperm-friendly" ones are not, yet cohort data show no effect on fecundity; an RCT is needed.

pmid:37532047.authors: Montano L, Giorgini E, Notarstefano V, et al.
pmid:37532047.title: Raman Microspectroscopy evidence of microplastics in human semen.
pmid:37532047.finding: Raman microspectroscopy found 16 microplastic fragments (2-6 um) in 6 of 10 semen samples from a polluted area of southern Italy.

pmid:24390681.authors: Mowat A, Newton C, Boothroyd C, et al.
pmid:24390681.title: The effects of vaginal lubricants on sperm function: an in vitro analysis.
pmid:24390681.finding: Of nine lubricants tested in vitro, Pre-Seed preserved motility (86%) and vitality (92%) best and Conceive Plus was second; none affected DNA fragmentation over 30 min.

pmid:22449571.authors: Specht IO, Hougaard KS, Spanò M, et al.
pmid:22449571.title: Sperm DNA integrity in relation to exposure to environmental perfluoroalkyl substances - a study of spouses of pregnant women in three geographical regions.
pmid:22449571.finding: No consistent association between serum PFAS and sperm DNA fragmentation (SCSA), apoptosis markers or reproductive hormones; only a slight TUNEL rise with PFOA in Greenland.

pmid:22914390.authors: Steiner AZ, Long DL, Tanner C, et al.
pmid:22914390.title: Effect of vaginal lubricants on natural fertility.
pmid:22914390.finding: Lubricant use in the fertile window did not reduce fecundability (fecundability ratio 1.05, 95% CI 0.59-1.85).

pmid:35369832.authors: Tomlinson J, Pooley K, Tomlinson M
pmid:35369832.title: Sperm toxicity testing on lubricant gels: should we be recommending 'fertility-friendly' specialist products?
pmid:35369832.finding: All gels reduced motility in vitro; products marketed as sperm-friendly (FertilSafe Plus) performed best, pleasure lubricants worst, and saliva was worse still.

pmid:6890474.authors: Tulandi T, Plouffe L, McInnes RA
pmid:6890474.title: Effect of saliva on sperm motility and activity.
pmid:6890474.finding: Saliva reduced sperm motility and progression in vitro, even at low concentrations.

pmid:36396760.authors: Wang H, Wei K, Wu Z, et al.
pmid:36396760.title: Association between per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and semen quality.
pmid:36396760.finding: PFOA and PFNA were associated with lower progressive sperm motility; other semen parameters were largely unaffected.

pmid:36948312.authors: Zhao Q, Zhu L, Weng J, et al.
pmid:36948312.title: Detection and characterization of microplastics in the human testis and semen.
pmid:36948312.finding: Py-GC/MS and laser-direct infrared found microplastics in testis (11.6 particles/g) and semen (0.23 particles/mL), mostly 20-100 um.

pmid:24529582.authors: Akasheh G, Sirati L, Noshad Kamran AR, et al.
pmid:24529582.title: Comparison of the effect of sertraline with behavioral therapy on semen parameters in men with primary premature ejaculation.
pmid:24529582.finding: Sertraline 50 mg/day for 3 months (vs behavioural therapy) lowered sperm concentration and normal morphology and raised sperm DNA fragmentation.

pmid:17299062.authors: Amory JK, Wang C, Swerdloff RS, et al.
pmid:17299062.title: The effect of 5alpha-reductase inhibition with dutasteride and finasteride on semen parameters and serum hormones in healthy men.
pmid:17299062.finding: Dutasteride 0.5 mg and finasteride 5 mg cut total sperm count by 28.6% and 34.3% at 26 weeks, lowered volume and motility, with largely reversible effects after stopping.

pmid:30864530.authors: Banerjee A, Scarpa M, Pathak S, et al.
pmid:30864530.title: Inflammatory Bowel Disease Therapies Adversely Affect Fertility in Men- A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
pmid:30864530.journal: Endocr Metab Immune Disord Drug Targets
pmid:30864530.finding: Sulphasalazine-treated men had lower sperm counts and motility and more oligospermia than mesalazine-treated men; biologics appeared safe.

pmid:25702934.authors: Bawor M, Bami H, Dennis BB, et al.
pmid:25702934.title: Testosterone suppression in opioid users: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:25702934.finding: Regular opioid use (including methadone) lowered testosterone in men by about 165 ng/dL versus controls; no effect seen in women.

pmid:31542895.title: Effect of antidepressant medications on semen parameters and male fertility.
pmid:31542895.finding: SSRIs, especially fluoxetine, are linked to lower sperm concentration and motility and higher DNA fragmentation in human and animal studies; effects appear reversible; data on other antidepressants are sparse.

pmid:28277353.authors: Eck LK, Jensen TB, Mastrogiannis D, et al.
pmid:28277353.title: Risk of Adverse Pregnancy Outcome After Paternal Exposure to Methotrexate Within 90 Days Before Pregnancy.
pmid:28277353.finding: Paternal methotrexate within 90 days before conception was not associated with major malformations (aOR 1.01), stillbirth or preterm birth.

pmid:29778387.authors: Evans-Hoeker EA, Eisenberg E, Diamond MP, et al.
pmid:29778387.title: Major depression, antidepressant use, and male and female fertility.
pmid:29778387.n: 1650 women and 1608 men in infertility trials
pmid:29778387.finding: Active major depression in the male partner lowered conception; maternal antidepressant use (n=90) was associated with first-trimester pregnancy loss.

pmid:16952675.title: Effects of acute treatment with tamsulosin versus alfuzosin on ejaculatory function in normal volunteers.
pmid:16952675.finding: Tamsulosin 0.8 mg daily lowered ejaculate volume by 2.4 mL and caused anejaculation in 35% of men; alfuzosin and placebo did not.

pmid:21776003.authors: Koyuncu H, Serefoglu EC, Yencilek E, et al.
pmid:21776003.title: Escitalopram treatment for premature ejaculation has a negative effect on semen parameters.
pmid:21776003.finding: Escitalopram 10 mg daily for 12 weeks lowered sperm concentration, motility and morphology.

pmid:6148293.authors: O'Moráin C, Smethurst P, Doré CJ, et al.
pmid:6148293.title: Reversible male infertility due to sulphasalazine: studies in man and rat.
pmid:6148293.n: men with IBD plus rat studies
pmid:6148293.finding: Sulphasalazine caused oligospermia, poor motility and abnormal forms that reversed on withdrawal (15 pregnancies at a median 2.5 months); the sulphapyridine moiety was responsible in rats.

pmid:10492183.authors: Overstreet JW, Fuh VL, Gould J, et al.
pmid:10492183.title: Chronic treatment with finasteride daily does not affect spermatogenesis or semen production in young men.
pmid:10492183.finding: Finasteride 1 mg daily for 48 weeks did not affect sperm concentration, count, motility or morphology versus placebo.

pmid:32743663.authors: Perez-Garcia LF, Dolhain RJEM, Vorstenbosch S, et al.
pmid:32743663.title: The effect of paternal exposure to immunosuppressive drugs on sexual function, reproductive hormones, fertility, pregnancy and offspring outcomes: a systematic review.
pmid:32743663.finding: Clear negative effects on sperm for sulfasalazine and cyclophosphamide; dubious effects for methotrexate, colchicine and sirolimus; no large negative offspring effects of paternal immunosuppressants reported.

pmid:37263756.authors: Perez-Garcia LF, Röder E, Krijthe BP, et al.
pmid:37263756.title: Is methotrexate safe for men with an immune-mediated inflammatory disease and an active desire to become a father? Results of a prospective cohort study (iFAME-MTX).
pmid:37263756.finding: Semen parameters and sperm DNA fragmentation did not change after starting low-dose methotrexate and matched healthy controls; methotrexate barely accumulated in sperm.

pmid:18804223.title: Sperm DNA damage and semen quality impairment after treatment with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors detected using semen analysis and sperm chromatin structure assay.
pmid:18804223.finding: Reported lower sperm count and motility and higher DNA denaturation with SSRIs; the journal issued an Expression of Concern in 2023, so this paper should not be relied on.

pmid:23082785.title: Investigation of ejaculatory disorder by silodosin in the treatment of prostatic hyperplasia.
pmid:23082785.finding: Among sexually active men on silodosin, 95% reported ejaculatory disorder.

pmid:24012200.authors: Samplaski MK, Lo K, Grober E, et al.
pmid:24012200.title: Finasteride use in the male infertility population: effects on semen and hormone parameters.
pmid:24012200.finding: In men presenting with infertility while on finasteride (mean 1 mg/day), sperm counts rose on average 11.6-fold after stopping; 57% of severely oligospermic men rose above 15 million/mL.

pmid:30676405.authors: Sylvester C, Menke M, Gopalan P
pmid:30676405.title: Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors and Fertility: Considerations for Couples Trying to Conceive.
pmid:30676405.finding: Insufficient evidence that SSRIs reduce female fertility or IVF outcomes; six of seven mostly poor-quality male studies found adverse effects on semen.

pmid:19515367.authors: Tanrikut C, Feldman AS, Altemus M, et al.
pmid:19515367.title: Adverse effect of paroxetine on sperm.
pmid:19515367.finding: Five weeks of paroxetine raised mean sperm DNA fragmentation from 13.8% to 30.3% (TUNEL); abnormal fragmentation rose from 9.7% to 50% of men (OR 9.3) without changes in standard semen parameters.

pmid:6114897.authors: Toovey S, Hudson E, Hendry WF, et al.
pmid:6114897.title: Sulphasalazine and male infertility: reversibility and possible mechanism.
pmid:6114897.finding: Sulphasalazine 2-4 g/day caused gross semen abnormalities in 18 men treated over 2 months; quality recovered after withdrawal and 10 pregnancies followed.

pmid:35144505.authors: Yland JJ, McKinnon CJ, Hatch EE, et al.
pmid:35144505.title: A Prospective Study of Male Depression, Psychotropic Medication Use, and Fecundability.
pmid:35144505.finding: Male depression history was weakly associated with lower fecundability (FR 0.89, CI crossing 1); current psychotropic medication use statistically mediated 44% of the depressive-symptom association.

pmid:32654822.authors: Practice Committees of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine and the Society for Assisted Reproductive Technology
pmid:32654822.title: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) for non-male factor indications: a committee opinion
pmid:32654822.finding: ASRM/SART committee opinion reviewing when ICSI may or may not benefit couples whose semen meets WHO reference values; routine ICSI for non-male factor is not supported.

pmid:35263457.authors: Aydın Ş, Bulgan Kılıçdağ E, Çağlar Aytaç P, et al.
pmid:35263457.title: Prospective randomized controlled study of a microfluidic chip technology for sperm selection in male infertility patients
pmid:35263457.finding: Single-centre RCT in male-factor ICSI: microfluidic chip vs swim-up gave similar fertilisation and embryo quality but higher live birth (46.8% vs 25%).

pmid:25602996.authors: Boulet SL, Mehta A, Kissin DM, et al.
pmid:25602996.title: Trends in use of and reproductive outcomes associated with intracytoplasmic sperm injection
pmid:25602996.finding: US registry: ICSI use without male factor rose from 15.4% to 66.9% (1996-2012) and, in those cycles, was associated with slightly lower live birth than conventional IVF (36.5% vs 39.2%; aRR 0.95).

pmid:33894833.authors: Dang VQ, Vuong LN, Luu TM, et al.
pmid:33894833.title: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection versus conventional in-vitro fertilisation in couples with infertility in whom the male partner has normal total sperm count and motility: an open-label, randomised controlled trial
pmid:33894833.finding: In couples with normal sperm count and motility, ICSI did not raise live birth over conventional IVF (35% vs 31%; RR 1.11, 95% CI 0.93-1.32); total fertilisation failure was similar (5% vs 6%).

pmid:37747409.authors: ESHRE Add-ons working group; Lundin K, Bentzen JG, Bozdag G, et al.
pmid:37747409.title: Good practice recommendations on add-ons in reproductive medicine
pmid:37747409.finding: ESHRE good practice recommendations on 42 add-ons: none based on high-quality evidence; not recommended include endometrial receptivity tests, immune testing and immunomodulators (Intralipid, IVIG), glucocorticoids, assisted hatching, time-lapse imaging (to improve live birth), intrauterine hCG, intrauterine and intraovarian PRP, mitochondrial replacement, adjuncts during stimulation (growth hormone, DHEA, testosterone), oral antioxidants and ICSI for non-male factor; PGT-A, endometrial scratching, MACS, PICSI and IMSI 'not recommended for routine clinical use'; microfluidics 'can be considered'; hyaluronan in transfer medium 'recommended' (with single embryo transfer).

pmid:42227305.authors: Garg A, Nakhla O, Steeper M, et al.
pmid:42227305.title: Advanced sperm selection techniques for assisted reproduction
pmid:42227305.finding: Cochrane 2026: hyaluronan-selected ICSI may make no or a slight difference to live birth (RR 1.09, 0.97-1.24; low certainty) and probably slightly reduces miscarriage (RR 0.59; moderate); effects of other techniques (MACS, microfluidics, IMSI) unknown due to very low certainty.

sperm:fer-hfea2026.title: Treatment add-ons with limited evidence (HFEA add-ons rating list)
sperm:fer-hfea2026.finding: HFEA traffic-light ratings for 'chances of having a baby' (page reviewed 28 Sep 2026; ratings set by SCAAC): yellow/amber (unclear) for endometrial scratching, hyaluronate-enriched transfer medium and elective freeze-all; grey (insufficient evidence) for assisted hatching, androgens, intralipids, IMSI, intrauterine culture, microbiome testing and SDF-guided treatments; black (no effect) for time-lapse imaging and PICSI; red (no benefit and/or safety concerns) for endometrial receptivity testing, IVIG, steroids, PRP and PGT-A (PGT-A rated green for reducing miscarriage). No green rating for live birth.

sperm:fer-hfea2026sdf.title: Sperm DNA fragmentation: treatment add-on rating
sperm:fer-hfea2026sdf.finding: After SDF testing: antioxidants and sperm selection (DGC/MACS with ICSI or PICSI) rated grey (insufficient evidence) for male factor and recurrent pregnancy loss; testicular sperm (TESE/TESA) with ICSI rated red for male factor (insufficient evidence plus surgical risk). Reviewed 24 Sep 2026.

pmid:41757843.authors: Huong DT, Tam DTM, Hoa NT, et al.
pmid:41757843.title: Comparative Efficacy of Microfluidics and Density Gradient Centrifugation for Sperm Preparation in IVF: A Randomized Controlled Trial
pmid:41757843.finding: Microfluidic preparation lowered sperm DNA fragmentation index more than density gradients, especially with high baseline DFI, but did not improve pregnancy or live birth.

pmid:38700621.title: In cases with raised sperm DNA fragmentation, can sperm selection by magnetic-activated cell sorting or testicular sperm aspiration help improve reproductive outcomes?
pmid:38700621.n: couples with failed IVF and SDF >30%
pmid:38700621.finding: In couples with raised sperm DNA fragmentation, MACS-selected and testicular sperm gave comparable live birth; no control arm without either.

pmid:30712901.authors: Miller D, Pavitt S, Sharma V, et al.
pmid:30712901.title: Physiological, hyaluronan-selected intracytoplasmic sperm injection for infertility treatment (HABSelect): a parallel, two-group, randomised trial
pmid:30712901.finding: HABSelect: hyaluronan-selected sperm (PICSI) did not raise term live birth vs ICSI (27.4% vs 25.2%; OR 1.12, 95% CI 0.95-1.34); miscarriage was a secondary finding.

pmid:25305728.authors: Romany L, Garrido N, Motato Y, et al.
pmid:25305728.title: Removal of annexin V-positive sperm cells for intracytoplasmic sperm injection in ovum donation cycles does not improve reproductive outcome: a controlled and randomized trial in unselected males
pmid:25305728.finding: Removing annexin V-positive sperm by MACS did not improve fertilisation, embryo quality or live birth (48.4% vs 56.4%, NS) in donor-egg ICSI.

pmid:30852746.authors: Ammar O, Houas Z, Mehdi M
pmid:30852746.title: The association between iron, calcium, and oxidative stress in seminal plasma and sperm quality
pmid:30852746.finding: Seminal iron was higher in subfertile men and correlated negatively with sperm motility and normal morphology.

pmid:42101252.authors: Carlomagno F, Tenuta M, Sansone A, et al.
pmid:42101252.title: Iron overload disorders in adults: a comprehensive review of gonadal function, reproductive, and sexual health
pmid:42101252.n: Systematic review: 1201 men, 2134 women with iron overload
pmid:42101252.finding: In iron overload disorders, 47% of men had hypogonadism and over half of those assessed had azoospermia or other sperm abnormalities; early chelation helps prevent but rarely reverses damage.

pmid:12093845.authors: Perera D, Pizzey A, Campbell A, et al.
pmid:12093845.title: Sperm DNA damage in potentially fertile homozygous beta-thalassaemia patients with iron overload
pmid:12093845.finding: Iron-overloaded men (median ferritin 2251 ug/L) had more sperm DNA damage, which rose with later onset of chelation.

pmid:21338668.authors: Abdelouahab N, Ainmelk Y, Takser L
pmid:21338668.title: Polybrominated diphenyl ethers and sperm quality.
pmid:21338668.finding: Serum BDE-47, BDE-100 and summed PBDEs were negatively related to sperm motility and thyroxine, with no relation to other semen parameters.

pmid:29684825.authors: Albert O, Huang JY, Aleksa K, et al.
pmid:29684825.title: Exposure to polybrominated diphenyl ethers and phthalates in healthy men living in the greater Montreal area: A study of hormonal balance and semen quality.
pmid:29684825.finding: Each 10-fold rise in BDE-47 was associated with borderline lower sperm concentration (-19.7%) and motility (-25.5%) but not with sperm chromatin damage (HT-COMET).

pmid:29241080.authors: Carignan CC, Mínguez-Alarcón L, Williams PL, et al.
pmid:29241080.title: Paternal urinary concentrations of organophosphate flame retardant metabolites, fertility measures, and pregnancy outcomes among couples undergoing in vitro fertilization.
pmid:29241080.finding: Paternal urinary OPFR metabolites were linked to a 12% lower fertilization proportion (2nd vs 1st quartile) and fewer best-quality embryos, but not consistently to implantation, pregnancy or live birth after adjusting for the female partner.

pmid:36069982.authors: Lv MQ, Wang HX, Yang YQ, et al.
pmid:36069982.title: Semen Quality Following Long-term Occupational Exposure to Formaldehyde in China.
pmid:36069982.finding: Long-term occupational formaldehyde exposure index was associated with lower total and progressive sperm motility and velocity.

pmid:20194068.title: House dust concentrations of organophosphate flame retardants in relation to hormone levels and semen quality parameters.
pmid:20194068.finding: An interquartile rise in house-dust TPHP was associated with 19% lower sperm concentration and 10% higher prolactin; TDCPP with 3% lower free T4 and 17% higher prolactin.

pmid:35839669.authors: Siddique S, Farhat I, Kubwabo C, et al.
pmid:35839669.title: Exposure of men living in the greater Montreal area to organophosphate esters: Association with hormonal balance and semen quality.
pmid:35839669.finding: Urinary OPE metabolites were nearly universally detected; a few were associated with hormone changes (e.g. TCIPP with lower testosterone) and some semen parameters.

pmid:41205372.authors: Tang W, Liu X, Cao Y, et al.
pmid:41205372.title: Exposure to individual organophosphate esters and their mixture in relation to semen quality in Chinese men.
pmid:41205372.finding: An organophosphate ester mixture was associated with lower progressive motility, but the signal was driven by organophosphate pesticide metabolites (DMTP), not flame-retardant metabolites.

pmid:26515386.authors: Wang HX, Li HC, Lv MQ, et al.
pmid:26515386.title: Associations between occupation exposure to Formaldehyde and semen quality, a primary study.
pmid:26515386.finding: Occupational formaldehyde exposure was associated with lower total and progressive sperm motility, with higher odds of abnormal motility at low and high exposure.

pmid:29421738.authors: Yu YJ, Lin BG, Liang WB, et al.
pmid:29421738.title: Associations between PBDEs exposure from house dust and human semen quality at an e-waste areas in South China-A pilot study.
pmid:29421738.finding: Dust and semen PBDE levels correlated, and BDE-47/BDE-100 were negatively associated with sperm concentration, count and motility in an e-waste area.

pmid:39483697.authors: Adegbola CA, Akhigbe TM, Adeogun AE, et al.
pmid:39483697.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of the impact of triclosan exposure on human semen quality.
pmid:39483697.finding: Pooled triclosan exposure was associated with lower sperm concentration (SMD -0.42) and total motility (SMD -1.30), with high heterogeneity.

pmid:29449081.authors: Adoamnei E, Mendiola J, Moñino-García M, et al.
pmid:29449081.title: Urinary concentrations of benzophenone-type ultra violet light filters and reproductive parameters in young men.
pmid:29449081.finding: Urinary BP-1 and BP-3 were weakly associated with higher FSH, but no BP-type filter was associated with any semen parameter; effects judged small and of unclear significance.

pmid:25395025.authors: Buck Louis GM, Kannan K, Sapra KJ, et al.
pmid:25395025.title: Urinary concentrations of benzophenone-type ultraviolet radiation filters and couples' fecundity.
pmid:25395025.finding: Men's urinary BP-2 (FOR 0.69) and 4-hydroxybenzophenone (FOR 0.74) were associated with lower couple fecundability; women's concentrations were not.

pmid:26253817.authors: Buck Louis GM, Chen Z, Kim S, et al.
pmid:26253817.title: Urinary concentrations of benzophenone-type ultraviolet light filters and semen quality.
pmid:26253817.finding: Among 35 semen endpoints, BP-2 was associated with lower concentration and some motility measures and BP-8 with two others; BP-1, BP-3 and 4OH-BP were not associated.

pmid:25767892.authors: Dodge LE, Williams PL, Williams MA, et al.
pmid:25767892.title: Paternal Urinary Concentrations of Parabens and Other Phenols in Relation to Reproductive Outcomes among Couples from a Fertility Clinic.
pmid:25767892.finding: Paternal urinary parabens and phenols were not associated with fertilization or live birth after IVF; an isolated second-quartile methylparaben association with lower IUI live birth lacked a dose-response.

pmid:30307509.authors: Hipwell AE, Kahn LG, Factor-Litvak P, et al.
pmid:30307509.title: Exposure to non-persistent chemicals in consumer products and fecundability: a systematic review.
pmid:30307509.finding: Systematic review: preliminary support for female paraben and glycol ether exposure and male benzophenone exposure with longer time to pregnancy; little to no indication for BPA, triclosan or triclocarban; heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis.

pmid:30245359.authors: Joensen UN, Jørgensen N, Thyssen JP, et al.
pmid:30245359.title: Urinary excretion of phenols, parabens and benzophenones in young men: Associations to reproductive hormones and semen quality are modified by mutations in the Filaggrin gene.
pmid:30245359.finding: Associations of BPA and benzophenones with reproductive hormones and semen quality appeared only in men with filaggrin skin-barrier mutations; parabens were not associated with any outcome.

pmid:28692609.authors: Jurewicz J, Radwan M, Wielgomas B, et al.
pmid:28692609.title: Human Semen Quality, Sperm DNA Damage, and the Level of Reproductive Hormones in Relation to Urinary Concentrations of Parabens.
pmid:28692609.finding: Urinary parabens were associated with more abnormal morphology, higher DNA stainability, lower motility and lower testosterone.

pmid:38103620.authors: Kiwitt-Cárdenas J, Arense-Gonzalo JJ, Adoamnei E, et al.
pmid:38103620.title: Urinary concentrations of bisphenol A, parabens and benzophenone-type ultra violet light filters in relation to sperm DNA fragmentation in young men: A chemical mixtures approach.
pmid:38103620.finding: In mixture models, urinary 4-hydroxybenzophenone was associated with slightly lower sperm DNA fragmentation (about -5%); parabens, BPA and other filters were not associated.

pmid:41429296.authors: Li XT, Miao Y, Zhang M, et al.
pmid:41429296.title: Associations of paraben exposures measured by repeated urinary biomarkers with sperm DNA damage and apoptosis.
pmid:41429296.n: Chinese men from an infertility clinic, 2 urine samples each
pmid:41429296.finding: Butylparaben was associated with longer comet tail length and tail moment (sperm DNA damage), more so in overweight and younger men.

pmid:20876036.authors: Meeker JD, Yang T, Ye X, et al.
pmid:20876036.title: Urinary concentrations of parabens and serum hormone levels, semen quality parameters, and sperm DNA damage.
pmid:20876036.finding: Methyl- and propylparaben were not associated with hormones, semen quality or sperm DNA damage; butylparaben categories tracked higher sperm DNA damage (p-trend 0.03).

pmid:31421444.authors: Nassan FL, Mínguez-Alarcón L, Williams PL, et al.
pmid:31421444.title: Urinary triclosan concentrations and semen quality among men from a fertility clinic.
pmid:31421444.finding: Detectable urinary triclosan was associated with about 1 percentage point fewer morphologically normal sperm, without a dose-response, mainly before 2013 when exposure was higher.

pmid:29165110.authors: Nishihama Y, Toshima H, Yoshinaga J, et al.
