pmid:29165110.title: Paraben exposure and semen quality of Japanese male partners of subfertile couples.
pmid:29165110.finding: No association between urinary parabens and semen volume, concentration or motility.

pmid:37688867.authors: Shen X, Zhan M, Wang Y, et al.
pmid:37688867.title: Exposure to parabens and semen quality in reproductive-aged men.
pmid:37688867.finding: A paraben mixture was associated with lower sperm concentration, total count and progressive motility; butylparaben and methylparaben were the main contributors.

pmid:35101560.authors: Yuan G, Ma Y, Zeng Y, et al.
pmid:35101560.title: Associations between low-dose triclosan exposure and semen quality in a Chinese population.
pmid:35101560.finding: Low-level triclosan had limited (none or modest) associations with semen quality and was not associated with abnormal count or motility.

pmid:26901211.authors: Zhu W, Zhang H, Tong C, et al.
pmid:26901211.title: Environmental Exposure to Triclosan and Semen Quality.
pmid:26901211.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
pmid:26901211.finding: Triclosan was modestly associated with fewer forward-moving sperm and, in the lowest tertile, lower morphology, concentration and count.

pmid:35480573.authors: Zhu W, Xie C, Zhao S, et al.
pmid:35480573.title: Environmental Exposure to Triclosan and Male Fecundity: A Prospective Study in China.
pmid:35480573.finding: Higher male urinary triclosan was associated with lower fecundability (FOR 0.77) and higher infertility risk (OR 1.6).

pmid:41803857.authors: Dhar S, Tomar A, N A, et al.
pmid:41803857.title: Phthalates as the silent saboteurs of male fertility via changes in semen quality: a systematic review
pmid:41803857.finding: Systematic review without meta-analysis: MEHP, DEHP and DBP associated with lower sperm concentration and morphology; certainty of evidence low to moderate because studies are observational and heterogeneous.

pmid:26456810.authors: Dodge LE, Williams PL, Williams MA, et al.
pmid:26456810.title: Associations between paternal urinary phthalate metabolite concentrations and reproductive outcomes among couples seeking fertility treatment
pmid:26456810.finding: Paternal MCPP and MCOP were associated with lower implantation and IVF live birth, but most paternal phthalate metabolites were not associated with outcomes.

pmid:12842768.authors: Duty SM, Singh NP, Silva MJ, et al.
pmid:12842768.title: The relationship between environmental exposures to phthalates and DNA damage in human sperm using the neutral comet assay
pmid:12842768.finding: An IQR rise in MEP was associated with 3.6 um greater Comet extent in sperm; other metabolites were not clearly associated.

pmid:40472759.authors: Génard-Walton M, Warembourg C, Williams PL, et al.
pmid:40472759.title: Using mixture and exposome methods to assess the associations and interactions of chemical biomarkers with semen parameters
pmid:40472759.finding: Across four mixture/exposome models of 24 biomarkers (BPA, parabens, triclosan, 17 phthalate metabolites, hair mercury), the consistent signals were mercury (positive) and triclosan (negative); the overall mixture had small, imprecise associations with semen parameters.

pmid:31376593.authors: Ghayda RA, Williams PL, Chavarro JE, et al.
pmid:31376593.title: Urinary bisphenol S concentrations: Potential predictors of and associations with semen quality parameters among men attending a fertility center
pmid:31376593.finding: Men with detectable BPS had lower sperm concentration (30.7 vs 38.3 million/mL) and semen volume, mostly among overweight men; BPS tracked fabric softener, paint and recent beef and cheese intake.

pmid:25462789.authors: Goldstone AE, Chen Z, Perry MJ, et al.
pmid:25462789.title: Urinary bisphenol A and semen quality, the LIFE Study
pmid:25462789.finding: In a general-population preconception cohort, urinary BPA was not associated with 34 of 35 semen measures; the only significant finding was less sperm DNA fragmentation with higher BPA.

pmid:17003688.authors: Hauser R, Meeker JD, Duty S, et al.
pmid:17003688.title: Altered semen quality in relation to urinary concentrations of phthalate monoester and oxidative metabolites
pmid:17003688.finding: Dose-response links of MBP with low sperm concentration (OR 3.3 top quartile) and motility; suggestive links for MBzP; single spot urine.

pmid:13953583.title: Spermatogenesis in man: an estimate of its duration
pmid:13953583.finding: One cycle of the human seminiferous epithelium lasts about 16 days and complete spermatogenesis about 64 days.

pmid:34004170.authors: Kiwitt-Cárdenas J, Adoamnei E, Arense-Gonzalo JJ, et al.
pmid:34004170.title: Associations between urinary concentrations of bisphenol A and sperm DNA fragmentation in young men
pmid:34004170.finding: No association between urinary BPA and sperm DNA fragmentation overall; a positive association only in the subgroup with SDF above 30%.

pmid:21035116.authors: Li DK, Zhou Z, Miao M, et al.
pmid:21035116.title: Urine bisphenol-A (BPA) level in relation to semen quality
pmid:21035116.n: 218 men with and without occupational BPA exposure (China)
pmid:21035116.finding: Men with detectable urinary BPA had more than three times the risk of low sperm concentration and vitality and more than four times the risk of low count; associations persisted at environmental levels.

pmid:33069985.authors: Mínguez-Alarcón L, Bellavia A, Gaskins AJ, et al.
pmid:33069985.title: Paternal mixtures of urinary concentrations of phthalate metabolites, bisphenol A and parabens in relation to pregnancy outcomes among couples attending a fertility center
pmid:33069985.finding: A paternal DEHP-metabolite factor was linked to a higher probability of failing to reach live birth (HR 1.41 per IQR); the BPA/non-DEHP factor HR 1.24 (0.97-1.59) and parabens null.

pmid:30336412.authors: Radke EG, Braun JM, Meeker JD, et al.
pmid:30336412.title: Phthalate exposure and male reproductive outcomes: A systematic review of the human epidemiological evidence
pmid:30336412.finding: EPA systematic review: robust evidence linking DEHP and DBP to male reproductive outcomes (AGD, semen, testosterone), moderate for DINP and BBP, slight for DIBP and DEP.

pmid:38919453.authors: Akhigbe RE, Oyedokun PA, Akhigbe TM, et al.
pmid:38919453.title: Does pyrethroid exposure lower human semen quality? a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:38919453.finding: Pyrethroid exposure was associated with lower sperm motility, but results were inconsistent across regions (concentration lower in Poland, higher in the US) and all studies were cross-sectional.

pmid:29848988.authors: Anifandis G, Katsanaki K, Lagodonti G, et al.
pmid:29848988.title: The Effect of Glyphosate on Human Sperm Motility and Sperm DNA Fragmentation.
pmid:29848988.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
pmid:29848988.finding: In vitro, glyphosate at 0.36 mg/L (far above environmental levels) reduced progressive sperm motility after 1 h but did not change sperm DNA fragmentation.

pmid:31783240.authors: Chen YJ, Duan P, Meng TQ, et al.
pmid:31783240.title: Associations of blood trihalomethanes with semen quality among 1199 healthy Chinese men screened as potential sperm donors.
pmid:31783240.finding: Blood chloroform, brominated and total trihalomethanes were inversely associated with sperm count in cross-sectional and repeated-measure analyses.

pmid:14569179.authors: Fenster L, Waller K, Windham G, et al.
pmid:14569179.title: Trihalomethane levels in home tap water and semen quality.
pmid:14569179.finding: Ingesting more than about two glasses a day of water with 80 ug/L THM was associated with 7.1 percentage points fewer normal-morphology sperm; authors noted limited exposure assessment.

pmid:34410018.authors: Giulioni C, Maurizi V, Scarcella S, et al.
pmid:34410018.title: Do environmental and occupational exposure to pyrethroids and organophosphates affect human semen parameters? Results of a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:34410018.finding: Organophosphate exposure was associated with lower ejaculate volume, sperm count and concentration; pyrethroid exposure was associated only with fewer normal-morphology sperm (WMD -7.6%).

pmid:23759536.authors: Iszatt N, Nieuwenhuijsen MJ, Bennett J, et al.
pmid:23759536.title: Chlorination by-products in tap water and semen quality in England and Wales.
pmid:23759536.finding: In the largest study of public-water DBPs and semen, trihalomethane concentrations were not associated with poor semen quality (OR per 10 ug/L 1.01, 0.91-1.12).

pmid:20955780.authors: Ji G, Xia Y, Gu A, et al.
pmid:20955780.title: Effects of non-occupational environmental exposure to pyrethroids on semen quality and sperm DNA integrity in Chinese men.
pmid:20955780.finding: Urinary 3-PBA was inversely associated with sperm concentration and positively with sperm DNA fragmentation after adjustment.

pmid:18579513.authors: Meeker JD, Barr DB, Hauser R
pmid:18579513.title: Human semen quality and sperm DNA damage in relation to urinary metabolites of pyrethroid insecticides.
pmid:18579513.finding: Urinary pyrethroid metabolites were associated with lower sperm concentration and motility and with more sperm DNA damage on the comet assay.

pmid:38696871.authors: Vasseur C, Serra L, El Balkhi S, et al.
pmid:38696871.title: Glyphosate presence in human sperm: First report and positive correlation with oxidative stress in an infertile French population.
pmid:38696871.finding: Glyphosate was detected in seminal plasma at about four times blood levels; seminal glyphosate tracked seminal 8-OHdG, and men with glyphosate had higher oxidant status and MDA.

pmid:23454109.authors: Zeng Q, Li M, Xie SH, et al.
pmid:23454109.title: Baseline blood trihalomethanes, semen parameters and serum total testosterone: a cross-sectional study in China.
pmid:23454109.finding: Moderate blood bromodichloromethane and dibromochloromethane levels were associated with lower sperm count and linearity, with suggestive trends for concentration and testosterone.

pmid:24632126.authors: Zeng Q, Chen YZ, Xu L, et al.
pmid:24632126.title: Evaluation of exposure to trihalomethanes in tap water and semen quality: a prospective study in Wuhan, China.
pmid:24632126.finding: THM uptake via drinking water was associated with decreasing trends in sperm concentration and count.

pmid:22748101.authors: Agarwal A, Aponte-Mellado A, Premkumar BJ, et al.
pmid:22748101.title: The effects of oxidative stress on female reproduction: a review
pmid:22748101.finding: Narrative review: oxidative stress is implicated in endometriosis, PCOS, unexplained infertility and pregnancy complications; antioxidant evidence is mostly animal/in-vitro and conflicting.

pmid:21220312.authors: Shkolnik K, Tadmor A, Ben-Dor S, et al.
pmid:21220312.title: Reactive oxygen species are indispensable in ovulation
pmid:21220312.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:21220312.finding: In mice, antioxidants injected into the ovarian bursa reduced ovulation and blocked LH-induced cumulus expansion; H2O2 mimicked LH. ROS are an essential pre-ovulatory signal.

pmid:27562289.authors: May-Panloup P, Boucret L, Chao de la Barca JM, et al.
pmid:27562289.title: Ovarian ageing: the role of mitochondria in oocytes and follicles
pmid:27562289.finding: Oocytes are the most mitochondria-rich cells in the body; ageing-related mtDNA instability and impaired mitochondrial biogenesis in oocytes and granulosa cells are closely linked to declining oocyte quality.

pmid:18223651.authors: Cree LM, Samuels DC, de Sousa Lopes SC, et al.
pmid:18223651.title: A reduction of mitochondrial DNA molecules during embryogenesis explains the rapid segregation of genotypes
pmid:18223651.finding: Mouse study: mtDNA is maternally inherited and passes through a genetic bottleneck (partitioning of mtDNA molecules during embryogenesis and germ-cell proliferation) that explains rapid shifts in heteroplasmy between generations.

pmid:24355045.authors: Franasiak JM, Forman EJ, Hong KH, et al.
pmid:24355045.title: The nature of aneuploidy with increasing age of the female partner: a review of 15,169 consecutive trophectoderm biopsies evaluated with comprehensive chromosomal screening
pmid:24355045.finding: Embryo aneuploidy was lowest at ages 26-30 and rose predictably after 26; the chance of having no euploid embryo was 2-6% at ages 26-37, 33% at 42 and 53% at 44.

pmid:31604276.authors: Gruhn JR, Zielinska AP, Shukla V, et al.
pmid:31604276.title: Chromosome errors in human eggs shape natural fertility over reproductive life span
pmid:31604276.finding: Aneuploidy in human eggs follows a U-curve with age; in older women it is driven by centromeric and more extensive loss of sister-chromatid cohesion.

pmid:32049001.authors: Bertoldo MJ, Listijono DR, Ho WJ, et al.
pmid:32049001.title: NAD(+) Repletion Rescues Female Fertility during Reproductive Aging
pmid:32049001.finding: In aged mice, oocyte NAD+ falls with age; the precursor NMN restored oocyte quality, fertility and embryo development. Mouse data only.

pmid:32755581.authors: Miao Y, Cui Z, Gao Q, et al.
pmid:32755581.title: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide Supplementation Reverses the Declining Quality of Maternally Aged Oocytes
pmid:32755581.finding: In naturally aged mice, NMN restored oocyte NAD+, spindle/chromosome structure, fertilization ability and mitochondrial function and lowered ROS. Mouse data only.

pmid:3558758.title: Dynamics of follicular growth in the human: a model from preliminary results
pmid:3558758.finding: Human follicle growth is very long: the ovulatory follicle comes from a cohort of preantral follicles that differentiated about 85 days earlier; it is recruited 15-20 days before ovulation.

pmid:20362973.title: Human ovarian follicular development: from activation of resting follicles to preovulatory maturation
pmid:20362973.finding: Several months are needed for a growing follicle to reach the preantral stage, then about 70 more days to reach 2 mm before cyclic selection.

pmid:16861701.authors: Das S, Chattopadhyay R, Ghosh S, et al.
pmid:16861701.title: Reactive oxygen species level in follicular fluid--embryo quality marker in IVF?
pmid:16861701.finding: Higher follicular fluid ROS and lipid peroxidation were associated with fertilization failure, pronuclear arrest and poor-grade embryos.

pmid:18339123.authors: Tamura H, Takasaki A, Miwa I, et al.
pmid:18339123.title: Oxidative stress impairs oocyte quality and melatonin protects oocytes from free radical damage and improves fertilization rate
pmid:18339123.finding: Follicular 8-OHdG (oxidative DNA damage) was higher where many oocytes degenerated; melatonin 3 mg/day and/or vitamin E 600 mg/day lowered follicular oxidative markers, and melatonin was associated with better fertilization vs the previous failed cycle (not randomized).

pmid:20643402.authors: Meseguer M, Santiso R, Garrido N, et al.
pmid:20643402.title: Effect of sperm DNA fragmentation on pregnancy outcome depends on oocyte quality
pmid:20643402.finding: Sperm DNA fragmentation lowered pregnancy odds when the woman's own (infertile-patient) oocytes were used, but had no significant effect with donor oocytes, implying good oocytes can compensate for sperm DNA damage.

pmid:20663262.authors: Ménézo Y, Dale B, Cohen M
pmid:20663262.title: DNA damage and repair in human oocytes and embryos: a review
pmid:20663262.finding: Early embryos rely on maternally stored DNA-repair transcripts until embryonic genome activation at the 4-8 cell stage; the oocyte must repair DNA damage brought in by sperm.

pmid:24559617.authors: ACOG Committee on Gynecologic Practice; ASRM Practice Committee
pmid:24559617.title: Female age-related fertility decline. Committee Opinion No. 589
pmid:24559617.finding: ACOG/ASRM: female fecundity declines gradually from about age 32 and more rapidly after 37; evaluate after 6 months of trying at >35 and immediately at >40.

pmid:23303572.authors: Murri M, Luque-Ramírez M, Insenser M, et al.
pmid:23303572.title: Circulating markers of oxidative stress and polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS): a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:23303572.finding: Women with PCOS had higher circulating malondialdehyde (+47%), homocysteine (+23%) and ADMA, and about 50% lower glutathione, independent of weight excess.

pmid:28701212.authors: Sanchez AM, Vanni VS, Bartiromo L, et al.
pmid:28701212.title: Is the oocyte quality affected by endometriosis? A review of the literature
pmid:28701212.finding: Systematic review: oocytes from women with endometriosis are more likely to fail in-vitro maturation, show altered morphology and lower mitochondrial content; granulosa cells show more ROS.

pmid:26168799.authors: Hamdan M, Dunselman G, Li TC, et al.
pmid:26168799.title: The impact of endometrioma on IVF/ICSI outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:26168799.finding: Endometrioma was associated with fewer oocytes retrieved and more cancelled cycles, but similar live birth rates (OR 0.98); surgery before IVF did not improve outcomes.

pmid:19574447.authors: Wang Q, Ratchford AM, Chi MM, et al.
pmid:19574447.title: Maternal diabetes causes mitochondrial dysfunction and meiotic defects in murine oocytes
pmid:19574447.finding: In diabetic mice, oocytes showed abnormal mitochondrial structure and distribution, lower ATP and TCA metabolites, more spindle defects and higher aneuploidy.

pmid:21170514.authors: Whitworth KW, Baird DD, Stene LC, et al.
pmid:21170514.title: Fecundability among women with type 1 and type 2 diabetes in the Norwegian Mother and Child Cohort Study
pmid:21170514.finding: Fecundability odds were lower in women with type 1 diabetes (FOR 0.76) and type 2 diabetes (FOR 0.64), even with regular cycles.

pmid:19223519.authors: Robker RL, Akison LK, Bennett BD, et al.
pmid:19223519.title: Obese women exhibit differences in ovarian metabolites, hormones, and gene expression compared with moderate-weight women
pmid:19223519.finding: Higher BMI was associated with higher follicular fluid insulin, lactate, triglycerides and C-reactive protein: an altered, more inflammatory follicular environment.

pmid:20861227.authors: Wu LL, Dunning KR, Yang X, et al.
pmid:20861227.title: High-fat diet causes lipotoxicity responses in cumulus-oocyte complexes and decreased fertilization rates
pmid:20861227.finding: High-fat-diet obese mice had lipid-laden oocytes with reduced mitochondrial membrane potential, ER stress, cumulus apoptosis and lower fertilization; ER stress markers were also raised in granulosa cells of obese women.

pmid:30941397.authors: Sermondade N, Huberlant S, Bourhis-Lefebvre V, et al.
pmid:30941397.title: Female obesity is negatively associated with live birth rate following IVF: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:30941397.finding: Obese women (BMI >= 30) had lower live birth rates after IVF than normal-weight women (RR 0.85); worse when combined with PCOS.

pmid:1559293.authors: Kiddy DS, Hamilton-Fairley D, Bush A, et al.
pmid:1559293.title: Improvement in endocrine and ovarian function during dietary treatment of obese women with polycystic ovary syndrome
pmid:1559293.finding: Women who lost more than 5% of body weight on a 1000 kcal diet had lower insulin, higher SHBG and 9 of 11 improved reproductive function; those losing less than 5% did not improve.

pmid:27192672.authors: Mutsaerts MA, van Oers AM, Groen H, et al.
pmid:27192672.title: Randomized Trial of a Lifestyle Program in Obese Infertile Women
pmid:27192672.finding: LIFEstyle trial: a 6-month lifestyle program before fertility treatment (mean loss 4.4 kg) did not increase healthy term singleton births at 24 months (27.1% vs 35.2%; RR 0.77).

pmid:28854592.authors: Einarsson S, Bergh C, Friberg B, et al.
pmid:28854592.title: Weight reduction intervention for obese infertile women prior to IVF: a randomized controlled trial
pmid:28854592.finding: Intensive weight loss (12 weeks 880 kcal/day, mean -9.4 kg) before IVF did not change IVF live birth (29.6% vs 27.5%), but more spontaneous conceptions occurred (10.5% vs 2.6%).

pmid:28961722.authors: Best D, Avenell A, Bhattacharya S
pmid:28961722.title: How effective are weight-loss interventions for improving fertility in women and men who are overweight or obese? A systematic review and meta-analysis of the evidence
pmid:28961722.finding: In overweight/obese women, reduced-calorie diet and exercise interventions increased pregnancy (RR 1.59) and improved ovulation; miscarriage was not reduced.

pmid:9688387.authors: Augood C, Duckitt K, Templeton AA
pmid:9688387.title: Smoking and female infertility: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:9688387.finding: Female smokers had higher odds of infertility (OR 1.60) and lower odds of pregnancy per IVF cycle (OR 0.66).

pmid:18927070.authors: Waylen AL, Metwally M, Jones GL, et al.
pmid:18927070.title: Effects of cigarette smoking upon clinical outcomes of assisted reproduction: a meta-analysis
pmid:18927070.finding: Smokers undergoing ART had lower odds of live birth per cycle (OR 0.54) and clinical pregnancy (OR 0.56) and higher miscarriage (OR 2.65).

pmid:30481189.authors: Zhu D, Chung HF, Pandeya N, et al.
pmid:30481189.title: Relationships between intensity, duration, cumulative dose, and timing of smoking with age at menopause: A pooled analysis of individual data from 17 observational studies
pmid:30481189.finding: Current smokers had about twice the risk of premature (RRR 2.05) and early (1.80) menopause, with clear dose-response; women who had quit more than 10 years earlier had the same risk as never smokers.

pmid:18252054.authors: Freour T, Masson D, Mirallie S, et al.
pmid:18252054.title: Active smoking compromises IVF outcome and affects ovarian reserve
pmid:18252054.finding: Active smokers had lower AMH, fewer mature oocytes (8.6 vs 12.1) and lower clinical pregnancy (10% vs 29.6%) than non-smokers.

pmid:38284953.authors: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
pmid:38284953.title: Tobacco or marijuana use and infertility: a committee opinion
pmid:38284953.finding: ASRM committee opinion reviewing deleterious effects of tobacco, nicotine and marijuana on conception, ovarian follicular dynamics, gamete mutations and ART outcomes, and smoking-cessation strategies.

pmid:29062133.authors: Fan D, Liu L, Xia Q, et al.
pmid:29062133.title: Female alcohol consumption and fecundability: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis
pmid:29062133.finding: Any alcohol use was associated with lower fecundability (RR 0.87); light (<=12.5 g/day) 0.89, moderate-heavy (>12.5 g/day) 0.77; per 12.5 g/day RR 0.98.

pmid:27581754.authors: Mikkelsen EM, Riis AH, Wise LA, et al.
pmid:27581754.title: Alcohol consumption and fecundability: prospective Danish cohort study
pmid:27581754.finding: Fewer than 14 servings/week had no discernible effect on fecundability; >=14 servings/week FR 0.82 (imprecise).

pmid:21173655.authors: Rossi BV, Berry KF, Hornstein MD, et al.
pmid:21173655.title: Effect of alcohol consumption on in vitro fertilization
pmid:21173655.finding: Women drinking >=4 drinks/week had 16% lower odds of IVF live birth (OR 0.84); 21% lower when both partners did.

pmid:28854726.authors: Abadia L, Chiu YH, Williams PL, et al.
pmid:28854726.title: The association between pre-treatment maternal alcohol and caffeine intake and outcomes of assisted reproduction in a prospectively followed cohort
pmid:28854726.finding: Low-to-moderate pre-treatment alcohol (<=12 g/day) and caffeine (<200 mg/day) were not associated with ART outcomes.

pmid:29276412.authors: Lyngsø J, Ramlau-Hansen CH, Bay B, et al.
pmid:29276412.title: Association between coffee or caffeine consumption and fecundity and fertility: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis
pmid:29276412.finding: Caffeine was associated with spontaneous abortion (RR 1.37 at 300 mg/day; 2.32 at 600 mg/day) but showed little or no association with fecundability or fertility-treatment outcomes.

pmid:27112524.authors: Wesselink AK, Wise LA, Rothman KJ, et al.
pmid:27112524.title: Caffeine and caffeinated beverage consumption and fecundability in a preconception cohort
pmid:27112524.finding: Female total caffeine intake was not associated with fecundability; male intake >=300 mg/day was (FR 0.72).

pmid:26329421.authors: Chen LW, Wu Y, Neelakantan N, et al.
pmid:26329421.title: Maternal caffeine intake during pregnancy and risk of pregnancy loss: a categorical and dose-response meta-analysis of prospective studies
pmid:26329421.finding: Caffeine in pregnancy: pregnancy-loss RR 1.02 at 50-149 mg/day, 1.16 at 150-349, 1.40 at 350-699, 1.72 at >=700; +7% per 100 mg/day.

pmid:20228391.authors: Legro RS, Sauer MV, Mottla GL, et al.
pmid:20228391.title: Effect of air quality on assisted human reproduction
pmid:20228391.finding: Higher NO2 at home and at the IVF lab was associated with lower live birth (e.g. OR 0.76 per 0.01 ppm after embryo transfer); PM2.5 during culture was associated with lower conception.

pmid:32951044.authors: La Marca A, Spaggiari G, Domenici D, et al.
pmid:32951044.title: Elevated levels of nitrous dioxide are associated with lower AMH levels: a real-world analysis
pmid:32951044.finding: Higher NO2 (and weakly PM10/PM2.5) exposure was associated with lower AMH; NO2 remained associated after age adjustment.

pmid:31241127.authors: Gaskins AJ, Mínguez-Alarcón L, Fong KC, et al.
pmid:31241127.title: Supplemental Folate and the Relationship Between Traffic-Related Air Pollution and Livebirth Among Women Undergoing Assisted Reproduction
pmid:31241127.finding: Among women taking <800 ug/day supplemental folate, each 20 ppb NO2 was associated with 24% lower odds of live birth; no association at >=800 ug/day.

pmid:26545148.authors: Hauser R, Gaskins AJ, Souter I, et al.
pmid:26545148.title: Urinary Phthalate Metabolite Concentrations and Reproductive Outcomes among Women Undergoing in Vitro Fertilization: Results from the EARTH Study
pmid:26545148.finding: Highest vs lowest quartile of urinary DEHP metabolites: fewer oocytes and mature oocytes, and 19 percentage points lower clinical pregnancy and live birth per cycle.

pmid:20002217.authors: Mok-Lin E, Ehrlich S, Williams PL, et al.
pmid:20002217.title: Urinary bisphenol A concentrations and ovarian response among women undergoing IVF
pmid:20002217.finding: Each log-unit increase in urinary BPA was associated with 12% fewer oocytes retrieved and lower peak estradiol.

pmid:34337160.authors: Butts CD, Bloom MS, McGough A, et al.
pmid:34337160.title: Toxic elements in follicular fluid adversely influence the likelihood of pregnancy and live birth in women undergoing IVF
pmid:34337160.finding: Follicular fluid mercury above ~0.51 ug/L and higher lead were associated with lower live birth after IVF (Pb RR 0.68).

pmid:12525451.authors: Wallace WH, Thomson AB, Kelsey TW
pmid:12525451.title: The radiosensitivity of the human oocyte
pmid:12525451.finding: Modelling estimates the radiation dose that destroys half of human oocytes (LD50) at less than 2 Gy.

pmid:29620997.authors: Oktay K, Harvey BE, Partridge AH, et al.
pmid:29620997.title: Fertility Preservation in Patients With Cancer: ASCO Clinical Practice Guideline Update
pmid:29620997.finding: ASCO: discuss infertility risk before cancer treatment as early as possible; oocyte and embryo cryopreservation are standard; GnRH agonists are not a substitute for proven preservation methods.

pmid:19801570.authors: Gudmundsdottir SL, Flanders WD, Augestad LB
pmid:19801570.title: Physical activity and fertility in women: the North-Trøndelag Health Study
pmid:19801570.finding: Women active on most days had 3.2-fold odds of fertility problems and exercising to exhaustion 2.3-fold, vs low activity; no association at lower activity levels.

pmid:27474489.authors: Gaskins AJ, Williams PL, Keller MG, et al.
pmid:27474489.title: Maternal physical and sedentary activities in relation to reproductive outcomes following IVF
pmid:27474489.finding: Pre-treatment moderate-to-vigorous activity (median 2.8 h/week) was not associated with IVF outcomes; some vigorous activities were associated with higher live birth.

pmid:31304974.authors: Mena GP, Mielke GI, Brown WJ
pmid:31304974.title: The effect of physical activity on reproductive health outcomes in young women: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:31304974.finding: Physical-activity interventions increased pregnancy (RR 2.10) and live birth (RR 2.11) vs no therapy in women with reproductive problems (small number of trials).

pmid:30987736.authors: Willis SK, Hatch EE, Wesselink AK, et al.
pmid:30987736.title: Female sleep patterns, shift work, and fecundability in a North American preconception cohort study
pmid:30987736.finding: Trouble sleeping >50% of the time was associated with lower fecundability (FR 0.87); <6 h sleep FR 0.89 (imprecise); shift work was not associated.

pmid:24664130.authors: Lynch CD, Sundaram R, Maisog JM, et al.
pmid:24664130.title: Preconception stress increases the risk of infertility: results from a couple-based prospective cohort study--the LIFE study
pmid:24664130.finding: Highest vs lowest tertile of salivary alpha-amylase (stress marker) was associated with 29% lower fecundability and 2-fold infertility risk; cortisol was not associated.

pmid:21345903.authors: Boivin J, Griffiths E, Venetis CA
pmid:21345903.title: Emotional distress in infertile women and failure of assisted reproductive technologies: meta-analysis of prospective psychosocial studies
pmid:21345903.finding: Pre-treatment anxiety or depression was not associated with pregnancy after a cycle of ART.

pmid:29390148.authors: Karayiannis D, Kontogianni MD, Mendorou C, et al.
pmid:29390148.title: Adherence to the Mediterranean diet and IVF success rate among non-obese women attempting fertility
pmid:29390148.finding: Lowest vs highest tertile of Mediterranean diet score had lower live birth (26.6% vs 48.8%; adjusted RR 0.32); association seen only in women under 35; no effect on oocyte or embryo measures.

pmid:30742825.authors: Gaskins AJ, Nassan FL, Chiu YH, et al.
pmid:30742825.title: Dietary patterns and outcomes of assisted reproduction
pmid:30742825.finding: The profertility diet was associated with 53% higher odds of live birth per SD; top vs bottom quartile +28 percentage points; not related to oocyte counts. Mediterranean diet benefit plateaued after the second quartile.

pmid:20189169.authors: Vujkovic M, de Vries JH, Lindemans J, et al.
pmid:20189169.title: The preconception Mediterranean dietary pattern in couples undergoing in vitro fertilization/intracytoplasmic sperm injection treatment increases the chance of pregnancy
pmid:20189169.finding: High couple adherence to a Mediterranean dietary pattern was associated with higher pregnancy odds after IVF/ICSI (OR 1.4) and higher folate and vitamin B6 in blood and follicular fluid.

pmid:36346903.authors: Muffone ARMC, de Oliveira Lübke PDP, Rabito EI
pmid:36346903.title: Mediterranean diet and infertility: a systematic review with meta-analysis of cohort studies
pmid:36346903.finding: Pooled evidence linking Mediterranean diet adherence to live birth and pregnancy was inconsistent and insufficient to support clinical application.

pmid:28844822.title: Diet and fertility: a review
pmid:28844822.finding: Review: supplemental folic acid (above neural-tube-defect doses) is consistently associated with better fertility; antioxidant supplements do not help women in fertility treatment; omega-3s appear beneficial; vitamin D matters mainly in deficiency.

pmid:17978119.authors: Chavarro JE, Rich-Edwards JW, Rosner BA, et al.
pmid:17978119.title: Diet and lifestyle in the prevention of ovulatory disorder infertility
pmid:17978119.finding: Highest vs lowest quintile of a 'fertility diet' score was associated with 66% lower risk of ovulatory infertility (RR 0.34); five or more low-risk lifestyle factors with 69% lower risk.

pmid:25198264.authors: Gaskins AJ, Afeiche MC, Wright DL, et al.
pmid:25198264.title: Dietary folate and reproductive success among women undergoing assisted reproduction
pmid:25198264.finding: Supplemental folate >800 ug/day vs <400 ug/day was associated with a 20 percentage-point higher live birth rate after ART.

pmid:29149263.authors: Chu J, Gallos I, Tobias A, et al.
pmid:29149263.title: Vitamin D and assisted reproductive treatment outcome: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:29149263.finding: Vitamin D-replete women undergoing ART had higher live birth than deficient/insufficient women (OR 1.33); no association with miscarriage.

pmid:35370977.authors: Zhou X, Wu X, Luo X, et al.
pmid:35370977.title: Effect of Vitamin D Supplementation on In Vitro Fertilization Outcomes: A Trial Sequential Meta-Analysis of 5 Randomized Controlled Trials
pmid:35370977.finding: In vitamin D-deficient infertile women, supplementation raised chemical pregnancy (RR 1.53) but not clinical pregnancy (RR 1.34, NS) or embryo quality.

pmid:29136189.authors: Chiu YH, Karmon AE, Gaskins AJ, et al.
pmid:29136189.title: Serum omega-3 fatty acids and treatment outcomes among women undergoing assisted reproduction
pmid:29136189.finding: Each 1% higher serum long-chain omega-3 was associated with 8% higher probability of live birth after ART.

pmid:22978268.authors: Nehra D, Le HD, Fallon EM, et al.
pmid:22978268.title: Prolonging the female reproductive lifespan and improving egg quality with dietary omega-3 fatty acids
pmid:22978268.finding: In mice, omega-3-rich diets prolonged reproductive function and improved oocyte quality at advanced maternal age; omega-6-rich diets worsened it.

pmid:32851663.authors: Showell MG, Mackenzie-Proctor R, Jordan V, et al.
pmid:32851663.title: Antioxidants for female subfertility
pmid:32851663.finding: Very low-quality evidence: antioxidants might raise live birth (OR 1.81) but evidence is unreliable; 2026 editorial note: 7 included trials since retracted and 2 under expression of concern (conclusions retained).

pmid:29587861.authors: Xu Y, Nisenblat V, Lu C, et al.
pmid:29587861.title: Pretreatment with coenzyme Q10 improves ovarian response and embryo quality in low-prognosis young women with decreased ovarian reserve: a randomized controlled trial
pmid:29587861.n: 186 women <35 with poor ovarian reserve (169 analysed)
pmid:29587861.finding: CoQ10 600 mg/day (200 mg three times daily) for 60 days before IVF increased oocytes retrieved (median 4 vs 2), fertilization and good embryos; live birth 29% vs 16% was not statistically significant.

pmid:26111777.authors: Ben-Meir A, Burstein E, Borrego-Alvarez A, et al.
pmid:26111777.title: Coenzyme Q10 restores oocyte mitochondrial function and fertility during reproductive aging
pmid:26111777.finding: Oocyte ageing in mice and humans involves reduced CoQ-synthesis enzymes and lower ATP; CoQ10 reversed age-related oocyte deficits in mice.

pmid:32767206.authors: Florou P, Anagnostis P, Theocharis P, et al.
pmid:32767206.title: Does coenzyme Q(10) supplementation improve fertility outcomes in women undergoing assisted reproductive technology procedures? A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized-controlled trials
pmid:32767206.finding: CoQ10 increased clinical pregnancy (28.8% vs 14.1%; OR 2.44) but not live birth (OR 1.67, NS) or miscarriage.

pmid:32045470.authors: Zhang Y, Zhang C, Shu J, et al.
pmid:32045470.title: Adjuvant treatment strategies in ovarian stimulation for poor responders undergoing IVF: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
pmid:32045470.finding: In poor responders, DHEA (OR 2.46) and CoQ10 (OR 2.22) were associated with higher clinical pregnancy vs control; CoQ10 had the lowest cancellation rate.

pmid:32292388.authors: Hu KL, Ye X, Wang S, et al.
pmid:32292388.title: Melatonin Application in Assisted Reproductive Technology: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials
pmid:32292388.finding: Melatonin increased clinical pregnancy (OR 1.43) and oocyte/embryo counts but not live birth (OR 1.38, 3 RCTs, NS); low-quality evidence.

pmid:31583699.authors: Fernando S, Wallace EM, Rombauts L, et al.
pmid:31583699.title: The effect of melatonin on ultrasound markers of follicular development: A double-blind placebo-controlled randomised trial
pmid:31583699.journal: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
pmid:31583699.finding: Melatonin 2, 4 or 8 mg twice daily during IVF stimulation did not change follicle number or ovarian vascular indices vs placebo (pilot).

pmid:30570133.authors: Showell MG, Mackenzie-Proctor R, Jordan V, et al.
pmid:30570133.title: Inositol for subfertile women with polycystic ovary syndrome
pmid:30570133.finding: Very low-quality evidence; uncertain whether myo-inositol improves live birth (OR 2.42, 95% CI 0.75-7.83) or clinical pregnancy in PCOS before IVF.

pmid:38163998.authors: Fitz V, Graca S, Mahalingaiah S, et al.
pmid:38163998.title: Inositol for Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis to Inform the 2023 Update of the International Evidence-based PCOS Guidelines
pmid:38163998.finding: For the 2023 PCOS guideline: inositol evidence is limited and inconclusive; possible metabolic benefits; little difference from metformin for reproductive outcomes.

pmid:26507336.authors: Pacchiarotti A, Carlomagno G, Antonini G, et al.
pmid:26507336.title: Effect of myo-inositol and melatonin versus myo-inositol, in a randomized controlled trial, for improving in vitro fertilization of patients with polycystic ovarian syndrome
pmid:26507336.finding: RETRACTED (2026). Claimed myo-inositol 4 g + folic acid 400 ug + melatonin 3 mg improved oocyte and embryo quality; should not be relied on.

pmid:25653680.authors: Thakker D, Raval A, Patel I, et al.
pmid:25653680.title: N-acetylcysteine for polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled clinical trials
pmid:25653680.finding: NAC improved ovulation and pregnancy vs placebo but was inferior to metformin; trials had high risk of bias.

pmid:15705376.authors: Rizk AY, Bedaiwy MA, Al-Inany HG
pmid:15705376.title: N-acetyl-cysteine is a novel adjuvant to clomiphene citrate in clomiphene citrate-resistant patients with polycystic ovary syndrome
pmid:15705376.finding: NAC 1.2 g/day added to clomiphene raised ovulation (49.3% vs 1.3%) and pregnancy (21.3% vs 0%) vs placebo.

pmid:38837771.authors: Naik S, Lepine S, Nagels HE, et al.
pmid:38837771.title: Androgens (dehydroepiandrosterone or testosterone) for women undergoing assisted reproduction
pmid:38837771.finding: Cochrane: DHEA probably makes little or no difference to live birth in poor responders (OR 1.30, NS, moderate certainty); testosterone probably improves it (OR 2.53).

pmid:20729538.authors: Wiser A, Gonen O, Ghetler Y, et al.
pmid:20729538.title: Addition of dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) for poor-responder patients before and during IVF treatment improves the pregnancy rate: a randomized prospective study
pmid:20729538.finding: DHEA 75 mg/day before and during IVF was associated with higher live birth (23.1% vs 4.0%) in a very small trial.

pmid:25015747.authors: Ismail AM, Hamed AH, Saso S, et al.
pmid:25015747.title: Adding L-carnitine to clomiphene resistant PCOS women improves the quality of ovulation and the pregnancy rate. A randomized clinical trial
pmid:25015747.journal: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
pmid:25015747.finding: RETRACTED. Claimed L-carnitine 3 g/day with clomiphene raised pregnancy from 5.8% to 51.5%; should not be relied on.

pmid:32273814.title: Preconception resveratrol intake against infertility: Friend or foe?
pmid:32273814.finding: Resveratrol may support ovarian function via SIRT1 but suppresses endometrial decidualization (anti-deciduogenic) and its teratogenicity is unknown; avoid in the luteal phase and pregnancy.

pmid:31160243.authors: Ochiai A, Kuroda K, Ikemoto Y, et al.
pmid:31160243.title: Influence of resveratrol supplementation on IVF-embryo transfer cycle outcomes
pmid:31160243.finding: Resveratrol 200 mg/day during embryo-transfer cycles was associated with lower clinical pregnancy (OR 0.54) and higher miscarriage (OR 2.60).

pmid:38987824.authors: Ardehjani NA, Agha-Hosseini M, Nashtaei MS, et al.
pmid:38987824.title: Resveratrol ameliorates mitochondrial biogenesis and reproductive outcomes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome undergoing assisted reproduction: a randomized, triple-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial
pmid:38987824.finding: Resveratrol 800 mg/day for 60 days lowered follicular fluid oxidative stress and raised oocyte maturity and good-quality embryos, but pregnancy rates did not differ.

pmid:33345661.authors: Di Tucci C, Galati G, Mattei G, et al.
pmid:33345661.title: The role of alpha lipoic acid in female and male infertility: a systematic review
pmid:33345661.finding: Systematic review (28 articles): alpha-lipoic acid shows some positive effects on oocyte maturation, embryo grade and endometriosis pain, but clinical evidence is limited and more trials are needed.

pmid:32395637.authors: ESHRE Guideline Group on Ovarian Stimulation; Bosch E, Broer S, et al.
pmid:32395637.title: ESHRE guideline: ovarian stimulation for IVF/ICSI(†)
pmid:32395637.finding: ESHRE ovarian stimulation guideline: hormone pre-treatment and adjuvants (metformin, growth hormone, testosterone, DHEA, aspirin, sildenafil) are not recommended for improving efficacy.

pmid:20685716.authors: Dechanet C, Anahory T, Mathieu Daude JC, et al.
pmid:20685716.title: Effects of cigarette smoking on reproduction
pmid:20685716.finding: Systematic review: cigarette smoke contains thousands of toxicants (nicotine, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, cadmium) that target folliculogenesis, steroidogenesis and every other reproductive stage, dose-dependently.

pmid:25788567.authors: Hahn KA, Wise LA, Rothman KJ, et al.
pmid:25788567.title: Caffeine and caffeinated beverage consumption and risk of spontaneous abortion
pmid:25788567.finding: Preconception caffeine was not associated with miscarriage (HR 1.09 for >=300 vs <100 mg/day), whereas early-pregnancy intake of 100-299 mg/day was (HR ~1.5-1.6).

pmid:30921477.authors: Lim SS, Hutchison SK, Van Ryswyk E, et al.
pmid:30921477.title: Lifestyle changes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome
pmid:30921477.finding: Cochrane: lifestyle interventions in PCOS may modestly reduce weight and free androgen index; no trial reported live birth or miscarriage.

pmid:32514568.authors: Szymanska KJ, Tan X, Oktay K
pmid:32514568.title: Unraveling the mechanisms of chemotherapy-induced damage to human primordial follicle reserve: road to developing therapeutics for fertility preservation and reversing ovarian aging
pmid:32514568.finding: Gonadotoxic chemotherapy (e.g. cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin) induces DNA double-strand breaks and apoptosis of primordial-follicle oocytes within 12-24 h, plus stromal and microvascular damage.

pmid:30895239.authors: Fernando S, Biggs SN, Horne RSC, et al.
pmid:30895239.title: The impact of melatonin on the sleep patterns of women undergoing IVF: a double blind RCT
pmid:30895239.finding: Melatonin 2, 4 or 8 mg twice daily from cycle day 2 to egg retrieval did not cause daytime sleepiness or change objective sleep vs placebo.

pmid:34517426.authors: Abdelazeem B, Abbas KS, Shehata J, et al.
pmid:34517426.title: The effects of curcumin as dietary supplement for patients with polycystic ovary syndrome: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.
pmid:34517426.finding: Curcumin improved fasting glucose (-3.7 mg/dL), insulin, HOMA-IR (-0.55) and total cholesterol, with no effect on LDL, HDL, sex hormones, weight or CRP.

pmid:31656219.authors: Azami SH, Nazarian H, Abdollahifar MA, et al.
pmid:31656219.title: The antioxidant curcumin postpones ovarian aging in young and middle-aged mice.
pmid:31656219.finding: In mice, intraperitoneal curcumin (100 mg/kg/day) preserved follicle numbers, AMH and oocyte quality with age.

pmid:22606002.title: Injurious effects of curcumin on maturation of mouse oocytes, fertilization and fetal development via apoptosis.
pmid:22606002.finding: In mice, curcumin (in vitro and 40 uM in drinking water) impaired oocyte maturation, fertilisation and early embryo development via apoptosis.

pmid:33669954.authors: Chien YJ, Chang CY, Wu MY, et al.
pmid:33669954.title: Effects of Curcumin on Glycemic Control and Lipid Profile in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis and Trial Sequential Analysis.
pmid:33669954.finding: Curcumin improved fasting glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR (-0.32), HDL and total cholesterol but not LDL or triglycerides.

pmid:39461199.authors: Feghhi F, Ghaznavi H, Sheervalilou R, et al.
pmid:39461199.title: Effects of metformin and curcumin in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: A factorial clinical trial.
pmid:39461199.finding: Nanocurcumin 80 mg three times daily plus metformin improved lipids, glucose markers, weight and testosterone more than either agent alone or placebo over 12 weeks.

pmid:36788534.authors: Ghanbarzadeh-Ghashti N, Ghanbari-Homaie S, Shaseb E, et al.
pmid:36788534.title: The effect of Curcumin on metabolic parameters and androgen level in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a randomized controlled trial.
pmid:36788534.finding: 1000 mg/day curcumin for 12 weeks lowered fasting glucose and reduced amenorrhoea/oligomenorrhoea (13% vs 22%) versus placebo, but did not change lipids, insulin, SHBG, testosterone or hirsutism.

pmid:37818734.authors: Gudarzi R, Shabani F, Mohammad-Alizadeh-Charandabi S, et al.
pmid:37818734.title: Effect of curcumin on painful symptoms of endometriosis: A triple-blind randomized controlled trial.
pmid:37818734.finding: Curcumin 1000 mg/day for 8 weeks did not improve endometriosis pain or quality of life versus placebo.

pmid:40088332.authors: Jannatifar R, Asa E, Cheraghi E, et al.
pmid:40088332.title: Nanomicelle curcumin improves oxidative stress, inflammatory markers, and assisted reproductive techniques outcomes in endometriosis cases: a randomized clinical trial.
pmid:40088332.n: 50 women with stage III/IV endometriosis undergoing ART
pmid:40088332.finding: Nanomicelle curcumin 120 mg/day for 10 weeks improved serum and follicular-fluid oxidative-stress markers and reported more oocytes, mature oocytes and good embryos; small single-centre trial.

pmid:40041784.authors: Mohammadi S, Ziaei S, Morvaridi M, et al.
pmid:40041784.title: Impacts of Curcumin Supplementation on Cardiometabolic Risk Factors in Patients With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis.
pmid:40041784.finding: Curcumin modestly lowered fasting glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR (SMD -0.36) and TC, but did not change BMI, testosterone, DHEA, LH or FSH.

pmid:34655047.authors: Simental-Mendía LE, Shah N, Sathyapalan T, et al.
pmid:34655047.title: Effect of Curcumin on Glycaemic and Lipid Parameters in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
pmid:34655047.finding: Curcumin lowered fasting glucose (-3.7 mg/dL), insulin and HOMA-IR (-0.94, I2 90%) but did not change any lipid index.

pmid:34939763.authors: Esfandyari S, Aleyasin A, Noroozi Z, et al.
pmid:34939763.title: The Protective Effect of Sulforaphane against Oxidative Stress through Activation of NRF2/ARE Pathway in Human Granulosa Cells.
pmid:34939763.finding: Sulforaphane pretreatment protected human granulosa cells from H2O2-induced ROS and apoptosis via NRF2, SOD and catalase.

pmid:36907095.authors: Feng Z, Wang T, Sun Y, et al.
pmid:36907095.title: Sulforaphane suppresses paraquat-induced oxidative damage in bovine in vitro-matured oocytes through Nrf2 transduction pathway.
pmid:36907095.finding: 1 µM sulforaphane during in vitro maturation raised bovine oocyte maturation and embryo rates and countered paraquat oxidative damage via Nrf2.

pmid:37783421.authors: Li WJ, Zhang X, Shen M, et al.
pmid:37783421.title: Sulforaphane alleviates the meiosis defects induced by 3-nitropropionic acid in mouse oocytes.
pmid:37783421.finding: Sulforaphane alleviated 3-nitropropionic-acid-induced meiotic, spindle and mitochondrial defects in mouse oocytes matured in vitro.

pmid:28583601.authors: Sohel MMH, Konca Y, Akyuz B, et al.
pmid:28583601.title: Concentration dependent antioxidative and apoptotic effects of sulforaphane on bovine granulosa cells in vitro.
pmid:28583601.finding: In bovine granulosa cells, low sulforaphane (2 µM) activated NRF2 antioxidant genes while concentrations above ~15 µM were cytotoxic.

pmid:34678578.authors: Taheri M, Hayati Roudbari N, Amidi F, et al.
pmid:34678578.title: The protective effect of sulforaphane against oxidative stress in granulosa cells of patients with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) through activation of AMPK/AKT/NRF2 signaling pathway.
pmid:34678578.n: granulosa cells from PCOS and control women (in vitro)
pmid:34678578.finding: Sulforaphane reduced ROS and apoptosis in granulosa-lutein cells from women with PCOS, with AMPK/AKT/NRF2 activation.

pmid:37020589.authors: Rostami S, Alyasin A, Saedi M, et al.
pmid:37020589.title: Astaxanthin ameliorates inflammation, oxidative stress, and reproductive outcomes in endometriosis patients undergoing assisted reproduction: A randomized, triple-blind placebo-controlled clinical trial.
pmid:37020589.finding: 6 mg/day astaxanthin for 12 weeks lowered serum MDA and cytokines and increased oocytes, MII oocytes and high-quality embryos.

pmid:39482765.authors: Shafie A, Aleyasin A, Saffari M, et al.
pmid:39482765.title: Astaxanthin improves assisted reproductive technology outcomes in poor ovarian responders through alleviating oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis: a randomized clinical trial.
pmid:39482765.finding: 12 mg/day astaxanthin for 8 weeks increased oocytes retrieved, MII oocytes and high-quality embryos and lowered serum MDA and follicular-fluid IL-6.

pmid:37845508.authors: Zhang Y, Bai J, Cui Z, et al.
pmid:37845508.title: Polyamine metabolite spermidine rejuvenates oocyte quality by enhancing mitophagy during female reproductive aging.
pmid:37845508.finding: Ovarian spermidine falls with age in mice; supplementation improved follicle development, oocyte maturation and fertility of aged mice by enhancing mitophagy.

pmid:41483483.authors: Arsenaki E, Stathi D, Triantafyllidis KK, et al.
pmid:41483483.title: The effects of ketogenic diet on polycystic ovary syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:41483483.finding: In mostly overweight women with PCOS, ketogenic diets reduced weight (-10.8 kg), LH and insulin resistance and shortened cycle length pre-post, and beat other diets for weight and LH; androgen results were inconsistent and heterogeneity high.

pmid:40394635.authors: Cannarella R, Rubulotta M, Leonardi A, et al.
pmid:40394635.title: Effects of ketogenic diets on polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:40394635.finding: High-fat ketogenic and very-low-energy ketogenic diets improved weight, glucose, HOMA, triglycerides and LH in PCOS; two RCTs found no weight advantage over low-calorie diets.

pmid:38565002.authors: de Amorim ALB, Rodrigues EF, Sussi EL, et al.
pmid:38565002.title: Carbohydrate restriction during lactation: A systematic review.
pmid:38565002.finding: Carbohydrate restriction during breastfeeding appears repeatedly in case reports of lactation ketoacidosis requiring hospital care.

pmid:29368448.authors: Desrosiers TA, Siega-Riz AM, Mosley BS, et al.
pmid:29368448.title: Low carbohydrate diets may increase risk of neural tube defects.
pmid:29368448.finding: Women with restricted periconceptional carbohydrate intake (<= 5th percentile) had half the dietary folic acid and 30% higher odds of a neural-tube-defect pregnancy (aOR 1.30, 1.02-1.67).

pmid:36688496.authors: Liu S, Yao Q, Li X, et al.
pmid:36688496.title: Effects of a ketogenic diet on reproductive and metabolic phenotypes in mice with polycystic ovary syndrome†.
pmid:36688496.finding: In DHEA-induced PCOS mice a 3-week ketogenic diet lowered weight and glucose, improved ovarian function in some mice and reduced ovarian inflammation and apoptosis, but impaired glucose tolerance.

pmid:16359551.authors: Mavropoulos JC, Yancy WS, Hepburn J, et al.
pmid:16359551.title: The effects of a low-carbohydrate, ketogenic diet on the polycystic ovary syndrome: a pilot study.
pmid:16359551.finding: A < 20 g/day carbohydrate diet for 24 weeks cut weight 12%, free testosterone 22%, LH/FSH 36% and fasting insulin 54% in PCOS; two women conceived.

pmid:34790167.authors: Shang Y, Zhou H, He R, et al.
pmid:34790167.title: Dietary Modification for Reproductive Health in Women With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
pmid:34790167.finding: Dietary interventions in PCOS increased clinical pregnancy, ovulation and menstrual regularity and lowered miscarriage; low-carbohydrate diets were the best subgroup for reproductive outcomes.

pmid:24168053.authors: Sussman D, Ellegood J, Henkelman M
pmid:24168053.title: A gestational ketogenic diet alters maternal metabolic status as well as offspring physiological growth and brain structure in the neonatal mouse.
pmid:24168053.finding: Gestational ketogenic diet lowered fertility and litter size in mice, put dams at risk of fatal ketoacidosis in lactation, and slowed offspring growth with altered brain structure.

pmid:28110175.authors: van der Louw EJ, Williams TJ, Henry-Barron BJ, et al.
pmid:28110175.title: Ketogenic diet therapy for epilepsy during pregnancy: A case series.
pmid:28110175.finding: Two women with epilepsy stayed on ketogenic/modified Atkins therapy in pregnancy with fewer seizures; one infant had ear deformities of unknown significance; safety not established.

pmid:35856159.authors: Whatley EG, Truong TT, Wilhelm D, et al.
pmid:35856159.title: β-hydroxybutyrate reduces blastocyst viability via trophectoderm-mediated metabolic aberrations in mice.
pmid:35856159.finding: Culturing mouse embryos with BHB at ketogenic-diet levels (2 mmol/L) slowed development, disturbed glycolysis and reduced fetal viability after transfer in a sex-specific way.

pmid:38593828.authors: Whatley EG, Harvey AJ, Gardner DK
pmid:38593828.title: A maternal ketogenic diet alters oviduct fluid nutrients and embryo histone acetylation in mice.
pmid:38593828.finding: A maternal ketogenic diet for 24-27 days raised BHB in mouse blood and oviduct fluid, delayed blastocyst development and reduced trophectoderm histone acetylation.

pmid:40674330.authors: Zala SM, Santos R, Strasser E, et al.
pmid:40674330.title: Sex-dependent effects of a gestational ketogenic diet on offspring birth and lifespan.
pmid:40674330.finding: A ketogenic diet in the second half of mouse pregnancy reduced litter size and the proportion of female pups and shortened male offspring lifespan.

pmid:31885557.authors: Zhang X, Zheng Y, Guo Y, et al.
pmid:31885557.title: The Effect of Low Carbohydrate Diet on Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
pmid:31885557.finding: Low-carbohydrate diets (< 45% energy) lowered BMI, HOMA-IR and LDL in PCOS; those lasting > 4 weeks raised SHBG and FSH and lowered testosterone.

pmid:39785103.authors: Al-Taiar A, Rahman ME, Salama M, et al.
pmid:39785103.title: Impacts of Ramadan fasting during pregnancy on pregnancy and birth outcomes: An umbrella review.
pmid:39785103.finding: Umbrella review: insufficient evidence that Ramadan fasting in pregnancy shortens gestation or reduces birth weight, but evidence quality is low and no firm guidance is possible.

pmid:9435419.authors: Alvero R, Kimzey L, Sebring N, et al.
pmid:9435419.title: Effects of fasting on neuroendocrine function and follicle development in lean women.
pmid:9435419.finding: In lean women a 72-h follicular-phase fast cut LH pulses 19%; 2 of 7 fasted cycles were anovulatory and follicular phases lengthened.

pmid:30359228.authors: Glazier JD, Hayes DJL, Hussain S, et al.
pmid:30359228.title: The effect of Ramadan fasting during pregnancy on perinatal outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:30359228.finding: Ramadan fasting in pregnancy did not affect birth weight or preterm delivery; lower placental weight came mainly from one large study; no perinatal mortality data.

pmid:33849562.authors: Li C, Xing C, Zhang J, et al.
pmid:33849562.title: Eight-hour time-restricted feeding improves endocrine and metabolic profiles in women with anovulatory polycystic ovary syndrome.
pmid:33849562.finding: 5 weeks of 8-h TRE (single arm) lowered weight, testosterone, free androgen index, insulin and hsCRP, raised SHBG, and improved menstrual regularity in 11 of 15 women.

pmid:12519869.title: Luteinizing hormone pulsatility is disrupted at a threshold of energy availability in regularly menstruating women.
pmid:12519869.finding: LH pulsatility was unaffected at an energy availability of 30 kcal/kg lean mass/day but disrupted below that threshold (10-20 kcal/kg).

pmid:6121184.authors: Metzger BE, Ravnikar V, Vileisis RA, et al.
pmid:6121184.title: "Accelerated starvation" and the skipped breakfast in late normal pregnancy.
pmid:6121184.finding: Extending the overnight fast from 12 to 18 h in late pregnancy ('skipped breakfast') caused falling glucose and rising fatty acids and beta-hydroxybutyrate ('accelerated starvation'); non-pregnant women barely changed.

pmid:7714088.authors: Olson BR, Cartledge T, Sebring N, et al.
pmid:7714088.title: Short-term fasting affects luteinizing hormone secretory dynamics but not reproductive function in normal-weight sedentary women.
pmid:7714088.finding: A 3-day mid-follicular fast reduced LH pulses but did not alter follicle growth, ovulation or cycle length in normal-weight women.

pmid:40806019.authors: Ranneh Y, Hamsho M, Shkorfu W, et al.
pmid:40806019.title: Effect of Intermittent Fasting on Anthropometric Measurements, Metabolic Profile, and Hormones in Women with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
pmid:40806019.finding: In PCOS, IF reduced weight (-4.25 kg), insulin resistance, free androgen index and DHEA-S and raised SHBG; total testosterone and AMH did not change.

pmid:1881416.authors: Rizzo T, Metzger BE, Burns WJ, et al.
pmid:1881416.title: Correlations between antepartum maternal metabolism and intelligence of offspring.
pmid:1881416.finding: Higher third-trimester maternal beta-hydroxybutyrate correlated with lower offspring IQ scores at ages 2-5 (r about -0.2), observational.

pmid:39143654.authors: Talebi S, Shab-Bidar S, Moini A, et al.
pmid:39143654.title: The effects of time-restricted eating alone or in combination with probiotic supplementation in comparison with a calorie-restricted diet on endocrine and metabolic profiles in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: A randomized clinical trial.
pmid:39143654.finding: 8 weeks of 14:10 early TRE (with or without probiotics) gave no greater weight loss or menstrual, androgen or metabolic improvement than daily calorie restriction.

pmid:33945905.authors: Björvang RD, Hassan J, Stefopoulou M, et al.
pmid:33945905.title: Persistent organic pollutants and the size of ovarian reserve in reproductive-aged women.
pmid:33945905.finding: PFAS were not associated with AMH or follicle density, whereas some organochlorines (HCB, PCBs) were linked to fewer non-growing follicles.

pmid:36801327.authors: Cohen NJ, Yao M, Midya V, et al.
pmid:36801327.title: Exposure to perfluoroalkyl substances and women's fertility outcomes in a Singaporean population-based preconception cohort.
pmid:36801327.finding: Each quartile increase in individual PFAS (PFDA, PFOS) was associated with 5-10% lower fecundability and lower odds of clinical pregnancy.

pmid:19176540.authors: Fei C, McLaughlin JK, Lipworth L, et al.
pmid:19176540.title: Maternal levels of perfluorinated chemicals and subfecundity.
pmid:19176540.finding: Higher plasma PFOS and PFOA were associated with longer time to pregnancy (fecundity odds ratios ~0.6-0.75 in upper quartiles).

pmid:22317809.authors: Fei C, Weinberg CR, Olsen J
pmid:22317809.title: Commentary: perfluorinated chemicals and time to pregnancy: a link based on reverse causation?
pmid:22317809.finding: Commentary by Fei, Weinberg and Olsen asking whether PFAS-time-to-pregnancy links reflect reverse causation (longer gaps since last pregnancy/breastfeeding let PFAS build up).

pmid:35636536.authors: Hong A, Zhuang L, Cui W, et al.
pmid:35636536.title: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) exposure in women seeking in vitro fertilization-embryo transfer treatment (IVF-ET) in China: Blood-follicular transfer and associations with IVF-ET outcomes.
pmid:35636536.finding: PFAS crossed readily from blood into follicular fluid (transfer 0.65-0.92) but showed no clear association with IVF outcomes.

pmid:30731307.authors: Wang W, Zhou W, Wu S, et al.
pmid:30731307.title: Perfluoroalkyl substances exposure and risk of polycystic ovarian syndrome related infertility in Chinese women.
pmid:30731307.finding: Most PFAS did not differ between PCOS-related infertility cases and controls; only PFDoA was associated with higher odds (OR 3.0 top vs bottom tertile).

pmid:22081060.authors: Whitworth KW, Haug LS, Baird DD, et al.
pmid:22081060.title: Perfluorinated compounds and subfecundity in pregnant women.
pmid:22081060.finding: Higher PFOS/PFOA was linked to subfecundity only in parous women (OR ~2.1), not in nulliparous women (OR 0.5-0.7), pointing to reverse causation.

pmid:40334213.authors: Xu J, Wang Q, Jiao X, et al.
pmid:40334213.title: Association between Perfluorooctanoic Acid-Related Poor Embryo Quality and Metabolite Alterations in Human Follicular Fluid during IVF: A Cohort Study.
pmid:40334213.finding: A follicular-fluid PFAS mixture, driven by PFOA, was associated with a lower high-quality embryo rate and lower clinical pregnancy.

pmid:37134253.authors: Zhan W, Qiu W, Ao Y, et al.
pmid:37134253.title: Environmental Exposure to Emerging Alternatives of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances and Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome in Women Diagnosed with Infertility: A Mixture Analysis.
pmid:37134253.finding: A PFAS mixture, led by emerging alternatives (6:2 Cl-PFESA, HFPO-DA), was associated with higher odds of PCOS (OR 1.20 per ln-unit).

pmid:37486661.title: Treatment and Management of Mental Health Conditions During Pregnancy and Postpartum: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 5.
pmid:37486661.finding: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 5 on treating perinatal depression and anxiety, supporting SSRIs as first-line pharmacotherapy and individualized decisions rather than stopping effective treatment.

pmid:26827878.authors: Casilla-Lennon MM, Meltzer-Brody S, Steiner AZ
pmid:26827878.title: The effect of antidepressants on fertility.
pmid:26827878.finding: Cycle-specific antidepressant use was associated with lower fecundability (FR 0.75, CI crossing 1; 0.66 after adjusting for depression history), with confounding by depression unresolved.

pmid:38079178.authors: Cesta CE, Rotem R, Bateman BT, et al.
pmid:38079178.title: Safety of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Other Second-Line Antidiabetics in Early Pregnancy.
pmid:38079178.n: 51,826 infants of mothers with type 2 diabetes (Nordic, US, Israel)
pmid:38079178.finding: First-trimester GLP-1 agonist exposure was not associated with more major congenital malformations than insulin (adjusted RR 0.95, 0.72-1.26).

pmid:41860479.title: The effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists on fertility, contraception, and pregnancy: clinical perspectives.
pmid:41860479.journal: Eur J Contracept Reprod Health Care
pmid:41860479.finding: GLP-1 agonists help obesity-related infertility (notably PCOS); clinicians should counsel on contraceptive reliability, ensure washout before conception and note limited pregnancy-safety data.

pmid:39181497.authors: Drummond RF, Seif KE, Reece EA
pmid:39181497.title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist use in pregnancy: a review.
pmid:39181497.finding: AJOG review: malformation data lack glycemic-control information, so periconceptional safety cannot be concluded; recommends contraception for all patients on GLP-1 agonists.

egg:med-fda-wegovy2021.authors: US Food and Drug Administration; Novo Nordisk
egg:med-fda-wegovy2021.title: WEGOVY (semaglutide) injection, prescribing information (revised 06/2021)
egg:med-fda-wegovy2021.finding: Label section 8.3: discontinue semaglutide at least 2 months before a planned pregnancy because of its long half-life; discontinue when pregnancy is recognized.

egg:med-fda-zepbound2023.authors: US Food and Drug Administration; Eli Lilly
egg:med-fda-zepbound2023.title: ZEPBOUND (tirzepatide) injection, prescribing information (revised 11/2023)
egg:med-fda-zepbound2023.finding: A single 5 mg tirzepatide dose cut ethinyl estradiol Cmax 59% and AUC 20%; users of oral contraceptives should switch to a non-oral method or add a barrier method for 4 weeks after starting and after each dose escalation.

pmid:41701618.authors: Forslund M, Wändell P, Forsberg L, et al.
pmid:41701618.title: GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment in women with polycystic ovary syndrome-a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:41701618.finding: Meta-analysis informing the PCOS guideline: GLP-1 agonists as add-on lowered BMI by 1.38 kg/m2 (low certainty); evidence on reproductive, metabolic and psychological outcomes remains insufficient.

pmid:30062044.title: Return of fertility after discontinuation of contraception: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:30062044.finding: 83.1% of women conceived within 12 months of stopping contraception, with no difference between hormonal methods and IUDs or by duration of pill use.

pmid:31229399.authors: Han Y, Li Y, He B
pmid:31229399.title: GLP-1 receptor agonists versus metformin in PCOS: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:31229399.finding: Versus metformin, GLP-1 agonists improved insulin sensitivity and lowered BMI and waist more in PCOS, with more nausea; evidence moderate to low.

pmid:41852577.authors: Hviid KVR, Banasik K, Mortensen LH, et al.
pmid:41852577.title: Periconceptional GLP-1 receptor agonist exposure and obstetric outcomes: a Danish nationwide cohort study.
pmid:41852577.finding: Periconceptional liraglutide or semaglutide was linked to preterm birth only in women with diabetes (aOR ~1.7-1.8), not in those using them for weight management, pointing to the underlying diabetes.

pmid:27131586.authors: Nillni YI, Wesselink AK, Gradus JL, et al.
pmid:27131586.title: Depression, anxiety, and psychotropic medication use and fecundability.
pmid:27131586.finding: Severe depressive symptoms lowered fecundability (FR 0.62) regardless of treatment; psychotropic medication use itself did not appear to harm fecundability.

pmid:41885132.authors: Ozbek L, Shah E, Al-Shiab R, et al.
pmid:41885132.title: Safety of GLP-1 and Dual GLP-1/GIP Receptor Agonists in Preconception, Pregnancy, and Lactation: A Systematic Review of Maternal, Fetal, and Neonatal Outcomes.
pmid:41885132.finding: Periconceptional or early-pregnancy GLP-1-based therapy was not consistently linked to malformations, growth restriction, stillbirth or neonatal death; data on continued use through pregnancy are limited.

pmid:29703793.authors: Salamun V, Jensterle M, Janez A, et al.
pmid:29703793.title: Liraglutide increases IVF pregnancy rates in obese PCOS women with poor response to first-line reproductive treatments: a pilot randomized study.
pmid:29703793.finding: Pilot open-label trial: 12 weeks of liraglutide 1.2 mg plus metformin before IVF (with a 4-week washout) gave higher pregnancy rate per transfer (85.7% vs 28.6%) than metformin alone despite similar weight loss.

pmid:37940101.authors: Skelley JW, Swearengin K, York AL, et al.
pmid:37940101.title: The impact of tirzepatide and glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists on oral hormonal contraception.
pmid:37940101.finding: Tirzepatide significantly reduced oral-contraceptive exposure (AUC, Cmax) via delayed gastric emptying, whereas studies of other GLP-1 agonists showed no clinically significant effect.

pmid:8646437.authors: Smith G, Roberts R, Hall C, et al.
pmid:8646437.title: Reversible ovulatory failure associated with the development of luteinized unruptured follicles in women with inflammatory arthritis taking non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs.
pmid:8646437.finding: Three women with inflammatory arthritis had recurrent luteinized unruptured follicles on NSAIDs, with normal ovulation after stopping.

pmid:33177047.authors: Yland JJ, Bresnick KA, Hatch EE, et al.
pmid:33177047.title: Pregravid contraceptive use and fecundability: prospective cohort study.
pmid:33177047.finding: Return to normal fertility took about 5-8 cycles after injectables (FR 0.65), 4 after the patch, 3 after pill or ring and 2 after IUDs or implants; total years of hormonal use did not matter.

pmid:38908019.title: The role of endometrial scratching in IVF/ICSI: a critical appraisal of individual participant data meta-analysis
pmid:38908019.finding: Critical letter questioning the methods and conclusions of the endometrial scratching IPD meta-analysis (with author reply).

pmid:31140578.authors: Armstrong S, Bhide P, Jordan V, et al.
pmid:31140578.title: Time-lapse systems for embryo incubation and assessment in assisted reproduction
pmid:31140578.finding: Cochrane: low to very low quality evidence; no clear difference in live birth/ongoing pregnancy with time-lapse systems (OR 0.91, 95% CI 0.67-1.23).

pmid:33280722.authors: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
pmid:33280722.title: Testing and interpreting measures of ovarian reserve: a committee opinion
pmid:33280722.finding: ASRM: ovarian reserve markers (AMH, AFC, FSH) predict egg yield after stimulation but are poor predictors of reproductive potential independent of age.

pmid:34148587.authors: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
pmid:34148587.title: Evidence-based outcomes after oocyte cryopreservation for donor oocyte in vitro fertilization and planned oocyte cryopreservation: a guideline
pmid:34148587.finding: ASRM guideline: insufficient evidence to predict live birth after planned egg freezing; outcomes appear better when frozen younger; neonatal outcomes similar to fresh eggs.

pmid:38430080.authors: Ethics Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
pmid:38430080.title: Planned oocyte cryopreservation to preserve future reproductive potential: an Ethics Committee opinion
pmid:38430080.finding: ASRM Ethics Committee: planned egg freezing is ethically permissible; people must be told about uncertain efficacy and long-term effects.

pmid:38423539.authors: Barrenetxea G, Celis R, Barrenetxea J, et al.
pmid:38423539.title: Intraovarian platelet-rich plasma injection and IVF outcomes in patients with poor ovarian response: a double-blind randomized controlled trial
pmid:38423539.finding: Double-blind RCT: intraovarian PRP slightly raised cumulative mature eggs (10.45 vs 8.91) over three retrievals but not euploid blastocysts (0.81 vs 0.81).

pmid:39033010.authors: Bhide P, Chan DYL, Lanz D, et al.
pmid:39033010.title: Clinical effectiveness and safety of time-lapse imaging systems for embryo incubation and selection in in-vitro fertilisation treatment (TILT): a multicentre, three-parallel-group, double-blind, randomised controlled trial
pmid:39033010.finding: TILT trial: live birth 33.7% with time-lapse imaging, 36.6% with undisturbed culture and 33.0% with standard care (aOR 1.04 and 1.20, both non-significant).

pmid:33712289.authors: Blakemore JK, Grifo JA, DeVore SM, et al.
pmid:33712289.title: Planned oocyte cryopreservation-10-15-year follow-up: return rates and cycle outcomes
pmid:33712289.finding: 10-15-year follow-up of planned egg freezing (mean age 38.2): 38.1% returned; live birth 33.8% among those with outcomes; 58.9% non-use.

pmid:35771604.authors: Boomsma CM, Kamath MS, Keay SD, et al.
pmid:35771604.title: Peri-implantation glucocorticoid administration for assisted reproductive technology cycles
pmid:35771604.finding: Cochrane: uncertain whether peri-implantation glucocorticoids improve live birth (OR 1.37, 95% CI 0.69-2.71; very low certainty).

pmid:20667894.authors: Broer SL, Dólleman M, Opmeer BC, et al.
pmid:20667894.title: AMH and AFC as predictors of excessive response in controlled ovarian hyperstimulation: a meta-analysis
pmid:20667894.finding: AMH and AFC both predict excessive ovarian response (sensitivity ~82%, specificity 76-80%).

pmid:23188168.authors: Broer SL, van Disseldorp J, Broeze KA, et al.
pmid:23188168.title: Added value of ovarian reserve testing on patient characteristics in the prediction of ovarian response and ongoing pregnancy: an individual patient data approach
pmid:23188168.finding: AMH and AFC predict poor ovarian response well (AUC 0.78 and 0.76) but add nothing to age for predicting ongoing pregnancy after IVF.

pmid:21130690.title: Oxidative stress
pmid:21130690.journal: Best Pract Res Clin Obstet Gynaecol
pmid:21130690.finding: Review of reactive oxygen species in the placenta: physiological signalling at low levels, and involvement in miscarriage, pre-eclampsia and membrane rupture at high levels.

pmid:31307997.authors: Burton GJ, Redman CW, Roberts JM, et al.
pmid:31307997.title: Pre-eclampsia: pathophysiology and clinical implications
pmid:31307997.finding: BMJ review: pre-eclampsia arises from syncytiotrophoblast stress; early-onset from defective placentation, late-onset from placental senescence plus maternal cardiometabolic predisposition.

pmid:34798051.authors: Capalbo A, Poli M, Rienzi L, et al.
pmid:34798051.title: Mosaic human preimplantation embryos and their developmental potential in a prospective, non-selection clinical trial
pmid:34798051.finding: Non-selection trial (Igenomix authors): low- and medium-grade mosaic embryos had live birth and miscarriage rates equivalent to euploid embryos, implying PGT-A labels can discard viable embryos.

pmid:26688429.authors: Cobo A, García-Velasco JA, Coello A, et al.
pmid:26688429.title: Oocyte vitrification as an efficient option for elective fertility preservation
pmid:26688429.finding: Elective egg freezing: cumulative live birth with 10-15 vitrified eggs reached ~85% at <=35 years vs ~36% plateau at >=36; 8-10 mature eggs needed for reasonable success; 9.3% had returned.

pmid:27031375.title: Why all women should freeze their eggs
pmid:27031375.finding: IVI review arguing for elective egg freezing: success is best when frozen before 35, but studies show freezing is most cost-effective at 37-38.

pmid:21529757.authors: Conde-Agudelo A, Romero R, Kusanovic JP, et al.
pmid:21529757.title: Supplementation with vitamins C and E during pregnancy for the prevention of preeclampsia and other adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes: a systematic review and metaanalysis
pmid:21529757.finding: Vitamins C and E did not prevent pre-eclampsia (9.6% vs 9.6%) and increased gestational hypertension and premature rupture of membranes.

pmid:32898291.authors: Cornelisse S, Zagers M, Kostova E, et al.
pmid:32898291.title: Preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidies (abnormal number of chromosomes) in in vitro fertilisation
pmid:32898291.finding: Cochrane: uncertain whether PGT-A increases cumulative live birth; low to moderate quality evidence; possible reduction in miscarriage.

pmid:30341915.authors: Craciunas L, Tsampras N, Raine-Fenning N, et al.
pmid:30341915.title: Intrauterine administration of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) for subfertile women undergoing assisted reproduction
pmid:30341915.finding: Cochrane: intrauterine hCG >=500 IU improved live birth only with cleavage-stage transfer (moderate quality); insufficient evidence for blastocyst transfer; no reduction in miscarriage.

pmid:26372034.authors: Depmann M, Broer SL, van der Schouw YT, et al.
pmid:26372034.title: Can we predict age at natural menopause using ovarian reserve tests or mother's age at menopause? A systematic literature review
pmid:26372034.finding: AMH is the most promising predictor of age at natural menopause but prediction intervals are too wide for individual use.

pmid:26604065.authors: Doyle JO, Richter KS, Lim J, et al.
pmid:26604065.title: Successful elective and medically indicated oocyte vitrification and warming for autologous in vitro fertilization, with predicted birth probabilities for fertility preservation according to number of cryopreserved oocytes and age at retrieval
pmid:26604065.finding: Vitrified eggs performed as well as fresh; overall vitrified egg-to-baby efficiency was 6.4% per egg, falling with age at retrieval.

pmid:36472596.authors: Doyle N, Jahandideh S, Hill MJ, et al.
pmid:36472596.title: Effect of Timing by Endometrial Receptivity Testing vs Standard Timing of Frozen Embryo Transfer on Live Birth in Patients Undergoing In Vitro Fertilization: A Randomized Clinical Trial
pmid:36472596.finding: Euploid frozen transfers timed by endometrial receptivity testing did not improve live birth (58.5% vs 61.9%; RR 0.95, 95% CI 0.79-1.13).

pmid:31684684.authors: Duley L, Meher S, Hunter KE, et al.
pmid:31684684.title: Antiplatelet agents for preventing pre-eclampsia and its complications
pmid:31684684.finding: Cochrane: antiplatelet agents cut proteinuric pre-eclampsia by 18% (RR 0.82; NNT 61), preterm birth by 9% and fetal/neonatal death by 14%; may slightly increase postpartum haemorrhage.

pmid:33225079.authors: ESHRE Guideline Group on Female Fertility Preservation
pmid:33225079.title: ESHRE guideline: female fertility preservation
pmid:33225079.finding: ESHRE female fertility preservation guideline covering medical and age-related egg freezing; 78 recommendations, mostly low or very low quality evidence.

pmid:37332387.authors: ESHRE Working Group on Recurrent Implantation Failure; Cimadomo D, de Los Santos MJ, Griesinger G, et al.
pmid:37332387.title: ESHRE good practice recommendations on recurrent implantation failure
pmid:37332387.finding: ESHRE recurrent implantation failure recommendations: RIF defined by a >60% predicted cumulative implantation chance; investigations and interventions graded recommended, to consider, or not recommended.

pmid:31965189.authors: Finkelstein JS, Lee H, Karlamangla A, et al.
pmid:31965189.title: Antimullerian Hormone and Impending Menopause in Late Reproductive Age: The Study of Women's Health Across the Nation
pmid:31965189.n: SWAN women in late reproductive age
pmid:31965189.finding: In women in their late 40s, very low AMH (<10 pg/mL) predicted the final period within 12 months (51-79% by age); AMH outperformed FSH.

pmid:32299733.authors: Gardner DK, Kuramoto T, Tanaka M, et al.
pmid:32299733.title: Prospective randomized multicentre comparison on sibling oocytes comparing G-Series media system with antioxidants versus standard G-Series media system
pmid:32299733.finding: Antioxidants (acetyl-L-carnitine, NAC, alpha-lipoic acid) in culture media raised good day-3 embryos (50.2% vs 40.7%) and, in women 35-40, ongoing pregnancy (50% vs 25.8%); no live-birth primary outcome.

pmid:28166330.authors: Goldman RH, Racowsky C, Farland LV, et al.
pmid:28166330.title: Predicting the likelihood of live birth for elective oocyte cryopreservation: a counseling tool for physicians and patients
pmid:28166330.finding: Counselling model predicting chance of 1-3 live births from age at retrieval and number of mature eggs frozen; derived from fresh ICSI data, not returning egg-freezers.

pmid:19076941.title: In favour of freezing eggs for non-medical reasons
pmid:19076941.finding: Bioethics argument in favour of egg freezing for non-medical reasons (autonomy, equality in work, time to find a partner).
