pmid:6511559.title: Time course of loss of adaptations after stopping prolonged intense endurance training
pmid:6511559.journal: J Appl Physiol Respir Environ Exerc Physiol
pmid:6511559.finding: After stopping long-term endurance training, VO2max fell 7% in 21 days and stabilised 16% below trained values by 56 days; muscle oxidative enzymes fell with a half-time of ~12 days but stayed 50% above sedentary levels and capillaries did not regress over 84 days.

pmid:10966148.title: Detraining: loss of training-induced physiological and performance adaptations. Part I: short term insufficient training stimulus
pmid:10966148.finding: Review of short-term detraining (<4 weeks): VO2max and blood volume fall quickly in athletes, insulin sensitivity, GLUT4 and oxidative enzymes decline, while strength declines are limited.

pmid:10999420.title: Detraining: loss of training-induced physiological and performance adaptations. Part II: Long term insufficient training stimulus
pmid:10999420.finding: Review of long-term detraining (>4 weeks): recently acquired VO2max gains are completely lost, whereas long-trained athletes stay above untrained values; reduced training that keeps intensity can prevent most losses.

pmid:7219129.title: Reduced training frequencies and maintenance of increased aerobic power
pmid:7219129.finding: After 10 weeks of 6 days/week training raised VO2max 20-25%, cutting to 2 or 4 days/week at the same intensity maintained VO2max for a further 15 weeks.

pmid:3156841.authors: Hickson RC, Foster C, Pollock ML, et al.
pmid:3156841.title: Reduced training intensities and loss of aerobic power, endurance, and cardiac growth
pmid:3156841.finding: Cutting training intensity by one-third or two-thirds (frequency and duration unchanged) did not maintain VO2max or long endurance over 15 weeks; intensity is key to maintenance.

pmid:33629972.authors: Spiering BA, Mujika I, Sharp MA, et al.
pmid:33629972.title: Maintaining Physical Performance: The Minimal Dose of Exercise Needed to Preserve Endurance and Strength Over Time
pmid:33629972.finding: Endurance can be maintained up to 15 weeks with as few as 2 sessions/week or 33-66% less volume if intensity is kept; strength and muscle size up to 32 weeks with 1 session/week and 1 set per exercise (younger adults).

pmid:18171435.title: Exercise training-induced improvements in insulin action
pmid:18171435.finding: A single exercise bout increases muscle glucose uptake and insulin sensitivity, but the effect is short-lived and disappears after about 48 h; repeated training produces a persistent increase.

pmid:3126668.authors: Mikines KJ, Sonne B, Farrell PA, et al.
pmid:3126668.title: Effect of physical exercise on sensitivity and responsiveness to insulin in humans
pmid:3126668.finding: One hour of cycling raised insulin-mediated glucose uptake immediately and still 48 h later in untrained men, with glycogen synthase activity elevated for 48 h.

pmid:2496077.authors: Mikines KJ, Sonne B, Tronier B, et al.
pmid:2496077.title: Effects of acute exercise and detraining on insulin action in trained men
pmid:2496077.finding: In endurance-trained men, insulin sensitivity measured 15 h after the last session fell to untrained levels after 5 days without training.

pmid:6352578.authors: Heath GW, Gavin JR 3rd, Hinderliter JM, et al.
pmid:6352578.title: Effects of exercise and lack of exercise on glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity
pmid:6352578.journal: J Appl Physiol Respir Environ Exerc Physiol
pmid:6352578.finding: Ten days without exercise doubled the insulin response to a glucose load in trained people with no change in VO2max or body fat; one bout of exercise largely restored it.

pmid:16032415.authors: Goulet ED, Mélançon MO, Aubertin-Leheudre M, et al.
pmid:16032415.title: Aerobic training improves insulin sensitivity 72-120 h after the last exercise session in younger but not in older women
pmid:16032415.finding: Six months of training improved insulin sensitivity measured 72-120 h after the last session in younger women but not in older women, whose benefit appeared to depend on the most recent bout.

pmid:17635103.authors: Magkos F, Tsekouras Y, Kavouras SA, et al.
pmid:17635103.title: Improved insulin sensitivity after a single bout of exercise is curvilinearly related to exercise energy expenditure
pmid:17635103.finding: A single moderate exercise bout improved next-morning insulin sensitivity (HOMA-IR down ~32%) only when it expended more than about 900 kcal; single-bout effects last 12-48 h.

pmid:24069271.authors: Egan B, O'Connor PL, Zierath JR, et al.
pmid:24069271.title: Time course analysis reveals gene-specific transcript and protein kinetics of adaptation to short-term aerobic exercise training in human skeletal muscle
pmid:24069271.finding: Fourteen consecutive daily 60-min sessions raised VO2peak 17.5%; mitochondrial markers rose within the first week, while some gene transcripts rose only transiently after the first session.

pmid:20921196.authors: Perry CG, Lally J, Holloway GP, et al.
pmid:20921196.title: Repeated transient mRNA bursts precede increases in transcriptional and mitochondrial proteins during training in human skeletal muscle
pmid:20921196.finding: During 7 interval sessions, PGC-1alpha mRNA spiked >10-fold 4 h after each bout and returned to baseline within 24 h (saw-tooth), while PGC-1alpha protein rose after one session and plateaued at +30-40% by session 3-7; VO2peak rose 12%.

pmid:20056848.authors: Murias JM, Kowalchuk JM, Paterson DH
pmid:20056848.title: Time course and mechanisms of adaptations in cardiorespiratory fitness with endurance training in older and young men
pmid:20056848.finding: VO2max rose within 3 weeks of training 3x/week and kept rising to +31% (older) and +18% (young) at 12 weeks; early gains came from muscle oxygen extraction, later ones from cardiac output.

pmid:17596778.authors: Michailidis Y, Jamurtas AZ, Nikolaidis MG, et al.
pmid:17596778.title: Sampling time is crucial for measurement of aerobic exercise-induced oxidative stress
pmid:17596778.finding: After strenuous treadmill exercise, blood oxidative markers peaked at different times (TBARS ~1.2 h, protein carbonyls ~4.4 h, GSH/GSSG nadir ~1.7 h) and returned toward baseline within 24 h.

pmid:11034627.authors: Tonkonogi M, Walsh B, Svensson M, et al.
pmid:11034627.title: Mitochondrial function and antioxidative defence in human muscle: effects of endurance training and oxidative stress
pmid:11034627.finding: Six weeks of endurance training raised VO2peak 24% and maximal mitochondrial respiration 40% in human muscle.

pmid:7707596.authors: Blair SN, Kohl HW 3rd, Barlow CE, et al.
pmid:7707596.title: Changes in physical fitness and all-cause mortality. A prospective study of healthy and unhealthy men
pmid:7707596.finding: Men who went from unfit to fit between two exams ~5 years apart had 44% lower mortality than men who stayed unfit.

pmid:22144631.authors: Lee DC, Sui X, Artero EG, et al.
pmid:22144631.title: Long-term effects of changes in cardiorespiratory fitness and body mass index on all-cause and cardiovascular disease mortality in men: the Aerobics Center Longitudinal Study
pmid:22144631.finding: Over ~6 years, men who kept or gained fitness had 30% and 39% lower mortality than those who lost fitness; each 1-MET gain was associated with 15% lower all-cause mortality.

pmid:27444976.authors: Laukkanen JA, Zaccardi F, Khan H, et al.
pmid:27444976.title: Long-term Change in Cardiorespiratory Fitness and All-Cause Mortality: A Population-Based Follow-up Study
pmid:27444976.finding: Over 11 years, each 1 mL/kg/min smaller decline in measured VO2max was associated with 9% lower subsequent mortality.

pmid:30848809.authors: Saint-Maurice PF, Coughlan D, Kelly SP, et al.
pmid:30848809.title: Association of Leisure-Time Physical Activity Across the Adult Life Course With All-Cause and Cause-Specific Mortality
pmid:30848809.finding: Adults who were inactive earlier but increased activity at ages 40-61 had mortality as low as those active throughout adulthood (HR 0.65 vs 0.64).

pmid:25901000.authors: Huang G, Wang R, Chen P, et al.
pmid:25901000.title: Dose-response relationship of cardiorespiratory fitness adaptation to controlled endurance training in sedentary older adults
pmid:25901000.finding: In sedentary older adults, aerobic training raised VO2max by 3.8 mL/kg/min on average; gains were largest at 66-73% of heart-rate reserve.

pmid:453338.title: Neural factors versus hypertrophy in the time course of muscle strength gain
pmid:453338.finding: In the first 3-5 weeks of strength training, gains came mainly from neural adaptation; hypertrophy became the dominant contributor after that.

pmid:9252485.authors: Phillips SM, Tipton KD, Aarsland A, et al.
pmid:9252485.title: Mixed muscle protein synthesis and breakdown after resistance exercise in humans
pmid:9252485.finding: Muscle protein synthesis stayed raised 112%, 65% and 34% at 3, 24 and 48 h after one bout of resistance exercise.

pmid:27219125.authors: Damas F, Phillips SM, Libardi CA, et al.
pmid:27219125.title: Resistance training-induced changes in integrated myofibrillar protein synthesis are related to hypertrophy only after attenuation of muscle damage
pmid:27219125.finding: Early in resistance training, protein synthesis mostly repaired damage; it tracked hypertrophy only from about week 3 onward as damage subsided.

pmid:21131862.authors: Bickel CS, Cross JM, Bamman MM
pmid:21131862.title: Exercise dosing to retain resistance training adaptations in young and older adults
pmid:21131862.finding: After 16 weeks of training 3x/week, one-third or one-ninth of the dose for 32 weeks preserved hypertrophy in young but not older adults; strength was largely retained.

pmid:30991013.authors: Psilander N, Eftestøl E, Cumming KT, et al.
pmid:30991013.title: Effects of training, detraining, and retraining on strength, hypertrophy, and myonuclear number in human skeletal muscle
pmid:30991013.finding: After 10 weeks of one-leg training and 20 weeks off, muscle size returned to baseline but ~60% of the strength gain remained; the previously trained leg did not regrow faster.

pmid:39159314.authors: Cumming KT, Reitzner SM, Hanslien M, et al.
pmid:39159314.title: Muscle memory in humans: evidence for myonuclear permanence and long-term transcriptional regulation after strength training
pmid:39159314.finding: After 10 weeks of arm training and 16 weeks off, fibre size fell but extra myonuclei persisted, and retraining gave larger type 2 fibres than in the untrained arm.

pmid:29382913.authors: Seaborne RA, Strauss J, Cocks M, et al.
pmid:29382913.title: Human Skeletal Muscle Possesses an Epigenetic Memory of Hypertrophy
pmid:29382913.finding: DNA methylation changes from an earlier hypertrophy phase persisted through 7 weeks of unloading and were associated with greater growth on reloading.

pmid:41701327.authors: Gonzalez DE, Dickerson BL, Roberts BM, et al.
pmid:41701327.title: International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: effects of dietary antioxidants on exercise and sports performance
pmid:41701327.finding: ISSN position stand: supraphysiological antioxidant doses can hinder training adaptations, whole-food antioxidants are preferred, and effects depend on timing, dose and type.

pmid:31513450.authors: Fyfe JJ, Broatch JR, Trewin AJ, et al.
pmid:31513450.title: Cold water immersion attenuates anabolic signaling and skeletal muscle fiber hypertrophy, but not strength gain, following whole-body resistance training
pmid:31513450.finding: 15 min at 10 C after each session for 7 weeks attenuated type II fibre hypertrophy and post-exercise mTORC1 signalling, but not strength gains.

pmid:33146851.authors: Malta ES, Dutra YM, Broatch JR, et al.
pmid:33146851.title: The Effects of Regular Cold-Water Immersion Use on Training-Induced Changes in Strength and Endurance Performance: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis
pmid:33146851.finding: Regular post-exercise cold-water immersion impaired strength-training gains (SMD about -0.6) but did not impair endurance-training gains.

pmid:34337408.authors: Ihsan M, Abbiss CR, Allan R
pmid:34337408.title: Adaptations to Post-exercise Cold Water Immersion: Friend, Foe, or Futile?
pmid:34337408.finding: Review: post-exercise cold-water immersion diminishes resistance-training adaptations, while aerobic adaptations appear unaffected and may even be enhanced.

pmid:42816732.authors: Berjisian E, Miraftabi H, Ihsan M, et al.
pmid:42816732.title: Strategic Application of Post-exercise Cold-Water Immersion to Enhance Performance Recovery and Adaptation: An Umbrella Review of 15 Published Systematic Reviews with Meta-analysis
pmid:42816732.finding: Umbrella review: post-exercise cold-water immersion helps short-term recovery of power and jump at 24-48 h, but certainty is low to very low and adaptation effects are mode-dependent.

pmid:26147760.authors: Hanssen MJ, Hoeks J, Brans B, et al.
pmid:26147760.title: Short-term cold acclimation improves insulin sensitivity in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus
pmid:26147760.finding: Ten days of mild cold acclimation (14-15 C) increased peripheral insulin sensitivity by ~43%.

pmid:20044474.authors: Krogh-Madsen R, Thyfault JP, Broholm C, et al.
pmid:20044474.title: A 2-wk reduction of ambulatory activity attenuates peripheral insulin sensitivity
pmid:20044474.finding: Cutting steps from ~10,500 to ~1,350/day for 2 weeks lowered peripheral insulin sensitivity 17% and VO2max 7%.

pmid:29095970.authors: McGlory C, von Allmen MT, Stokes T, et al.
pmid:29095970.title: Failed Recovery of Glycemic Control and Myofibrillar Protein Synthesis With 2 wk of Physical Inactivity in Overweight, Prediabetic Older Adults
pmid:29095970.journal: J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci
pmid:29095970.finding: In prediabetic older adults, 2 weeks of <1,000 steps/day worsened glycaemic control and muscle protein synthesis, which had not recovered after 2 weeks of normal activity.

pmid:22028408.authors: Vendelbo MH, Clasen BF, Treebak JT, et al.
pmid:22028408.title: Insulin resistance after a 72-h fast is associated with impaired AS160 phosphorylation and accumulation of lipid and glycogen in human skeletal muscle
pmid:22028408.finding: A 72-h fast profoundly reduced muscle insulin sensitivity compared with an overnight fast.

pmid:28275127.authors: Marlatt KL, Redman LM, Burton JH, et al.
pmid:28275127.title: Persistence of weight loss and acquired behaviors 2 y after stopping a 2-y calorie restriction intervention
pmid:28275127.finding: Two years after the 2-year CALERIE restriction ended, participants had regained 54% of the 9 kg lost, but weight and fat stayed below baseline and controls.

pmid:11684524.authors: Anderson JW, Konz EC, Frederich RC, et al.
pmid:11684524.title: Long-term weight-loss maintenance: a meta-analysis of US studies
pmid:11684524.finding: Five years after structured weight-loss programmes, people maintained on average only 17-29% of the weight they had lost.

pmid:18299315.authors: Ceriello A, Esposito K, Piconi L, et al.
pmid:18299315.title: Oscillating glucose is more deleterious to endothelial function and oxidative stress than mean glucose in normal and type 2 diabetic patients
pmid:18299315.finding: Glucose oscillating between 5 and 15 mmol/L over 24 h worsened endothelial function and oxidative stress more than constant high glucose.

pmid:7497851.title: Kinetics of HbA1c, glycated albumin, and fructosamine and analysis of their weight functions against preceding plasma glucose level
pmid:7497851.finding: After glucose was normalised, fasting glucose fell with a half-time of ~6 days, fructosamine ~12 days, glycated albumin ~17 days and HbA1c ~35 days.

pmid:18784090.authors: Holman RR, Paul SK, Bethel MA, et al.
pmid:18784090.title: 10-year follow-up of intensive glucose control in type 2 diabetes
pmid:18784090.finding: UKPDS: HbA1c differences vanished within a year after the trial, but lower microvascular risk persisted and lower MI and death emerged over 10 years (legacy effect), including with metformin.

pmid:38772405.authors: Adler AI, Coleman RL, Leal J, et al.
pmid:38772405.title: Post-trial monitoring of a randomised controlled trial of intensive glycaemic control in type 2 diabetes extended from 10 years to 24 years (UKPDS 91)
pmid:38772405.finding: UKPDS 91: legacy benefits of early intensive glucose control and of metformin showed no sign of waning up to 24 years after the trial ended.

pmid:16371630.authors: Nathan DM, Cleary PA, Backlund JY, et al.
pmid:16371630.title: Intensive diabetes treatment and cardiovascular disease in patients with type 1 diabetes
pmid:16371630.finding: DCCT/EDIC: 6.5 years of intensive therapy reduced cardiovascular events by 42% over 17 years of follow-up, long after HbA1c differences had narrowed.

pmid:10102706.authors: Monnier VM, Bautista O, Kenny D, et al.
pmid:10102706.title: Skin collagen glycation, glycoxidation, and crosslinking are lower in subjects with long-term intensive versus conventional therapy of type 1 diabetes: relevance of glycated collagen products versus HbA1c as markers of diabetic complications. DCCT Skin Collagen Ancillary Study Group. Diabetes Control and Complications Trial
pmid:10102706.finding: After ~5 years of intensive versus conventional therapy, skin collagen glycation was 30-32% lower and glycoxidation products 9-13% lower.

pmid:10976109.authors: Verzijl N, DeGroot J, Thorpe SR, et al.
pmid:10976109.title: Effect of collagen turnover on the accumulation of advanced glycation end products
pmid:10976109.finding: AGEs accumulate in proportion to collagen residence time; long-lived collagen (cartilage, skin) accumulates AGEs over years.

pmid:29976596.authors: Ludvigsson JF, Neovius M, Söderling J, et al.
pmid:29976596.title: Periconception glycaemic control in women with type 1 diabetes and risk of major birth defects: population based cohort study in Sweden
pmid:29976596.n: 2,458 infants of mothers with type 1 diabetes
pmid:29976596.finding: Higher HbA1c within 3 months around conception was associated with higher major birth-defect risk in a graded way.

pmid:21241070.authors: Graham GG, Punt J, Arora M, et al.
pmid:21241070.title: Clinical pharmacokinetics of metformin
pmid:21241070.finding: Metformin has ~55% oral bioavailability and an elimination half-life of about 5 h with good kidney function.

pmid:11523724.title: Clinical pharmacokinetics of sirolimus
pmid:11523724.finding: Sirolimus (rapamycin) has a long elimination half-life (allowing once-daily dosing) and reaches steady-state trough levels after at least 4 days.

pmid:26463117.authors: Arriola Apelo SI, Neuman JC, Baar EL, et al.
pmid:26463117.title: Alternative rapamycin treatment regimens mitigate the impact of rapamycin on glucose homeostasis and the immune system
pmid:26463117.finding: In mice, an intermittent rapamycin schedule had minimal effects on glucose tolerance and the immune system compared with daily dosing.

pmid:29408453.authors: Kraig E, Linehan LA, Liang H, et al.
pmid:29408453.title: A randomized control trial to establish the feasibility and safety of rapamycin treatment in an older human cohort: Immunological, physical performance, and cognitive effects
pmid:29408453.finding: 1 mg/day rapamycin for 8 weeks was tolerated but lowered some red-cell indices, with no change in cognition or physical performance.

pmid:14975482.authors: Meier-Ewert HK, Ridker PM, Rifai N, et al.
pmid:14975482.title: Effect of sleep loss on C-reactive protein, an inflammatory marker of cardiovascular risk
pmid:14975482.finding: Both 88 h of total sleep deprivation and 10 nights of 4.2 h sleep raised high-sensitivity CRP.

pmid:10543671.authors: Spiegel K, Leproult R, Van Cauter E
pmid:10543671.title: Impact of sleep debt on metabolic and endocrine function
pmid:10543671.finding: Six nights of 4 h in bed lowered glucose tolerance and raised evening cortisol and sympathetic activity, which normalised after 6 nights of recovery sleep.

pmid:23941878.authors: Pejovic S, Basta M, Vgontzas AN, et al.
pmid:23941878.title: Effects of recovery sleep after one work week of mild sleep restriction on interleukin-6 and cortisol secretion and daytime sleepiness and performance
pmid:23941878.finding: After 6 nights of 6 h sleep, IL-6 rose and returned to baseline after 2 recovery nights of 10 h, but attention performance did not recover.

pmid:30827911.authors: Depner CM, Melanson EL, Eckel RH, et al.
pmid:30827911.title: Ad libitum Weekend Recovery Sleep Fails to Prevent Metabolic Dysregulation during a Repeating Pattern of Insufficient Sleep and Weekend Recovery Sleep
pmid:30827911.finding: Weekend catch-up sleep did not prevent loss of insulin sensitivity (down 9-27%) and weight gain during recurrent weekday sleep restriction.

pmid:21632481.title: Effect of 1 week of sleep restriction on testosterone levels in young healthy men
pmid:21632481.finding: One week of 5 h sleep per night lowered daytime testosterone by roughly 10-15% (research letter).

pmid:21836134.authors: Kohler M, Stoewhas AC, Ayers L, et al.
pmid:21836134.title: Effects of continuous positive airway pressure therapy withdrawal in patients with obstructive sleep apnea: a randomized controlled trial
pmid:21836134.journal: Am J Respir Crit Care Med
pmid:21836134.finding: Stopping CPAP brought sleep apnoea back within a few days and within 2 weeks raised morning blood pressure (+8.5/6.9 mmHg) and impaired endothelial function, without raising inflammation markers.

pmid:19074930.authors: Alonso-Fernández A, García-Río F, Arias MA, et al.
pmid:19074930.title: Effects of CPAP on oxidative stress and nitrate efficiency in sleep apnoea: a randomised trial
pmid:19074930.finding: Twelve weeks of effective versus sham CPAP lowered plasma 8-isoprostane (38.5 to 22.5 pg/mL) and raised nitrate/nitrite.

pmid:26997243.authors: Paz Y Mar HL, Hazen SL, Tracy RP, et al.
pmid:26997243.title: Effect of Continuous Positive Airway Pressure on Cardiovascular Biomarkers: The Sleep Apnea Stress Randomized Controlled Trial
pmid:26997243.finding: Two months of CPAP versus sham did not change F2-isoprostanes, myeloperoxidase or other oxidative markers.

pmid:26022961.authors: Stradling JR, Schwarz EI, Schlatzer C, et al.
pmid:26022961.title: Biomarkers of oxidative stress following continuous positive airway pressure withdrawal: data from two randomised trials
pmid:26022961.finding: Two weeks of CPAP withdrawal brought back severe OSA but did not raise blood oxidative-stress markers; urinary F2-isoprostanes actually fell.

pmid:15890736.authors: Eskiocak S, Gozen AS, Yapar SB, et al.
pmid:15890736.title: Glutathione and free sulphydryl content of seminal plasma in healthy medical students during and after exam stress
pmid:15890736.finding: During exam stress, seminal glutathione and sperm motility were lower and abnormal forms higher than 3 months after the exams.

pmid:26477499.authors: Nordkap L, Jensen TK, Hansen ÅM, et al.
pmid:26477499.title: Psychological stress and testicular function: a cross-sectional study of 1,215 Danish men
pmid:26477499.finding: Men with the highest self-rated stress had 38% lower sperm concentration than men with intermediate stress.

pmid:26799456.title: Mindfulness meditation and the immune system: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials
pmid:26799456.finding: Mindfulness meditation may affect some inflammation and immune-ageing markers, but results are tentative and heterogeneous.

pmid:27021514.authors: Creswell JD, Taren AA, Lindsay EK, et al.
pmid:27021514.title: Alterations in Resting-State Functional Connectivity Link Mindfulness Meditation With Reduced Interleukin-6: A Randomized Controlled Trial
pmid:27021514.finding: A 3-day intensive mindfulness retreat (versus relaxation training) was followed by lower IL-6 at 4-month follow-up, mediated by brain connectivity changes.

pmid:28627195.authors: Rosety MÁ, Díaz AJ, Rosety JM, et al.
pmid:28627195.title: Exercise improved semen quality and reproductive hormone levels in sedentary obese adults
pmid:28627195.finding: A 16-week treadmill programme (3 sessions/week) improved sperm count, motility and morphology and testosterone versus controls.

pmid:34164675.authors: De Souza MJ, Mallinson RJ, Strock NCA, et al.
pmid:34164675.title: Randomised controlled trial of the effects of increased energy intake on menstrual recovery in exercising women with menstrual disturbances: the 'REFUEL' study
pmid:34164675.finding: REFUEL: eating ~330 kcal/day more for up to 12 months made menstrual recovery more likely (HR 1.91) in women with exercise-related oligo/amenorrhoea; of those who recovered, 67% did so in the first 3 months and 78% within 6 months (full text).

pmid:21849026.authors: Håkonsen LB, Thulstrup AM, Aggerholm AS, et al.
pmid:21849026.title: Does weight loss improve semen quality and reproductive hormones? Results from a cohort of severely obese men
pmid:21849026.finding: A 14-week residential weight-loss programme (median 15% weight loss) was followed by higher total sperm count, semen volume and testosterone, most in men who lost the most weight.

pmid:29020262.authors: Whitcomb BW, Purdue-Smithe AC, Szegda KL, et al.
pmid:29020262.title: Cigarette Smoking and Risk of Early Natural Menopause
pmid:29020262.finding: Current smokers had higher risk of early menopause (HR 1.90), former smokers slightly higher (HR 1.10); light smokers who quit by 25 matched never-smokers.

pmid:21397293.authors: Benedict MD, Missmer SA, Vitonis AF, et al.
pmid:21397293.title: Cotinine concentrations in follicular fluid as a measure of secondhand tobacco smoke exposure in women undergoing in vitro fertilization: inter-matrix comparisons with urine and temporal variability
pmid:21397293.finding: Cotinine is measurable in follicular fluid of IVF patients and reflects tobacco smoke exposure reaching the follicle.

pmid:12568842.authors: Klonoff-Cohen H, Lam-Kruglick P, Gonzalez C
pmid:12568842.title: Effects of maternal and paternal alcohol consumption on the success rates of in vitro fertilization and gamete intrafallopian transfer
pmid:12568842.finding: Female drinking was linked to fewer eggs (per drink/day in the year before), higher risk of no pregnancy (month before) and miscarriage (week before) in IVF/GIFT.

pmid:26920258.authors: Cesta CE, Viktorin A, Olsson H, et al.
pmid:26920258.title: Depression, anxiety, and antidepressant treatment in women: association with in vitro fertilization outcome
pmid:26920258.finding: SSRI-only prescriptions before a first IVF cycle were not associated with pregnancy or live birth; untreated depression/anxiety and non-SSRI antidepressants were.

pmid:24941178.authors: Huybrechts KF, Palmsten K, Avorn J, et al.
pmid:24941178.title: Antidepressant use in pregnancy and the risk of cardiac defects
pmid:24941178.finding: First-trimester antidepressant use was not associated with cardiac defects after adjustment for depression and confounders (SSRI RR 1.06).

pmid:16449615.authors: Cohen LS, Altshuler LL, Harlow BL, et al.
pmid:16449615.title: Relapse of major depression during pregnancy in women who maintain or discontinue antidepressant treatment
pmid:16449615.finding: Relapse of major depression in pregnancy: 68% after discontinuing antidepressants near conception vs 26% when maintained.

pmid:23117129.authors: Domar AD, Moragianni VA, Ryley DA, et al.
pmid:23117129.title: The risks of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor use in infertile women: a review of the impact on fertility, pregnancy, neonatal health and beyond
pmid:23117129.finding: Argues SSRI use in infertile women carries pregnancy risks without proven benefit and favours psychotherapy and exercise first.

pmid:9068931.title: Clinically relevant pharmacology of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors. An overview with emphasis on pharmacokinetics and effects on oxidative drug metabolism
pmid:9068931.finding: Most SSRIs have half-lives of about 1 day; fluoxetine 2-4 days and its metabolite norfluoxetine 7-15 days.

pmid:11278209.authors: Meirow D, Epstein M, Lewis H, et al.
pmid:11278209.title: Administration of cyclophosphamide at different stages of follicular maturation in mice: effects on reproductive performance and fetal malformations
pmid:11278209.finding: After cyclophosphamide, conceptions from follicles exposed at mature stages failed more often and malformations were >10-fold higher; malformation rates fell toward normal by 12 weeks after exposure.

pmid:42497321.authors: Balachandren N, Kastora SL, Anderson RA, et al.
pmid:42497321.title: Assessing the reproductive lifespan of female cancer survivors using AMH: a meta-synthesis of longitudinal studies
pmid:42497321.finding: AMH fell 76% at 12 months after breast-cancer chemotherapy and recovered partly between 6 and 12-24 months; survivors who kept ovarian function then tracked age-matched controls.

pmid:35038360.authors: Mailliez A, Pigny P, Bogart E, et al.
pmid:35038360.title: Is ovarian recovery after chemotherapy in young patients with early breast cancer influenced by controlled ovarian hyperstimulation for fertility preservation or tumor characteristics? Results of a prospective study in 126 patients
pmid:35038360.finding: After breast-cancer chemotherapy, 94% had amenorrhoea and 33% still had undetectable AMH 12 months after treatment, though most resumed menses.

pmid:30403424.authors: Hartnett KP, Mertens AC, Kramer MR, et al.
pmid:30403424.title: Pregnancy after cancer: Does timing of conception affect infant health?
pmid:30403424.finding: Conceiving within 1 year of starting chemotherapy was linked to more preterm birth (RR 1.9; 2.4 with radiation); conceiving later was not.

pmid:20655585.authors: Signorello LB, Mulvihill JJ, Green DM, et al.
pmid:20655585.title: Stillbirth and neonatal death in relation to radiation exposure before conception: a retrospective cohort study
pmid:20655585.finding: Uterine/ovarian radiation >10 Gy (or >=1 Gy before menarche) raised stillbirth and neonatal death; alkylating chemotherapy did not.

pmid:10782364.title: Initial and cyclic recruitment of ovarian follicles
pmid:10782364.finding: Defines initial recruitment (resting primordial follicles start growing, continuously and gonadotropin-independent) and cyclic recruitment (FSH rescues a cohort of antral follicles each cycle).

pmid:22068695.authors: Baerwald AR, Adams GP, Pierson RA
pmid:22068695.title: Ovarian antral folliculogenesis during the human menstrual cycle: a review
pmid:22068695.finding: Review of >200 studies: two or three waves of antral follicles develop during the human cycle, and a single dominant follicle is usually selected in the mid-follicular phase.

pmid:35258085.authors: Erden M, Mumusoglu S, Polat M, et al.
pmid:35258085.title: The LH surge and ovulation re-visited: a systematic review and meta-analysis and implications for true natural cycle frozen thawed embryo transfer
pmid:35258085.finding: Mean interval from LH-surge onset to ovulation was 33.9 h (95% CI 30.8-37.0), with individual intervals from 22 to 56 h.

pmid:7477165.authors: Wilcox AJ, Weinberg CR, Baird DD
pmid:7477165.title: Timing of sexual intercourse in relation to ovulation. Effects on the probability of conception, survival of the pregnancy, and sex of the baby
pmid:7477165.finding: Conception occurred only from intercourse in a six-day window ending on the day of ovulation; probability rose from 0.10 five days before to 0.33 on ovulation day.

pmid:10362823.authors: Wilcox AJ, Baird DD, Weinberg CR
pmid:10362823.title: Time of implantation of the conceptus and loss of pregnancy
pmid:10362823.finding: Implantation (first hCG) occurred 6-12 days after ovulation, 84% on days 8-10; early loss rose from 13% when implanting by day 9 to 82% after day 11.

pmid:23959022.authors: Steegers-Theunissen RP, Twigt J, Pestinger V, et al.
pmid:23959022.title: The periconceptional period, reproduction and long-term health of offspring: the importance of one-carbon metabolism
pmid:23959022.finding: Defines the periconception period as about 5-6 months spanning oocyte growth, fertilisation and embryo development to gestational week 10, during which one-carbon (folate/B12) metabolism and lifestyle shape fertility and offspring health.

pmid:29673874.authors: Fleming TP, Watkins AJ, Velazquez MA, et al.
pmid:29673874.title: Origins of lifetime health around the time of conception: causes and consequences
pmid:29673874.finding: Lancet review: from gamete maturation to early embryo development, parental nutrition, obesity and ART can programme long-term offspring health; calls for preparation before conception.

pmid:27189655.authors: Copp AJ, Adzick NS, Chitty LS, et al.
pmid:27189655.title: Spina bifida
pmid:27189655.finding: Primer: human neural tube closure starts on day 22 after fertilisation and finishes at the posterior neuropore around day 26; periconceptional folic acid prevents a share of spina bifida.

pmid:11106583.authors: Jauniaux E, Watson AL, Hempstock J, et al.
pmid:11106583.title: Onset of maternal arterial blood flow and placental oxidative stress. A possible factor in human early pregnancy failure
pmid:11106583.finding: Placental oxygen tension rises from <20 mmHg at 8 weeks to >50 mmHg at 12 weeks of gestation as maternal arterial flow begins, with a burst of oxidative stress and up-regulated antioxidant enzymes.

pmid:20111701.title: Human ovarian reserve from conception to the menopause
pmid:20111701.finding: Model of non-growing follicle numbers: by age 30 about 12%, and by 40 about 3%, of the maximum pre-birth pool remains; age explains 81% of the variance.

pmid:22705668.authors: Nagaoka SI, Hassold TJ, Hunt PA
pmid:22705668.title: Human aneuploidy: mechanisms and new insights into an age-old problem
pmid:22705668.finding: Aneuploidy arises almost always in the oocyte; the age-related increase reflects an interplay of features unique to oogenesis (decades-long meiotic arrest) and other factors.

pmid:23019302.authors: Valckx SD, De Pauw I, De Neubourg D, et al.
pmid:23019302.title: BMI-related metabolic composition of the follicular fluid of women undergoing assisted reproductive treatment and the consequences for oocyte and embryo quality
pmid:23019302.finding: Most serum metabolite differences between women were mirrored in follicular fluid, and some follicular fluid components were associated with oocyte quality.

pmid:25775080.authors: Reynolds KA, Boudoures AL, Chi MM, et al.
pmid:25775080.title: Adverse effects of obesity and/or high-fat diet on oocyte quality and metabolism are not reversible with resumption of regular diet in mice
pmid:25775080.finding: Mice fed a high-fat diet for 6 weeks then a control diet for 8 weeks normalised weight and glucose but kept abnormal oocyte spindles, low mitochondrial membrane potential and lipid accumulation.

pmid:40707970.authors: Xinyan C, Ting Y, Xi Z, et al.
pmid:40707970.title: Exercise-diet intervention ameliorates but fails to fully reverse obesity-induced ovarian dysfunction: evidence spanning folliculogenesis to embryonic development
pmid:40707970.finding: In obese mice an exercise-diet intervention improved but did not fully reverse ovarian and oocyte defects (spindles, mitochondria).

pmid:24987272.authors: Bentov Y, Hannam T, Jurisicova A, et al.
pmid:24987272.title: Coenzyme Q10 Supplementation and Oocyte Aneuploidy in Women Undergoing IVF-ICSI Treatment
pmid:24987272.finding: CoQ10 600 mg vs placebo before IVF: aneuploidy 46.5% vs 62.8%, not significant; trial stopped early and underpowered.

pmid:24796766.authors: Yeung TW, Chai J, Li RH, et al.
pmid:24796766.title: A randomized, controlled, pilot trial on the effect of dehydroepiandrosterone on ovarian response markers, ovarian response, and in vitro fertilization outcomes in poor responders
pmid:24796766.finding: DHEA 25 mg three times daily for at least 12 weeks raised serum and follicular DHEA-S but did not change AFC, AMH, FSH, ovarian response or IVF outcome versus placebo.

pmid:20638339.authors: Gleicher N, Weghofer A, Barad DH
pmid:20638339.title: Improvement in diminished ovarian reserve after dehydroepiandrosterone supplementation
pmid:20638339.finding: Uncontrolled: AMH rose about 60% over 30-120 days (mean 73) of DHEA, more with longer use and in women under 38.

pmid:16997936.title: Effect of dehydroepiandrosterone on oocyte and embryo yields, embryo grade and cell number in IVF
pmid:16997936.finding: Before-after IVF cycles around DHEA 75 mg/day for a mean 17.6 weeks: more fertilised oocytes and normal day-3 embryos.

pmid:27489169.authors: Polyzos NP, Davis SR, Drakopoulos P, et al.
pmid:27489169.title: Testosterone for Poor Ovarian Responders: Lessons From Ovarian Physiology
pmid:27489169.finding: Argues that androgens act mainly at early follicle stages, so the 5-21-day high-dose testosterone courses used in trials do not fit ovarian physiology.

pmid:25949183.authors: Kim CH, Ahn JW, Moon JW, et al.
pmid:25949183.title: Ovarian Features after 2 Weeks, 3 Weeks and 4 Weeks Transdermal Testosterone Gel Treatment and Their Associated Effect on IVF Outcomes in Poor Responders
pmid:25949183.finding: Transdermal testosterone for 3-4 weeks (not 2) raised AFC and lowered FSH dose; live birth rose only with 4 weeks.

pmid:15206484.authors: Gerli S, Mignosa M, Di Renzo GC
pmid:15206484.title: Effects of inositol on ovarian function and metabolic factors in women with PCOS: a randomized double blind placebo-controlled trial
pmid:15206484.finding: Inositol 100 mg twice daily for 14 weeks in PCOS: E2 rose in the first week and first ovulation came sooner (23.6 vs 41.8 days); expression of concern issued in 2025.

pmid:18074942.authors: Gerli S, Papaleo E, Ferrari A, et al.
pmid:18074942.title: Randomized, double blind placebo-controlled trial: effects of myo-inositol on ovarian function and metabolic factors in women with PCOS
pmid:18074942.finding: RETRACTED (2023): placebo-controlled myo-inositol PCOS trial; cited only to flag the retraction.

pmid:40712462.authors: Papaleo E, Unfer V, Baillargeon JP, et al.
pmid:40712462.title: Retraction notice to "Contribution of myo-inositol to reproduction". [Eur. J. Obstet. Gynecol. Reprod. Biol. 147 (2009) 120-123]
pmid:40712462.journal: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
pmid:40712462.finding: Retraction notice (2025) for the 2009 review "Contribution of myo-inositol to reproduction".

pmid:36703143.authors: Greff D, Juhász AE, Váncsa S, et al.
pmid:36703143.title: Inositol is an effective and safe treatment in polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmid:36703143.finding: Inositols raised the chance of regular cycles (RR 1.79 vs placebo) and lowered androgens, non-inferior to metformin.

pmid:26008214.authors: Harpsøe NG, Andersen LP, Gögenur I, et al.
pmid:26008214.title: Clinical pharmacokinetics of melatonin: a systematic review
pmid:26008214.finding: Systematic review of melatonin pharmacokinetics: oral Tmax about 50 min, elimination half-life about 45 min, oral bioavailability 9-33%.

pmid:35041662.authors: Legro RS, Hansen KR, Diamond MP, et al.
pmid:35041662.title: Effects of preconception lifestyle intervention in infertile women with obesity: The FIT-PLESE randomized controlled trial
pmid:35041662.finding: FIT-PLESE: 16 weeks of intensive weight loss (-6.6%) before treatment did not raise healthy live birth vs exercise alone (12.2% vs 15.2%) but cut metabolic syndrome.

pmid:26401593.authors: Legro RS, Dodson WC, Kris-Etherton PM, et al.
pmid:26401593.title: Randomized Controlled Trial of Preconception Interventions in Infertile Women With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
pmid:26401593.finding: In obese PCOS, 16 weeks of preconception lifestyle (-6.2%) or combined treatment raised cumulative ovulation (60-67% vs 46% with OCP alone).

pmid:27172435.authors: Legro RS, Dodson WC, Kunselman AR, et al.
pmid:27172435.title: Benefit of Delayed Fertility Therapy With Preconception Weight Loss Over Immediate Therapy in Obese Women With PCOS
pmid:27172435.finding: Delaying clomiphene for 16 weeks of weight loss in obese PCOS gave higher live birth (25% vs 10.2% with immediate treatment).

pmid:25826729.authors: Sim KA, Dezarnaulds GM, Denyer GS, et al.
pmid:25826729.title: Weight loss improves reproductive outcomes in obese women undergoing fertility treatment: a randomized controlled trial
pmid:25826729.finding: A 12-week VLED-based weight-loss programme before fertility treatment: pregnancy 48% vs 14% and live birth 44% vs 14%.

pmid:35441470.authors: Wilding JPH, Batterham RL, Davies M, et al.
pmid:35441470.title: Weight regain and cardiometabolic effects after withdrawal of semaglutide: The STEP 1 trial extension
pmid:35441470.finding: STEP 1 extension: one year after stopping semaglutide 2.4 mg, people regained two-thirds of the 17.3% weight lost and cardiometabolic gains reverted.

pmid:31831368.authors: Landersoe SK, Birch Petersen K, Sørensen AL, et al.
pmid:31831368.title: Ovarian reserve markers after discontinuing long-term use of combined oral contraceptives
pmid:31831368.finding: After stopping long-term combined pills, AMH rose 53% and AFC 41%, plateauing by 2 months.

pmid:34126087.authors: Hariton E, Shirazi TN, Douglas NC, et al.
pmid:34126087.title: Anti-Müllerian hormone levels among contraceptive users: evidence from a cross-sectional cohort of 27,125 individuals
pmid:34126087.finding: AMH was about 24% lower on the combined pill, 22% lower on the ring, 23% on the implant and 7% on the hormonal IUD than in non-users (data from a direct-to-consumer testing company).

pmid:24943117.authors: Wong F, MacLeod M, Mueller JF, et al.
pmid:24943117.title: Enhanced elimination of perfluorooctane sulfonic acid by menstruating women: evidence from population-based pharmacokinetic modeling
pmid:24943117.finding: Modelled PFOS half-life was 4.7 years in men and 4.0 years in women; menstruation explains about 30% of the sex difference.

pmid:21521276.authors: Moleti M, Di Bella B, Giorgianni G, et al.
pmid:21521276.title: Maternal thyroid function in different conditions of iodine nutrition in pregnant women exposed to mild-moderate iodine deficiency: an observational study
pmid:21521276.finding: Women using iodised salt for >2 years before pregnancy had fewer low-FT4 values and no TSH rise, whereas starting 150 ug iodine in early pregnancy raised TSH; authors advise starting months before conception.

pmid:32320029.authors: Dineva M, Fishpool H, Rayman MP, et al.
pmid:32320029.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of the effects of iodine supplementation on thyroid function and child neurodevelopment in mildly-to-moderately iodine-deficient pregnant women
pmid:32320029.finding: Insufficient good-quality evidence that iodine supplementation in mildly deficient pregnancy improves thyroid function or child cognition; preconception iodine stores should be considered.

pmid:6954898.authors: Knutti R, Rothweiler H, Schlatter C
pmid:6954898.title: The effect of pregnancy on the pharmacokinetics of caffeine
pmid:6954898.finding: Caffeine half-life rose from about 3 h in non-pregnant women to 10.5 h in the last 4 weeks of pregnancy, with the increase starting early in pregnancy.

pmid:4029248.title: Impairment of caffeine clearance by chronic use of low-dose oestrogen-containing oral contraceptives
pmid:4029248.finding: Chronic low-dose oral contraceptive use prolonged caffeine half-life from 5.4 to 7.9 h.

pmid:27016456.authors: Buck Louis GM, Sapra KJ, Schisterman EF, et al.
pmid:27016456.title: Lifestyle and pregnancy loss in a contemporary cohort of women recruited before conception: The LIFE Study
pmid:27016456.finding: More than two caffeinated drinks a day before conception, by either partner, was associated with pregnancy loss (aHR ~1.7).

pmid:12204391.title: A review of the literature relating caffeine consumption by women to their risk of reproductive hazards
pmid:12204391.finding: Argues the caffeine-miscarriage link may reflect the Stein-Susser effect (nausea from a healthy pregnancy lowers caffeine intake) and confounding by smoking.

pmid:29032957.authors: Stoffel NU, Cercamondi CI, Brittenham G, et al.
pmid:29032957.title: Iron absorption from oral iron supplements given on consecutive versus alternate days and as single morning doses versus twice-daily split dosing in iron-depleted women: two open-label, randomised controlled trials
pmid:29032957.finding: Alternate-day iron gave higher fractional (21.8% vs 16.3%) and total absorption than consecutive days; split twice-daily dosing gave no gain and raised hepcidin.

pmid:38021373.authors: von Siebenthal HK, Gessler S, Vallelian F, et al.
pmid:38021373.title: Alternate day versus consecutive day oral iron supplementation in iron-depleted women: a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled study
pmid:38021373.finding: At equal total dose, alternate-day iron for 6 months matched daily iron for 3 months on ferritin, caused fewer GI side effects and less iron deficiency at 6 months (3.0% vs 11.4%).

pmid:18689382.authors: Hao L, Yang QH, Li Z, et al.
pmid:18689382.title: Folate status and homocysteine response to folic acid doses and withdrawal among young Chinese women in a large-scale randomized double-blind trial
pmid:18689382.finding: Plasma folate plateaued at 3 months of daily folic acid; split vs single doses did not differ; 4 mg weekly raised plasma folate far less than 0.4 mg daily (142% vs 259%); levels fell fast after stopping.

pmid:30609688.authors: Crider KS, Devine O, Qi YP, et al.
pmid:30609688.title: Systematic Review and Bayesian Meta-analysis of the Dose-response Relationship between Folic Acid Intake and Changes in Blood Folate Concentrations
pmid:30609688.finding: RBC folate took a median 36 weeks (27-52) to reach steady state on 375-570 ug/day folic acid, rising 1.78-fold.

pmid:37545008.authors: Dong J, Yin LL, Deng XD, et al.
pmid:37545008.title: Initiation and duration of folic acid supplementation in preventing congenital malformations
pmid:37545008.finding: Lowest malformation risk with folic acid started about 1.5 months (1.1-1.9) before conception and taken for about 4 months; heart defects needed earlier start (2.2 months).

pmid:31870562.authors: Kermack AJ, Lowen P, Wellstead SJ, et al.
pmid:31870562.title: Effect of a 6-week "Mediterranean" dietary intervention on in vitro human embryo development: the Preconception Dietary Supplements in Assisted Reproduction double-blinded randomized controlled trial
pmid:31870562.finding: A 6-week omega-3/vitamin D/olive-oil dietary intervention before IVF accelerated later embryo cleavage and improved day-3 KIDScore (no live-birth outcome).

pmid:31747470.authors: Georgiou EX, Melo P, Baker PE, et al.
pmid:31747470.title: Long-term GnRH agonist therapy before in vitro fertilisation (IVF) for improving fertility outcomes in women with endometriosis
pmid:31747470.finding: Cochrane: uncertain whether 3-6 months of GnRH agonist before IVF in endometriosis affects live birth (very low-quality evidence), reversing the earlier positive review.

pmid:36151012.authors: Michaeli J, Dior UP, Fainaru O, et al.
pmid:36151012.title: Long-term pituitary down-regulation pretreatment for endometriosis - chronicles of guidelines and recommendations
pmid:36151012.finding: Traces how guidelines endorsed then (ESHRE 2022) withdrew the recommendation for long-term pituitary down-regulation before IVF in endometriosis.

pmid:40179834.authors: Murdock C, Murdock C, Sanchez-Ramos L, et al.
pmid:40179834.title: The Impact of Laparoscopic Cystectomy for Ovarian Endometrioma on Anti-Müllerian Hormone Levels: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmid:40179834.finding: AMH fell after endometrioma cystectomy at short, medium and long-term follow-up (long-term -2.1 ng/mL), with no recovery over time.

pmid:38527601.authors: Cobo A, Coello A, De Los Santos MJ, et al.
pmid:38527601.title: Embryo long-term storage does not affect assisted reproductive technologies outcome: analysis of 58,001 vitrified blastocysts over 11 years
pmid:38527601.finding: Storage time of vitrified blastocysts (up to 11 years) was not associated with live birth after adjustment.

pmid:34630326.authors: Zhang X, Wu S, Hao G, et al.
pmid:34630326.title: Prolonged Cryopreservation Negatively Affects Embryo Transfer Outcomes Following the Elective Freeze-All Strategy: A Multicenter Retrospective Study
pmid:34630326.finding: Multicentre retrospective study: longer cryostorage of vitrified embryos was associated with lower pregnancy and live birth.

pmid:27640943.authors: Roberge S, Nicolaides K, Demers S, et al.
pmid:27640943.title: The role of aspirin dose on the prevention of preeclampsia and fetal growth restriction: systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:27640943.finding: Aspirin started at <=16 weeks reduced pre-eclampsia (RR 0.57) with a dose-response; started after 16 weeks the effect was small (RR 0.81).

pmid:27810551.authors: Meher S, Duley L, Hunter K, et al.
pmid:27810551.title: Antiplatelet therapy before or after 16 weeks' gestation for preventing preeclampsia: an individual participant data meta-analysis
pmid:27810551.finding: Individual-participant data: antiplatelet effect was the same whether started before or after 16 weeks (RR 0.90 both).

pmid:24702835.authors: Schisterman EF, Silver RM, Lesher LL, et al.
pmid:24702835.title: Preconception low-dose aspirin and pregnancy outcomes: results from the EAGeR randomised trial
pmid:24702835.finding: EAGeR: preconception aspirin 81 mg did not raise live birth overall (58% vs 53%, NS) in women with prior loss.

pmid:33493011.authors: Naimi AI, Perkins NJ, Sjaarda LA, et al.
pmid:33493011.title: The Effect of Preconception-Initiated Low-Dose Aspirin on Human Chorionic Gonadotropin-Detected Pregnancy, Pregnancy Loss, and Live Birth : Per Protocol Analysis of a Randomized Trial
pmid:33493011.finding: Per-protocol EAGeR: taking preconception aspirin on at least 4-5 of 7 days was linked to 15 more live births per 100 women; post-conception initiation reduced the effect.

pmid:39673334.authors: Mourad A, Jamal W, Hemmings R, et al.
pmid:39673334.title: Empirical use of growth hormone in IVF is useless: the largest randomized controlled trial
pmid:39673334.finding: Growth hormone 2.5 mg daily from day 1 of stimulation to retrieval did not improve oocytes, embryos or pregnancy in normal responders.

deep-timing-egg:tegg-fda-wegovy2021.authors: US Food and Drug Administration; Novo Nordisk
deep-timing-egg:tegg-fda-wegovy2021.title: WEGOVY (semaglutide) injection, prescribing information (revised 06/2021)
deep-timing-egg:tegg-fda-wegovy2021.finding: Semaglutide half-life is about 1 week and it stays in the circulation 5-7 weeks after the last dose; discontinue at least 2 months before a planned pregnancy.

deep-timing-egg:tegg-fda-zepbound2023.authors: US Food and Drug Administration; Eli Lilly
deep-timing-egg:tegg-fda-zepbound2023.title: ZEPBOUND (tirzepatide) injection, prescribing information (revised 11/2023)
deep-timing-egg:tegg-fda-zepbound2023.finding: Tirzepatide half-life is about 5 days with steady state after 4 weeks; oral contraceptive users need non-oral or barrier back-up for 4 weeks after starting and after each dose increase; stop when pregnancy is recognised.

deep-timing-env-indoor:eia-whoradonfs.title: Radon and health (fact sheet)
deep-timing-env-indoor:eia-whoradonfs.finding: WHO recommends a national reference level of 100 Bq/m3 (not above 300 Bq/m3 where that is unachievable); radon causes 3-14% of lung cancers and risk rises about 16% per 100 Bq/m3.

pmid:17416783.authors: Dinkova-Kostova AT, Fahey JW, Wade KL, et al.
pmid:17416783.title: Induction of the phase 2 response in mouse and human skin by sulforaphane-containing broccoli sprout extracts
pmid:17416783.finding: Topical sulforaphane raised human skin NQO1 activity 1.5-fold after one dose and 4.5-fold after three doses 24 h apart, showing that induced enzyme carries over and stacks between daily doses.

pmid:11752465.authors: Gao X, Dinkova-Kostova AT, Talalay P
pmid:11752465.title: Powerful and prolonged protection of human retinal pigment epithelial cells, keratinocytes, and mouse leukemia cells against oxidative damage: the indirect antioxidant effects of sulforaphane
pmid:11752465.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:11752465.finding: In human cells, a 24 h sulforaphane exposure gave protection against oxidants that kept rising for 24-48 h after removal and returned to control levels over the following days, tracking NQO1 and glutathione.

pmid:11160862.authors: Siegel D, Anwar A, Winski SL, et al.
pmid:11160862.title: Rapid polyubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of a mutant form of NAD(P)H:quinone oxidoreductase 1
pmid:11160862.finding: Wild-type NQO1 protein had a half-life over 18 h in cells (the common NQO1*2 variant was degraded in 1.2 h).

pmid:17925401.authors: Lee OH, Jain AK, Papusha V, et al.
pmid:17925401.title: An auto-regulatory loop between stress sensors INrf2 and Nrf2 controls their cellular abundance
pmid:17925401.finding: Nrf2 induces transcription of its own inhibitor KEAP1, a negative feedback loop that limits the size and duration of the response.

pmid:27457280.authors: Xu Z, Wang S, Ji H, et al.
pmid:27457280.title: Broccoli sprout extract prevents diabetic cardiomyopathy via Nrf2 activation in db/db T2DM mice
pmid:27457280.finding: Broccoli sprout extract or sulforaphane by gavage every other day for 3 months prevented diabetic cardiomyopathy in mice via Nrf2.

pmid:29888232.authors: Sedlak TW, Nucifora LG, Koga M, et al.
pmid:29888232.title: Sulforaphane Augments Glutathione and Influences Brain Metabolites in Human Subjects: A Clinical Pilot Study
pmid:29888232.finding: Seven days of daily oral sulforaphane raised blood glutathione in healthy volunteers.

pmid:27071063.authors: Doss JF, Jonassaint JC, Garrett ME, et al.
pmid:27071063.title: Phase 1 Study of a Sulforaphane-Containing Broccoli Sprout Homogenate for Sickle Cell Disease
pmid:27071063.finding: Escalating broccoli sprout homogenate raised whole-blood HMOX1 mRNA on the last day of treatment.

pmid:27339168.authors: Bauman JE, Zang Y, Sen M, et al.
pmid:27339168.title: Prevention of Carcinogen-Induced Oral Cancer by Sulforaphane
pmid:27339168.finding: Sulforaphane induced NQO1 and GCLC in mucosal cells; in a pilot, buccal NQO1 mRNA rose 2-fold or more in 3-6 of 6-9 people depending on beverage.

pmid:38772511.authors: Ribeiro M, Alvarenga L, Coutinho-Wolino KS, et al.
pmid:38772511.title: Sulforaphane upregulates the mRNA expression of NRF2 and NQO1 in non-dialysis patients with chronic kidney disease
pmid:38772511.finding: 400 µg/day sulforaphane for 1 month raised blood NRF2 and NQO1 mRNA.

pmid:17312446.authors: Heiss C, Finis D, Kleinbongard P, et al.
pmid:17312446.title: Sustained increase in flow-mediated dilation after daily intake of high-flavanol cocoa drink over 1 week
pmid:17312446.finding: Single doses of high-flavanol cocoa raised FMD with a peak at 2 h; with daily intake, fasting FMD rose stepwise on days 3, 5 and 8 and returned to baseline after a 1-week washout.

pmid:18510961.authors: Balzer J, Rassaf T, Heiss C, et al.
pmid:18510961.title: Sustained benefits in vascular function through flavanol-containing cocoa in medicated diabetic patients a double-masked, randomized, controlled trial
pmid:18510961.finding: Thrice-daily flavanol cocoa for 30 days raised fasting FMD 30% and acute post-dose FMD rises persisted with no tachyphylaxis.

pmid:20620742.authors: Heiss C, Jahn S, Taylor M, et al.
pmid:20620742.title: Improvement of endothelial function with dietary flavanols is associated with mobilization of circulating angiogenic cells in patients with coronary artery disease
pmid:20620742.finding: High-flavanol cocoa twice daily for 30 days improved FMD 47% and lowered systolic BP 4.2 mmHg vs low-flavanol.

pmid:16418281.authors: Schroeter H, Heiss C, Balzer J, et al.
pmid:16418281.title: (-)-Epicatechin mediates beneficial effects of flavanol-rich cocoa on vascular function in humans
pmid:16418281.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:16418281.finding: Cocoa flavanols, specifically epicatechin, acutely raised NO species and FMD within hours of ingestion.

pmid:40568979.authors: Ottaviani JI, Schroeter H, Bier DM, et al.
pmid:40568979.title: The overlooked impact of background diet and adherence in nutrition trials
pmid:40568979.finding: In COSMOS, about a third of the cocoa group did not reach expected flavanol biomarker levels and 20% of the placebo group had high background intake; biomarker-based analyses gave larger effects (major CVD HR 0.48).

pmid:31524216.authors: Sun Y, Zimmermann D, De Castro CA, et al.
pmid:31524216.title: Dose-response relationship between cocoa flavanols and human endothelial function: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials
pmid:31524216.finding: Cocoa flavanols improved FMD by 1.17%, with an inverted-U dose response peaking near 710 mg/day; most trials had high risk of bias.

pmid:19516176.authors: Grassi D, Mulder TP, Draijer R, et al.
pmid:19516176.title: Black tea consumption dose-dependently improves flow-mediated dilation in healthy males
pmid:19516176.finding: One-week periods of black tea (100-800 mg flavonoids/day) dose-dependently raised FMD from 7.8% to 10.3%.

pmid:23038021.authors: Hodgson JM, Woodman RJ, Puddey IB, et al.
pmid:23038021.title: Short-term effects of polyphenol-rich black tea on blood pressure in men and women
pmid:23038021.finding: One day of polyphenol-rich black tea did not change 24 h blood pressure, whereas the same group had earlier found lower BP after 6 months of regular intake.

pmid:19460943.authors: Stalmach A, Mullen W, Barron D, et al.
pmid:19460943.title: Metabolite profiling of hydroxycinnamate derivatives in plasma and urine after the ingestion of coffee by humans: identification of biomarkers of coffee consumption
pmid:19460943.finding: After coffee, some chlorogenic acid metabolites peaked within 1 h (small intestine) and others after 4 h (colonic); 29% of intake was excreted in 24 h.

pmid:8422743.authors: Shi J, Benowitz NL, Denaro CP, et al.
pmid:8422743.title: Pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic modeling of caffeine: tolerance to pressor effects
pmid:8422743.finding: Tolerance to the blood-pressure-raising effect of caffeine develops and regresses with a half-life of about 1 h and can blunt the effect by over 90%; habitual drinkers regain the response after brief abstinence.

pmid:12765992.authors: Miro-Casas E, Covas MI, Farre M, et al.
pmid:12765992.title: Hydroxytyrosol disposition in humans
pmid:12765992.finding: After 25 mL virgin olive oil, plasma hydroxytyrosol peaked at 32 min (3-O-methyl form at 53 min) with a half-life of 2.43 h; ~98% circulated as conjugates.

pmid:17563030.authors: Fitó M, Guxens M, Corella D, et al.
pmid:17563030.title: Effect of a traditional Mediterranean diet on lipoprotein oxidation: a randomized controlled trial
pmid:17563030.finding: After 3 months of a Mediterranean diet with virgin olive oil or nuts, oxidized LDL fell (-10.6 and -7.3 U/L) vs no change on a low-fat diet.

pmid:30733217.title: PREDIMED trial of Mediterranean diet: retracted, republished, still trusted?
pmid:30733217.finding: Critical analysis of the retraction and republication of PREDIMED after randomization irregularities, questioning how much its revised estimates can be trusted.

pmid:11285356.authors: Setchell KD, Brown NM, Desai P, et al.
pmid:11285356.title: Bioavailability of pure isoflavones in healthy humans and analysis of commercial soy isoflavone supplements
pmid:11285356.finding: Genistein and daidzein aglycones peaked at 5-7 h and their glycosides at about 9 h after a single dose.

pmid:16351761.authors: Frankenfeld CL, Atkinson C, Thomas WK, et al.
pmid:16351761.title: High concordance of daidzein-metabolizing phenotypes in individuals measured 1 to 3 years apart
pmid:16351761.finding: Equol-producer status was concordant in 82% of people measured 1-3 years apart.

pmid:15795437.authors: Kuijsten A, Arts IC, Vree TB, et al.
pmid:15795437.title: Pharmacokinetics of enterolignans in healthy men and women consuming a single dose of secoisolariciresinol diglucoside
pmid:15795437.finding: After flax lignan (SDG), enterolactone peaked at about 20 h with a half-life of 12.6 h and mean residence time of 36 h; enterolignans accumulate with intake 2-3 times a day.

pmid:18598186.authors: Seeram NP, Zhang Y, McKeever R, et al.
pmid:18598186.title: Pomegranate juice and extracts provide similar levels of plasma and urinary ellagitannin metabolites in human subjects
pmid:18598186.finding: Pomegranate juice ellagic acid peaked in plasma at about 0.65 h; extracts gave similar exposure with a later peak; urolithin A glucuronide appeared in urine.

pmid:12571654.authors: Manach C, Morand C, Gil-Izquierdo A, et al.
pmid:12571654.title: Bioavailability in humans of the flavanones hesperidin and narirutin after the ingestion of two doses of orange juice
pmid:12571654.finding: Orange juice flavanone metabolites appeared at 3 h, peaked at 5-7 h and returned to baseline by 24 h.

pmid:18250365.authors: Webb AJ, Patel N, Loukogeorgakis S, et al.
pmid:18250365.title: Acute blood pressure lowering, vasoprotective, and antiplatelet properties of dietary nitrate via bioconversion to nitrite
pmid:18250365.finding: After 500 mL beetroot juice, blood pressure fell most at 2.5-3 h (about -10/-8 mmHg), with a smaller reduction still present at 24 h.

pmid:25421976.authors: Kapil V, Khambata RS, Robertson A, et al.
pmid:25421976.title: Dietary nitrate provides sustained blood pressure lowering in hypertensive patients: a randomized, phase 2, double-blind, placebo-controlled study
pmid:25421976.finding: Daily dietary nitrate for 4 weeks lowered home BP within 1 week, sustained with no tachyphylaxis (clinic -7.7/-2.4 mmHg); BP began returning to baseline in a 2-week washout.

pmid:25824023.authors: Chiu YH, Afeiche MC, Gaskins AJ, et al.
pmid:25824023.title: Fruit and vegetable intake and their pesticide residues in relation to semen quality among men from a fertility clinic
pmid:25824023.finding: High-pesticide-residue produce intake was associated with lower sperm count (-49%) and fewer normal forms over semen samples collected up to 18 months after diet assessment.

pmid:9099655.authors: Appel LJ, Moore TJ, Obarzanek E, et al.
pmid:9099655.title: A clinical trial of the effects of dietary patterns on blood pressure. DASH Collaborative Research Group
pmid:9099655.finding: Over 8 weeks of controlled feeding, the DASH combination diet lowered BP 5.5/3.0 mmHg vs control (11.4/5.5 in hypertensives).

pmid:10981543.authors: Conlin PR, Chow D, Miller ER 3rd, et al.
pmid:10981543.title: The effect of dietary patterns on blood pressure control in hypertensive patients: results from the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) trial
pmid:10981543.finding: DASH lowered systolic BP 11.4 mmHg; BP changes were evident within 2 weeks of starting the feeding.

pmid:28993451.authors: Juraschek SP, Woodward M, Sacks FM, et al.
pmid:28993451.title: Time Course of Change in Blood Pressure From Sodium Reduction and the DASH Diet
pmid:28993451.finding: In DASH-Sodium, DASH lowered systolic BP 4.4 mmHg vs control within 1 week, with no further fall after that; sodium reduction kept lowering BP through 4 weeks.

pmid:26086182.authors: Morris MC, Tangney CC, Wang Y, et al.
pmid:26086182.title: MIND diet slows cognitive decline with aging
pmid:26086182.finding: Higher MIND diet scores were associated with slower cognitive decline over 4.7 years, equivalent to 7.5 years younger.

pmid:24336217.authors: David LA, Maurice CF, Carmody RN, et al.
pmid:24336217.title: Diet rapidly and reproducibly alters the human gut microbiome
pmid:24336217.finding: Animal- or plant-based diets shifted gut microbiota within 1 day of reaching the gut, and the community reverted 2 days after the diet ended.

pmid:21885731.authors: Wu GD, Chen J, Hoffmann C, et al.
pmid:21885731.title: Linking long-term dietary patterns with gut microbial enterotypes
pmid:21885731.finding: Gut microbiome composition changed within 24 h of a high-fat/low-fiber or low-fat/high-fiber diet, but enterotype stayed stable over 10 days; enterotypes tracked long-term diet.

pmid:34256014.authors: Wastyk HC, Fragiadakis GK, Perelman D, et al.
pmid:34256014.title: Gut-microbiota-targeted diets modulate human immune status
pmid:34256014.finding: A 17-week high-fiber diet raised microbial fiber-degrading enzymes with person-specific immune responses; fermented foods steadily raised diversity and lowered inflammatory markers.

pmid:26762459.authors: Sonnenburg ED, Smits SA, Tikhonov M, et al.
pmid:26762459.title: Diet-induced extinctions in the gut microbiota compound over generations
pmid:26762459.finding: In humanized mice, low-fiber diets caused microbiota changes that were reversible within one generation, but over several generations taxa were lost and did not return with fiber alone.

pmid:29097438.authors: Roager HM, Vogt JK, Kristensen M, et al.
pmid:29097438.title: Whole grain-rich diet reduces body weight and systemic low-grade inflammation without inducing major changes of the gut microbiome: a randomised cross-over trial
pmid:29097438.finding: An 8-week whole-grain diet lowered weight, IL-6 and CRP vs refined grain but did not change insulin sensitivity or cause major gut microbiome shifts.

pmid:23089999.authors: Jenkins DJ, Kendall CW, Augustin LS, et al.
pmid:23089999.title: Effect of legumes as part of a low glycemic index diet on glycemic control and cardiovascular risk factors in type 2 diabetes mellitus: a randomized controlled trial
pmid:23089999.finding: A low-GI diet with at least 1 cup/day of legumes for 3 months lowered HbA1c 0.5% and systolic BP more than a wheat-fiber diet.

pmid:33579652.authors: Montano L, Ceretti E, Donato F, et al.
pmid:33579652.title: Effects of a Lifestyle Change Intervention on Semen Quality in Healthy Young Men Living in Highly Polluted Areas in Italy: The FASt Randomized Controlled Trial
pmid:33579652.finding: A 4-month Mediterranean diet plus exercise program raised sperm concentration, motility, normal morphology and semen antioxidant capacity vs control.

pmid:18497337.title: The cycle of the seminiferous epithelium in humans: a need to revisit?
pmid:18497337.finding: The 1960s estimate of human spermatogenesis duration (~74 days) rests on weak data and may be off by about 6 days.

pmid:21947005.authors: Arner P, Bernard S, Salehpour M, et al.
pmid:21947005.title: Dynamics of human adipose lipid turnover in health and metabolic disease
pmid:21947005.n: adipose samples dated by bomb-pulse carbon-14
pmid:21947005.finding: Adipocyte triglycerides are renewed about six times during an adipocyte's roughly 10-year lifespan, giving a lipid age of about 1.6 years that is stable across adult ages.

pmid:33595593.authors: Berg DD, Jhund PS, Docherty KF, et al.
pmid:33595593.title: Time to Clinical Benefit of Dapagliflozin and Significance of Prior Heart Failure Hospitalization in Patients With Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction
pmid:33595593.finding: Dapagliflozin's reduction in cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure became statistically significant by 28 days after randomization and was sustained.

pmid:28403435.authors: Brandt EJ, Myerson R, Perraillon MC, et al.
pmid:28403435.title: Hospital Admissions for Myocardial Infarction and Stroke Before and After the Trans-Fatty Acid Restrictions in New York
pmid:28403435.n: 11.7 million adults in New York counties
pmid:28403435.finding: Three or more years after trans-fat restrictions, restricted counties had 6.2% fewer combined myocardial infarction and stroke admissions and 7.8% fewer myocardial infarctions than unrestricted counties.

pmid:6894292.authors: Buchet JP, Lauwerys R, Roels H
pmid:6894292.title: Comparison of the urinary excretion of arsenic metabolites after a single oral dose of sodium arsenite, monomethylarsonate, or dimethylarsinate in man
pmid:6894292.finding: After a single oral dose, 46% of inorganic arsenite and about 75-78% of methylated arsenic was excreted in urine within 4 days, so urinary arsenic reflects only the last few days of intake.

pmid:12401247.authors: Clancy L, Goodman P, Sinclair H, et al.
pmid:12401247.title: Effect of air-pollution control on death rates in Dublin, Ireland: an intervention study
pmid:12401247.n: Dublin, 72 months before and after a coal ban
pmid:12401247.finding: After Dublin's 1990 coal ban cut black smoke by 36 ug/m3, respiratory deaths fell 15.5% and cardiovascular deaths 10.3% in an interrupted time-series analysis.

pmid:30472992.authors: D'Aiuto F, Gkranias N, Bhowruth D, et al.
pmid:30472992.title: Systemic effects of periodontitis treatment in patients with type 2 diabetes: a 12 month, single-centre, investigator-masked, randomised trial
pmid:30472992.finding: Intensive periodontal treatment lowered HbA1c by 0.6 percentage points versus control treatment at 12 months.

pmid:6049677.authors: Dayton S, Hashimoto S, Pearce ML
pmid:6049677.title: Adipose tissue linoleic acid as a criterion of adherence to a modified diet
pmid:6049677.n: institutionalized men on a high-linoleic diet
pmid:6049677.finding: Adipose linoleic acid correlated poorly with dietary adherence after 1 year but well after 5-6 years (r 0.81 and 0.74), showing adipose composition integrates intake over years.

pmid:24155956.authors: Demmer RT, Trinquart L, Zuk A, et al.
pmid:24155956.title: The influence of anti-infective periodontal treatment on C-reactive protein: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmid:24155956.finding: Versus no treatment, periodontal therapy lowered CRP by 0.37 mg/L at the earliest post-treatment time point (typically 1-3 months), with larger effects when antibiotics were added.

pmid:20847294.title: Incomplete recovery and individualized responses of the human distal gut microbiota to repeated antibiotic perturbation
pmid:20847294.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
pmid:20847294.finding: Ciprofloxacin cut gut diversity within 3-4 days; communities began returning within a week of each course but recovery was incomplete and the final state differed from baseline.

pmid:24024358.authors: Dockery DW, Rich DQ, Goodman PG, et al.
pmid:24024358.title: Effect of air pollution control on mortality and hospital admissions in Ireland
pmid:24024358.n: Dublin, Cork and four Irish counties, 1981-2004
pmid:24024358.finding: Extending the analysis to three sequential Irish coal bans found respiratory mortality reductions of 17%, 9% and 3% but no clear reduction in total or cardiovascular mortality.

pmid:39453837.authors: EMPA-KIDNEY Collaborative Group, Herrington WG, Staplin N, et al.
pmid:39453837.title: Long-Term Effects of Empagliflozin in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease
pmid:39453837.finding: After empagliflozin was stopped, its cardiorenal benefit continued for up to about 12 months (post-trial hazard ratio 0.87) before the groups converged.

pmid:24346989.authors: Engebretson SP, Hyman LG, Michalowicz BS, et al.
pmid:24346989.title: The effect of nonsurgical periodontal therapy on hemoglobin A1c levels in persons with type 2 diabetes and chronic periodontitis: a randomized clinical trial
pmid:24346989.finding: A large US trial stopped for futility: non-surgical periodontal therapy improved periodontal measures but did not change HbA1c at 6 months (difference -0.05%).

pmid:15625188.authors: Fennell TR, Sumner SC, Snyder RW, et al.
pmid:15625188.title: Metabolism and hemoglobin adduct formation of acrylamide in humans
pmid:15625188.finding: Oral labelled acrylamide was excreted mostly as glutathione conjugates within days and formed haemoglobin adducts in linear proportion to dose; dermal uptake was about 6.6% of oral.

pmid:26842828.authors: Frazer K, Callinan JE, McHugh J, et al.
pmid:26842828.title: Legislative smoking bans for reducing harms from secondhand smoke exposure, smoking prevalence and tobacco consumption
pmid:26842828.finding: Cochrane review: national smoking bans consistently improved cardiovascular outcomes, most clearly acute coronary syndrome admissions, with less consistent effects on respiratory and perinatal outcomes.

pmid:26164495.authors: Freedberg DE, Toussaint NC, Chen SP, et al.
pmid:26164495.title: Proton Pump Inhibitors Alter Specific Taxa in the Human Gastrointestinal Microbiome: A Crossover Trial
pmid:26164495.finding: Four weeks of omeprazole 40 mg twice daily did not change overall gut microbial diversity but reproducibly increased Enterococcaceae and Streptococcaceae and decreased Clostridiales.

pmid:31268361.authors: Gaskins AJ, Fong KC, Abu Awad Y, et al.
pmid:31268361.title: Time-Varying Exposure to Air Pollution and Outcomes of in Vitro Fertilization among Couples from a Fertility Clinic
pmid:31268361.finding: Air pollution exposure during ovarian stimulation, not later stages, carried the strongest association with IVF failure: each interquartile rise in NO2 raised the odds of failing before retrieval by 42%.

pmid:28534225.authors: Goempel K, Tedsen L, Ruenz M, et al.
pmid:28534225.title: Biomarker monitoring of controlled dietary acrylamide exposure indicates consistent human endogenous background
pmid:28534225.finding: Labelled acrylamide was excreted essentially completely as urinary mercapturic acids within 72-96 h, ruling out release from deep body stores; a baseline excretion persisted on an acrylamide-minimised diet, implying endogenous formation.

pmid:12568766.authors: Gulson BL, Mizon KJ, Korsch MJ, et al.
pmid:12568766.title: Mobilization of lead from human bone tissue during pregnancy and lactation--a summary of long-term research
pmid:12568766.finding: Isotope tracing showed the maternal skeleton supplied about a third of blood lead during pregnancy, with a larger release after delivery during lactation, especially on low calcium intake.

pmid:26567191.title: Increase in adipose tissue linoleic acid of US adults in the last half century
pmid:26567191.finding: Systematic review: adipose linoleic acid in US adults rose by 136% over half a century, closely tracking the rise in dietary linoleic acid.

pmid:25047090.authors: Heard K, Green JL, Anderson V, et al.
pmid:25047090.title: A randomized, placebo-controlled trial to determine the course of aminotransferase elevation during prolonged acetaminophen administration
pmid:25047090.finding: Of adults taking 4 g/day acetaminophen, 77% had no or only transient ALT elevation by day 16, and 47 of the 48 with raised ALT at day 16 saw it resolve by day 40 while still taking the drug.

pmid:22762246.authors: Hess MW, Hoenderop JG, Bindels RJ, et al.
pmid:22762246.title: Systematic review: hypomagnesaemia induced by proton pump inhibition
pmid:22762246.finding: PPI-induced hypomagnesaemia appeared after a median 5.5 years of use (range 14 days to 13 years), resolved within about 4 days of stopping, and recurred within about 4 days on re-challenge.

pmid:24225449.authors: Hodson L, Eyles HC, McLachlan KJ, et al.
pmid:24225449.title: Plasma and erythrocyte fatty acids reflect intakes of saturated and n-6 PUFA within a similar time frame
pmid:24225449.finding: Switching between high-saturated-fat and high-linoleic-acid diets changed plasma, erythrocyte and buccal fatty acids within the first 2 weeks and then plateaued, with no detectable change in adipose tissue over 16 weeks.

pmid:18043614.authors: Jernberg C, Löfmark S, Edlund C, et al.
pmid:18043614.title: Long-term ecological impacts of antibiotic administration on the human intestinal microbiota
pmid:18043614.n: 4 exposed and 4 control adults over 2 years
pmid:18043614.finding: A 7-day clindamycin course caused a sharp loss of Bacteroides clonal diversity and enrichment of resistance genes that persisted for up to 2 years after treatment.

pmid:24909636.authors: Jesam C, Salvatierra AM, Schwartz JL, et al.
pmid:24909636.title: Effect of oral administration of a continuous 18 day regimen of meloxicam on ovulation: experience of a randomized controlled trial
pmid:24909636.finding: Meloxicam on cycle days 5-22 caused dose-dependent dysfunctional ovulation in up to 55% of cycles, yet more than 20% of women ovulated normally even on the higher dose, and cycles recovered after treatment.

pmid:31569235.authors: Johnston BC, Zeraatkar D, Han MA, et al.
pmid:31569235.title: Unprocessed Red Meat and Processed Meat Consumption: Dietary Guideline Recommendations From the Nutritional Recommendations (NutriRECS) Consortium
pmid:31569235.n: systematic reviews of meat and health
pmid:31569235.finding: The NutriRECS panel issued weak recommendations that adults continue their current unprocessed red meat and processed meat intake, judging the certainty of benefit from cutting back to be low.

pmid:9374124.authors: Katan MB, Deslypere JP, van Birgelen AP, et al.
pmid:9374124.title: Kinetics of the incorporation of dietary fatty acids into serum cholesteryl esters, erythrocyte membranes, and adipose tissue: an 18-month controlled study
pmid:9374124.finding: Fatty-acid incorporation half-lives differed by pool: 4.8 days for cholesteryl esters (plateau 4-8 weeks), 28 days for erythrocytes (plateau about 180 days), and adipose tissue still rising at 12 months.

pmid:9875693.authors: Larsen SB, Giwercman A, Spanò M, et al.
pmid:9875693.title: A longitudinal study of semen quality in pesticide spraying Danish farmers. The ASCLEPIOS Study Group
pmid:9875693.finding: Across a spraying season, sperm concentration fell similarly in pesticide-using and non-using farmers, with no exposure-related change in semen quality or hormones.

pmid:16343471.authors: Li JJ, Li YS, Chu JM, et al.
pmid:16343471.title: Changes of plasma inflammatory markers after withdrawal of statin therapy in patients with hyperlipidemia
pmid:16343471.finding: Six weeks of pravastatin lowered CRP and IL-6, and both rebounded above treated levels by days 3 and 7 after abrupt withdrawal despite unchanged LDL cholesterol.

pmid:16451864.authors: Lu C, Toepel K, Irish R, et al.
pmid:16451864.title: Organic diets significantly lower children's dietary exposure to organophosphorus pesticides
pmid:16451864.finding: Urinary malathion and chlorpyrifos metabolites fell to undetectable immediately after organic food was introduced and stayed undetectable until conventional food came back.

pmid:18950185.authors: Melo A, Viegas O, Petisca C, et al.
pmid:18950185.title: Effect of beer/red wine marinades on the formation of heterocyclic aromatic amines in pan-fried beef
pmid:18950185.finding: Beer and red-wine marinades cut heterocyclic amines in pan-fried beef, with reductions of about 88% (beer) and 40% (wine) after 6 hours of marinating and smaller effects at 2-4 hours.

pmid:2374566.title: Effect of dietary trans fatty acids on high-density and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels in healthy subjects
pmid:2374566.finding: Three weeks on each diet was enough for trans fatty acids at 10% of energy to lower HDL cholesterol by 0.17 mmol/L and raise LDL relative to oleic acid.

pmid:19778665.authors: Meyers DG, Neuberger JS, He J
pmid:19778665.title: Cardiovascular effect of bans on smoking in public places: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:19778665.finding: After public smoking bans, myocardial infarction rates fell 17% overall, and the incidence rate ratio fell a further 26% for each additional year of observation after the ban.

pmid:19337517.authors: Milbrath MO, Wenger Y, Chang CW, et al.
pmid:19337517.title: Apparent half-lives of dioxins, furans, and polychlorinated biphenyls as a function of age, body fat, smoking status, and breast-feeding
