pmid:19337517.finding: Review of congener-specific data: adult half-lives of dioxins, furans and PCBs are mostly years to decades and lengthen with age and body fat, shortening with smoking and breastfeeding.

pmid:10578481.authors: Nerurkar PV, Le Marchand L, Cooney RV
pmid:10578481.title: Effects of marinating with Asian marinades or western barbecue sauce on PhIP and MeIQx formation in barbecued beef
pmid:10578481.finding: Overnight teriyaki or turmeric-garlic marinades cut PhIP and MeIQx in barbecued beef, whereas a honey barbecue sauce raised PhIP about three-fold and MeIQx about four-fold.

pmid:1891443.authors: Nilsson U, Attewell R, Christoffersson JO, et al.
pmid:1891443.title: Kinetics of lead in bone and blood after end of occupational exposure
pmid:1891443.finding: Followed for 18 years after exposure ended, finger-bone lead fell with a half-time of 16 years and blood lead showed three phases with half-times of 34 days, 1.2 years and 13 years.

pmid:22852484.authors: Noonan CW, Ward TJ, Navidi W, et al.
pmid:22852484.title: Assessing the impact of a wood stove replacement program on air quality and children's health
pmid:22852484.finding: A community wood-stove change-out cut winter ambient PM2.5 by 30% and was followed by fewer reports of childhood wheeze, though indoor reductions varied widely between homes.

pmid:24769399.authors: Oates L, Cohen M, Braun L, et al.
pmid:24769399.title: Reduction in urinary organophosphate pesticide metabolites in adults after a week-long organic diet
pmid:24769399.finding: Seven days of an at least 80% organic diet lowered total urinary dialkylphosphate metabolites by 89% compared with a conventional week.

pmid:9270507.authors: Olsen EA, Katz HI, Levine N, et al.
pmid:9270507.title: Tretinoin emollient cream for photodamaged skin: results of 48-week, multicenter, double-blind studies
pmid:9270507.finding: Improvement in photodamage from daily tretinoin emollient cream was maintained or increased during a further 24 weeks of use, and side effects were less common in the extension than in the first 24 weeks.

pmid:9270508.authors: Olsen EA, Katz HI, Levine N, et al.
pmid:9270508.title: Sustained improvement in photodamaged skin with reduced tretinoin emollient cream treatment regimen: effect of once-weekly and three-times-weekly applications
pmid:9270508.finding: After 48 weeks of daily tretinoin, three-times-weekly application maintained and sometimes further improved photodamage, once-weekly did so less well, and stopping led to partial regression.

pmid:11425807.authors: Pall M, Fridén BE, Brännström M
pmid:11425807.title: Induction of delayed follicular rupture in the human by the selective COX-2 inhibitor rofecoxib: a randomized double-blind study
pmid:11425807.finding: Periovulatory rofecoxib delayed follicular rupture beyond 48 h after the LH peak in 4 of 6 treated women, with no change in circulating hormones, and cycles were normal otherwise.

pmid:19400850.authors: Paradisi R, Vanella S, Barzanti R, et al.
pmid:19400850.title: Effects of indoor air purification by an air cleaning system (Koala technology) on semen parameters in male factor infertility: results of a pilot study
pmid:19400850.finding: A year of indoor air purification in men with unexplained infertility produced no improvement in semen parameters or reproductive hormones, with an unexplained rise in seminal leucocytes.

pmid:11401937.authors: Peters A, Dockery DW, Muller JE, et al.
pmid:11401937.title: Increased particulate air pollution and the triggering of myocardial infarction
pmid:11401937.finding: Case-crossover analysis found myocardial infarction risk raised by fine particles in the previous 2 hours (OR 1.48 per 25 ug/m3) and again by the 24-hour average one day before onset.

pmid:19164188.authors: Pope CA 3rd, Ezzati M, Dockery DW
pmid:19164188.title: Fine-particulate air pollution and life expectancy in the United States
pmid:19164188.n: 211 county units in 51 US metro areas
pmid:19164188.finding: A 10 ug/m3 fall in fine particulate matter between about 1980 and 2000 was associated with a 0.61-year gain in mean life expectancy, up to 15% of the overall gain.

pmid:27749441.authors: Randhawa M, Wang S, Leyden JJ, et al.
pmid:27749441.title: Daily Use of a Facial Broad Spectrum Sunscreen Over One-Year Significantly Improves Clinical Evaluation of Photoaging
pmid:27749441.finding: Daily SPF 30 broad-spectrum sunscreen improved all photoageing scores from week 12 onward, with 40-52% improvement in texture, clarity and pigmentation by week 52 (uncontrolled).

pmid:27015911.authors: Rangel-Zuñiga OA, Haro C, Tormos C, et al.
pmid:27015911.title: Frying oils with high natural or added antioxidants content, which protect against postprandial oxidative stress, also protect against DNA oxidation damage
pmid:27015911.finding: Breakfast fried in repeatedly heated sunflower oil raised DNA-repair gene expression and urinary 8-OHdG within the postprandial period, while virgin olive oil and antioxidant-enriched oils did not.

pmid:18046699.authors: Recio-Vega R, Ocampo-Gómez G, Borja-Aburto VH, et al.
pmid:18046699.title: Organophosphorus pesticide exposure decreases sperm quality: association between sperm parameters and urinary pesticide levels
pmid:18046699.finding: In a longitudinal follow-up, the most heavily organophosphate-exposed workers had the lowest total sperm counts, and sperm measures varied with season and changing exposure levels.

pmid:19362552.authors: Reimer C, Søndergaard B, Hilsted L, et al.
pmid:19362552.title: Proton-pump inhibitor therapy induces acid-related symptoms in healthy volunteers after withdrawal of therapy
pmid:19362552.finding: Eight weeks of esomeprazole produced clinically relevant acid-related symptoms in 21-22% of healthy volunteers in the 4 weeks after withdrawal versus 2-7% on placebo, consistent with rebound acid hypersecretion.

pmid:9463528.authors: Reistad R, Rossland OJ, Latva-Kala KJ, et al.
pmid:9463528.title: Heterocyclic aromatic amines in human urine following a fried meat meal
pmid:9463528.finding: After one fried-meat meal, heterocyclic amines appeared in urine and were largely excreted within 24 h, so these biomarkers reflect only the previous day's cooking.

pmid:26319518.title: Denmark's Policy on Artificial Trans Fat and Cardiovascular Disease
pmid:26319518.finding: In the 3 years after Denmark's 2004 artificial trans-fat regulation, cardiovascular mortality fell by about 14.2 deaths per 100,000 per year relative to a synthetic control.

pmid:28845751.authors: Ridker PM, Everett BM, Thuren T, et al.
pmid:28845751.title: Antiinflammatory Therapy with Canakinumab for Atherosclerotic Disease
pmid:28845751.finding: Canakinumab lowered CRP by 26-41 percentage points more than placebo and cut cardiovascular events by 15% at the 150 mg dose over a median 3.7 years, without changing lipids.

pmid:20934951.authors: Ritter R, Scheringer M, MacLeod M, et al.
pmid:20934951.title: Intrinsic human elimination half-lives of polychlorinated biphenyls derived from the temporal evolution of cross-sectional biomonitoring data from the United Kingdom
pmid:20934951.finding: Modelling UK biomonitoring data gave intrinsic human elimination half-lives of 15.5 years for PCB-170, 14.4 for PCB-153 and 11.5 for PCB-180, suggesting a ceiling of roughly 10-15 years.

pmid:15210526.authors: Rundek T, Naini A, Sacco R, et al.
pmid:15210526.title: Atorvastatin decreases the coenzyme Q10 level in the blood of patients at risk for cardiovascular disease and stroke
pmid:15210526.finding: Atorvastatin 80 mg/day halved blood coenzyme Q10 (1.26 to 0.62 ug/mL) by 30 days, with a significant fall already detectable at 14 days.

pmid:40886599.authors: Russo LM, Pilsner JR, Canty TP, et al.
pmid:40886599.title: Ambient air pollution during developmental windows of spermatogenesis and semen quality among an infertility treatment seeking population
pmid:40886599.finding: Across the 74-day spermatogenesis window, ozone during meiosis and spermiogenesis was associated with lower normal morphology, while PM2.5 and ozone during spermiation were associated with lower count, concentration and motility.

pmid:17210875.authors: Selvin E, Paynter NP, Erlinger TP
pmid:17210875.title: The effect of weight loss on C-reactive protein: a systematic review
pmid:17210875.finding: Across lifestyle and surgical weight-loss studies, each kilogram lost was associated with a 0.13 mg/L fall in CRP, in a roughly linear relationship.

pmid:21465828.authors: Shetty KD, DeLeire T, White C, et al.
pmid:21465828.title: Changes in U.S. hospitalization and mortality rates following smoking bans
pmid:21465828.n: US national hospitalization and mortality data
pmid:21465828.finding: Using nationally representative data, smoking bans were not associated with significant short-term falls in myocardial infarction admissions or mortality, and subsampling showed large apparent increases were as common as the published decreases.

pmid:35420698.authors: Simpson TC, Clarkson JE, Worthington HV, et al.
pmid:35420698.title: Treatment of periodontitis for glycaemic control in people with diabetes mellitus
pmid:35420698.finding: Cochrane review: treating periodontitis lowered HbA1c by 0.43 percentage points at 3-4 months, 0.30 at 6 months and 0.50 at 12 months in people with diabetes (moderate certainty).

pmid:7981177.authors: Staprãns I, Rapp JH, Pan XM, et al.
pmid:7981177.title: Oxidized lipids in the diet are a source of oxidized lipid in chylomicrons of human serum
pmid:7981177.finding: Feeding oxidized oil raised conjugated dienes in postprandial chylomicrons 4.7-fold and made the chylomicrons more susceptible to further oxidation, showing dietary oxidized lipids enter the circulation within hours.

pmid:14600072.authors: Strawford A, Antelo F, Christiansen M, et al.
pmid:14600072.title: Adipose tissue triglyceride turnover, de novo lipogenesis, and cell proliferation in humans measured with 2H2O
pmid:14600072.finding: Heavy-water labelling gave an adipose triglyceride half-life of 200-270 days and adipocyte half-life of 240-425 days, with de novo lipogenesis contributing about 20% of new triglyceride.

pmid:30193113.authors: Suez J, Zmora N, Zilberman-Schapira G, et al.
pmid:30193113.title: Post-Antibiotic Gut Mucosal Microbiome Reconstitution Is Impaired by Probiotics and Improved by Autologous FMT
pmid:30193113.finding: After antibiotics, probiotics delayed and left incomplete the recovery of the indigenous mucosal microbiome, whereas autologous faecal transplant restored it within days.

pmid:32678738.authors: Sun S, Zhao J, Cao W, et al.
pmid:32678738.title: Identifying critical exposure windows for ambient air pollution and semen quality in Chinese men
pmid:32678738.finding: Distributed-lag modelling put the critical windows at sperm-development weeks 6-12 for PM10, 10-11 for ozone and 0-5 for SO2, with large falls in sperm concentration and count per interquartile rise in PM10.

pmid:19330585.authors: Suwazono Y, Kido T, Nakagawa H, et al.
pmid:19330585.title: Biological half-life of cadmium in the urine of inhabitants after cessation of cadmium exposure
pmid:19330585.finding: Over 24 years of follow-up after cadmium pollution stopped, urinary cadmium fell with an estimated half-life of 13.6-14.2 years in men and 13.9-23.5 years in women.

pmid:22062584.authors: Tellez-Plaza M, Navas-Acien A, Caldwell KL, et al.
pmid:22062584.title: Reduction in cadmium exposure in the United States population, 1988-2008: the contribution of declining smoking rates
pmid:22062584.finding: Urinary cadmium, a marker of cumulative body burden, fell substantially in US adults between 1988 and 2008, and declining smoking explained a large part of the drop.

pmid:17329698.authors: Tonetti MS, D'Aiuto F, Nibali L, et al.
pmid:17329698.title: Treatment of periodontitis and endothelial function
pmid:17329698.finding: Intensive periodontal treatment worsened flow-mediated dilation and raised inflammatory markers at 24 hours, then improved endothelial function by 0.9% at 60 days and 2.0% at 180 days versus control care.

pmid:17132769.authors: van der Pols JC, Williams GM, Pandeya N, et al.
pmid:17132769.title: Prolonged prevention of squamous cell carcinoma of the skin by regular sunscreen use
pmid:17132769.finding: Eight years after the sunscreen trial ended, squamous-cell carcinoma rates remained almost 40% lower in the former daily-sunscreen group, with no effect on basal-cell carcinoma.

pmid:30535398.authors: Wang Z, Bergeron N, Levison BS, et al.
pmid:30535398.title: Impact of chronic dietary red meat, white meat, or non-meat protein on trimethylamine N-oxide metabolism and renal excretion in healthy men and women
pmid:30535398.finding: Four weeks of red meat raised plasma and urinary TMAO about three-fold through more precursor, more microbial production and less renal excretion, and stopping red meat brought TMAO down within 4 weeks.

pmid:10091835.authors: Williams MJ, Sutherland WH, McCormick MP, et al.
pmid:10091835.title: Impaired endothelial function following a meal rich in used cooking fat
pmid:10091835.finding: A meal rich in cooking fat taken from a fast-food fryer cut flow-mediated dilation from 5.9% to 0.8% at 4 h, while the same meal with unused fat and a low-fat meal did not.

pmid:11590989.authors: Williams MJ, Sutherland WH, McCormick MP, et al.
pmid:11590989.title: Normal endothelial function after meals rich in olive or safflower oil previously used for deep frying
pmid:11590989.finding: Meals rich in olive or safflower oil used for 8 hours of deep frying raised postprandial triglycerides but did not impair endothelial function, contradicting the earlier used-fat finding.

pmid:17365039.title: The big ban on bituminous coal sales revisited: serious epidemics and pronounced trends feign excess mortality previously attributed to heavy black-smoke exposure
pmid:17365039.finding: Reanalysis argued that pre-ban influenza epidemics and the underlying downward mortality trend account for the Dublin coal-ban mortality drop, and that black-smoke changes alone showed no effect in non-epidemic seasons.

pmid:36731563.authors: Xu R, Zhong Y, Li R, et al.
pmid:36731563.title: Association between exposure to ambient air pollution and semen quality: A systematic review and meta-analysis
pmid:36731563.finding: Each 10 ug/m3 of PM10 or SO2 was associated with roughly 2-9% lower sperm concentration and total count, and PM2.5 and PM10 with small falls in motility, with no association for most gaseous pollutants.

pmid:22293416.authors: Yaginuma-Sakurai K, Murata K, Iwai-Shimada M, et al.
pmid:22293416.title: Hair-to-blood ratio and biological half-life of mercury: experimental study of methylmercury exposure through fish consumption in humans
pmid:22293416.finding: Volunteers ate fish to the tolerable weekly methylmercury intake for 14 weeks then washed out for 15 weeks; blood mercury half-life was 94 days crude (57 days after subtracting background) and hair 102 days.

pmid:33196766.authors: Yourman LC, Cenzer IS, Boscardin WJ, et al.
pmid:33196766.title: Evaluation of Time to Benefit of Statins for the Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Events in Adults Aged 50 to 75 Years: A Meta-analysis
pmid:33196766.finding: Survival meta-analysis: 2.5 years of statin treatment were needed to prevent one major adverse cardiovascular event per 100 adults aged 50-75, and only 0.8 years to prevent one per 500.

pmid:24252845.authors: Flock MR, Skulas-Ray AC, Harris WS, et al.
pmid:24252845.title: Determinants of erythrocyte omega-3 fatty acid content in response to fish oil supplementation: a dose-response randomized controlled trial.
pmid:24252845.finding: Over about 5 months of 0-1800 mg/day EPA+DHA the omega-3 index rose in a dose-dependent way; dose per kg body weight explained about 70% of the response.

pmid:22932281.authors: Browning LM, Walker CG, Mander AP, et al.
pmid:22932281.title: Incorporation of eicosapentaenoic and docosahexaenoic acids into lipid pools when given as supplements providing doses equivalent to typical intakes of oily fish.
pmid:22932281.finding: EPA/DHA given as if oily fish were eaten 1, 2 or 4 times a week produced dose responses; time to maximal incorporation ranged from days (plasma phosphatidylcholine) to months (mononuclear cells) to more than 12 months (adipose).

pmid:17053155.authors: Cao J, Schwichtenberg KA, Hanson NQ, et al.
pmid:17053155.title: Incorporation and clearance of omega-3 fatty acids in erythrocyte membranes and plasma phospholipids.
pmid:17053155.finding: 8 weeks of fish oil (2.2 g/day EPA+DHA) raised red-cell EPA 300% and DHA 42% (omega-3 index 7.8%); the index stayed relatively high 4 weeks after stopping, while plasma levels fell faster.

pmid:26500082.authors: Patterson AC, Chalil A, Aristizabal Henao JJ, et al.
pmid:26500082.title: Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid blood biomarkers increase linearly in men and women after tightly controlled intakes of 0.25, 0.5, and 1 g/d of EPA + DHA.
pmid:26500082.finding: Blood EPA+DHA rose linearly with 0.25, 0.5 and 1 g/day given in successive 4-week periods.

pmid:10757545.authors: Conquer JA, Martin JB, Tummon I, et al.
pmid:10757545.title: Effect of DHA supplementation on DHA status and sperm motility in asthenozoospermic males.
pmid:10757545.finding: Three months of 400-800 mg/day DHA raised serum DHA 71-131% but did not change sperm phospholipid DHA or motility in asthenozoospermic men.

pmid:18689406.title: Pharmacokinetics of vitamin D toxicity.
pmid:18689406.finding: Vitamin D itself has a body half-life of about 2 months (adipose storage), circulating 25(OH)D3 about 15 days, and 1,25(OH)2D about 15 hours.

pmid:24885631.authors: Jones KS, Assar S, Harnpanich D, et al.
pmid:24885631.title: 25(OH)D2 half-life is shorter than 25(OH)D3 half-life and is influenced by DBP concentration and genotype.
pmid:24885631.finding: Stable-isotope tracer: plasma 25(OH)D3 half-life 15.1 days and 25(OH)D2 13.9 days, longer with higher vitamin D binding protein.

pmid:12499343.authors: Heaney RP, Davies KM, Chen TC, et al.
pmid:12499343.title: Human serum 25-hydroxycholecalciferol response to extended oral dosing with cholecalciferol.
pmid:12499343.finding: Over about 20 winter weeks of 0-250 ug/day cholecalciferol, equilibrium 25(OH)D rose about 0.7 nmol/L per ug/day; tissue stores from summer sun supplied about 80 ug/day.

pmid:18544622.authors: Ish-Shalom S, Segal E, Salganik T, et al.
pmid:18544622.title: Comparison of daily, weekly, and monthly vitamin D3 in ethanol dosing protocols for two months in elderly hip fracture patients.
pmid:18544622.finding: 1500 IU daily, 10,500 IU weekly or 45,000 IU every 28 days gave similar 25(OH)D after 2 months; all rose by day 7, but only the monthly dose spiked 25(OH)D and 1,25(OH)2D the next day.

pmid:20460620.authors: Sanders KM, Stuart AL, Williamson EJ, et al.
pmid:20460620.title: Annual high-dose oral vitamin D and falls and fractures in older women: a randomized controlled trial.
pmid:20460620.finding: A single annual 500,000 IU oral dose raised falls (RR 1.15) and fractures (RR 1.26); falls were most increased in the first 3 months after dosing (RR 1.31); 25(OH)D was about 120 nmol/L at 1 month, 90 at 3 months and still above placebo at 12 months.

pmid:26747333.authors: Bischoff-Ferrari HA, Dawson-Hughes B, Orav EJ, et al.
pmid:26747333.title: Monthly High-Dose Vitamin D Treatment for the Prevention of Functional Decline: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
pmid:26747333.finding: Monthly 60,000 IU, or 24,000 IU plus calcifediol, reached higher 25(OH)D than 24,000 IU but did not improve leg function and increased falls (67% vs 48%).

pmid:28202713.authors: Martineau AR, Jolliffe DA, Hooper RL, et al.
pmid:28202713.title: Vitamin D supplementation to prevent acute respiratory tract infections: systematic review and meta-analysis of individual participant data.
pmid:28202713.finding: Vitamin D cut acute respiratory infections overall (OR 0.88); protection was seen with daily or weekly dosing (OR 0.81) but not when bolus doses were given (OR 0.97).

pmid:33798465.authors: Jolliffe DA, Camargo CA Jr, Sluyter JD, et al.
pmid:33798465.title: Vitamin D supplementation to prevent acute respiratory infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis of aggregate data from randomised controlled trials.
pmid:33798465.finding: Small overall protection against respiratory infection (OR 0.92); daily dosing was protective (OR 0.78) but the formal test for interaction by dosing frequency was not significant.

pmid:39993397.authors: Jolliffe DA, Camargo CA Jr, Sluyter JD, et al.
pmid:39993397.title: Vitamin D supplementation to prevent acute respiratory infections: systematic review and meta-analysis of stratified aggregate data.
pmid:39993397.finding: After adding new large trials the overall effect on respiratory infection was no longer significant (OR 0.94) and there was no effect modification by dosing frequency.

pmid:24106283.title: Clinical review: The role of the parent compound vitamin D with respect to metabolism and function: Why clinical dose intervals can affect clinical outcomes.
pmid:24106283.finding: Argues that parent vitamin D has a short circulating half-life and acts as tissue substrate, so daily dosing giving stable levels may work better than large intermittent doses.

pmid:35676320.authors: Keum N, Chen QY, Lee DH, et al.
pmid:35676320.title: Vitamin D supplementation and total cancer incidence and mortality by daily vs. infrequent large-bolus dosing strategies: a meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
pmid:35676320.finding: Daily vitamin D reduced total cancer mortality (SRR 0.87), whereas infrequent large-bolus dosing did not.

pmid:35026158.authors: Neale RE, Baxter C, Romero BD, et al.
pmid:35026158.title: The D-Health Trial: a randomised controlled trial of the effect of vitamin D on mortality.
pmid:35026158.finding: Monthly 60,000 IU for 5 years did not reduce mortality (HR 1.04); excluding the first 2 years, cancer mortality was numerically higher (HR 1.24).

pmid:37380191.authors: Thompson B, Waterhouse M, English DR, et al.
pmid:37380191.title: Vitamin D supplementation and major cardiovascular events: D-Health randomised controlled trial.
pmid:37380191.finding: Monthly 60,000 IU for up to 5 years gave a borderline reduction in major cardiovascular events (HR 0.91, 0.81-1.01) and fewer myocardial infarctions (HR 0.81).

pmid:16551570.title: Coenzyme Q10: absorption, tissue uptake, metabolism and pharmacokinetics.
pmid:16551570.finding: Oral CoQ10 is absorbed slowly; Tmax about 6 h and elimination half-life about 33 h; large doses reach all tissues in animals.

pmid:3781673.authors: Tomono Y, Hasegawa J, Seki T, et al.
pmid:3781673.title: Pharmacokinetic study of deuterium-labelled coenzyme Q10 in man.
pmid:3781673.journal: Int J Clin Pharmacol Ther Toxicol
pmid:3781673.finding: Deuterium-labelled CoQ10 peaked at 6.5 h with a second peak at 24 h (liver/VLDL redistribution) and a terminal half-life of 33 h.

pmid:30823449.authors: Martucci A, Reurean-Pintilei D, Manole A
pmid:30823449.title: Bioavailability and Sustained Plasma Concentrations of CoQ10 in Healthy Volunteers by a Novel Oral Timed-Release Preparation.
pmid:30823449.finding: With 100 mg once or twice daily, plasma CoQ10 rose for about 7 days and then stayed high through 4 weeks of dosing.

pmid:16431002.authors: Ikematsu H, Nakamura K, Harashima S, et al.
pmid:16431002.title: Safety assessment of coenzyme Q10 (Kaneka Q10) in healthy subjects: a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial.
pmid:16431002.finding: 300-900 mg/day for 4 weeks was safe; plasma CoQ10 measured 8 months after stopping was back to pre-treatment levels.

pmid:420145.authors: Kallner A, Hartmann D, Hornig D
pmid:420145.title: Steady-state turnover and body pool of ascorbic acid in man.
pmid:420145.finding: Radiolabel study: the half-life of ascorbic acid shortened as intake rose, and the body pool reached about 20 mg/kg at about 100 mg/day.

pmid:15749381.authors: Leonard SW, Paterson E, Atkinson JK, et al.
pmid:15749381.title: Studies in humans using deuterium-labeled alpha- and gamma-tocopherols demonstrate faster plasma gamma-tocopherol disappearance and greater gamma-metabolite production.
pmid:15749381.finding: Deuterium-labelled tocopherols: plasma alpha-tocopherol half-life 57 h vs 13 h for gamma-tocopherol.

pmid:9537614.authors: Burton GW, Traber MG, Acuff RV, et al.
pmid:9537614.title: Human plasma and tissue alpha-tocopherol concentrations in response to supplementation with deuterated natural and synthetic vitamin E.
pmid:9537614.finding: Labelled vitamin E made up a smaller share of tissue than plasma vitamin E after up to 41 days of dosing; after 361-615 days tissue and plasma shares were similar.

pmid:8172086.authors: Handelman GJ, Epstein WL, Peerson J, et al.
pmid:8172086.title: Human adipose alpha-tocopherol and gamma-tocopherol kinetics during and after 1 y of alpha-tocopherol supplementation.
pmid:8172086.finding: Adipose alpha/gamma-tocopherol ratio rose through 1 year of 800 mg/day and fell only gradually over the following year; at least 2 years needed to reach a new steady state.

pmid:11481400.authors: Burri BJ, Neidlinger TR, Clifford AJ
pmid:11481400.title: Serum carotenoid depletion follows first-order kinetics in healthy adult women fed naturally low carotenoid diets.
pmid:11481400.finding: On low-carotenoid diets serum carotenoids fell by first-order kinetics with half-lives of 76 days (lutein), 37-45 days (beta-carotene, alpha-carotene, cryptoxanthin, zeaxanthin) and 26 days (lycopene).

pmid:25008856.authors: Jahns L, Johnson LK, Mayne ST, et al.
pmid:25008856.title: Skin and plasma carotenoid response to a provided intervention diet high in vegetables and fruit: uptake and depletion kinetics.
pmid:25008856.finding: Skin and plasma carotenoids rose more than 200% after 8 weeks of a high vegetable-fruit diet; plasma returned to baseline about 3 weeks into a low-carotenoid phase, skin only about 10 weeks after the high phase ended.

pmid:15309451.authors: Cohn W, Thürmann P, Tenter U, et al.
pmid:15309451.title: Comparative multiple dose plasma kinetics of lycopene administered in tomato juice, tomato soup or lycopene tablets.
pmid:15309451.finding: 20 mg/day lycopene for 8 days raised plasma lycopene; effective half-lives were about 5 days (all-E) and 9 days (5-Z).

pmid:12867539.authors: Diwadkar-Navsariwala V, Novotny JA, Gustin DM, et al.
pmid:12867539.title: A physiological pharmacokinetic model describing the disposition of lycopene in healthy men.
pmid:12867539.finding: Single lycopene doses of 10-120 mg were absorbed to a similar absolute amount (about 4.7 mg), suggesting saturable absorption; slow-turnover tissues acted as a slowly depleting reservoir.

pmid:12876090.authors: Virtamo J, Pietinen P, Huttunen JK, et al.
pmid:12876090.title: Incidence of cancer and mortality following alpha-tocopherol and beta-carotene supplementation: a postintervention follow-up.
pmid:12876090.finding: In ATBC the excess lung cancer and mortality from beta-carotene was no longer evident 4-6 years after supplementation stopped.

pmid:15572756.authors: Goodman GE, Thornquist MD, Balmes J, et al.
pmid:15572756.title: The Beta-Carotene and Retinol Efficacy Trial: incidence of lung cancer and cardiovascular disease mortality during 6-year follow-up after stopping beta-carotene and retinol supplements.
pmid:15572756.finding: In CARET the excess lung cancer and all-cause mortality persisted (RR 1.12 and 1.08, no longer significant) through 6 years after stopping, while excess cardiovascular mortality returned to 1.0 rapidly.

pmid:20573787.authors: Xia Y, Hill KE, Li P, et al.
pmid:20573787.title: Optimization of selenoprotein P and other plasma selenium biomarkers for the assessment of the selenium nutritional requirement: a placebo-controlled, double-blind study of selenomethionine supplementation in selenium-deficient Chinese subjects.
pmid:20573787.finding: Over 40 weeks of selenomethionine, selenoprotein P was optimised by about 49 ug/day total intake; plasma selenium itself never plateaued.

pmid:16614127.authors: Burk RF, Norsworthy BK, Hill KE, et al.
pmid:16614127.title: Effects of chemical form of selenium on plasma biomarkers in a high-dose human supplementation trial.
pmid:16614127.finding: Selenomethionine and selenium yeast raised plasma selenium dose-dependently over 16 weeks while selenite did not; selenoprotein P and GPx did not respond in replete people.

pmid:19420098.authors: Lowe NM, Fekete K, Decsi T
pmid:19420098.title: Methods of assessment of zinc status in humans: a systematic review.
pmid:19420098.finding: Plasma, urinary and hair zinc respond to changes in zinc intake; cell zinc measures do not.

pmid:9400511.authors: Daly S, Mills JL, Molloy AM, et al.
pmid:9400511.title: Minimum effective dose of folic acid for food fortification to prevent neural-tube defects.
pmid:9400511.finding: Six months of 100, 200 or 400 ug/day extra folic acid raised red-cell folate by a median 67, 130 and 200 ug/L.

pmid:25073783.authors: Crider KS, Devine O, Hao L, et al.
pmid:25073783.title: Population red blood cell folate concentrations for prevention of neural tube defects: Bayesian model.
pmid:25073783.finding: Neural tube defect risk fell as red-cell folate at neural tube closure (day 28 of gestation) rose, levelling off above about 1000 nmol/L.

pmid:26289639.authors: Moretti D, Goede JS, Zeder C, et al.
pmid:26289639.title: Oral iron supplements increase hepcidin and decrease iron absorption from daily or twice-daily doses in iron-depleted young women.
pmid:26289639.finding: Doses of 60 mg iron or more raised hepcidin 24 h later and cut absorption of the next day's dose by 35-45%; twice-daily dosing added little.

pmid:31413088.authors: Stoffel NU, Zeder C, Brittenham GM, et al.
pmid:31413088.title: Iron absorption from supplements is greater with alternate day than with consecutive day dosing in iron-deficient anemic women.
pmid:31413088.finding: Even in anaemia, 100-200 mg iron raised hepcidin for 24 h; absorption on alternate days was 40-50% higher than on the second consecutive day.

pmid:36725875.authors: Pasupathy E, Kandasamy R, Thomas K, et al.
pmid:36725875.title: Alternate day versus daily oral iron for treatment of iron deficiency anemia: a randomized controlled trial.
pmid:36725875.finding: 120 mg iron on alternate days and 60 mg daily raised haemoglobin similarly over 8 weeks.

pmid:40841680.authors: Dhanvijay AD, Patidar V, Singh J, et al.
pmid:40841680.title: Efficacy of daily versus alternate day oral iron supplementation for management of anaemia among general population: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:40841680.finding: Daily and alternate-day oral iron were comparably effective for anaemia (Hb MD 0.28 g/dL favouring daily, not significant), with alternate-day somewhat better tolerated; very low certainty.

pmid:25668261.authors: Kiss JE, Brambilla D, Glynn SA, et al.
pmid:25668261.title: Oral iron supplementation after blood donation: a randomized clinical trial.
pmid:25668261.finding: After one donation, 37.5 mg/day iron cut time to 80% haemoglobin recovery to about 32 days (vs 78-158 without); without iron 67% had not recovered iron stores by 168 days.

pmid:32243609.authors: Mast AE, Szabo A, Stone M, et al.
pmid:32243609.title: The benefits of iron supplementation following blood donation vary with baseline iron status.
pmid:32243609.finding: Iron supplements sped recovery mainly when ferritin was below 50 ng/mL; full recovery from donation took more than 100 days even with iron.

pmid:27402922.authors: Zhang X, Li Y, Del Gobbo LC, et al.
pmid:27402922.title: Effects of Magnesium Supplementation on Blood Pressure: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Double-Blind Placebo-Controlled Trials.
pmid:27402922.finding: Magnesium (median 368 mg/day, median 3 months) lowered BP by about 2/1.8 mmHg; 300 mg/day or 1 month was enough to raise serum magnesium and lower BP.

pmid:2029805.title: Clinical pharmacokinetics of N-acetylcysteine.
pmid:2029805.finding: Oral NAC peaks in plasma within 1-2 h and has a terminal half-life of about 6 h.

pmid:21875351.title: Effects of oral glutathione supplementation on systemic oxidative stress biomarkers in human volunteers.
pmid:21875351.finding: Oral glutathione 1 g/day for 4 weeks did not change glutathione status or oxidative-stress markers.

pmid:16224142.authors: Hong SY, Gil HW, Yang JO, et al.
pmid:16224142.title: Pharmacokinetics of glutathione and its metabolites in normal subjects.
pmid:16224142.finding: Kinetic modelling after IV glutathione suggested redosing every 205-427 minutes to keep its cysteine and methionine metabolites above target levels.

pmid:8828669.authors: Hultman E, Söderlund K, Timmons JA, et al.
pmid:8828669.title: Muscle creatine loading in men.
pmid:8828669.finding: 20 g/day for 6 days raised muscle creatine about 20%, as did 3 g/day over 28 days; after stopping, muscle creatine was back to baseline by 30 days.

pmid:1327657.authors: Harris RC, Söderlund K, Hultman E
pmid:1327657.title: Elevation of creatine in resting and exercised muscle of normal subjects by creatine supplementation.
pmid:1327657.finding: Creatine uptake into muscle was greatest in the first 2 days of high-dose supplementation and largest in people with low starting levels.

pmid:22331997.authors: Ghandforoush-Sattari M, Mashayekhi S, Krishna CV, et al.
pmid:22331997.title: Pharmacokinetics of oral taurine in healthy volunteers.
pmid:22331997.finding: 4 g oral taurine peaked in plasma at 1.5 h with an elimination half-life of about 1 h.

pmid:18583380.authors: Galloway SD, Talanian JL, Shoveller AK, et al.
pmid:18583380.title: Seven days of oral taurine supplementation does not increase muscle taurine content or alter substrate metabolism during prolonged exercise in humans.
pmid:18583380.finding: 5 g/day taurine for 7 days produced large plasma peaks but did not raise muscle taurine content.

pmid:15591001.title: Kinetics, pharmacokinetics, and regulation of L-carnitine and acetyl-L-carnitine metabolism.
pmid:15591001.finding: Oral L-carnitine supplements are 14-18% bioavailable; whole-body carnitine turnover is 38-119 h, mostly in a large slow muscle pool, and high plasma levels are cleared rapidly by the kidney.

pmid:21224234.authors: Wall BT, Stephens FB, Constantin-Teodosiu D, et al.
pmid:21224234.title: Chronic oral ingestion of L-carnitine and carbohydrate increases muscle carnitine content and alters muscle fuel metabolism during exercise in humans.
pmid:21224234.finding: 2 g L-carnitine plus 80 g carbohydrate twice daily raised muscle carnitine 21%, with all significant effects seen only after 24 weeks.

pmid:12568837.authors: Lenzi A, Lombardo F, Sgrò P, et al.
pmid:12568837.title: Use of carnitine therapy in selected cases of male factor infertility: a double-blind crossover trial.
pmid:12568837.finding: Crossover with 2-month washout and 2-month treatment periods: L-carnitine 2 g/day improved sperm concentration and motility more than placebo.

pmid:15193480.authors: Lenzi A, Sgrò P, Salacone P, et al.
pmid:15193480.title: A placebo-controlled double-blind randomized trial of the use of combined l-carnitine and l-acetyl-carnitine treatment in men with asthenozoospermia.
pmid:15193480.finding: L-carnitine 2 g plus acetyl-L-carnitine 1 g daily for 6 months improved sperm motility, most in men with the lowest baseline values.

pmid:19131472.authors: Baguet A, Reyngoudt H, Pottier A, et al.
pmid:19131472.title: Carnosine loading and washout in human skeletal muscles.
pmid:19131472.finding: After 5-6 weeks of beta-alanine, muscle carnosine fell only 2-4% per week, returning to baseline in 6-15 weeks.

pmid:29211728.authors: Airhart SE, Shireman LM, Risler LJ, et al.
pmid:29211728.title: An open-label, non-randomized study of the pharmacokinetics of the nutritional supplement nicotinamide riboside (NR) and its effects on blood NAD+ levels in healthy volunteers.
pmid:29211728.finding: NR titrated to 1000 mg twice daily doubled whole-blood NAD+ by day 9.

pmid:37111071.authors: Senekowitsch S, Wietkamp E, Grimm M, et al.
pmid:37111071.title: High-Dose Spermidine Supplementation Does Not Increase Spermidine Levels in Blood Plasma and Saliva of Healthy Adults: A Randomized Placebo-Controlled Pharmacokinetic and Metabolomic Study.
pmid:37111071.finding: 15 mg/day spermidine for 5 days raised plasma spermine but not spermidine.

pmid:18716159.authors: Egert S, Wolffram S, Bosy-Westphal A, et al.
pmid:18716159.title: Daily quercetin supplementation dose-dependently increases plasma quercetin concentrations in healthy humans.
pmid:18716159.finding: 50-150 mg/day quercetin for 2 weeks raised fasting plasma quercetin dose-dependently (up to 570%) without changing oxidative or inflammatory markers.

pmid:11361045.authors: Graefe EU, Wittig J, Mueller S, et al.
pmid:11361045.title: Pharmacokinetics and bioavailability of quercetin glycosides in humans.
pmid:11361045.finding: Quercetin glucosides peaked in plasma at about 0.7 h (rutin 4-7 h) and had a terminal half-life of about 11 h.

pmid:36304817.authors: Krishnakumar IM, Jaja-Chimedza A, Joseph A, et al.
pmid:36304817.title: Enhanced bioavailability and pharmacokinetics of a novel hybrid-hydrogel formulation of fisetin orally administered in healthy individuals: a randomised double-blinded comparative crossover study.
pmid:36304817.finding: Unformulated 1000 mg fisetin gave very low plasma levels over 12 h; a hydrogel formulation raised exposure about 27-fold.

pmid:10952480.authors: Peter C, Hongwan D, Küpfer A, et al.
pmid:10952480.title: Pharmacokinetics and organ distribution of intravenous and oral methylene blue.
pmid:10952480.finding: Methylene blue has a terminal blood half-life of about 5 h after IV dosing; oral dosing gave much lower blood exposure.

pmid:19652760.authors: Shimouchi A, Nose K, Yamaguchi M, et al.
pmid:19652760.title: Breath hydrogen produced by ingestion of commercial hydrogen water and milk.
pmid:19652760.finding: Hydrogen water raised breath hydrogen to a peak 10-15 minutes after drinking, then it rapidly fell back to baseline.

pmid:12885395.authors: Mercke Odeberg J, Lignell A, Pettersson A, et al.
pmid:12885395.title: Oral bioavailability of the antioxidant astaxanthin in humans is enhanced by incorporation of lipid based formulations.
pmid:12885395.finding: A single 40 mg astaxanthin dose had an elimination half-life of about 16 h; lipid formulations raised bioavailability 1.7-3.7-fold.

pmid:10072479.authors: Breithaupt-Grögler K, Niebch G, Schneider E, et al.
pmid:10072479.title: Dose-proportionality of oral thioctic acid--coincidence of assessments via pooled plasma and individual data.
pmid:10072479.finding: Oral alpha-lipoic acid (50-600 mg) peaked at 0.5-1 h and declined steeply with a half-life of about 0.5 h.

pmid:19403631.authors: Hoey L, McNulty H, Strain JJ
pmid:19403631.title: Studies of biomarker responses to intervention with riboflavin: a systematic review.
pmid:19403631.finding: EGRac and glutathione reductase activity respond to changes in riboflavin intake.

pmid:15867002.authors: Greco E, Iacobelli M, Rienzi L, et al.
pmid:15867002.title: Reduction of the incidence of sperm DNA fragmentation by oral antioxidant treatment.
pmid:15867002.finding: 1 g vitamin C plus 1 g vitamin E daily for 2 months reduced sperm DNA fragmentation (22% to 9%) vs no change on placebo.

pmid:18294328.authors: Imai H, Kotegawa T, Tsutsumi K, et al.
pmid:18294328.title: The recovery time-course of CYP3A after induction by St John's wort administration.
pmid:18294328.finding: After 14 days of St John's wort, CYP3A activity recovered with a half-life of about 46 h and was back to baseline about 7 days after stopping.

deep-timing-nutrients:tnut-ods2025b12.title: Vitamin B12: Fact Sheet for Health Professionals (updated July 2, 2025)
deep-timing-nutrients:tnut-ods2025b12.finding: The body stores about 1-5 mg of B12 (1000-2000 times daily intake), so deficiency symptoms can take several years to appear; B-vitamin trials of 1-2 years did not improve cognition.

pmid:6772801.title: Daily spermatozoal production and epididymal spermatozoal reserves of the human male
pmid:6772801.finding: Estimated transit through caput, corpus and cauda epididymidis at 0.72, 0.71 and 1.76 days; maturation in caput plus corpus takes under 2 days and human sperm reserves are small.

pmid:3207807.title: Effect of daily spermatozoan production but not age on transit time of spermatozoa through the human epididymis
pmid:3207807.finding: Epididymal transit time was shorter in men with higher daily sperm production and did not change with age.

pmid:22265039.authors: Ahmad G, Moinard N, Esquerré-Lamare C, et al.
pmid:22265039.title: Mild induced testicular and epididymal hyperthermia alters sperm chromatin integrity in men
pmid:22265039.finding: Raising testis/epididymis temperature by about 2 C for 15 h/day raised DFI by day 20 and HDS by day 34, before sperm output fell; all values returned to baseline 73 days after heating stopped.

pmid:32038961.authors: Abdelhamid MHM, Walschaerts M, Ahmad G, et al.
pmid:32038961.title: Mild experimental increase in testis and epididymis temperature in men: effects on sperm morphology according to spermatogenesis stages
pmid:32038961.finding: Mild sustained testicular and epididymal heating raised abnormal morphology from day 34 (multiple anomalies index from day 20), persisting to 45 days after heating and normalising by day 73; attributed mainly to impaired spermiogenesis and meiosis.

pmid:10975421.authors: Evenson DP, Jost LK, Corzett M, et al.
pmid:10975421.title: Characteristics of human sperm chromatin structure following an episode of influenza and high fever: a case study
pmid:10975421.finding: After a 1-day 39.9 C influenza fever, 36% of sperm had denatured DNA at day 18 and 23% at day 39; a protamine-2 precursor appeared at days 33-39 and almost vanished by day 52.

pmid:14507826.authors: Carlsen E, Andersson AM, Petersen JH, et al.
pmid:14507826.title: History of febrile illness and variation in semen quality
pmid:14507826.finding: Fever during meiosis or spermiogenesis lowered sperm concentration in later samples by about 33-35% (7-9% per fever day); fever during spermiogenesis also worsened morphology and motility.

pmid:25652627.authors: Rao M, Zhao XL, Yang J, et al.
pmid:25652627.title: Effect of transient scrotal hyperthermia on sperm parameters, seminal plasma biochemical markers, and oxidative stress in men
pmid:25652627.finding: Ten 30-min 43 C scrotal baths reversibly lowered concentration and motility and raised seminal malondialdehyde over a 16-week follow-up; in this report the every-third-day schedule lowered concentration more than daily baths.

pmid:15804867.title: Chromatin remodeling in spermatids: a sensitive step for the genetic integrity of the male gamete
pmid:15804867.finding: Transient DNA strand breaks appear in all elongating spermatids during chromatin remodelling; if not resealed they may persist into mature sperm.

pmid:25786204.authors: Muratori M, Tamburrino L, Marchiani S, et al.
pmid:25786204.title: Investigation on the Origin of Sperm DNA Fragmentation: Role of Apoptosis, Immaturity and Oxidative Stress
pmid:25786204.finding: Most DNA-fragmented sperm carried active caspases and excess histones, pointing to apoptosis triggered by defective chromatin maturation in the testis; oxidative damage tracked fragmentation mainly in live sperm.

pmid:26466911.authors: Gawecka JE, Boaz S, Kasperson K, et al.
pmid:26466911.title: Luminal fluid of epididymis and vas deferens contributes to sperm chromatin fragmentation
pmid:26466911.finding: In mice, luminal fluid from the epididymis and especially the vas deferens was needed to activate sperm chromatin fragmentation.

pmid:15539441.authors: Greco E, Scarselli F, Iacobelli M, et al.
pmid:15539441.title: Efficient treatment of infertility due to sperm DNA damage by ICSI with testicular spermatozoa
pmid:15539441.finding: Testicular sperm had markedly lower TUNEL DNA fragmentation than ejaculated sperm in men with high SDF; ICSI with testicular sperm gave 44% pregnancies versus 1 (miscarried) with ejaculated sperm.

pmid:19108827.authors: Moskovtsev SI, Jarvi K, Mullen JB, et al.
pmid:19108827.title: Testicular spermatozoa have statistically significantly lower DNA damage compared with ejaculated spermatozoa in patients with unsuccessful oral antioxidant treatment
pmid:19108827.finding: In men whose high SDF did not respond to antioxidants, testicular sperm had about one third of the DNA damage of same-day ejaculated sperm (13.3% vs 39.7%).

pmid:22432504.authors: Moskovtsev SI, Alladin N, Lo KC, et al.
pmid:22432504.title: A comparison of ejaculated and testicular spermatozoa aneuploidy rates in patients with high sperm DNA damage
pmid:22432504.finding: Testicular sperm had less DNA damage (14.9% vs 40.6%) but more than twice the aneuploidy (12.4% vs 5.8%) of ejaculated sperm from the same men.

pmid:23996278.authors: Pons I, Cercas R, Villas C, et al.
pmid:23996278.title: One abstinence day decreases sperm DNA fragmentation in 90 % of selected patients
pmid:23996278.n: 416 men screened, 35 with high SDF completed the protocol
pmid:23996278.finding: With 1-day abstinence, SDF normalised in 91% of men with high SDF within three attempts (81% at the first).

pmid:34759617.authors: Gupta S, Singh VJ, Fauzdar A, et al.
pmid:34759617.title: Short Ejaculatory Abstinence in Normozoospermic Men is Associated with Higher Clinical Pregnancy Rates in Sub-fertile Couples Undergoing Intra-Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection in Assisted Reproductive Technology: A Retrospective Analysis of 1691 Cycles
pmid:34759617.finding: One-day abstinence was linked to higher clinical pregnancy than longer abstinence (30.0% vs 25.4%) in normozoospermic men.

pmid:30169150.authors: Masterson TA, Greer AB, Ramasamy R
pmid:30169150.title: Time to improvement in semen parameters after microsurgical varicocelectomy in men with severe oligospermia
pmid:30169150.finding: After microsurgical varicocelectomy, total motile count rose from 1.5 to 7.3 million at 3-6 months and 12.2 million after 6 months, with no significant gain after 3-6 months.

pmid:39376021.authors: Wang L, Zheng L, Jiang H, et al.
pmid:39376021.title: Does Sperm DNA Fragmentation Index Continuously Decrease Over Time After Varicocelectomy in Varicocele-Induced Infertility? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmid:39376021.finding: After varicocelectomy, DFI fell by 3.7 points within 3 months, a further 1.5 points by 6 months, and did not fall significantly further by 12 months.

pmid:1730313.title: Deterioration of semen parameters over time in men with untreated varicocele: evidence of progressive testicular damage
pmid:1730313.finding: Men with untreated varicocele and initially normal semen showed significant deterioration when re-tested 9-96 months later.

pmid:19490779.authors: Tunc O, Thompson J, Tremellen K
pmid:19490779.title: Improvement in sperm DNA quality using an oral antioxidant therapy
pmid:19490779.finding: Three months of an oral antioxidant improved TUNEL DNA integrity and protamination and lowered seminal ROS, in an uncontrolled study.

pmid:34937665.authors: Donders GGG, Bosmans E, Reumers J, et al.
pmid:34937665.title: Sperm quality and absence of SARS-CoV-2 RNA in semen after COVID-19 infection: a prospective, observational study and validation of the SpermCOVID test
pmid:34937665.finding: After COVID-19, reduced motility was seen in 60% of men tested within a month, 37% at 1-2 months and 28% after 2 months; the authors estimate recovery takes about 3 months.

pmid:37307756.authors: Depuydt C, Bosmans E, Jonckheere J, et al.
pmid:37307756.title: SARS-CoV-2 infection reduces quality of sperm parameters: prospective one year follow-up study in 93 patients
pmid:37307756.finding: SARS-CoV-2 infection was followed by temporary declines in motility, morphology, DFI and concentration that mostly returned to baseline over a year of follow-up, at different speeds in different men.

pmid:36743823.authors: Stigliani S, Massarotti C, Bovis F, et al.
pmid:36743823.title: Semen parameters and male reproductive potential are not adversely affected after three or more months of recovery from COVID-19 disease
pmid:36743823.finding: Semen collected 3 or more months (mean 8 months) after COVID-19 did not differ from the same men's pre-infection samples.

pmid:23755953.authors: Bujan L, Walschaerts M, Moinard N, et al.
pmid:23755953.title: Impact of chemotherapy and radiotherapy for testicular germ cell tumors on spermatogenesis and sperm DNA: a multicenter prospective study from the CECOS network
pmid:23755953.finding: After testicular-cancer treatment, sperm values were lowest at 3-6 months; count recovered by 12 months after two or fewer BEP cycles but not after radiotherapy or more cycles.

pmid:25180491.authors: Paoli D, Gallo M, Rizzo F, et al.
pmid:25180491.title: Testicular cancer and sperm DNA damage: short- and long-term effects of antineoplastic treatment
pmid:25180491.n: testicular cancer patients (number not in abstract)
pmid:25180491.finding: DFI rose from 18% to 28% three months after treatment and 23% at six months, then improved to about 14% at 12-24 months.

pmid:18083744.authors: Tempest HG, Ko E, Chan P, et al.
pmid:18083744.title: Sperm aneuploidy frequencies analysed before and after chemotherapy in testicular cancer and Hodgkin's lymphoma patients
pmid:18083744.n: testicular cancer and Hodgkin lymphoma patients plus controls
pmid:18083744.finding: Sperm aneuploidy rose after chemotherapy, generally returned to pre-treatment levels by 18 months but persisted for some chromosomes up to 24 months.

pmid:15784814.title: Spermatogenesis after cancer treatment: damage and recovery
pmid:15784814.finding: After cisplatin chemotherapy about 50% of men recover spermatogenesis by 2 years and 80% by 5 years; testicular radiation of 0.2-0.7 Gy lowers counts transiently with recovery in 12-24 months.

pmid:7558380.authors: World Health Organization Task Force on Methods for the Regulation of Male Fertility
pmid:7558380.title: Rates of testosterone-induced suppression to severe oligozoospermia or azoospermia in two multinational clinical studies. World Health Organization Task force on Methods for The Regulations of Male Fertility
pmid:7558380.finding: Weekly 200 mg testosterone enanthate suppressed sperm to under 3 million/mL in 96-98% of men and to azoospermia in 67-89% within 6 months.

pmid:11836283.authors: McLachlan RI, O'Donnell L, Stanton PG, et al.
pmid:11836283.title: Effects of testosterone plus medroxyprogesterone acetate on semen quality, reproductive hormones, and germ cell populations in normal young men
pmid:11836283.finding: Testosterone (with or without DMPA) cut sperm counts to 10% of baseline in about 24 days, through blocked spermatogonial maturation and striking spermiation failure.

pmid:32030409.authors: Shankara-Narayana N, Yu C, Savkovic S, et al.
pmid:32030409.title: Rate and Extent of Recovery from Reproductive and Cardiac Dysfunction Due to Androgen Abuse in Men
pmid:32030409.finding: Past androgen abusers looked like non-users except for smaller testes; estimated recovery took 7-11 months for hormones and about 14 months for sperm output.

pmid:26283092.authors: Gundersen TD, Jørgensen N, Andersson AM, et al.
pmid:26283092.title: Association Between Use of Marijuana and Male Reproductive Hormones and Semen Quality: A Study Among 1,215 Healthy Young Men
pmid:26283092.finding: Marijuana more than once a week in the past 3 months was linked to 28% lower concentration and 29% lower total count; with other drugs, about 52-55% lower.

pmid:30726923.authors: Nassan FL, Arvizu M, Mínguez-Alarcón L, et al.
pmid:30726923.title: Marijuana smoking and markers of testicular function among men from a fertility centre
pmid:30726923.finding: Men who had ever smoked marijuana had higher sperm concentration and count than never-users; current and past users did not differ.

pmid:36990913.authors: Hedges JC, Hanna CB, Shorey-Kendrick LE, et al.
pmid:36990913.title: Cessation of chronic delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol use partially reverses impacts on male fertility and the sperm epigenome in rhesus macaques
pmid:36990913.finding: Daily THC shrank testes, lowered sex steroids and raised sperm DNA fragmentation; stopping THC gave partial recovery (testes back to 73% of original volume).

pmid:20117050.authors: Sermondade N, Elloumi H, Berthaut I, et al.
pmid:20117050.title: Progressive alcohol-induced sperm alterations leading to spermatogenic arrest, which was reversed after alcohol withdrawal
pmid:20117050.finding: Heavy drinking progressively led to azoospermia with pachytene arrest; after stopping alcohol, semen was normal within 3 months.

pmid:1123724.authors: Mendelson JH, Mendelson JE, Patch VD
pmid:1123724.title: Plasma testosterone levels in heroin addiction and during methadone maintenance
pmid:1123724.n: heroin and methadone users plus controls
pmid:1123724.finding: High-dose methadone (80-150 mg/day) and heroin lowered testosterone; low-dose methadone did not, and testosterone tracked dose during detoxification.

pmid:15483091.authors: Bliesener N, Albrecht S, Schwager A, et al.
pmid:15483091.title: Plasma testosterone and sexual function in men receiving buprenorphine maintenance for opioid dependence
pmid:15483091.finding: High-dose methadone users had much lower testosterone than buprenorphine users, whose levels matched healthy controls.

pmid:24389625.authors: Maleki BH, Tartibian B, Vaamonde D
pmid:24389625.title: The effects of 16 weeks of intensive cycling training on seminal oxidants and antioxidants in male road cyclists
pmid:24389625.finding: Sixteen weeks of intensive cycling raised seminal ROS and malondialdehyde and lowered antioxidants; they were still abnormal 30 days after training stopped (same author group has several retracted exercise-and-semen trials; read with caution).

pmid:35447437.authors: Li Y, Andersson A, Xu Y, et al.
pmid:35447437.title: Determinants of serum half-lives for linear and branched perfluoroalkyl substances after long-term high exposure-A study in Ronneby, Sweden
pmid:35447437.finding: Serum half-lives of PFAS after long-term high exposure ranged from about 0.9 years (PFPeS) to 5 years (branched PFOS); younger age and better kidney function shortened them.

pmid:32558890.authors: Holmboe SA, Priskorn L, Jensen TK, et al.
pmid:32558890.title: Use of e-cigarettes associated with lower sperm counts in a cross-sectional study of young men from the general population
pmid:32558890.finding: Daily e-cigarette users had lower total sperm count (91 vs 147 million) than non-users.

pmid:21866274.authors: O'Donnell L, Nicholls PK, O'Bryan MK, et al.
pmid:21866274.title: Spermiation: The process of sperm release
pmid:21866274.finding: Spermiation releases mature spermatids from Sertoli cells over several days; its failure, for example during hormonal suppression, lowers sperm counts and harms sperm quality.

pmid:19066291.authors: Safarinejad MR, Azma K, Kolahi AA
pmid:19066291.title: The effects of intensive, long-term treadmill running on reproductive hormones, hypothalamus-pituitary-testis axis, and semen quality: a randomized controlled study
pmid:19066291.finding: RETRACTED. A widely cited trial claiming intensive treadmill running harms semen; it must not be used as evidence.

pmid:26997174.authors: Stockwell T, Zhao J, Panwar S, et al.
pmid:26997174.title: Do "Moderate" Drinkers Have Reduced Mortality Risk? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Alcohol Consumption and All-Cause Mortality.
pmid:26997174.finding: Unadjusted data reproduced the J-curve (low-volume RR 0.86), but after adjusting for abstainer biases and study quality low-volume drinkers had no mortality benefit (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.88-1.07); former drinkers had raised risk (RR 1.22).

pmid:37000449.authors: Zhao J, Stockwell T, Naimi T, et al.
pmid:37000449.title: Association Between Daily Alcohol Intake and Risk of All-Cause Mortality: A Systematic Review and Meta-analyses.
pmid:37000449.finding: Versus lifetime non-drinkers, occasional (RR 0.96) and low-volume drinkers (1.3-24 g/day, RR 0.93) had no significant mortality reduction; risk rose at 45-64 g/day (RR 1.19) and 65+ g/day (RR 1.35).

pmid:30955975.authors: Millwood IY, Walters RG, Mei XW, et al.
pmid:30955975.title: Conventional and genetic evidence on alcohol and vascular disease aetiology: a prospective study of 500 000 men and women in China.
pmid:30955975.finding: Self-reported drinking showed U-shaped associations with stroke and MI, but genotype-predicted intake showed no U-shape: stroke risk rose log-linearly (ischaemic RR 1.27, haemorrhagic 1.58 per 280 g/week); MI was not associated.

pmid:25011450.authors: Holmes MV, Dale CE, Zuccolo L, et al.
pmid:25011450.title: Association between alcohol and cardiovascular disease: Mendelian randomisation analysis based on individual participant data.
pmid:25011450.n: Individual-participant data from studies with ADH1B genotype
pmid:25011450.finding: Carriers of the ADH1B variant drank 17% less alcohol and had lower blood pressure, BMI and coronary heart disease odds (OR 0.90), across all drinking categories, suggesting less alcohol is better even for light drinkers.

pmid:35333364.authors: Biddinger KJ, Emdin CA, Haas ME, et al.
pmid:35333364.title: Association of Habitual Alcohol Intake With Risk of Cardiovascular Disease.
pmid:35333364.finding: Light-moderate drinkers had healthier lifestyles, and adjusting for them attenuated apparent cardioprotection; genetically predicted higher intake raised hypertension (1.3-fold) and coronary disease (1.4-fold) per SD, with steeply rising risk at heavier intake.

pmid:38508868.authors: Kassaw NA, Zhou A, Mulugeta A, et al.
pmid:38508868.title: Alcohol consumption and the risk of all-cause and cause-specific mortality-a linear and nonlinear Mendelian randomization study.
pmid:38508868.finding: Conventional analysis was J-shaped, but Mendelian randomization showed a linear rise in mortality with genetically predicted intake (OR 1.27 per unit for all-cause mortality) and no protective dip.

pmid:36603913.authors: Anderson BO, Berdzuli N, Ilbawi A, et al.
pmid:36603913.title: Health and cancer risks associated with low levels of alcohol consumption.
pmid:36603913.finding: WHO staff commentary: no safe amount of alcohol for cancer and health can be established; in the EU in 2017 light-to-moderate drinking (<20 g/day) caused about 23,000 new cancers, about half of them breast cancers.

pmid:35843246.title: Population-level risks of alcohol consumption by amount, geography, age, sex, and year: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2020.
pmid:35843246.n: Global Burden of Disease 2020 analysis, 204 countries
pmid:35843246.finding: The theoretical minimum-risk intake was 0 to 0.6 drinks/day for ages 15-39, while for people 40+ the burden-weighted curve remained J-shaped in all regions (minimum-risk 0.1-1.9 drinks/day).

pmid:40393408.authors: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine; Health and Medicine Division; Food and Nutrition Board; Committee on Review of Evidence on Alcohol and Health, Stone KB, Calonge BN
pmid:40393408.title: Review of Evidence on Alcohol and Health.
pmid:40393408.finding: US National Academies committee review, commissioned for the Dietary Guidelines, of moderate alcohol intake and eight health outcomes including all-cause mortality, cancer and cardiovascular disease; it offers no dietary recommendations.

pmid:37651993.title: Violation of the Constant Genetic Effect Assumption Can Result in Biased Estimates for Non-Linear Mendelian Randomization.
pmid:37651993.finding: Methods paper showing that violation of the 'constant genetic effect' assumption can badly bias non-linear Mendelian randomization estimates from the residual method.

pmid:38789826.authors: Hamilton FW, Hughes DA, Spiller W, et al.
pmid:38789826.title: Non-linear Mendelian randomization: detection of biases using negative controls with a focus on BMI, Vitamin D and LDL cholesterol.
pmid:38789826.finding: Negative-control analyses found clearly biased non-linear MR estimates for BMI, vitamin D and LDL with both the residual and doubly-ranked methods; the doubly-ranked method failed to reproduce the trial-proven LDL-MI shape.

pmid:38749693.authors: Burgess S, Sun YQ, Zhou A, et al.
pmid:38749693.title: Body mass index and all-cause mortality in HUNT and UK biobank studies: revised non-linear Mendelian randomisation analyses.
pmid:38749693.finding: Revised non-linear MR (correcting an earlier J-shape built on a violated assumption) showed clear harm from higher BMI above 25 kg/m2; evidence that low BMI is harmful was weak and confined to BMI below 20.

pmid:30957776.authors: Sun YQ, Burgess S, Staley JR, et al.
pmid:30957776.title: Body mass index and all cause mortality in HUNT and UK Biobank studies: linear and non-linear mendelian randomisation analyses.
pmid:30957776.finding: Original residual-method non-linear MR reporting a J-shaped BMI-mortality relation with a nadir near 25 kg/m2; later reanalysed because its key assumption was violated.

pmid:27423262.authors: Global BMI Mortality Collaboration, Di Angelantonio E, Bhupathiraju ShN, et al.
pmid:27423262.title: Body-mass index and all-cause mortality: individual-participant-data meta-analysis of 239 prospective studies in four continents.
pmid:27423262.finding: Among 3.95 million never-smokers without chronic disease who survived 5 years, mortality was lowest at BMI 20-25 and rose log-linearly above 25 (HR 1.45 for BMI 30-35, 2.76 for 40-60), removing the apparent 'overweight paradox'.

pmid:36106800.authors: Horita N, Kato S, Utsunomiya D
pmid:36106800.title: Collider bias and the obesity paradox.
pmid:36106800.finding: Commentary arguing collider bias is one of the most plausible explanations for 'obesity paradoxes' and that meta-analyses inherit the bias.

pmid:35104295.authors: Venkatesh SS, Ferreira T, Benonisdottir S, et al.
pmid:35104295.title: Obesity and risk of female reproductive conditions: A Mendelian randomisation study.
pmid:35104295.n: up to 257,193 women (UK Biobank and GWAS)
pmid:35104295.finding: Mendelian randomization: genetically higher BMI and waist-hip ratio raised risk of PCOS, heavy menstrual bleeding, fibroids and pre-eclampsia; visceral fat mass was implicated.

pmid:23796131.authors: Look AHEAD Research Group, Wing RR, Bolin P, et al.
pmid:23796131.title: Cardiovascular effects of intensive lifestyle intervention in type 2 diabetes.
pmid:23796131.n: 5145 adults with type 2 diabetes and overweight
pmid:23796131.finding: An intensive lifestyle weight-loss programme (8.6% vs 0.7% loss at 1 year) did not reduce cardiovascular events over 9.6 years (HR 0.95, 0.83-1.09).

pmid:37952131.authors: Lincoff AM, Brown-Frandsen K, Colhoun HM, et al.
pmid:37952131.title: Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Obesity without Diabetes.
pmid:37952131.n: 17,604 adults with CVD and overweight/obesity without diabetes
pmid:37952131.finding: Semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly cut major cardiovascular events by 20% (6.5% vs 8.0%; HR 0.80) over ~40 months; 16.6% vs 8.2% stopped for adverse events.

pmid:33053284.authors: Carlsson LMS, Sjöholm K, Jacobson P, et al.
pmid:33053284.title: Life Expectancy after Bariatric Surgery in the Swedish Obese Subjects Study.
pmid:33053284.finding: In the prospective controlled Swedish Obese Subjects study, bariatric surgery lowered mortality (HR 0.77) and added about 3 years of life, though life expectancy stayed 5.5 years below the general population.

pmid:26666586.authors: Karvinen S, Waller K, Silvennoinen M, et al.
pmid:26666586.title: Physical activity in adulthood: genes and mortality.
pmid:26666586.n: Finnish twins plus rats bred for fitness
pmid:26666586.finding: The same genetic factors influenced activity, fitness and mortality; monozygotic twin pairs discordant for activity showed no mortality difference, and in rats bred for intrinsic fitness exercise did not extend life, suggesting genetic pleiotropy.

pmid:28642251.authors: Sabia S, Dugravot A, Dartigues JF, et al.
pmid:28642251.title: Physical activity, cognitive decline, and risk of dementia: 28 year follow-up of Whitehall II cohort study.
pmid:28642251.finding: Physical activity did not predict dementia over 27 years, but activity began to decline up to 9 years before diagnosis, illustrating how prodromal disease produces reverse causation.

pmid:33774696.authors: Bahls M, Leitzmann MF, Karch A, et al.
pmid:33774696.title: Physical activity, sedentary behavior and risk of coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction and ischemic stroke: a two-sample Mendelian randomization study.
pmid:33774696.finding: Genetically predicted self-reported or accelerometer-measured activity and sedentary behaviour were not associated with coronary disease, MI or ischaemic stroke.

pmid:41579440.authors: Han M, Qu Y, Zeng M, et al.
pmid:41579440.title: Associations of physical activity and sedentary behaviors with mortality: An observational analysis and Mendelian randomization study.
pmid:41579440.finding: Observationally, higher activity predicted lower and more sitting/TV higher mortality, but two-sample MR did not support causal effects of activity or sedentary behaviour on mortality.

pmid:39294593.authors: Zhao J, Ke Z, Huang R, et al.
pmid:39294593.title: Physical activity and the risk of developing 8 age-related diseases: epidemiological and Mendelian randomization studies.
pmid:39294593.finding: MR supported genetically higher vigorous activity lowering risk of angina, hypertension and type 2 diabetes.

pmid:32317632.authors: van de Vegte YJ, Said MA, Rienstra M, et al.
pmid:32317632.title: Genome-wide association studies and Mendelian randomization analyses for leisure sedentary behaviours.
pmid:32317632.n: UK Biobank GWAS plus two-sample MR
pmid:32317632.finding: Genetically predicted 1.5 h/day more leisure TV watching raised coronary artery disease risk (OR 1.44), partly independent of education and BMI.

pmid:20469800.authors: Cappuccio FP, D'Elia L, Strazzullo P, et al.
pmid:20469800.title: Sleep duration and all-cause mortality: a systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective studies.
pmid:20469800.finding: Both short sleep (RR 1.12) and long sleep (RR 1.30) predicted death, with significant heterogeneity for long sleep.

pmid:31488267.authors: Daghlas I, Dashti HS, Lane J, et al.
pmid:31488267.title: Sleep Duration and Myocardial Infarction.
pmid:31488267.finding: Short (<6 h) and long (>9 h) sleep predicted MI, but MR supported a causal effect only for short sleep (HR 1.19-1.21).

pmid:35129580.authors: Tasali E, Wroblewski K, Kahn E, et al.
pmid:35129580.title: Effect of Sleep Extension on Objectively Assessed Energy Intake Among Adults With Overweight in Real-life Settings: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
pmid:35129580.n: 80 adults with overweight who habitually curtailed sleep
pmid:35129580.finding: Extending sleep by about 1.2 h/night cut energy intake by 270 kcal/day, producing negative energy balance.

pmid:17478574.title: Shift work, confounding and death from ischaemic heart disease.
pmid:17478574.n: Nested case-control in a UK industrial cohort
pmid:17478574.finding: Shift workers were more often in lower social classes; after adjusting for pre-employment risk and social class, shift work was not associated with ischaemic heart disease death (OR 1.04).

pmid:31243001.authors: Richmond RC, Anderson EL, Dashti HS, et al.
pmid:31243001.title: Investigating causal relations between sleep traits and risk of breast cancer in women: mendelian randomisation study.
pmid:31243001.finding: MR supported a protective effect of morning chronotype on breast cancer (OR 0.88 per category) and a harmful effect of longer sleep.

pmid:41129148.authors: Windred DP, Burns AC, Rutter MK, et al.
pmid:41129148.title: Light Exposure at Night and Cardiovascular Disease Incidence.
pmid:41129148.finding: The brightest-night decile had higher incident coronary disease (aHR 1.32), MI (1.47), heart failure (1.56), AF (1.32) and stroke (1.28) after adjustment including socioeconomic status and polygenic risk.

pmid:35908583.authors: Kunutsor SK, Jae SY, Laukkanen JA
pmid:35908583.title: Frequent sauna bathing offsets the increased risk of death due to low socioeconomic status: A prospective cohort study of middle-aged and older men.
pmid:35908583.finding: In the same cohort, high vs low sauna frequency was associated with 14% lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.86) after multivariable adjustment, and appeared to offset the extra risk of low socioeconomic status.

pmid:29849692.title: Clinical Effects of Regular Dry Sauna Bathing: A Systematic Review.
pmid:29849692.finding: Systematic review: only 13 of 40 sauna studies were RCTs and most were small (n<40); reported benefits were heterogeneous.

pmid:39879231.authors: Cain T, Brinsley J, Bennett H, et al.
pmid:39879231.title: Effects of cold-water immersion on health and wellbeing: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:39879231.finding: Cold-water immersion produced an acute inflammatory response, a reduction in stress only at 12 h, and no significant immune effects; longer-term benefits came mainly from narrative synthesis.

pmid:27631616.authors: Buijze GA, Sierevelt IN, van der Heijden BC, et al.
pmid:27631616.title: The Effect of Cold Showering on Health and Work: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
pmid:27631616.finding: A routine hot-to-cold shower for 30-90 s cut self-reported sickness absence by 29% but did not reduce illness days.

pmid:24395196.authors: Goyal M, Singh S, Sibinga EM, et al.
pmid:24395196.title: Meditation programs for psychological stress and well-being: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:24395196.finding: Mindfulness programs gave small-to-moderate improvements in anxiety, depression and pain, and were not better than active treatments such as exercise or drugs.

pmid:37867573.authors: Galante J, Friedrich C, Collaboration of Mindfulness Trials (CoMinT) 3, et al.
pmid:37867573.title: Individual participant data systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials assessing adult mindfulness-based programmes for mental health promotion in non-clinical settings.
pmid:37867573.finding: Group mindfulness programmes reduced psychological distress versus passive controls (SMD -0.32) in community volunteers.

pmid:34531021.authors: Howard JP, Wood FA, Finegold JA, et al.
pmid:34531021.title: Side Effect Patterns in a Crossover Trial of Statin, Placebo, and No Treatment.
pmid:34531021.finding: Symptom scores were similar on statin (16.3) and placebo (15.4) months versus 8.0 with no tablet; 90% of statin symptom burden was nocebo.

pmid:33627334.authors: Herrett E, Williamson E, Brack K, et al.
pmid:33627334.title: Statin treatment and muscle symptoms: series of randomised, placebo controlled n-of-1 trials.
pmid:33627334.finding: In people who had stopped statins for muscle symptoms, atorvastatin 20 mg produced no more muscle symptoms than placebo; two thirds intended to restart.

pmid:23173135.title: Metformin and the risk of cancer: time-related biases in observational studies.
pmid:23173135.finding: Thirteen observational studies of metformin and cancer had immortal time bias and others time-window bias, producing illusory 20-94% risk reductions; studies avoiding these biases found no effect.

pmid:40388602.authors: Shadyab AH, Espeland MA, Odegaard AO, et al.
pmid:40388602.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Metformin Versus Sulfonylureas on Exceptional Longevity in Women With Type 2 Diabetes: Target Trial Emulation.
pmid:40388602.journal: J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci
pmid:40388602.finding: Target trial emulation: metformin initiation versus sulfonylurea was associated with 30% lower risk of death before age 90 (HR 0.70); authors note residual confounding prevents causal inference.

pmid:41207796.authors: Sheikh J, Allotey J, Sobhy S, et al.
pmid:41207796.title: Maternal paracetamol (acetaminophen) use during pregnancy and risk of autism spectrum disorder and attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder in offspring: umbrella review of systematic reviews.
pmid:41207796.finding: Umbrella review: confidence in reviews reporting a paracetamol-autism/ADHD link was low to critically low; in sibling-controlled studies the associations disappeared.

pmid:42773841.authors: Tayebi-Hillali H, Blanco-Suárez M, Rivas-Mundiña B, et al.
pmid:42773841.title: Prenatal exposure to paracetamol and the risk of autism and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: An umbrella review and meta-meta-analysis.
pmid:42773841.finding: Unrestricted pooling showed small associations (autism RR 1.17, ADHD 1.29) that attenuated toward null when restricted to higher-quality studies, consistent with residual confounding.

pmid:39562663.authors: Xie K, Li J, Tang C, et al.
pmid:39562663.title: Association between proton pump inhibitors and dementia risk: a Mendelian randomization study.
pmid:39562663.finding: No robust causal association between genetically proxied PPI use and dementia after false-discovery correction.

pmid:24491470.authors: Daniel S, Koren G, Lunenfeld E, et al.
pmid:24491470.title: Fetal exposure to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and spontaneous abortions.
pmid:24491470.finding: NSAID exposure was not an independent risk factor for spontaneous abortion (non-selective COX inhibitors aHR 1.10, 0.99-1.22), with no dose-response.

pmid:25265406.authors: Daniel S, Koren G, Lunenfeld E, et al.
pmid:25265406.title: Immortal time bias in drug safety cohort studies: spontaneous abortion following nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drug exposure.
pmid:25265406.finding: Treating NSAID exposure as fixed rather than time-varying produced immortal time bias that materially changed miscarriage hazard ratios.

pmid:25858169.authors: Daniel S, Koren G, Lunenfeld E, et al.
pmid:25858169.title: NSAIDs and spontaneous abortions - true effect or an indication bias?
pmid:25858169.finding: NSAID dispensing rose sharply in the days before a miscarriage (pain from the miscarriage itself); excluding those days removed the association, indicating protopathic/indication bias.

pmid:35816897.title: Appraising the causal role of smoking in multiple diseases: A systematic review and meta-analysis of Mendelian randomization studies.
pmid:35816897.finding: Genetic liability to smoking caused a wide range of diseases including 13 circulatory diseases, type 2 diabetes, periodontitis, PCOS and multiple cancers.

pmid:30646298.authors: Goniewicz ML, Smith DM, Edwards KC, et al.
pmid:30646298.title: Comparison of Nicotine and Toxicant Exposure in Users of Electronic Cigarettes and Combustible Cigarettes.
pmid:30646298.finding: Exclusive vapers had 10-98% lower toxicant biomarkers than smokers but higher than never users; dual users had the highest exposure.

pmid:35514292.authors: Berlowitz JB, Xie W, Harlow AF, et al.
pmid:35514292.title: E-Cigarette Use and Risk of Cardiovascular Disease: A Longitudinal Analysis of the PATH Study (2013-2019).
pmid:35514292.finding: Exclusive e-cigarette use was not associated with incident CVD (HR 1.00, 0.69-1.45), whereas exclusive smoking (1.53) and dual use (1.54) were; few events among vapers limited precision.

pmid:31165662.title: Electronic Cigarette Use and Myocardial Infarction Among Adults in the US Population Assessment of Tobacco and Health.
pmid:31165662.finding: RETRACTED (2020): reported e-cigarette use associated with having had a myocardial infarction; the journal retracted it because the authors did not show whether infarctions occurred before or after vaping began, so the conclusion was judged unreliable.

pmid:41212103.authors: Lindson N, Livingstone-Banks J, Butler AR, et al.
pmid:41212103.title: Electronic cigarettes for smoking cessation.
pmid:41212103.finding: Cochrane: nicotine e-cigarettes increase quit rates compared with nicotine replacement therapy (RR 1.55, high certainty).

pmid:33251770.authors: Belladelli F, Del Giudice F, Kasman A, et al.
pmid:33251770.title: The association between cannabis use and testicular function in men: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
pmid:33251770.finding: Cannabis use was not significantly associated with abnormal semen parameters (RR 1.16, 0.84-1.60) or testosterone; FSH slightly lower.

pmid:36047080.authors: Belladelli F, Chen T, Basran S, et al.
pmid:36047080.title: The Association between Monthly, Yearly, and Lifetime Cannabis Use, and Semen Parameters in Asian-American Men.
pmid:36047080.finding: Recent cannabis use was linked to slightly worse morphology and motility, but there was no consistent association with semen quality.

pmid:37042163.authors: Zufferey F, Buitrago E, Rahban R, et al.
pmid:37042163.title: Gonadotropin axis and semen quality in young Swiss men after cannabis consumption: Effect of chronicity and modulation by cannabidiol.
pmid:37042163.finding: Cannabis users had higher androgens and, apparently, better progressive motility, which was explained by shorter abstinence time rather than cannabis.

pmid:24697969.authors: Lindqvist PG, Epstein E, Landin-Olsson M, et al.
pmid:24697969.title: Avoidance of sun exposure is a risk factor for all-cause mortality: results from the Melanoma in Southern Sweden cohort.
pmid:24697969.finding: Women who avoided sun had about twice the mortality of the most sun-exposed, an observational finding the authors used to question restrictive sun advice.

pmid:21803414.authors: Holmes MV, Newcombe P, Hubacek JA, et al.
pmid:21803414.title: Effect modification by population dietary folate on the association between MTHFR genotype, homocysteine, and stroke risk: a meta-analysis of genetic studies and randomised trials.
pmid:21803414.finding: MTHFR-homocysteine effects and stroke associations were large only in low-folate regions; trials in folate-replete regions matched genetic predictions of no benefit.

pmid:21325005.authors: C Reactive Protein Coronary Heart Disease Genetics Collaboration (CCGC), Wensley F, Gao P, et al.
pmid:21325005.title: Association between C reactive protein and coronary heart disease: mendelian randomisation analysis based on individual participant data.
pmid:21325005.finding: Genetically raised CRP was not associated with coronary heart disease (RR 1.00), unlike measured CRP (RR 1.33), so CRP itself is unlikely to be causal.

pmid:22421340.authors: Interleukin-6 Receptor Mendelian Randomisation Analysis (IL6R MR) Consortium, Swerdlow DI, Holmes MV, et al.
pmid:22421340.title: The interleukin-6 receptor as a target for prevention of coronary heart disease: a mendelian randomisation analysis.
pmid:22421340.finding: An IL6R variant mimicking IL-6 receptor blockade lowered CRP and coronary heart disease odds (OR 0.95 per allele), supporting a causal role for IL-6 signalling.

pmid:32865380.authors: Nidorf SM, Fiolet ATL, Mosterd A, et al.
pmid:32865380.title: Colchicine in Patients with Chronic Coronary Disease.
pmid:32865380.finding: Low-dose colchicine cut cardiovascular events by 31% (HR 0.69), with a non-significant rise in non-cardiovascular death.

pmid:39555823.authors: Jolly SS, d'Entremont MA, Lee SF, et al.
pmid:39555823.title: Colchicine in Acute Myocardial Infarction.
pmid:39555823.finding: Colchicine started soon after MI lowered CRP but did not reduce cardiovascular events over 3 years (HR 0.99).

pmid:25948669.authors: Kobylecki CJ, Afzal S, Davey Smith G, et al.
